name: Aam Panna

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Aam Tel Muri Makha (Mango-Pickle Oil & Spiced Puffed Rice Tiffin)

ingredients.name: Aam Tel (Mango Pickle Oil with Masala)

steps.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine chopped onion, green chillies, coriander, black salt, and aam tel (mango pickle oil with its spice bits). Toss lightly so the onion absorbs the tangy pickle masala.
Add crisp puffed rice, roasted peanuts, and chanachur. Toss briskly by hand or spoon for 30 seconds and serve immediately while crunchy.

notes: Classic Bengali tiffin using leftover mango pickle oil; serve right away so muri stays crisp.

name: Aar Macher Khichuri (Bengali River Catfish & Roasted Moong Dal Khichuri)

steps.text: Marinate Aar fish pieces with salt and turmeric, sear lightly in hot mustard oil, and set aside. In the same oil, fry halved potatoes, then saute sliced onions and ginger-garlic-chilli paste with ground spices.

Add dry-roasted moong dal, washed Gobindobhog rice, and fried potatoes to the pot. Pour 4.5 cups of hot water, cover, and simmer on medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes until rice and dal are soft and creamy.

steps.section: Nestle fish and finish with ghee
steps.text: Gently tuck the fried Aar fish steaks into the simmering khichuri, drizzle desi ghee and Bengali garam masala, cover for 5 minutes on low heat to infuse fish flavor, and serve hot.

notes: Rich, savory Bengali river fish khichuri where meaty Aar steaks infuse the spiced rice-lentil pot.

name: Abar Khabo Sandesh (Stuffed Pistachio-Khoya & Rose Chhena Sandesh)

steps.text: Lightly cook grated khoya with 2 tbsp sugar, cardamom powder, rose water, and finely chopped pistachios, cashews, and raisins; cool and roll into small balls.
Knead chhena with the remaining sugar until smooth and cook on low flame for 7–8 minutes until soft and pliable without browning.

steps.section: Encase khoya filling inside chhena spheres
steps.text: Flatten portions of warm chhena dough, stuff each with a spiced khoya-nut ball, seal into smooth spheres, and garnish with saffron and pistachios.

notes: Legendary Kolkata sweet created by Nobin Chandra Das whose name translates to 'I will eat it again'.

name: Achari Aloo (Pickled Five-Spice Tangy Baby Potatoes)

ingredients.name: Achari Masala (Fennel, Mustard, Nigella, Fenugreek & Cumin Seeds, Coarsely Crushed)

steps.section: Crack achari spices in smoking mustard oil
steps.text: Heat mustard oil until smoking, cool slightly, and crackle dry red chillies, hing, and the coarsely crushed achari five-spice blend.
Add halved boiled potatoes, ginger, turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli, amchur, and salt; toss on medium flame for 10-12 minutes until crusted and tangy.

notes: Bold, tangy pickle-spiced potatoes great with poori, paratha, or dal-chawal.

name: Achari Gobi Roll (Pickled Mustard-Spice Cauliflower Kathi Roll)

ingredients.name: Whole Wheat Flour or Maida Parathas

steps.text: Heat mustard oil in a kadhai until smoking slightly, lower flame, and crackle panch phoron. Add minced ginger and chopped cauliflower florets with salt, turmeric, and chilli powder; stir-fry on medium-high heat for 10 minutes until tender and charred at the edges.

steps.section: Finish with pickle spice and assemble
steps.text: Toss the cooked cauliflower with amchur and mango pickle masala oil. Warm two flaky parathas on a tawa, spoon the achari gobi down the center, top with sliced onion and lemon juice, and roll tightly.

notes: No blender or mixer needed; hand-minced ginger and ready pickle masala give deep achari tang.

name: Achari Khichdi (Tangy Pickled-Spice Moong & Chana Dal Khichdi)

ingredients.name: Panch Phoron / Achari Spices (Fennel, Mustard, Nigella, Fenugreek, Cumin)

steps.text: Wash rice, moong dal, and chana dal after soaking for 15 minutes. Pressure-cook with 4 cups water, turmeric, and salt for 3 whistles until soft and porridge-like.
Heat mustard oil and ghee in a small pan until smoking, crackle fennel, mustard, nigella, fenugreek, cumin seeds, hing, dry red chillies, and garlic until golden.
Stir tangy mango pickle masala into the tempering, pour over the hot khichdi, mix gently, and garnish with fresh coriander leaves.

notes: Elevated everyday khichdi infused with aromatic five-spice pickle tempering and tangy mango pickle oil.

name: Achari Mathri (Tangy Pickle-Masala Layered Flaky Savory Crackers)

ingredients.name: Mango or Mixed Pickle Masala (Achari Sambhar)

steps.section: Knead dough with achari masala and five-spice
steps.text: Mix maida, besan, ghee, pickle masala oil, crushed achari spices, turmeric, and salt, and knead into a firm dough.
Roll out the dough, brush with a thin layer of pickle masala, roll into a tight log, slice into pinwheels, and flatten slightly.

steps.section: Fry slowly until crisp and golden
steps.text: Fry on low-medium flame for 12–15 minutes until crisp and fragrant with tangy pickle spices.

notes: Bold, tangy pickle-spiced flaky mathri pinwheels.

name: Achari Paneer Masala (Tangy Five-Spice Pickling Masala Paneer Curry)

steps.section: Coarsely crush roasted achari spices and temper in mustard oil
steps.text: Coarsely crush half the fennel, mustard, cumin, and fenugreek seeds; heat mustard oil until smoking, crackle the remaining whole achari seeds and dry red chillies, and sauté chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste.

steps.section: Simmer tangy tomato-yogurt gravy with paneer
steps.text: Cook tomato puree, whisked yogurt, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli, and the crushed achari masala until oil separates; add warm water and seared paneer cubes, simmer 4 minutes, and garnish with coriander.

notes: Pungent mustard oil and freshly crushed panch-phoron/achari spices give this curry a bold pickle-like tang.

name: Achari Sooji Toast Sandwich (Pickled Spice Semolina & Curd Vegetable Bread Toast)

steps.text: Mix fine sooji, whisked curd, mango pickle masala oil, chopped onion, capsicum, tomato, and salt with 2–3 tbsp water into a thick spreadable paste; rest 8 minutes.

steps.section: Spread on bread and tawa-toast crisp
steps.text: Spread the achari sooji mix evenly on one side of each bread slice. Heat butter/oil on a flat tawa, place slices sooji-side down, cook 3–4 minutes on medium-low heat until golden crisp, then flip and toast the other side 2 minutes.

notes: Resting the sooji for 8 minutes softens the grains so they toast crisp instead of gritty.

name: Ajwain Paratha (Carom Seed Layered Flaky Paratha)

steps.text: Knead soft wheat dough. Roll into a circle, brush with ghee, sprinkle crushed ajwain and salt, fold into a square or triangle, and roll out.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until crisp golden blisters appear. Serve with masala chai or pickle.

notes: Digestive, aromatic everyday Indian breakfast paratha.

name: Aloo Baingan Masala (Homestyle Potato & Brinjal Curry)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with panch phoron/cumin and hing, and fry cubed potatoes for 4 minutes before adding cubed brinjal.
Add ginger, chopped tomatoes, turmeric, coriander, red chilli powder, and salt; cover and cook on medium-low heat until soft and jammy.

notes: Comforting homestyle sabzi that pairs with both roti and dal-rice.

name: Aloo Beans Bhaja (Crispy French Beans & Potato Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Nigella Seeds (Kalo Jeere) or Cumin Seeds

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with nigella/cumin seeds and green chillies, and fry potato strips for 4 minutes.
Add French beans, turmeric, cumin powder, and salt; cook covered for 5 minutes, then uncover and stir-fry with black pepper until crisp-tender.

notes: Quick everyday dry side dish for lunchboxes and weekday meals.

name: Aloo Bhaja

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Aloo Bharta (Potato Mash)

ingredients.name: Red Chilli (Shukno Lonka) or Green Chilli

steps.text: Wash and boil the potatoes until fork-tender, then drain, cool slightly, and peel off the skins.
Heat mustard oil until smoking, fry dry red chillies until crisp, and crush them with a pinch of salt. Optionally lightly sauté half of the chopped onion.
Mash the warm potatoes smoothly with crushed chillies, raw or fried onion, green chilli, fresh coriander leaves, salt, and raw mustard oil. Serve warm with steamed rice and dal.

notes: Using pungent kachi ghani mustard oil and a mix of raw and lightly fried onions gives authentic Bengali Aloo Bharta flavour.

name: Aloo Bhindi Masala (Crispy Okra & Potato Stir-Fry)

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle cumin and ajwain, and fry potato wedges until golden and 75% tender.
Add okra pieces and sliced onion; cook uncovered on medium flame with turmeric, coriander, and chilli powder for 8 minutes, then season with salt and amchur at the end.

notes: Adding salt and amchur at the very end keeps the okra crisp and non-slimy.

name: Aloo Bhujia (Crispy Spiced Mashed Potato, Mint & Besan Sev Namkeen)

steps.text: Knead finely grated boiled potatoes with besan, rice flour, turmeric, chilli powder, garam masala, hing, and 1 tbsp oil into a smooth dough without adding water.

steps.section: Press fine sev into medium-hot oil
steps.text: Extrude the dough through the fine disc of a sev maker into medium-hot oil and fry for 1–2 minutes per side until crisp and golden.

steps.section: Toss warm strands with mint-amchur masala
steps.text: Drain excess oil, crush lightly into short noodles, and toss with dry mint powder, chaat masala, amchur, and black salt.

notes: Tangy, melt-in-the-mouth potato sev seasoned with dried mint and chaat masala.

name: Aloo Bori Jhol (Bengali Sun-Dried Lentil Dumpling & Potato Light Broth)

ingredients.name: Bengali Urad/moong Dal Bori (Sun-dried Lentil Dumplings)

steps.text: Fry the sun-dried lentil dumplings (bori) in hot mustard oil until golden brown and remove immediately.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, fry potato wedges with ginger paste, cumin powder, turmeric, and tomato, then add warm water and cook until potatoes are soft.
Drop in the fried boris, simmer for 3 minutes until they soften slightly while keeping a bite, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Soothing, light Bengali summer lunch jhol.

name: Aloo Chingri Kalia (Bengali Prawn & Potato Kalia)

steps.text: Marinate prawns and potatoes with turmeric and salt. Lightly fry prawns for 2 minutes; fry potatoes until golden brown.
Temper mustard oil with whole garam masala and bay leaf. Fry onions, then add ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, whisked yogurt, and spices until oil separates.
Add potatoes and warm water; simmer until potatoes soften, then add prawns and cook for 5 minutes. Finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: A richer, festive version of prawn potato curry ideal for Sunday lunches and special occasions.

name: Aloo Chokha (Bihari Spiced Potato Bharta)

steps.text: Boil potatoes until soft, peel, and mash while warm so no large lumps remain.
Roast dry red chillies and garlic cloves over a direct flame or in a dry pan until aromatic, then crush coarsely.
Fold finely chopped onion, crushed garlic-chilli, green chillies, coriander, lemon juice, salt, and raw mustard oil into the mashed potatoes.

notes: Pairs classically with dal-chawal, khichdi, or litti.

name: Aloo Chorchori (Bengali Mustard-Seasoned Potato Baton Medley)

steps.text: Temper mustard oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies; add potato batons, chopped tomato, turmeric, and salt, and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add warm water, cover and cook until potatoes are soft, then stir in mustard paste and simmer for 4 minutes until semi-dry. Finish with coriander and raw mustard oil.

notes: Tangy, pungent Bengali mustard potato chorchori.

name: Aloo Diye Macher Dimer Jhuri (Crisp Potato Matchsticks & Crumbled Fish Egg Stir-Fry)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with nigella seeds, and fry potato matchsticks with a pinch of turmeric until golden and tender-crisp.
Push potatoes aside, add sliced onion, green chillies, and mashed fish eggs with salt and chilli powder, and stir-fry until the roe turns crumbly.
Mix the crisp potatoes and golden fish roe granules together and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Great side dish alongside masoor dal and steamed rice.

name: Aloo Do Pyaza

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Aloo Dry Curry

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.

Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Aloo Gobi Adraki (Dry Spiced Ginger Potato & Cauliflower Stir-Fry)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle cumin seeds, and pan-roast potato wedges and cauliflower florets on medium-high flame for 6 minutes until lightly browned.
Add chopped onion, ginger juliennes, green chillies, turmeric, coriander, red chilli powder, and salt; cover on low heat (no water) until tender-crisp.
Add chopped tomato, amchur, garam masala, and kasuri methi; toss uncovered for 3 minutes.

notes: Cooking without water keeps the cauliflower florets firm and flavorful.

name: Aloo Gobi Paratha (Dhaba-Style Spiced Potato & Cauliflower Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Combine mashed potato, finely grated cauliflower, ginger, chillies, coriander, ajwain, amchur, garam masala, and salt just before rolling so the stuffing stays dry.
Enclose a generous ball of filling inside a cup of rolled wheat dough, dust with flour, and roll out gently without bursting.
Roast on a hot tawa with ghee or butter, pressing the edges until blistered and crisp. Serve with curd, butter, and mango pickle.

notes: Quintessential Punjabi highway dhaba breakfast paratha uniting spiced potatoes and cauliflower.

name: Aloo Gobi Roll (Spiced Potato & Cauliflower Kathi Roll)

steps.text: Heat oil in a pan, crackle cumin seeds, and saute chopped onion and grated ginger for 3 minutes. Add diced potato, cauliflower, turmeric, coriander powder, and salt; cover and cook on low-medium heat for 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until dry and crisp-edged.

Sprinkle garam masala over the dry aloo gobi. Crisp two parathas on a tawa, layer the hot aloo gobi down the middle with raw onion rings, green chillies, chaat masala, and lemon juice, then roll tightly.

notes: Keep the aloo gobi filling completely dry so the paratha stays crisp.

name: Aloo Jhol

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Aloo Kabli (Kolkata Street-Style Tangy Boiled Potato & Chickpea Chaat)

steps.section: Toss potatoes with chickpeas, salad and spices
steps.text: Combine cubed boiled potatoes, chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, onion, green chillies, and coriander in a bowl.

steps.section: Dress with tamarind, bhaja masala and chanachur
steps.text: Add tangy tamarind pulp, Gondhoraj lemon juice, bitnoon, and roasted bhaja masala; toss well and top with crunchy chanachur.

notes: A nostalgic outside-school-gate Kolkata street chaat.

name: Aloo Kabli Muri Makha (Spiced Potato, Sprouted Gram & Puffed Rice)

steps.text: Toss diced boiled potato, kala chana, onion, tomato, cucumber, green chilli, coriander, bhaja masala, black salt, and tamarind pulp in a bowl.
Just before serving, fold in crisp muri and toss gently so every grain gets lightly coated with tangy Aloo Kabli spices.

notes: Hand-soak seedless tamarind in warm water and squeeze through a strainer—no blender needed.

name: Aloo Kabuli Chana Tarkari (Bengali Chickpea & Potato Curry)

steps.text: Temper mustard oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and hing; fry cubed potatoes and chopped onion until golden.
Add ginger paste, chopped tomato, cumin, coriander, and turmeric; cook until pulpy.
Add boiled kabuli chana and warm water; simmer for 9 minutes, lightly mashing a few potatoes, and finish with roasted bhaja masala.

notes: Hearty accompaniment to luchi, radhaballabhi, or pitai paratha.

name: Aloo Korma

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Aloo Laccha Tawa Hashbrowns (Indian Spiced Crispy Grated Potato Patties)

steps.section: Rinse, squeeze, and season grated potatoes
steps.text: Rinse coarsely grated potatoes in cold water until the water runs clear, then squeeze firmly in a clean cloth by hand until completely dry. Toss with cornflour, chopped green chilli, ginger, cumin powder, coriander, and salt.
Heat oil on a flat tawa, press small flat patties of the mixture onto the surface, and cook 5–6 minutes per side on medium heat until deep golden and crisp. Dust with chaat masala and serve hot.

notes: Hand-squeezing out all starch water is the key to ultra-crisp laccha hashbrowns.

name: Aloo Lachha Namkeen / Farali Potato Chiwda (Crispy Potato Juliennes, Peanuts & Cashews)

steps.section: Rinse starch from potato juliennes and dry completely
steps.text: Wash grated potato sticks 3–4 times in cold water until the water runs clear, then spread on a kitchen towel to dry completely.

steps.section: Deep-fry potato sticks and nuts until crisp
steps.text: Fry the dried potato juliennes in medium-hot oil in batches until crisp and golden; separately fry peanuts, cashews, almonds, raisins, and curry leaves.

steps.section: Toss lightly with rock salt, pepper, and sugar
steps.text: Gently toss the crisp potato lachha and dry fruits with rock salt, freshly ground black pepper, roasted cumin, and powdered sugar.

notes: Crisp potato-and-nut namkeen popular both as an everyday snack and on fasting days.

name: Aloo Makha Muri (Mustard-Oil Mashed Potato & Crisp Puffed Rice Tiffin)

ingredients.name: Red Chillies (Fried Crisp in Mustard Oil)

steps.text: Crush the fried dry red chillies with salt by hand, then mash boiled potatoes with chopped onion and mustard oil until smooth and fragrant.
Serve the warm spiced aloo makha alongside or lightly folded into crisp puffed rice for a comforting Bengali morning or evening tiffin.

notes: Homestyle Bengali comfort tiffin; crumble dry red chillies with salt using fingertips.

name: Aloo Masala

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Aloo Masala Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Aloo Masala Sooji Sandwich (Breadless Crisp Semolina Sandwich Stuffed with Spiced Potato)

steps.section: Make sooji batter and spiced potato patties
steps.text: Whisk sooji, curd, salt, and 1/2 cup water into a thick batter; rest 10 minutes. Mix mashed potatoes with onion, green chilli, coriander, turmeric, cumin, chaat masala, and salt; shape into 2 thin flat patties.

steps.section: Layer and cook on covered tawa
steps.text: Stir baking soda into the batter. Pour a thin layer on a greased hot tawa/toast maker, place a potato patty in the center, cover with more batter, and cook covered on low heat 4 minutes per side until golden and crisp. Slice into triangles.

notes: Completely breadless crispy sandwich made with just a covered pan or sandwich toaster.

name: Aloo Matar (Homestyle Spiced Potato & Green Peas Curry)

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle cumin seeds, brown chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste, then cook tomato puree and spice powders until oil separates.
Add cubed potatoes, green peas, salt, and warm water; cover and simmer for 12 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Stir in garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, and chopped coriander leaves.

notes: Comforting everyday curry for roti, paratha, poori, or jeera rice.

name: Aloo Matar Paratha (Spiced Potato & Green Peas Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Mix mashed potatoes with crushed green peas, grated ginger, chillies, coriander, chaat masala, cumin, crushed kasuri methi, and salt.
Wrap the potato-pea mixture inside dough portions, pinch to seal, and roll into even round flatbreads.
Roast on medium flame with generous ghee until golden brown specks appear on both sides. Serve hot with chilled raita.

notes: A wholesome winter favorite combining soft potatoes with sweet green peas.

name: Aloo Methi (Fresh Fenugreek Leaves & Crispy Potato Stir-Fry)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with cumin seeds, hing, chopped garlic, and dry red chillies, and fry cubed potatoes with turmeric until golden and 80% cooked.
Add chopped fenugreek leaves, coriander powder, and salt; stir-fry uncovered on medium-low heat for 6 minutes until the methi wilts and coats the potatoes.

notes: Cooking uncovered after adding methi prevents the leaves from turning bitter.

name: Aloo Methi Paratha (Spiced Potato & Fresh Fenugreek Leaves Stuffed Paratha)

steps.section: Sauté methi and mix with potato
steps.text: Briefly sauté chopped fresh methi leaves in 1 tsp oil to remove raw bitterness, then fold into mashed potatoes with ginger-chilli paste, ajwain, amchur, chilli powder, and salt.
Stuff the fragrant aloo-methi mixture inside whole wheat dough balls and roll into thick round parathas.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until blistered and crusty on both sides. Serve with plain yogurt or fresh mint chutney.

notes: Combines the earthy bitterness of fresh seasonal fenugreek with comforting spiced potatoes.

name: Aloo Palak (Potatoes in Spiced Garlic Spinach Gravy)

steps.text: Pan-fry cubed potatoes in oil with a pinch of salt and turmeric until golden and tender; set aside.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and chopped garlic, fry chopped onion and tomato with spices until soft.
Stir in the blanched spinach puree and fried potatoes, simmer gently for 5 minutes, and finish with garam masala.

notes: Nutritious spinach and potato curry great with phulkas or steamed rice.

name: Aloo Paneer Dalna (Bengali Homestyle Niramish Paneer & Potato Curry with Cumin & Gorom Moshla)

steps.section: Golden-fry paneer cubes and soak in warm salted water
steps.text: Lightly fry paneer cubes in oil with a pinch of turmeric until pale golden, then soak immediately in warm salted water for 5 minutes so the paneer stays pillowy soft.

steps.section: Sauté potatoes and cook ginger-cashew-tomato masala
steps.text: Fry potato cubes until golden; temper oil with bay leaf, whole cumin, and whole garam masala, cook ginger paste, tomato, cumin powder, and cashew-melon seed paste until oil separates.

steps.section: Simmer with drained paneer and finish with ghee
steps.text: Add 1.25 cups warm water and potatoes, simmer until tender, fold in the soaked paneer cubes, sugar, ghee, and gorom moshla, and simmer 3 minutes.

notes: Soaking lightly fried paneer cubes in warm salted water keeps them melt-in-the-mouth soft inside the curry.

name: Aloo Paneer Paratha (Spiced Potato & Grated Cottage Cheese Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Combine mashed potato and grated paneer with green chillies, ginger, fresh coriander, garam masala, amchur, and salt into a smooth, malleable stuffing.
Enclose stuffing balls in whole wheat dough portions, seal tightly, and roll gently on a floured board.
Cook on a hot tawa with generous butter or ghee until crisp and spotted with golden blisters. Serve with dahi and mixed pickle.

notes: The ultimate crowd-pleasing combination of creamy paneer and spiced potato.

name: Aloo Papad / Sun-Dried Grated Potato & Red Chilli Flake Papad (Traditional Hand-Pressed Boiled Potato Crisps)

steps.section: Grate boiled potatoes and knead smooth spiced dough
steps.text: Grate cooled boiled potatoes using the fine side of a handheld grater so there are zero lumps. Add cumin seeds, red chilli flakes, hing, chopped coriander, salt, and 1 tbsp oil, and knead by hand for 4–5 minutes into a smooth, elastic potato dough.

steps.section: Press thin rounds between oiled plastic sheets
steps.text: Grease palms with oil, roll small balls of potato dough, place between two oiled plastic sheets, and press firmly with a flat steel plate or chakla into thin, even circles.
Peel off the top sheet, sun-dry the potato discs for 1–2 days until crisp and dry, and flash-fry in medium-hot oil for 2–3 seconds per side until golden.

notes: Using a fine handheld grater instead of mashing produces silky, lump-free Aloo Papads that press paper-thin without tearing.

name: Aloo Paratha

steps.text: Mix flour and salt; add water gradually and knead to a soft dough. Rest covered.
Divide into portions and roll or shape according to the bread style.
Cook on a hot tawa or fry as appropriate, turning until cooked and golden.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Aloo Peyajkoli Bhaja (Winter Spring Onion Stalks & Potato Stir-Fry)

steps.text: Temper mustard oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies; fry potato strips with turmeric for 4 minutes.
Add onion flower stalks and salt; stir-fry on medium heat for 7-8 minutes until tender-crisp and lightly charred.

notes: Winter staple in Bengali homes.

name: Aloo Phulkopi Bori Jhol (Winter Cauliflower, New Potato & Fried Bori Light Cumin-Ginger Curry)

ingredients.name: Biulir Daler Bori or Motor Daler Bori

steps.section: Fry bori and golden-roast cauliflower florets
steps.text: Fry the bori in mustard oil until golden and set aside; pan-roast cauliflower florets and potato wedges with a pinch of turmeric and salt until lightly browned.

steps.section: Simmer in ginger-cumin gravy with fried bori
steps.text: Temper oil with cumin and bay leaf, cook ginger paste, tomato, cumin-coriander powder, and turmeric, add 1.5 cups warm water, potatoes, cauliflower, and fried bori, and simmer until tender; finish with coriander and ghee.

notes: A classic winter Bengali household curry that pairs with both steamed rice and hot rotis.

name: Aloo Phulkopi Dalna (Bengali Roasted Cauliflower & Potato Curry)

steps.text: Fry cauliflower florets and potato wedges in mustard oil until golden-brown spots appear; set aside.
Temper oil with bay leaf, whole garam masala, and cumin seeds; cook ginger paste, chopped tomato, and spice powders until fragrant.
Add roasted potatoes, cauliflower, green peas, and warm water; simmer until tender and finish with ghee and garam masala.

notes: Pairs equally well with steamed rice, luchi, or radhaballabhi.

name: Aloo Posto

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Aloo Potol Dalna (Bengali Pointed Gourd & Potato Curry)

steps.text: Fry scraped pointed gourd halves and potato wedges in mustard oil with a pinch of turmeric and salt until golden brown; remove.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste, chopped tomato, and spice powders until oil separates.
Return fried potol and potatoes with warm water, salt, and a pinch of sugar; simmer covered until tender and finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: One of the most beloved everyday and festive Bengali vegetable curries.

name: Aloo Potol Diye Macher Dimer Borar Jhol (Pointed Gourd, Potato & Fish Egg Fritter Curry)

steps.section: Fry fish egg boras, potol and potatoes
steps.text: Make small boras from fish eggs, chopped onion, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry in mustard oil. Fry potol halves and potato wedges until golden.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste, chopped tomato, turmeric, and cumin-coriander powder.
Add fried potatoes, potol, and warm water; simmer until tender, then add the fish roe boras for the final 4 minutes and finish with garam masala.

notes: Wholesome Bengali summer lunch curry.

name: Aloo Puri (Mashed Potato & Spice Kneaded Crispy Poori)

steps.text: Mix finely grated boiled potatoes, wheat flour, sooji, ajwain, kasuri methi, coriander, spices, and salt; knead into a firm dough using minimal water.
Roll oiled dough balls into small discs and fry in hot oil until puffed and golden brown.

notes: So flavorful they can be eaten on their own with curd, pickle, or chai.

name: Aloo Pyaz Paratha (Dhaba-Style Spiced Potato & Crunchy Onion Stuffed Paratha)

steps.section: Mix potato and crunchy onion filling
steps.text: Toss mashed potatoes with finely chopped raw onions, chillies, ginger, coriander, crushed coriander seeds, ajwain, amchur, chilli powder, and salt.
Stuff a large portion of filling into each rolled wheat dough disc, seal the top, and roll into a medium-thick circle.
Roast on a hot griddle with dollops of ghee or butter until deeply golden and flaky with crunchy onion bits. Serve with white makkhan and spiced boondi raita.

notes: The most ordered paratha at Grand Trunk Road dhabas, celebrated for its crunchy onion texture.

name: Aloo Sadeko (Nepali Spiced Boiled Potato Salad with Timur & Mustard Oil)

steps.text: Place diced boiled potatoes in a mixing bowl with sliced onion, green chillies, fresh coriander, timur, roasted cumin powder, and salt.
Heat mustard oil in a small pan until smoking. Add fenugreek seeds and fry until dark brown and aromatic. Stir in turmeric powder and immediately pour the sizzling oil over the potatoes.
Drizzle with fresh lemon juice, toss thoroughly to coat every potato cube in the fragrant spiced oil, and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Classic Nepali potato salad renowned for the tingling citrus aroma of Himalayan timur and smoky fenugreek-mustard oil.

name: Aloo Shimla Mirch (Potato & Capsicum Stir-Fry)

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle cumin seeds, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, and cook cubed potatoes with turmeric and salt covered until nearly tender.
Add cubed bell peppers, chopped tomato, coriander powder, chilli powder, and amchur; stir-fry for 5-6 minutes so the capsicum retains a slight crunch.

notes: Flavorful tiffin sabzi that pairs wonderfully with parathas.

name: Aloo Shorshe

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Aloo Soyabean Kosha (Bengali Soya Chunks & Potato Curry)

steps.text: Boil soya chunks in salted water, squeeze dry, and pan-fry in mustard oil with turmeric alongside potato cubes until golden.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, brown chopped onions, and roast ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and spice powders until oil separates.
Add fried potatoes, soya chunks, and warm water; simmer covered for 7 minutes until tender and finish with garam masala.

notes: High-protein homestyle Bengali soya-potato curry.

name: Aloo Stuffed Bread Pakora (Classic Street-Style Spiced Potato Bread Fritters)

steps.section: Prepare spiced potato stuffing and besan batter
steps.text: Mix mashed boiled potatoes with grated ginger, green chillies, coriander, amchur, red chilli, coriander powder, garam masala, and salt. In another bowl, whisk besan, rice flour, ajwain, turmeric, baking soda, salt, and water by hand into a smooth medium-thick coating batter.

steps.section: Stuff, dip, and fry crisp triangles
steps.text: Spread the potato masala between two bread slices, press gently, and slice diagonally into triangles. Dip each triangle completely in the besan batter and fry in hot oil on medium heat until puffed and golden brown.

notes: Adding 1 tbsp rice flour to the besan batter keeps the crust crisp and less oily.

name: Aloo Tikki

steps.text: Wash, chop or mash ingredients and mix with seasoning.
Mash potatoes with spices, shape into patties and shallow-fry until golden.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

name: Aloo Torkari

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Aloo Uchhe Bhaja (Crispy Fried Bitter Gourd & Potato Slices)

steps.text: Toss thinly sliced bitter gourd and potatoes with salt and turmeric powder.
Heat mustard oil in a wide skillet and fry the slices on medium heat until crisp and golden brown.

notes: Classic Bengali first-course lunch accompaniment eaten with plain hot rice and ghee.

name: Aloor Bora / Potato Bajji (Crispy Spiced Besan Batter-Fried Potato Round Fritters)

steps.section: Soak and dry thin potato discs
steps.text: Slice potatoes evenly into thin discs, rinse in cold water to remove surface starch, and pat dry on a cloth.

steps.section: Dip in aerated spiced besan batter and fry
steps.text: Whisk besan, rice flour, kalo jeere, ajwain, ginger paste, turmeric, chilli powder, salt, baking soda, and water into a smooth batter; dip potato slices and fry in medium-hot oil until puffed like pooris.

notes: Quick, crowd-pleasing evening snack served with muri (puffed rice) or masala chai.

name: Aloor Chokka (Bengali Spiced Potato & Black Chickpea Curry)

ingredients.name: Boiled Kala Chana (Black Chickpeas) or Grated Coconut

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and panch phoron, and fry cubed potatoes for 4-5 minutes until lightly golden.
Add ginger paste, chopped tomato, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and salt; sauté until tomatoes soften.

steps.section: Simmer with chana and bhaja masala
steps.text: Add boiled kala chana and warm water; cover and cook until potatoes are tender and gravy is thick. Finish with sugar and roasted bhaja masala.

notes: Classic Bengali winter and festive side dish for luchi, porota, or khichuri.

name: Alsi ke Laddoo (Roasted Flaxseed, Wheat & Jaggery Winter Laddoo)

ingredients.name: Flaxseeds (Alsi, Dry-roasted & Hand-crushed with Rolling Pin)

steps.section: Roast flaxseeds and whole wheat flour
steps.text: Dry-roast flaxseeds on low heat until they pop, cool, and crush coarsely on a board with a rolling pin. In the same kadhai, roast whole wheat flour in ghee on low flame for 12 minutes until nutty and golden.
Toss in crushed flaxseeds, chopped nuts, cardamom, and sonth. Turn off heat, mix in grated jaggery until melted from the residual warmth, and roll into firm round laddoos while warm.

notes: Crushing roasted flaxseeds under a rolling pin releases their nutty oils without needing a grinder.

name: Alu Kochuri (Kolkata Sweet-Shop Spiced Mashed Potato Stuffed Kochuri)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil with hing and kalo jeere. Add ginger-green chilli paste, mashed potatoes, bhaja masala, salt, and sugar. Sauté until completely dry and aromatic; let cool.
Rub maida with ghee and salt, knead into a soft pliable dough with warm water, rest 15 minutes, divide into balls, fill each with potato stuffing, and roll out gently.
Fry in medium-hot oil until puffed, crisp, and lightly golden. Serve hot with cholar dal or Kolkata-style aloor torkari.

notes: Classic neighborhood mishtir dokan (sweet-shop) breakfast kochuri of Bengal.

name: Alu Vadi / Gujarati Patra (Spiced Tamarind-Jaggery Besan Coated Colocasia Leaf Pinwheel Rolls)

ingredients.name: Tender Colocasia / Taro Leaves (Arbi Ke Patte, Veins Trimmed)

steps.section: Layer colocasia leaves with tangy besan paste
steps.text: Whisk besan, rice flour, tamarind pulp, jaggery, ginger-garlic-chilli paste, spices, sesame seeds, and water into a thick spreadable paste. Lay a large colocasia leaf vein-side up, smear paste evenly, layer 3–4 more coated leaves in alternating directions, fold sides in, and roll into a tight cylinder.
Place the leaf logs in a greased steamer and steam for 18–20 minutes until firm. Cool completely and slice into 1/2-inch pinwheels.
Heat oil in a wide pan, crackle mustard seeds, sesame seeds, hing, and curry leaves, sear the pinwheels until crisp on both sides, and garnish with fresh grated coconut.

notes: Tamarind plays an essential culinary role by neutralizing the natural calcium oxalate itchiness of colocasia leaves.

name: Alur Chop

steps.text: Chop or mash the main ingredients and combine with onion, chilli, spices and binder.
Shape into portions or coat in batter or breadcrumbs as appropriate.
Shallow-fry, deep-fry or bake until golden and cooked through. Drain and serve hot.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: American Chopsuey (Crispy Fried Noodles Topped with Sweet & Tangy Indo-Chinese Vegetable Sauce)

steps.section: Deep-fry cornflour-dusted noodles into a crispy nest
steps.text: Spread boiled noodles to air-dry for 10 minutes, toss with cornflour, and deep-fry in hot oil until crisp and golden on both sides; drain on paper towels.

Sauté minced garlic in 1 tbsp oil, stir-fry onion, carrot, cabbage, and capsicum for 3 minutes, then add ketchup, chilli sauce, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and cornflour slurry; simmer until glossy and thick.
Place the crispy fried noodle nest on a platter, pour the hot sweet-and-tangy vegetable gravy over the top, and crown with spring onions (and an optional sunny-side-up fried egg).

notes: Crunchy fried noodle nest smothered in glossy sweet, sour, and spicy Indo-Chinese sauce.

name: Americano

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Amish Chingri Paporer Dolma (Bengali Prawn & Potato Stuffed Papad Rolls in Spiced Onion-Tomato-Ginger Gravy)

ingredients.name: Small Prawns (Chingri, Shelled, Deveined & Finely Chopped)

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil, saute half the chopped onion, garlic, ginger, and finely chopped prawns with turmeric, chilli powder, and salt for 4 minutes. Mix in boiled mashed potato and 1/2 tsp gorom moshla to form a cohesive filling; cool.

steps.section: Roll dampened papads and fry golden
steps.text: Moisten each papad briefly in water until pliable, stuff with a portion of prawn-potato filling, fold sides in and roll tightly, seal with flour paste, and fry in mustard oil until golden brown.

Temper bay leaf and whole spices in mustard oil, brown the remaining onion, ginger, garlic, and tomato with spices, add 1.25 cups warm water, and simmer 5 minutes. Finish with ghee and gorom moshla, and ladle over the chingri paporer dolmas before serving.

notes: Festive Bengali non-vegetarian variation of Paporer Dolma combining sweet river prawns with crisp-fried papad shells.

name: Amritsari Aloo Kulcha (Crispy Spiced Potato Stuffed Kulcha)

steps.text: Knead flour with yogurt, baking powder, salt, and water; roll out, spread softened butter, fold like an envelope, and rest for 20 minutes so the crust bakes flaky.
Mix mashed potatoes with chopped onion, green chillies, coriander, crushed coriander seeds, and anardana/amchur. Stuff inside the laminated dough, top with coriander leaves, and roll oval.
Cook on a hot iron tawa (or bake at 220°C) until crisp and blistered, then slather generously with butter.

notes: Laminating the dough with butter gives Amritsari Kulcha its signature flaky crunch.

name: Anarsa (Traditional Crispy Rice Flour & Jaggery Pastry Crusted with White Sesame Seeds)

steps.text: Combine fine moist rice flour with powdered jaggery, knead firmly into balls using natural moisture, and let rest in an airtight jar for 2 days to ferment naturally.
Knead the rested dough soft with a few drops of milk, shape into small balls, flatten on a bed of white sesame seeds so one side is generously coated.
Slide sesame-side-up into warm ghee on low heat; spoon hot ghee continuously over the top without flipping until it turns golden brown with a characteristic netted, porous texture.

notes: An ancient festive Diwali delicacy with a shatteringly crisp sesame crust and soft caramelized interior.

name: Anda Sadeko (Nepali Spiced Hard-Boiled Egg Salad with Onion & Lime)

steps.text: In a mixing bowl, toss chopped onions, tomatoes, green chillies, coriander, roasted cumin, chaat masala, timur, salt, black salt, raw mustard oil, and lime juice.
Add the quartered boiled eggs and gently toss with your hands or a rubber spatula so the yolks remain intact while absorbing the spicy dressing.
Serve fresh as a high-protein Nepali khaja snack with beaten rice (chiura).

notes: Popular quick protein street snack served across Kathmandu cafes and local bhattis.

name: Andhra Challapunugulu / Sour Buttermilk Punugulu (Crispy Bite-Sized Maida, Rice Flour & Curd Street Fritters)

ingredients.name: Thick Sour Buttermilk or Whisked Sour Curd

steps.section: Whip sour buttermilk and flour batter
steps.text: Combine maida, rice flour, cumin seeds, salt, and sour buttermilk in a bowl. Beat well by hand for 4 minutes until smooth and thick; cover and rest for 30 minutes.

steps.section: Fold in chopped onions and aromatics
steps.text: Mix in finely chopped onion, green chillies, grated ginger, curry leaves, and baking soda right before frying.
Drop small bite-sized pearls of batter into medium-hot oil and fry until crisp and golden brown. Serve piping hot with peanut chutney or spicy tomato-red chilli chutney.

notes: Popular Vijayawada and Guntur evening street snack made instantly without idli-dosa batter.

name: Andhra Royyala Iguru (Spicy Andhra Prawn Masala)

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle curry leaves and slit green chillies, and fry chopped onions until deep golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste.
Add cleaned prawns, turmeric, red chilli powder, and salt; cook on medium heat until the moisture released by the prawns mostly evaporates.
Stir in the ground poppy seed and spice paste with a splash of water, roast until thick and oil separates, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Traditional coastal Andhra semi-dry prawn curry that pairs wonderfully with steamed rice and rasam.

name: Anjeer Dry Fruit Barfi (Sugar-Free Fig, Almond, Cashew & Pistachio Sweet)

steps.section: Roast nuts and poppy seeds in ghee
steps.text: Toast chopped almonds, cashews, pistachios, and walnuts in 1 tbsp ghee until crunchy; separately dry-roast poppy seeds.

steps.section: Cook fig and date paste until thick
steps.text: Sauté ground anjeer paste and dates in 1 tbsp ghee over low-medium heat for 8–10 minutes until glossy and thick.

steps.section: Fold in roasted nuts, roll in poppy seeds, and slice
steps.text: Mix in the toasted nuts and cardamom powder, shape into a firm log coated with poppy seeds, chill for 1 hour, and slice into discs.

notes: Naturally sweetened, nutrient-dense dry-fruit sweet with zero refined sugar.

name: Appam

steps.text: Wash, chop and measure the ingredients. Soak or ferment the base if the recipe requires it.
Heat oil, add mustard or cumin seeds, onion, chilli and vegetables.
Add the main ingredient and the required water or batter; cook until tender and serve hot.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

Heat oil or ghee; add cumin, garlic, onion and tomato and cook until fragrant.
Mix the tempering into the cooked dal, adjust water and salt, and simmer briefly.

name: Arisha Pitha / Odia Rice-Jaggery Sesame Sweet Discs (Crispy & Soft Fried Festive Pitha)

steps.section: Make jaggery syrup and rice-flour dough
steps.text: Melt grated jaggery in 1/2 cup water and boil 4–5 minutes until a soft-ball syrup forms. Lower heat and stir in fine rice flour and cardamom powder continuously with a wooden spoon until a smooth, non-sticky dough forms.
Grease palms with ghee, flatten lemon-sized dough balls into 3-inch discs, press white sesame seeds onto both sides, and fry in medium-hot oil/ghee until deep golden brown.

notes: Using store-bought fine rice flour keeps this festive pitha completely manual without soaking or grinding.

name: Assamese Maasor Dimo Tenga (Assamese Tangy Tomato & Lemon Fish Egg Curry)

ingredients.name: Fresh Lemon Juice (Kaji Nemu) or Tenga

steps.text: Mix fish eggs with chopped onion, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry small golden fritters in mustard oil.
Temper oil with fenugreek and mustard seeds, add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, salt, and lightly mashed boiled potato; cook until tomatoes break down into a tangy sauce.
Pour in warm water, add the fish egg boras and slit green chillies, simmer 5 minutes, and finish off-heat with lemon juice and fresh coriander.

notes: Light, oil-sparing Assamese sour curry ideal for warm days.

name: Assamese Maasor Konir Bora (Assamese Herb & Onion Fish Egg Fritters)

steps.section: Mash roe with onions and rice flour
steps.text: Mash the fish eggs with sliced onions, green chillies, fresh coriander, turmeric, salt, rice flour, and besan.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy pan and fry flat spoonfuls on medium-low heat until crisp and golden brown on both sides.

notes: Rice flour gives Assamese Maasor Konir Bora its signature light crunch.

name: Assamese Til Pitha (Roasted Rice-Flour Crepes Stuffed with Black Sesame & Jaggery)

ingredients.name: Fine Sticky or Gobindobhog Rice Flour

steps.section: Prepare sesame-jaggery filling and moistened flour
steps.text: Dry-roast black sesame seeds in a pan until aromatic, cool slightly, and crush coarsely by hand with a rolling pin, then mix with grated jaggery. Sprinkle warm water sparingly into rice flour and rub between palms until damp like breadcrumbs.

steps.section: Roast crisp on dry tawa and roll
steps.text: Heat a flat iron or non-stick tawa on low flame. Spread 2 tbsp damp rice flour into a thin 5-inch disc, cook 1 minute until set, spoon sesame-jaggery filling down the center, and roll into a crisp cylinder on the tawa.

notes: Dry-tawa roasting with zero oil creates the signature papery crunch of Assamese Bihu Til Pitha.

name: Atta Ladoo

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Atta Veg Momo (Whole Wheat Steamed Vegetable Dumplings)

steps.section: Knead soft wheat dough and prepare veg filling
steps.text: Knead whole wheat flour with a pinch of salt, 1 tsp oil, and warm water into a smooth soft dough; rest 15 minutes. Squeeze excess moisture from grated cabbage and carrot by hand, then mix with onion, spring onion, minced ginger, garlic, remaining oil, soy sauce, black pepper, and salt.

Roll small thin circles, place 1 tbsp filling in the center, and pleat edges tightly to seal. Steam over boiling water in a greased steamer or idli stand for 12–14 minutes until glossy and cooked through.

notes: Wholesome whole-wheat alternative to maida momos; rolling thin keeps them tender.

name: Avocado Chocolate Pudding (Silky Dark Cacao & Ripe Avocado Chilled Vegan Pudding)

ingredients.name: Dutch-processed Cocoa Powder or Raw Cacao
Pure Maple Syrup or Wild Honey

steps.text: Add ripe avocado flesh, cocoa powder, maple syrup, vanilla extract, almond milk, and a pinch of sea salt into a blender. Blend on high for 2-3 minutes until completely glossy, thick, and velvet-smooth.
Spoon the pudding into serving ramekins or glasses and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to set. Garnish with dark chocolate shavings and fresh raspberries before serving.

notes: A luxurious dairy-free and eggless vegan pudding where ripe avocado provides incredible richness without any avocado flavor once paired with dark cocoa.

name: Avocado Toast Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Badam & Pista Laddoo (Chopped Almond, Pistachio & Jaggery Energy Laddoo)

steps.text: Roast finely chopped almonds, pistachios, and sesame seeds in 1 tsp ghee on low heat for 4 minutes until crisp and fragrant; transfer to a plate.

steps.section: Coat in jaggery syrup and shape
steps.text: Melt jaggery with remaining ghee and 1 tbsp water until bubbling. Stir in the toasted nuts and cardamom, cool 2 minutes, and roll with greased palms into bite-sized laddoos.

notes: Crunchy, nut-rich laddoo made entirely with a knife and pan.

name: Badam Halwa

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Badam Milk

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Baigan Pakora / Begun Bora (Spiced Gram-Flour Coated Brinjal / Eggplant Fritters)

steps.section: Season eggplant slices and whisk spiced besan batter
steps.text: Dust brinjal slices lightly with salt and turmeric; whisk besan, rice flour, ajwain, kalo jeere, chilli powder, roasted cumin, salt, baking soda, and 1 tbsp hot oil with water into a smooth coating batter.
Dip each baigan slice in the batter, let excess drip off, and deep-fry in hot mustard oil over medium heat until puffed and golden brown; sprinkle chaat masala before serving.

notes: Delicious with puffed rice (muri), green chutney, or alongside khichuri on rainy days.

name: Baingan Bharta

steps.text: Roast eggplant over a flame or in an oven until the skin chars and the flesh is soft. Cool, peel and mash.
Sauté onion and garlic in oil, add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft.
Mix in mashed eggplant, salt and spices; cook together until well combined.

name: Bajra Khichdi (Rajasthani Winter Pearl Millet & Moong Dal Khichdi)

steps.text: Sprinkle a little water over bajra grains, rest for 15 minutes, then pulse coarsely in a mortar or mixer to loosen the outer husk. Winnow or rinse to remove husks.
Combine cleaned bajra, washed moong dal, 4.5 cups water, turmeric, and salt in a heavy pressure cooker. Cook on low heat for 4-5 whistles until creamy and thoroughly cooked.
Heat generous desi ghee, crackle cumin seeds, hing, ginger, and green chillies, and pour over the steaming bajra khichdi. Serve hot with jaggery and a dollop of white butter.

notes: Traditional Marwari winter superfood prized for its earthy warmth, nutty texture, and high iron content.

name: Baked Rosogolla / Baked Rasgulla (Caramelized Kheer & Khoya Baked Sponge Rasgulla)

steps.section: Arrange squeezed rasgullas in baking dish
steps.text: Gently press about half the sugar syrup out of the sponge rasgullas and arrange them snugly in an earthen or ovenproof dish.
Simmer thickened milk, condensed milk, grated khoya, cardamom powder, and saffron for 5 minutes until creamy, then pour evenly over the rasgullas.

steps.section: Bake until golden-brown and blistered on top
steps.text: Top with pistachios and almonds and bake at 200°C (or broil) for 12–15 minutes until the top develops golden caramelized spots.

notes: Contemporary Kolkata winter favorite served warm straight from the oven.

name: Baked Ziti / Pasta al Forno (Four-Cheese Baked Ziti with Rich Tomato Sauce)

ingredients.name: Marinara or Crushed Plum Tomato Sauce

steps.text: Cook ziti in heavily salted boiling water for 8 minutes until slightly firmer than al dente. Drain and toss with 1 tbsp olive oil.
In a large bowl, fold together cooked ziti, ricotta, 1 cup of mozzarella, half the Parmesan, minced garlic, dried oregano, and 2 cups of marinara sauce.
Transfer into a greased baking dish, top with remaining marinara sauce, mozzarella, and Parmesan. Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 25-30 minutes until bubbling and golden brown on top.

notes: Classic Italian-American comfort baked pasta; letting it rest for 10 minutes after baking allows the layers to set cleanly for slicing.

name: Balekai Bajji / Vazhakkai Bajji (South Indian Crispy Spiced Besan-Rice Batter Fried Raw Banana Fritters)

steps.section: Slice raw bananas in salted water
steps.text: Peel the green skin of raw bananas and slice lengthwise into 1/8-inch thin slices; soak briefly in salted water so they do not darken, then pat dry on a cloth.
Whisk besan, rice flour, ajwain, hing, Kashmiri red chilli, turmeric, cumin powder, baking soda, salt, 1 tsp hot oil, and water into a smooth, ribbon-thick batter.

Coat each raw banana slice evenly in the batter, scrape off excess drip against the bowl rim, and slide into hot oil. Spoon hot oil on top so the bajjis puff up crisp and golden. Serve with coconut chutney.

notes: Classic Marina Beach and Udupi tea-time bajji.

name: Balushahi / Badusha (Flaky Ghee-Shortened Glazed Sweet Doughnuts)

ingredients.name: Ghee or Oil for Slow Deep-frying

steps.section: Bring together flaky ghee-yogurt dough without over-kneading
steps.text: Mix maida, baking soda, salt, ghee, and yogurt, gently pressing and stacking the dough 4–5 times to create flaky layers; shape into balls with a thumb indentation in the center.
Slide the discs into barely warm ghee and fry on low heat for 16–18 minutes, flipping once they float, until crisp and golden.
Immerse warm balushahis in single-thread saffron-cardamom syrup for 4 minutes per side, drain, and garnish with pistachio slivers.

notes: Crisp outside and flaky-juicy inside — a festive favorite across Bengal, Bihar, and North India.

name: Banana Custard Pudding (Layered Vanilla Custard, Sliced Bananas & Marie Biscuit Pudding)

steps.text: Dissolve custard powder in 0.5 cup cold milk. Bring remaining milk and sugar to a gentle boil, slowly whisk in the custard slurry, and cook on low heat for 3-4 minutes until thick and glossy. Let cool completely to room temperature.

In a clear glass dessert dish or glasses, create a bottom layer of crushed Marie biscuits, arrange a layer of sliced ripe bananas, and pour over a generous layer of cooled vanilla custard. Repeat for a second layer.
Top with a dollop of whipped cream and toasted sliced almonds and pistachios. Chill in the refrigerator for 2 hours so the biscuits soften into a cake-like pudding texture.

notes: A timeless comfort dessert beloved at Indian dinner parties; chilling allows the biscuit layers to absorb the vanilla custard and banana aromas.

name: Banana Fritters (Sweet)

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Banana Milkshake

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Banarasi Dum Aloo (Stuffed Potatoes in Rich Tomato-Fennel-Cashew Gravy)

steps.text: Scoop the center of peeled potatoes, fry the shells golden, and stuff with a mixture of crumbled paneer, fried scooped potato bits, cashews, raisins, and spices.
Cook tomato puree, ginger paste, cashew paste, roasted fennel powder, and Kashmiri chilli in ghee until velvety and rich.
Halve the stuffed potatoes, nestle into the hot gravy, and garnish with cream, kasuri methi, and coriander.

notes: Festive Banarasi banquet potato dish.

name: Bandel Cheese Paratha (Smoky Bengali Artisanal Bandel Cheese & Black Pepper Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Crumble the soaked and drained smoked Bandel cheese, mix with a little mashed potato, crushed black pepper, green chillies, coriander, and roasted cumin (no extra salt needed due to the cured cheese).
Stuff the cheese filling inside dough balls, dust with flour, and roll into neat circles.
Pan-roast on medium heat with ghee until crusty, golden, and deeply aromatic. Serve warm with sweet tomato relish or sour cream.

notes: Artisanal Bengali Portuguese-heritage cheese paratha featuring smoky, dry-cured Bandel cheese.

name: Bandhakopi Bhaja

steps.text: Wash and cut the vegetables into even-sized pieces.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Bandhakopi Bharta (Steamed Cabbage Mash)

steps.text: Boil or steam shredded cabbage until soft, then squeeze out excess water thoroughly.
Heat mustard oil, fry dry red chillies and garlic cloves, and toss the cabbage over high heat for 3 minutes until dry.
Grind or mash coarsely and fold in chopped onion, green chilli, fresh coriander, salt, and a drop of raw mustard oil.

notes: Drying the steamed cabbage over high heat gives a smoky flavour.

name: Bandhakopi Chingri Ghonto (Bengali Cabbage with Prawns)

steps.text: Toss prawns with salt and turmeric, fry lightly in mustard oil, and set aside. Fry cubed potatoes until golden.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, cook ginger paste, tomato, and spices, then add shredded cabbage, potatoes, and salt. Cover and cook until soft.
Mix in green peas and fried prawns, cook uncovered until excess moisture dries up, and finish with ghee and garam masala.

notes: A beloved Bengali winter dish combining sweet winter cabbage and peas with savory small prawns.

name: Bandhakopir Bora / Cabbage Pakora (Crispy Shredded Cabbage & Onion Fritters)

steps.section: Massage shredded cabbage with salt and spices
steps.text: Toss shredded cabbage (and sliced onion if using) with salt, turmeric, green chillies, ginger, coriander leaves, and kalo jeere; rest for 5 minutes so the cabbage releases moisture.

steps.section: Bind with besan and rice flour and fry crisp clusters
steps.text: Add besan and rice flour to bind into a stiff, shaggy mixture without extra water; drop rough clusters into hot mustard oil and fry until dark golden and crunchy.

notes: Holding back water when mixing the batter ensures the cabbage strands fry up ultra-crispy.

name: Bandhakopir Porota (Bengali Spiced Shredded Cabbage & Ginger Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil with kalo jeere. Add shredded cabbage, grated ginger, chillies, turmeric, cumin, garam masala, and salt. Sauté on high heat until the cabbage wilts and dries out completely without losing its sweet crunch.
Enclose cooled cabbage puran inside wheat dough portions, seal the seams, and roll out with light pressure.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until speckled with brown blisters. Serve hot with dimer torkari or aloor dum.

notes: A comforting Bengali winter breakfast paratha using tender, sweet winter cabbage.

name: Barbati Fry / Borboti Aloo Bhaja (Crispy Yardlong Beans & Potato Stir-Fry)

steps.section: Temper and fry yardlong beans with potato
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle panch phoron and green chillies, add barbati and potato wedges with turmeric and salt, and stir-fry until tender and blistered.

steps.section: Toss with onions and roasted cumin
steps.text: Add sliced onions, red chilli powder, and roasted cumin powder, frying on medium-high flame for 4 minutes until caramelized.

notes: Delicious with both hot steamed rice and roti/paratha.

name: Barik Nylon Sev (Ultra-Fine Crispy Gram Flour Noodles for Namkeen & Chaat)

steps.section: Emulsify oil and water and knead soft besan dough
steps.text: Whisk 2 tbsp hot oil, 2 tbsp water, salt, hing, and a tiny pinch of soda until milky, then mix with double-sieved besan and turmeric into a soft, smooth dough.
Load the dough into a sev press fitted with the finest pinhole disc and press thin loops into hot oil.
Fry briefly on medium heat until the bubbles subside and the threads are pale yellow and crisp; cool and crush lightly.

notes: Essential delicate crispy sev for bhel puri, phuchka, ghugni chaat, and standalone snacking.

name: Basmati Rice

steps.text: Wash rice until the water runs mostly clear; soak briefly if appropriate.
Heat ghee or oil, add spices and vegetables if using, and stir until fragrant.
Add rice and measured water, cover and cook until tender. Rest briefly before serving.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Batata Vada / Mumbai Aloo Bonda (Garlic-Mustard Tempered Mashed Potato Spheres in Golden Besan Batter)

steps.section: Temper mashed potatoes and shape spheres
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil, crackle mustard seeds, hing, and curry leaves, saute pounded garlic-ginger-green chillies and turmeric for 1 minute, and mix into mashed potatoes with lemon juice, coriander, and salt. Roll into 8 lemon-sized balls.
Whisk besan, rice flour, ajwain, turmeric, salt, a pinch of baking soda, and water into a smooth medium-thick batter.
Coat each potato ball in the besan batter and fry in medium-hot oil until evenly golden and crisp. Serve hot with dry red garlic chutney, fried green chillies, or inside ladi pav as Vada Pav.

notes: Adding 1.5 tbsp rice flour to the besan batter keeps the outer shell crisp long after frying.

name: BBQ Paneer Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Bebinca (Traditional Goan 7-Layered Coconut Milk & Nutmeg Steamed Pudding)

ingredients.name: Pure Desi Ghee (Melted, for Brushing Layers)

steps.text: Whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale and creamy. Add thick coconut milk, nutmeg, and cardamom, then gently fold in sifted maida to create a smooth, velvety batter.

steps.section: Bake layer by layer under broiler
steps.text: Grease an oven-safe tin with 1 tbsp ghee, pour a thin layer (0.5 cup) of batter, and bake under the top oven grill/broiler for 5-6 minutes until firm and golden brown.
Brush the baked layer with ghee, pour the next layer of batter, and bake. Repeat process until all 7 distinct caramelized layers are formed. Cool completely and slice into wedges.

notes: The Queen of Goan desserts: a rich Indo-Portuguese layered coconut cake celebrating coconut milk and nutmeg.

name: Bedmi Puri (Old Delhi Spiced Urad Dal & Semolina Poori)

steps.section: Knead or stuff spiced urad dough
steps.text: Sauté coarsely ground urad dal with hing, ginger-green chilli, crushed fennel, coriander, and spices; either knead directly into the wheat-semolina dough or stuff inside dough balls.
Roll slightly thicker than regular pooris and fry in medium-hot oil until crisp, flaky, and golden brown.

notes: Classic Old Delhi and Mathura street breakfast served with spicy hing-wale aloo sabzi.

name: Beetroot Bharta (Chukandar Mash)

steps.text: Peel beetroot, grate or cube, and steam/boil until tender.
Mash or mix the cooked beetroot with finely chopped onion, green chillies, roasted cumin, lemon juice, coriander, salt, and mustard oil.
Serve warm or at room temperature alongside rice, dal, or roti.

notes: Earthy beetroot pairs well with sharp mustard oil and lemon.

name: Beetroot Paratha (Spiced Grated Beetroot & Ajwain Stuffed Flatbread)

steps.text: Sauté grated beetroot with ginger, green chillies, ajwain, and cumin in 1 tsp oil until tender and dry; fold in mashed potato, amchur, and salt.
Enclose beetroot stuffing inside wheat dough balls and roll gently into circular flatbreads.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee on both sides until crisp and beautifully speckled. Serve with fresh curd.

notes: A stunning ruby-red stuffed paratha packed with iron, natural sweetness, and tangy spices.

name: Beetroot Puri (Vibrant Spiced Beetroot Poori)

steps.text: Combine wheat flour, semolina, spices, salt, 1 tbsp oil, and smooth beetroot puree to knead a firm dough.

steps.section: Roll and puff in hot oil
steps.text: Roll into small rounds and deep-fry in hot oil until puffed and crisp around the edges.

notes: Naturally colorful, nutrient-rich pooris that pair wonderfully with aloo rasedar or raita.

name: Begun Aloo Diye Macher Dimer Jhal (Eggplant, Potato & Fish Egg Mustard Medley)

steps.text: Fry eggplant wedges in mustard oil until golden and set aside. Pan-fry seasoned fish roe and cut into chunks.
Temper oil with nigella seeds, sauté sliced onion, potato wedges, and chopped tomato with turmeric and salt until potatoes are tender.

steps.section: Simmer with mustard, roe and eggplant
steps.text: Add mustard paste mixed with warm water, fried eggplant, and fish roe chunks; simmer for 5 minutes and garnish with coriander.

notes: Silky eggplant and fish roe soaked in a tangy mustard-tomato sauce.

name: Begun Bharta (Roasted Eggplant Mash)

steps.text: Wash the brinjal, make 2–3 slits to check for blemishes, optionally tuck garlic cloves and a green chilli inside, and rub the skin lightly with oil.
Roast directly over an open gas flame, turning frequently until the skin is completely charred and the flesh collapses softly.
Cool slightly, peel off the charred skin, and mash the smoky flesh with raw chopped onion, green chillies, fresh coriander, salt, and pungent mustard oil.

notes: In Bengal this raw-onion mustard-oil mash is called Begun Pora / Begun Bharta and pairs wonderfully with hot roti or winter khichuri.

name: Begun Chingri Jhal (Eggplant & Prawn Mustard Curry)

steps.text: Season eggplant wedges and prawns with salt and turmeric. Fry eggplant until golden and lightly sear prawns; set both aside.
Temper mustard oil with nigella seeds and green chillies, sauté chopped tomato with turmeric, then add mustard paste strained with warm water.
Add fried eggplant and prawns to the bubbling gravy, simmer gently for 5 minutes, and drizzle raw mustard oil before serving.

notes: Silky fried eggplant absorbs the pungent mustard and prawn broth beautifully.

steps.text: Cut the eggplant into 1/2-inch thick round discs, score a light crisscross pattern on both faces, and rub generously with turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, and a pinch of sugar.
Sear the eggplant medallions in smoking mustard oil over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until deep golden-brown outside and melt-in-the-mouth creamy inside.

notes: Essential companion to Bengali khichuri, luchi, or गरम ভাত (steamed rice) and dal.

steps.text: Mix besan, rice flour, turmeric, chilli powder, salt and water to make a coating batter.
Cut eggplant into thin lengthwise slices and lightly salt them.
Dip slices in batter and fry in hot oil until crisp and golden on both sides.

name: Beguni Diye Muri Makha (Crispy Eggplant Fritter & Mustard-Oil Puffed Rice)

steps.text: Whisk besan with turmeric, kalonji, chilli powder, salt, and water into a smooth batter. Dip brinjal slices and fry in hot oil until golden and crisp; drain and break into bite-sized pieces.
Toss puffed rice with 1 tsp raw mustard oil, chopped onion, green chillies, black salt, chanachur, and the crisp beguni pieces.

notes: Traditional Bengali rainy-evening tiffin pairing hot beguni with pungent mustard-oil muri.

name: Bel Sherbet

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.
