name: Bengali Amriti (Crispy Flower-Shaped Urad Dal Sweet in Saffron Syrup)

ingredients.name: Split Skinless Black Gram (Biuli / Urad Dal)

steps.section: Grind and whip airy urad dal batter
steps.text: Grind soaked urad dal with minimal iced water into a thick paste, add rice flour, and whisk vigorously by hand for 8–10 minutes until light and fluffy enough to float on water.
Boil sugar, water, saffron strands, and cardamom to a single-thread consistency syrup.

steps.section: Pipe floral rings into hot ghee and soak
steps.text: Pipe concentric scalloped rings directly into medium-hot ghee, fry until crisp and golden, and dip into warm saffron syrup for 3–4 minutes.

notes: Crisp scalloped urad-dal cousin of jalebi popular across Bengal during Maha Ashtami andBijoya.

name: Bengali Bhoger Khichuri (Thakurbarir Niramish Gobindobhog Rice & Roasted Moong Dal Khichuri)

ingredients.name: Whole Spices (Bay Leaves, Dry Red Chillies, Cinnamon, Cardamom, Cloves, Cumin)

steps.section: Dry-roast sonamung dal and fry vegetables
steps.text: Dry-roast sonamung dal in a heavy pan on low heat until golden and nutty, then rinse. Fry cauliflower florets and potato halves in mustard oil with a pinch of turmeric and set aside.

steps.section: Temper whole spices and ginger masala
steps.text: Heat ghee and mustard oil in a large handi, temper bay leaves, dry chillies, cumin seeds, and whole garam masala. Saute ginger paste, tomatoes, turmeric, and roasted cumin powder until oil separates.

steps.section: Simmer with Gobindobhog rice, cashews, and ghee
steps.text: Add roasted dal, Gobindobhog rice, fried potatoes, and 6 cups boiling water. Simmer covered for 15 minutes, then gently fold in fried cauliflower, green peas, cashews, raisins, sugar, and slit chillies. Finish with a generous spoonful of desi ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Sacred Durga Puja and Saraswati Puja temple offering (Bhog) made strictly without onion or garlic, celebrated for its velvety texture and heavenly aroma of Gobindobhog rice and ghee.

name: Bengali Bhuni Khichuri / Jhura Khichuri (Dry-Roasted Moong Dal & Fragrant Gobindobhog Pilaf-Style Khichuri)

ingredients.name: Whole Garam Masala (Cinnamon, Green Cardamom, Cloves, Bay Leaves)

steps.text: Dry-roast moong dal until fragrant and golden-pink, then wash and drain completely alongside the Gobindobhog rice.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot, temper bay leaves, dry chillies, cumin, and whole garam masala. Add grated ginger, drained rice, and roasted dal, frying for 5-6 minutes until every grain glistens.

Pour exactly 3.5 cups of boiling water (double the volume of rice + dal), add salt, sugar, turmeric, and fried potatoes/nuts. Cover tightly and cook on lowest flame for 14 minutes until grains are fluffy, separate, and tender.

notes: Unlike wet porridge-like khichuri, Bhuni Khichuri is cooked pilaf-style with exact water ratios so every grain of rice and dal remains separate and fluffy.

name: Bengali Biyebari Style Mishti Veg Fried Rice (Bengali Ghee, Cashew, Raisin & Vegetable Fried Rice)

steps.section: Parboil aromatic Basmati rice with whole spices
steps.text: Boil soaked Basmati rice in salted water with bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon until 85% cooked; drain in a colander and spread to dry completely.

steps.section: Fry cashews, raisins, and vegetables in pure ghee
steps.text: Heat pure cow ghee in a heavy kadai, fry cashews and raisins until golden, then stir-fry carrots, French beans, green peas, and capsicum with a pinch of salt for 4 minutes until tender-crisp.

steps.section: Layer and toss rice with sugar, pepper, and nutmeg-mace
steps.text: Gently fold the cooled Basmati rice into the ghee-fried vegetables and nuts along with sugar, crushed white/black pepper, and a pinch of jayitri-jaiphal (mace-nutmeg) powder; cover on low heat (dum) for 4 minutes.

notes: Signature fragrant, lightly sweet Bengali wedding ('biyebari') and festive fried rice served with Kosha Mangsho or Aloor Dom.

name: Bengali Chira Bhaja Mixture (Crispy Fried Poha with Peanuts, Sev & Curry Leaves)

steps.section: Flash-fry chira in a wire strainer
steps.text: Lower a metal mesh strainer holding a handful of chira into hot oil for 8–10 seconds until puffed and white; drain well on paper towels.

steps.section: Fry peanuts, cashews, curry leaves, and chillies
steps.text: In the same strainer, fry peanuts, cashews, slit green chillies, and curry leaves with a pinch of turmeric until crisp.

steps.section: Toss with black salt, cumin, and sev
steps.text: Combine puffed chira, nuts, curry leaves, black salt, roasted cumin powder, and fine sev; store airtight once cool.

notes: Classic Bengali evening snack ('chira-badam bhaja') served alongside hot milk tea or black tea.

name: Bengali Dim Pauruti Chop / Egg Stuffed Bread Pakora (Spiced Boiled Egg & Potato Bread Fritters)

steps.section: Season potato and nestle egg halves
steps.text: Mix mashed potato with chopped onion, green chillies, bhaja masala, and salt. Spread a layer on a bread slice, place a boiled egg half cut-side down, cover with a thin layer of potato and a second bread slice, and cut in half.

steps.section: Coat in spiced besan and fry
steps.text: Whisk besan with turmeric, kalonji, salt, and water into a thick batter. Dip each stuffed bread sandwich and fry in hot oil until deep golden. Sprinkle black salt and serve with kasundi.

notes: Kolkata telebhaja-style fusion of dim-er chop and bread pakora.

name: Bengali Goja / Misti Gaja (Flaky Ghee-Shortened Sweet Pastry Cubes in Sugar Glaze)

steps.section: Rub ghee into maida and laminate dough
steps.text: Rub ghee, baking soda, salt, and kalonji into maida until crumbly, bind with minimal cold water into a stiff dough, fold and roll 3 times to build flaky layers, and cut into 1.5-inch thick squares.

steps.section: Slow-fry on low heat until flaky and golden
steps.text: Drop the squares into barely warm oil and fry on low heat for 15–18 minutes so the interior layers open up and turn crisp through to the center.

steps.section: Toss in 1-thread sugar syrup until frosted
steps.text: Transfer warm fried gojas into thick 1-thread cardamom sugar syrup, toss for 3–4 minutes, and remove to a rack so a crystalline sugar glaze sets on the outside.

notes: Traditional Bengali festive and Bijoya Dashami sweet pastry with a flaky crumb and frosted sugar crust.

name: Bengali Homestyle Aloo Diye Veg Chowmin / Chowmein (Homestyle Noodles with Potato, Beans, Carrot & Peanuts)

steps.text: Boil chowmin until just tender, drain, and coat with 1 tsp oil; fry raw peanuts in 2 tbsp oil until golden and set aside.

steps.section: Crisp the potato matchsticks and veggies
steps.text: In the same pan, fry thin potato matchsticks with a tiny pinch of salt and turmeric until golden-crisp, then add onions, green chillies, carrots, beans, and capsicum and stir-fry for 4 minutes.

steps.section: Toss with noodles, peanuts, and black pepper
steps.text: Add boiled chowmin, fried peanuts, a splash of soy sauce, tomato ketchup, and freshly crushed black pepper; toss over medium-high heat for 3 minutes.

notes: Nostalgic Bengali household tiffin and evening chowmin featuring golden-fried potato juliennes and crunchy peanuts.

name: Bengali Masoor Daler Khichuri (Monsoon Red Lentil, Onion & Mustard Oil Homestyle Khichuri)

steps.section: Temper panch phoron and fry onions
steps.text: Heat mustard oil in a deep pot until smoking. Temper bay leaf, dry red chillies, and panch phoron. Add sliced onions and crushed garlic, frying until golden brown.

steps.section: Saute rice, masoor dal, and potatoes
steps.text: Add washed rice, red masoor dal, potato halves, ginger paste, turmeric, and chilli powder. Stir-fry for 4 minutes on medium flame.

Pour in 4.5 cups of warm water and salt. Cover and simmer on medium-low heat for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the masoor dal melts into a comforting gravy. Drizzle raw mustard oil before serving with dim bhaja (fried eggs).

notes: The quintessential everyday rainy-day Bengali household comfort meal, typically paired with crispy fried omelette or begun bhaja.

name: Bengali Phuluri / Teler Bora (Fluffy Hand-Whipped Besan, Onion, Kalo Jeere & Posto Monsoon Fritters)

ingredients.name: Rice Flour (or Poppy Seeds / Posto for Crunch)

steps.section: Whip besan batter by hand until it floats on water
steps.text: Whisk sifted besan, rice flour, turmeric, red chilli, baking soda, salt, and water vigorously by hand for 5–6 minutes until pale and airy (a tiny drop of batter should float in a bowl of water).

steps.section: Fold in kalo jeere, posto, and chillies
steps.text: Stir in kalo jeere, posto (if using), finely chopped onion, green chillies, and coriander.

steps.section: Fry puffed golden phuluris in mustard oil
steps.text: Drop small round dollops into medium-hot mustard oil; they will immediately puff into light, hollow-centered golden spheres. Serve hot with muri (puffed rice) and kasundi.

notes: The Bengali cousin of Mysore Bonda—whipping besan by hand until a drop floats in water guarantees feather-light phuluris.

name: Besan Arbi Fry (Crispy Carom & Gram Flour Coated Taro Root Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Arbi (Taro Root / Colocasia, Boiled 80%, Peeled & Sliced)

steps.section: Coat parboiled arbi in spiced besan
steps.text: Toss parboiled and cooled arbi rounds with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder, amchur, salt, and roasted besan so each slice is evenly coated.
Heat smoking mustard oil in a heavy pan, crackle ajwain and hing, and roast the coated arbi on medium flame for 10–12 minutes until a golden, crunchy besan crust forms on all sides.
Finish with roasted cumin powder and fresh coriander; serve hot with pooris or parathas.

notes: Carom seeds (ajwain) are the classic digestive pairing for both taro root (arbi) and gram flour (besan).

name: Besan Chilla / Besan ka Puda (Classic Spiced Gram Flour, Onion, Tomato & Coriander Savory Crepes)

steps.section: Whisk smooth besan batter and rest
steps.text: Sift besan into a bowl, add ajwain (crushed between palms), turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, and water gradually while whisking into a smooth, pourable, lump-free batter. Rest for 10 minutes so the gram flour hydrates.
Stir finely chopped onion, tomato, grated ginger, green chillies, and fresh coriander leaves into the rested batter.

steps.section: Spread and roast golden on hot tawa
steps.text: Heat a seasoned cast-iron or non-stick tawa over medium flame, brush lightly with ghee/oil, pour a ladleful of batter, and spread gently in concentric circles. Drizzle a few drops of ghee around the edges and cook 2–3 minutes per side until golden-brown and crisp. Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney.

notes: Resting the batter for 10 minutes before cooking prevents cracking and makes the chilla lacy and pliable.

name: Besan Doodh Barfi / Besan Milk Cake (Caramelized Milk-Soaked Gram Flour & Khoya Fudge)

steps.text: Rub besan with 3 tbsp melted ghee and 4 tbsp warm milk until crumbly like wet sand, cover for 15 minutes, then pass through a coarse sieve or pulse briefly in a mixer to form fine granules.

steps.section: Roast granulated besan and fold in khoya
steps.text: Roast the granulated besan in 1/2 cup ghee on low flame for 15 minutes until deep golden, then stir in crumbled khoya and roast 3 more minutes.

steps.section: Bind with sugar syrup and set
steps.text: Stir in warm 1-string sugar syrup flavored with cardamom and saffron, transfer to a greased tray, top with pistachio and almond slivers, and cut into rich barfi squares.

notes: The traditional halwai 'dhabba' technique of rubbing milk and ghee into raw besan before roasting gives this barfi a rich, grainy milk-cake texture.

name: Besan ka Halwa / Besan Sheera (Rich Slow-Roasted Gram Flour, Ghee, Milk & Saffron Pudding with Almonds)

steps.section: Slow-roast besan and suji in desi ghee
steps.text: Heat ghee in a heavy pan, lightly fry nuts, then roast besan and suji over low flame for 12–15 minutes until deep golden brown and nutty.

steps.section: Stir in warm saffron milk and sugar
steps.text: Carefully pour in warm saffron-infused milk and water in a steady stream while stirring continuously so no lumps form. Add sugar and cardamom powder.

steps.section: Simmer until glossy and ghee separates
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 minutes until the halwa absorbs the liquid, pulls away from the pan in a glossy mass, and releases ghee around the edges. Garnish with roasted nuts and serve piping hot.

notes: Also cherished in winter as a warming, soothing household remedy for colds when served hot.

name: Besan Karele ki Sabzi (Spiced Roasted Gram Flour, Fennel & Raw Mango Stuffed Bitter Gourd)

steps.section: Prep karela and roast besan-onion masala
steps.text: Squeeze salted karelas to remove excess bitter juice. In 1 tbsp mustard oil, saute grated onion, crushed fennel, kalonji, and besan on low flame until golden and aromatic; mix in raw mango/amchur, spices, jaggery, and salt.
Stuff the slit karelas (or toss thick karela rings) with the roasted besan masala and shallow-fry in mustard oil under a lid on low heat for 12–15 minutes until tender and caramelized.
Serve hot with dal-roti; stays fresh for 2–3 days.

notes: Nutty roasted besan and tangy amchur mellow the bitterness of karela while creating a rich, crumbly filling.

name: Besan ki Barfi / Besan Chakki (Rajasthani Ghee-Roasted Gram Flour, Cardamom & Pistachio Fudge Squares)

steps.section: Roast besan and suji in ghee
steps.text: Heat desi ghee in a heavy kadai and slow-roast besan and suji over low heat for 15–18 minutes until fragrant, frothy, and golden-amber.
Boil sugar and 1/2 cup water with saffron strands and cardamom powder for 4–5 minutes until it reaches a single-thread (ek-taar) consistency.

steps.section: Combine, set, and slice into diamonds
steps.text: Pour the warm sugar syrup into the roasted besan off the heat, stir vigorously until it thickens and leaves the sides of the pan, spread into a greased tray, scatter sliced pistachios and almonds, and cut into neat barfi squares while warm.

notes: A festive North Indian and Rajasthani winter sweet with a melt-in-the-mouth fudge texture.

name: Besan Ladoo / Danedar Besan ke Laddu (Slow-Roasted Coarse Gram Flour, Ghee, Cardamom & Cashew Ladoo)

ingredients.name: Coarse Besan (Laddoo Besan, or Regular Besan + 2 Tbsp Fine Suji)

steps.section: Slow-roast besan in desi ghee on low flame
steps.text: Melt ghee in a heavy-bottomed kadai, add coarse besan (and suji if using fine besan), and roast patiently over the lowest flame for 18–22 minutes, stirring constantly until it loosens, turns deep golden-hazel, and fills the kitchen with a nutty aroma.

steps.section: Splash water for signature danedar grain
steps.text: Sprinkle 1 tbsp water over the hot roasted besan so it foams up and creates fine granules (danedar texture); stir 2 more minutes until moisture evaporates, fold in chopped nuts and toasted melon seeds, and transfer to a wide plate to cool until lukewarm.

steps.section: Mix boora and roll into glossy ladoos
steps.text: Once lukewarm (never hot, or the sugar will melt), mix in boora/powdered sugar, cardamom, and nutmeg powder, and roll firmly between palms into smooth, glossy spheres garnished with pistachio slivers.

notes: Waiting until the roasted besan cools to lukewarm before adding boora/sugar ensures firm, round ladoos that never turn runny.

name: Besan Omelette / Vegetarian Tomato-Besan Omelette (Fluffy Whisked Gram Flour, Tomato & Herb Savory Omelette)

steps.text: Whisk besan vigorously with water, turmeric, red chilli powder, hing, ginger-garlic paste, and salt for 2 minutes to incorporate air. Fold in juicy chopped tomatoes, onion, green chillies, coriander, and a pinch of fruit salt/soda right before cooking.
Melt butter in a small skillet, pour a thick ladle of frothy batter, cover for 2 minutes on medium-low flame until puffy, then flip and sear until golden brown.

steps.section: Serve with toasted pav or bread
steps.text: Serve hot with buttered pav, bread toast, and green chutney.

notes: Famous across Mumbai and Pune Irani cafes and street stalls as 'Tomato Omelette'—completely eggless yet remarkably fluffy.

name: Besan Papdi Gathiya (Crisp Flat Gram Flour Ribbon Crackers)

steps.text: Emulsify oil, water, salt, hing, and baking soda, then knead with besan and crushed ajwain into a soft, pliable dough.

steps.section: Press flat ribbons into medium-hot oil
steps.text: Use the flat slotted ribbon plate in a farsan press to extrude thin strips directly into medium-hot oil.

steps.section: Fry until crisp and light yellow
steps.text: Fry for 1–2 minutes turning once so the ribbons stay pale yellow and crunchy; cool and break into pieces.

notes: Light, flaky gram-flour ribbon namkeen enjoyed with tea or fried green chillies.

name: Besan Paratha (Spiced Roasted Gram Flour, Ajwain & Kasuri Methi Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Combine dry-roasted besan with minced onion, ginger, chillies, crushed kasuri methi, ajwain, amchur, chilli powder, salt, and 1 tbsp mustard oil with a few drops of water into a crumbly mixture.
Pack the seasoned besan mixture into dough balls, seal edges, and roll out into round flatbreads.
Roast on medium flame with ghee until crisp and fragrant on both sides. Serve with mango pickle and yogurt.

notes: A protein-rich, travel-friendly North Indian paratha that stays soft for hours.

name: Besan Shimla Mirch / Besan Wali Capsicum (Dry Roasted Gram Flour, Amchur & Fennel Tossed Bell Peppers)

ingredients.name: Green Bell Peppers (Capsicum, Cubed into 1-inch Pieces)

steps.text: Dry-roast 4 tbsp besan in a pan over low heat for 3–4 minutes until nutty and lightly golden; transfer to a bowl.
Heat mustard oil, crackle cumin, mustard, fennel seeds, and hing, then toss in cubed capsicum, ginger, turmeric, and salt. Stir-fry for 4–5 minutes so the peppers stay vibrant and slightly crisp.

steps.section: Coat with roasted besan and amchur
steps.text: Add coriander powder, Kashmiri chilli, amchur, garam masala, and the roasted besan. Toss on low heat for 3–4 minutes with a tiny splash of water so the spiced besan hugs every capsicum piece.

notes: Quick no-onion, no-garlic Rajasthani tiffin sabzi where sweet crunch of capsicum meets nutty roasted gram flour.

name: Besan Toast / Savory Besan French Toast (Crispy Spiced Gram Flour, Onion & Green Chilli Coated Bread Toast)

steps.text: Mix besan, rice flour, ajwain, turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, and water into a coating-consistency batter. Fold in finely chopped onion, tomato, capsicum, green chillies, and coriander.

steps.section: Dip bread and pan-toast in butter
steps.text: Dip each bread slice into the spiced besan batter, spooning extra chopped vegetables onto the top surface. Place on a hot buttered tawa and toast on medium flame for 2–3 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Dust with chaat masala, cut diagonally into triangles, and serve hot with tomato ketchup or mint chutney.

notes: Quick 15-minute vegetarian street-style savory French toast loved for breakfast or tiffin boxes.

name: Bhaja Puli Pithe (Crispy Golden Fried Coconut-Jaggery Stuffed Rice Dumplings)

steps.section: Cook coconut-gur pur and knead rice dough
steps.text: Cook grated coconut with nolen gur in a kadhai on low heat for 8 minutes until sticky and glossy; add cardamom powder and cool. Boil 1.5 cups water with a pinch of salt, stir in rice flour, cover 5 minutes, and knead while warm into a smooth dough.
Flatten small dough balls into discs, fill with coconut pur, fold into half-moons, crimp edges firmly, and fry in medium-hot oil until golden and crisp.

notes: Crimp the edges tightly so the molten jaggery-coconut filling stays sealed inside.

name: Bhakarwadi (Crispy Spiral Namkeen Rolls Stuffed with Coconut, Sesame & Poppy Masala)

steps.section: Roast and grind sweet-spicy coconut-sesame stuffing
steps.text: Dry-roast sesame seeds, poppy seeds, grated dry coconut, coriander, cumin, and fennel; pulse coarsely with red chilli powder, garam masala, sugar, and salt.

steps.section: Roll dough, brush tamarind chutney, and roll tight spirals
steps.text: Knead a stiff maida-besan dough with hot oil; roll into rectangles, brush lightly with tamarind chutney, press the coconut-sesame masala on top, roll tightly into logs, and slice into 0.5-inch spirals.

steps.section: Deep-fry on low-medium flame until crunchy
steps.text: Deep-fry the spiral slices over low-medium heat for 10–12 minutes until dark golden and crisp all the way to the center.

notes: Classic Pune/Gujarati sweet, tangy, and spicy spiral namkeen with a shelf life of several weeks.

name: Bhandare Wale Aloo Ki Sabzi (Temple-Style No-Onion No-Garlic Tomato Potato Curry)

steps.section: Roast coarsely crushed whole spices in ghee
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle cumin, fennel, crushed coriander seeds, cloves, peppercorns, bay leaf, dry red chilli, and a generous pinch of hing, then sauté grated ginger and green chillies.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli powder, and black salt; cook until oil separates.
Add hand-crushed boiled potatoes and hot water; simmer for 10 minutes until thick and aromatic, finishing with amchur, crushed kasuri methi, and coriander.

notes: Iconic North Indian temple-feast (bhandara) sabzi served with crispy bedmi puri or plain poori.

name: Bhanga Aloor Torkari (Bengali Hand-Crushed Potato Curry for Kochuri & Luchi)

steps.text: Boil potatoes until tender, peel (or leave skin partially on), and break them roughly by hand (bhanga) instead of cutting with a knife so craggy edges release starch.

steps.section: Temper with panch phoron and hing
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle bay leaf, dry red chillies, panch phoron, and hing, then sauté grated ginger, green chillies, chopped tomato, turmeric, and cumin powder.

steps.section: Simmer and finish with bhaja masala
steps.text: Toss in the hand-broken potatoes, pour in warm water, salt, and a pinch of sugar, and simmer for 8 minutes until thick and glossy. Finish with roasted bhaja masala and fresh coriander.

notes: Hand-crushing (bhanga) the boiled potatoes gives this sweet-shop style curry its signature velvety, starchy gravy.

name: Bhapa Chingri (Steamed Mustard & Coconut Prawns)

steps.text: Grind soaked mustard seeds, poppy seeds, grated coconut, 2 green chillies, and a pinch of salt with a splash of water into a smooth paste.
In a steel tiffin box with a tight lid, toss cleaned prawns with the ground paste, whisked yogurt, turmeric, salt, sugar, and 1.5 tbsp raw mustard oil. Top with slit green chillies.
Close the lid tightly and steam in a covered pan with water reaching halfway up the box for 15-18 minutes. Rest 5 minutes before opening.

notes: Traditional Bengali steamed delicacy; grind mustard with a pinch of salt and green chilli to prevent bitterness.

name: Bhapa Pitha / Vapa Pitha (Bengali Steamed Rice-Cake Stuffed with Coconut & Nolen Gur)

steps.text: Sprinkle lukewarm salted water gradually into rice flour and rub by hand until damp enough to hold shape when pressed in your fist, yet crumbly. Pass through a coarse strainer.

steps.section: Layer in small bowl and steam
steps.text: In a small bowl, layer damp rice flour, grated patali gur, and grated coconut, then cover with another layer of rice flour without pressing too hard. Wrap the bowl in a damp muslin cloth, invert over a steaming kettle/pot rim, remove the bowl gently, and steam covered for 4–5 minutes per pitha.

notes: Winter Bengali street and home classic; serve warm with extra melted nolen gur.

name: Bharwa Besan Mirch / Rajasthani Besan Stuffed Moti Hari Mirch (Tangy Spiced Roasted Besan Stuffed Mild Green Peppers)

ingredients.name: Large Mild Green Chillies (Bhavnagari / Achari Mirch)

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil, temper cumin, ajwain, and hing, and roast besan on low flame for 5 minutes until nutty and golden. Cool and mix with coarse fennel, coriander powder, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli, amchur, black salt, regular salt, and lemon juice with a few drops of oil.
Wash and dry the large mild chillies, make a lengthwise slit (removing seeds if desired), and pack generously with the spiced roasted besan masala.

Heat remaining 2 tbsp mustard oil in a wide pan, arrange the stuffed chillies, cover and cook on medium-low flame for 6–8 minutes, turning gently until the skins are lightly blistered and tender. Sprinkle any leftover besan masala on top.

notes: Elevates any Indian thali, dal-chawal, or khichdi meal with its tangy, nutty, and mildly spiced flavor.

name: Bhatmas Sadeko (Nepali Spiced Crunchy Roasted Soybean Salad)

steps.text: Dry-roast soybeans in a heavy skillet on medium-low heat for 4-5 minutes until crisp, nutty, and lightly blistered (or use store-bought roasted bhatmas).
In a bowl, combine roasted soybeans with chopped onion, tomato, ginger, green chillies, and fresh coriander.

steps.section: Dress with mustard oil and lime
steps.text: Drizzle with pungent raw mustard oil, lime juice, roasted cumin, timur, and salt; toss vigorously and serve immediately while crunch is at its peak.

notes: Quintessential Newari and Nepali khaja snack packed with plant-based protein and addictive crunch.

name: Bhatura (Fluffy Punjabi Leavened Fried Bread)

steps.text: Soak sooji in yogurt for 10 minutes, then mix with maida, baking powder, baking soda, sugar, salt, and 1 tbsp oil. Knead with warm water into a soft, smooth dough and rest covered for 1 hour.
Grease the rolling surface with oil (avoid dry flour) and roll each ball into an oval or large circle.
Slide into hot oil, press gently with a slotted spoon so it balloons immediately, flip once until golden, and serve with chole.

notes: Soaking semolina in yogurt gives bhaturas a crisp exterior that stays puffed.

name: Bhavnagari Gathiya (Soft-Crunch Carom & Asafoetida Gram Flour Namkeen Sticks)

steps.section: Whip oil-soda emulsion and knead stretchy besan dough
steps.text: Whisk 3.5 tbsp oil, 1/3 cup water, salt, and baking soda until white and frothy; mix in besan, ajwain, black pepper, and hing, kneading for 6–8 minutes until light and pale.

steps.section: Extrude thick gathiya logs into medium oil
steps.text: Fit a gathiya/murukku press with the thick round-hole disc and press spirals into medium-hot oil.

steps.section: Fry until crisp outside and airy inside
steps.text: Fry on medium-low heat until pale golden and crisp without browning; drain and break into sticks.

notes: Classic melt-in-the-mouth tea-time gathiya seasoned with carom seeds and black pepper.

name: Bhel Muri Makha (Sukha Bhel-Style Crunchy Puffed Rice Tiffin)

steps.text: Mix chopped onion, deseeded tomato, diced potato, coriander, chaat masala, cumin powder, black salt, and tamarind-jaggery syrup in a bowl.
Add puffed rice, roasted peanuts, and nylon sev; toss briskly with lemon juice and serve immediately.

notes: Deseeding the tomato keeps the puffed rice crisp for longer.

Cook potato, tomato and spices, add water, then return fish and simmer gently until cooked through.

name: Bhindi Bharta (Okra / Dherosh Mash)

steps.text: Wash tender okra pods, trim only the tips after steaming, and steam over boiling water (or char on a dry tawa) for 7–8 minutes until tender.
Fry dry red chillies in mustard oil until crisp, then crush with salt and chopped onion.
Trim stems from the cooked okra and mash gently with the onion-chilli mixture, mustard oil, and optional lemon juice.

notes: Steaming whole okra before trimming the caps prevents excessive mucilage (stickiness).

name: Bhindi Chingri (Okra & Prawn Stir-Fry Curry)

steps.text: Pan-fry okra pieces in oil with a pinch of turmeric until non-sticky and lightly browned. Lightly fry seasoned prawns and set aside.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and green chillies, fry sliced onion until soft, and stir in spices with a splash of water.
Add fried okra and prawns, toss gently with a little water, and cook covered for 4-5 minutes until tender.

notes: A quick weekday homestyle side dish combining tender okra with savory prawns.

name: Bhuttar Bora / Crispy Sweet Corn Fritters (Spiced Corn Kernel Pakora)

steps.section: Coarsely pulse corn kernels and mix with spices
steps.text: Pulse three-quarters of the sweet corn in a mixer for 2 seconds into a coarse mash, combine with the remaining whole kernels, onion, ginger, green chillies, coriander, fennel, cumin, besan, and rice flour.
Drop spoonfuls or flattened patties into medium-hot oil and fry until crisp and golden brown on the outside while sweet and juicy inside.

notes: Pulsing most of the corn prevents the kernels from popping in hot oil while locking in natural sweetness.

name: Bihari Besan ki Sabzi / Besan Katli Curry (Mustard-Garlic Gravy with Pan-Seared Gram Flour Cakes)

ingredients.name: Amchur (Dry Mango Powder) or Tangy Mustard Paste

steps.section: Prepare and shallow-fry besan katli / cheela rolls
steps.text: Whisk besan with water, turmeric, red chilli, garlic paste, and salt; either cook into a thick pitor slab and cut into diamond katlis, or spread as thick cheelas on a tawa, fold into flat logs, and slice into 2-inch pieces. Shallow-fry in mustard oil until golden.

Heat smoking mustard oil, temper methi dana and panch phoron, then fry the ground yellow mustard-garlic paste with turmeric, coriander, and chilli powder until oil separates. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until pulpy.

steps.section: Simmer besan katlis in mustard gravy
steps.text: Pour 2 cups hot water, bring the gravy to a rolling boil for 5 minutes, gently drop in the fried besan katlis, simmer 3 minutes, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Authentic Bihari and Eastern UP homestyle specialty—often called 'vegetarian fish curry' because the mustard-garlic gravy mirrors classic machhli jhol.

name: Bikaneri Bhujia (Crispy Moth Dal & Besan Spiced Fine Noodle Namkeen)

steps.section: Knead spiced moth-dal and besan dough
steps.text: Sieve moth flour and besan with ground clove, black pepper, hing, chilli powder, and salt; add 2 tbsp hot oil and warm water to knead a soft, sticky dough.

steps.section: Extrude through fine bhujia plate into hot oil
steps.text: Fill a fine-mesh sev press with the dough and press circular rounds directly into medium-hot oil.

steps.section: Fry briefly and crush into short bhujia strands
steps.text: Fry for 1–2 minutes per side until crisp and pale golden, drain, and gently break into short strands tossed with black salt and amchur.

notes: Authentic Rajasthani moth-bean bhujia with signature warming clove and black-pepper notes.

name: Bisi Bele Bath (Karnataka Spiced Toor Dal, Tamarind & Vegetable Rice Khichdi)

ingredients.name: Mixed Vegetables (Carrots, Beans, Peas, Drumstick, Shallots)

steps.section: Cook rice, toor dal, and vegetables
steps.text: Pressure-cook washed rice and toor dal with 4 cups water and turmeric until soft. In a separate pan, boil drumsticks, carrots, beans, and shallots in 1.5 cups water until tender.

steps.section: Simmer with tamarind and spice blend
steps.text: Add tamarind extract, jaggery, salt, and Bisi Bele Bath masala mixed with a little water to the cooked vegetables. Simmer for 5 minutes, then fold in the cooked rice-dal mixture.

steps.section: Temper with cashews and curry leaves in ghee
steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp desi ghee, fry cashews until golden, and crackle mustard seeds, hing, dry red chillies, and curry leaves. Pour over the hot Bisi Bele Bath and serve with crispy Kara Boondi.

notes: Literally meaning 'hot lentil rice' in Kannada, balancing roasted spice warmth, tangy tamarind, and sweet jaggery.

name: Black Tea

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Blue Lagoon Mocktail

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Bodi ko Achar / Bodi Sadeko (Nepali Spiced Black-Eyed Pea Salad)

steps.text: Combine boiled black-eyed peas in a bowl with sliced onion, sesame powder, ginger, green chillies, cilantro, salt, and lemon juice.
Heat mustard oil in a small ladle, fry fenugreek seeds until dark brown, stir in turmeric and chilli powder, and pour sizzling over the peas.
Toss well so the nutty sesame paste and pungent oil coat the peas. Let rest 5 minutes for flavors to deepen.

notes: Traditional festive salad served during Dashain and Tihar feasts alongside beaten rice and sel roti.

name: Boiled Egg

steps.text: Place eggs in a saucepan, cover with water and bring to a boil.
Simmer 9–12 minutes for firm yolks, cool in cold water, then peel.

notes: For softer yolks, reduce simmering time; refrigerate promptly if not serving immediately.

Sauté onion and tomato with spices until soft and fragrant.
Add eggs and a little water for curry, or scramble gently for bhurji; cook through.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Bokphuler Bora /Agati Flower Fritters (Crispy Hummingbird Tree Blossom Fritters)

ingredients.name: Fresh White or Red Bokphul (Sesbania Grandiflora / Agati Flowers)

steps.text: Gently open each bokphul, snap off the long curved inner stamen/pistil (which tastes bitter), wash lightly, and drain well.

steps.section: Dip in airy rice-besan batter and fry
steps.text: Dip each blossom in a smooth batter of besan, rice flour, posto, kalo jeere, turmeric, chilli powder, and salt, then fry in medium-hot mustard oil until crisp and golden.

notes: An iconic Bengali autumn-winter telebhaja served with afternoon muri or hot dal-rice.

name: Bokul Phuler Khichuri / Keema Khichuri (Mughlai-Bengali Spiced Mutton Mince & Basmati Khichuri)

steps.text: Heat oil and ghee, temper whole spices, and fry chopped onions until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste, mutton keema, yogurt, and ground spices, cooking for 15 minutes until the keema is tender and oil separates.
Add roasted moong dal, masoor dal, and washed rice into the spiced keema pot. Stir-fry for 3 minutes, then add 4 cups hot water and salt.

steps.section: Dum cook with birista and ghee
steps.text: Cover and cook on low heat for 15-18 minutes until grains and keema meld into a rich, savory feast. Garnish with crispy fried onions (birista) and ghee.

notes: Royal zamindari monsoon delicacy where spiced minced mutton is cooked directly inside the fragrant rice and lentil pot.

Add chicken and a little water; cover and cook until fully cooked and tender.
