name: Chilli Chicken Roll (Kolkata Tangra-Style Indo-Chinese Chilli Chicken Kathi Roll)

steps.text: Crisp-fry cornflour-coated chicken strips, then toss on high heat with garlic, ginger, green chillies, onion petals, capsicum, soy sauce, chilli sauce, and ketchup until coated in a glossy dry glaze.
Place the hot dry chilli chicken onto egg-fried laccha parathas, top with spring onions and raw onion rings, and roll up.

notes: A beloved Kolkata street fusion combining Tangra-style dry Chilli Chicken with a flaky Kathi Roll.

name: Chilli Garlic Bread Pakora (Tangra-Style Spicy Garlic & Capsicum Stuffed Bread Fritters)

steps.text: Saute minced garlic, ginger, capsicum, and spring onion in 1 tsp oil for 2 minutes; mix with mashed potato, chilli sauce, soy sauce, pepper, and salt.
Sandwich the filling between bread slices, cut diagonally, dip in a crisp besan-cornflour batter, and fry until golden.

notes: Crisp Indo-Chinese twist on classic bread pakora.

name: Chilli Garlic Butter Noodles / Spaghetti (Fiery Indo-Western Garlic Butter Pasta)

ingredients.name: Red Chilli Flakes or Crushed Sichuan Chilli

steps.text: Cook spaghetti in boiling salted water until al dente. Reserve 0.33 cup pasta water and drain.
Melt butter with 1 tbsp oil in a wok on low heat. Add finely chopped garlic and saute for 2 minutes until light golden and aromatic, then add chilli flakes and soy sauces.
Add drained spaghetti and reserved pasta water to the sizzling garlic butter. Toss vigorously on high heat for 1 minute until glazed, finish with spring onion greens and sesame seeds.

notes: Bold, addictive late-night fusion pasta balancing nutty caramelized garlic, rich butter, and fiery red chilli heat.

name: Chilli Garlic Egg Chowmin / Burnt Garlic Egg Chowmein

steps.section: Crisp golden burnt garlic and scramble eggs
steps.text: Fry 2 tbsp minced garlic in oil until golden-crisp and reserve half; scramble the beaten eggs in the garlic oil into soft ribbons and set aside.

steps.section: Stir-fry dry red chillies and vegetables
steps.text: Sauté remaining fresh garlic and broken dry red chillies on high flame, then toss in carrots, beans, cabbage, and capsicum for 3 minutes.

steps.section: Toss noodles, egg, and crispy burnt garlic
steps.text: Add boiled chowmin, scrambled eggs, soy sauce, red chilli sauce, vinegar, and black pepper; toss on high flame and top with crispy burnt garlic and spring onions.

notes: Smoky egg chowmin infused with roasted garlic oil and topped with crunchy golden garlic bits.

name: Chilli Garlic Pan-Tossed Momo (Tangra-Style Spicy Indo-Chinese Chilli Momos)

steps.text: Shallow-fry or pan-sear pre-steamed momos in 1 tbsp oil until edges turn golden and crisp; set aside.

steps.section: Toss in glossy Tangra chilli glaze
steps.text: In a hot wok with 1 tbsp oil, flash-saute minced garlic, ginger, onion petals, and capsicum for 2 minutes. Stir in chilli sauce, ketchup, soy sauce, vinegar, salt, pepper, and cornflour slurry; toss momos on high heat until coated and garnish with spring onion.

notes: Works equally well with veg, paneer, or chicken momos.

name: Chilli Garlic Veg Chowmin / Burnt Garlic Noodles (Crispy Golden Garlic & Dry Red Chilli Noodles)

steps.text: Heat 2.5 tbsp oil in a wok, fry half the minced garlic on medium-low heat until golden and crisp, and scoop out 1 tbsp of crispy garlic for garnish.

steps.section: Flash-fry dry red chillies and vegetables
steps.text: Increase to high flame, add remaining fresh garlic and broken dry red chillies, and stir-fry carrots, beans, cabbage, and capsicum for 3 minutes.

steps.section: Toss noodles and crown with crispy burnt garlic
steps.text: Add boiled noodles, soy sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar, and black pepper; toss on high heat and finish with spring onion greens and the reserved crispy burnt garlic.

notes: Fragrant Indo-Chinese chowmin infused with garlic oil and topped with crunchy golden burnt garlic.

name: Chilli Gobi Roll (Tangra-Style Crispy Indo-Chinese Cauliflower Roll)

steps.text: Blanch cauliflower florets in salted boiling water for 2 minutes, drain well, and toss with cornflour, maida, salt, and pepper using a splash of water to coat. Shallow- or deep-fry in hot oil until crisp and golden.

steps.section: Toss in Tangra chilli sauce and roll
steps.text: In a hot wok or kadhai with 1 tbsp oil, flash-saute minced garlic, ginger, sliced onion, and capsicum for 2 minutes. Add soy sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar, and fried gobi; toss on high heat until glossy, then wrap inside warm tawa parathas.

notes: Toss the crispy gobi with sauces just before rolling to preserve crunch.

name: Chilli Paneer Dry (Kolkata Tangra-Style Crispy Batter-Fried Paneer with Green Chillies & Bell Peppers)

steps.section: Batter-fry spiced paneer cubes until crisp
steps.text: Toss paneer cubes with cornflour, maida, black pepper, 1 tsp soy sauce, ginger-garlic paste, salt, and a splash of water; fry in hot oil until crisp and golden.

steps.section: Wok-toss on high flame with garlic, chillies and sauces
steps.text: In a smoking wok, stir-fry chopped garlic, ginger, and slit green chillies for 30 seconds, toss in onion petals and bell peppers for 1 minute, add soy sauce, chilli sauce, ketchup, vinegar, and 2 tbsp cornflour slurry, then toss in crispy paneer and spring onions.

notes: Kolkata Tangra-style Chilli Paneer relies on generous chopped garlic and slit green chillies for its signature punch.

name: Chilli Paneer Gravy (Indo-Chinese Fried Paneer Cubes in Spicy Soy-Garlic-Chilli Sauce)

steps.text: Coat paneer cubes in a seasoned batter of cornflour, maida, pepper, and salt, and fry in hot oil until golden and crisp.

steps.section: Simmer glossy soy-chilli-garlic gravy and fold in paneer
steps.text: Stir-fry garlic, ginger, green chillies, onion petals, and capsicum on high flame, add sauces and 1.25 cups water/stock, thicken with cornflour slurry until glossy, and fold in the fried paneer and spring onion greens.

notes: The quintessential Kolkata companion to Veg Chowmin or Egg/Veg Fried Rice.

name: Chilli Paneer Roll (Kolkata Street-Style Indo-Chinese Chilli Paneer Kathi Roll)

steps.text: Toss golden-fried paneer cubes in a hot wok with minced garlic, ginger, chillies, capsicum, onions, soy sauce, chilli sauce, and ketchup.
Spoon the glossy chilli paneer along crisp tawa-fried laccha parathas, garnish with spring onions, cucumber, and chaat masala, and wrap tightly.

notes: Spicy, tangy Indo-Chinese Chilli Paneer wrapped in a flaky Kolkata paratha.

name: Chilli Paneer Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Chilli Prawns (Indo-Chinese Dry / Semi-Gravy)

steps.text: Toss prawns with cornflour, flour, black pepper, salt, and a splash of soy sauce. Crisp-fry in hot oil for 2-3 minutes and drain.
In a hot wok with 1 tbsp oil, stir-fry chopped garlic, ginger, and green chillies for 30 seconds, then toss in cubed onions and capsicum for 1 minute.
Add soy sauce, chilli sauce, ketchup, vinegar, and a splash of cornflour slurry. Toss in the crispy prawns and spring onion greens on high flame.

notes: Kolkata Tangra-style Indo-Chinese favorite; add 1/2 cup stock and extra cornflour slurry if you prefer a gravy version.

name: Chingri / Prawn Steamed Momo (Juicy Hand-Minced Prawn, Ginger & Spring Onion Dumplings)

ingredients.name: Shelled Deveined Prawns (Finely Chopped By Knife)

steps.text: Finely chop cleaned prawns with a sharp knife until coarse-minced, then toss with spring onion, coriander, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, lemon juice, black pepper, 1 tsp oil, and salt.
Fill thin maida wrappers with 1 tbsp prawn mixture, pleat cleanly, and steam for 10–11 minutes (do not over-steam so prawns stay juicy and tender).

notes: Hand-chopping prawns gives bouncy dim-sum-style texture without a food processor.

name: Chingri Aloo Dum (Bengali Spiced Potato & Prawn Dum)

steps.text: Prick parboiled potatoes and fry in mustard oil with turmeric and salt until golden. Lightly sear prawns for 1-2 minutes and set aside.
Temper oil with bay leaf and whole garam masala, brown the chopped onion, and cook ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, and spice powders until oil separates.
Add fried potatoes and warm water, cover and cook on low heat for 6 minutes, then fold in prawns, simmer 4 minutes, and finish with ghee and roasted bhaja masala.

notes: Rich Bengali aloor dum elevated with juicy prawns; pairs wonderfully with luchi or parotta.

name: Chingri Bharta (Bengali Smoky Mashed Prawn with Mustard Oil)

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil, fry dry red chillies until crisp and set aside. Pan-roast garlic cloves and turmeric-salted prawns until cooked and lightly charred.
Coarsely mash or pulse the cooked prawns, roasted garlic, and crushed dry red chillies on a shil-nora (grinding stone) or food processor.
Fold in finely chopped raw onion, green chillies, fresh coriander, salt, and 1 tbsp pungent raw mustard oil.

notes: A fiery, intensely flavorful Bengali & Bangladeshi mash served with steaming hot plain rice.

name: Chingri Diye Borboti Aloo (Yardlong Beans, Potato & Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Season prawns with salt and turmeric, fry briefly in mustard oil, and set aside.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and sliced onion, add potato strips and yardlong beans, and sauté with turmeric, cumin, and coriander powder.
Add fried prawns, slit green chillies, and a splash of warm water; cover and cook until tender.

notes: Homestyle Bengali weekday vegetable-and-prawn curry.

name: Chingri Diye Chichinda (Snake Gourd with Small Prawns)

steps.text: Lightly fry turmeric-salted prawns in mustard oil and set aside.
Temper oil with nigella seeds, green chillies, and sliced onion; add sliced snake gourd, turmeric, and salt, and cook covered until soft.
Stir in fried prawns, grated coconut, and a pinch of sugar; cook uncovered until excess moisture evaporates.

notes: Light, wholesome monsoon side dish for steamed rice.

name: Chingri Diye Dhundul (Sponge Gourd with Prawns)

ingredients.name: Mustard Seeds or Poppy Seed Paste

steps.text: Season prawns with salt and turmeric, sear lightly in mustard oil, and remove.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, add sliced sponge gourd, turmeric, and salt, and cook in its own natural juices.
Stir in mustard or poppy seed paste and fried prawns; simmer for 5 minutes until creamy.

notes: Soft, naturally sweet sponge gourd pairs delicately with small river prawns.

name: Chingri Diye Kakrol Aloo (Spiny Gourd, Potato & Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Lightly sear seasoned prawns and remove. Fry spiny gourd and potato wedges in mustard oil until lightly browned.
Temper oil with nigella seeds, sauté onion-ginger paste, cumin powder, and turmeric with a splash of water.
Add fried vegetables, warm water, and salt; cook until tender, then stir in prawns and mustard paste for 4 minutes.

notes: Seasonal monsoon gourd curry popular across West Bengal.

name: Chingri Diye Kanchkola Aloo Jhol (Raw Banana, Potato & Prawn Light Curry)

steps.section: Soak raw banana and sear prawns
steps.text: Soak cut raw banana in turmeric water to prevent darkening, then drain. Lightly fry prawns and potato wedges in mustard oil.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste, cumin powder, and turmeric, then add raw banana, potatoes, and warm water.
Once vegetables are tender, add seared prawns and slit green chillies, and simmer for 4-5 minutes.

notes: Wholesome, stomach-friendly Bengali light lunch jhol.

name: Chingri Diye Korola Aloo Chorchori (Bitter Gourd, Potato & Prawn Medley)

steps.text: Fry bitter gourd slices in mustard oil until crisp-golden to reduce bitterness; lightly sear prawns and set aside.
Temper oil with panch phoron, sauté sliced onion and potato wedges with turmeric and salt until nearly tender.
Add fried bitter gourd, prawns, mustard paste, and a splash of water; cover and cook on low heat for 5 minutes.

notes: Traditional first-course Bengali bitter dish (shukto/teto) for lunch.

name: Chingri Diye Mulo Ghonto (White Radish with Small Prawns)

steps.text: Lightly squeeze or parboil grated radish with a pinch of salt and drain excess water. Sear seasoned prawns in mustard oil.
Temper oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and nigella seeds, fry finely cubed potatoes, then add radish, ginger paste, turmeric, and cumin powder.
Add fried prawns, slit green chillies, a pinch of sugar, and chopped coriander; cook until dry and fragrant.

notes: Classic Bengali winter radish preparation enriched with small prawns.

name: Chingri Diye Note Shak Chorchori (Amaranth Greens with Prawns)

steps.text: Toss small prawns with salt and turmeric, sear in mustard oil, and set aside.
Temper oil with panch phoron and dry red chilli, fry potato and brinjal cubes, then add chopped amaranth stems and leaves with salt and turmeric.
Stir in fried prawns, mustard paste, slit green chillies, and a pinch of sugar; cook until moisture evaporates.

notes: Summer leafy green chorchori loved across Bengal.

name: Chingri Diye Olkopi Dalna (Kohlrabi, Potato & Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Parboil cubed kohlrabi for 4 minutes, drain, and fry with potato cubes in mustard oil. Sear seasoned prawns and set aside.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste, tomato, and spice powders until oil separates.
Add kohlrabi, potatoes, and warm water; simmer until tender, then add prawns, garam masala, and ghee.

notes: Winter kohlrabi (olkopi) and prawn curry.

name: Chingri Diye Palong Shak Ghonto (Spinach & Vegetable Medley with Prawns)

steps.text: Lightly fry seasoned prawns in mustard oil and remove. Fry cubed potato, radish, and brinjal until golden.
Temper oil with panch phoron and dry red chilli, sauté ginger paste and cumin powder, then add fried vegetables and chopped spinach.
Fold in fried prawns, slit green chillies, salt, and a pinch of sugar; cook until thick and cohesive.

notes: Traditional Bengali winter spinach ghonto with prawns.

name: Chingri Diye Pepe Aloo Jhol (Raw Papaya, Potato & Prawn Light Curry)

steps.text: Lightly sear turmeric-salted prawns in mustard oil and remove. Sauté cubed raw papaya and potato for 4 minutes.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, add ginger paste, turmeric, cumin powder, papaya, potatoes, and warm water; cook covered until soft.
Stir in seared prawns, slit green chillies, and a drop of ghee; simmer for 5 minutes.

notes: Light, nourishing, and easy-to-digest Bengali everyday prawn curry.

name: Chingri Jhal (Bengali Spicy Prawn Mustard-Tomato Gravy)

steps.text: Season prawns with salt and turmeric and sear lightly in hot mustard oil for 1-2 minutes; set aside.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, cook grated tomato with turmeric and chilli powder, then add mustard paste mixed with warm water.
Add seared prawns, simmer for 4-5 minutes until the gravy coats the prawns, and finish with chopped coriander and raw mustard oil.

notes: Quick, fiery Bengali prawn jhal ready in under 25 minutes.

name: Chingri Kalia (Festive Bengali Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Season cleaned prawns with turmeric and salt, fry briefly in hot mustard oil until golden-pink, and remove.
Temper oil with bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves. Fry grated onion until deep golden, then cook ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, yogurt, and spices until oil separates.
Add warm water to form a rich gravy, return the prawns, simmer gently for 5-6 minutes, and finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Serve with basanti pulao, vegetable pulao, or steamed basmati rice.

name: Chingri Khichuri (Bengali Roasted Moong Dal Khichuri with Prawns)

steps.text: Dry-roast moong dal until golden and aromatic, then wash with Gobindobhog rice. Separately, fry seasoned prawns with ginger and spices in mustard oil and set aside.
Temper oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and cumin seeds. Sauté ginger, tomato, turmeric, and cumin powder, then add washed rice, roasted dal, and hot water; cook until soft.
Gently fold the spiced fried prawns, slit green chillies, garam masala, and a generous spoonful of ghee into the hot khichuri.

notes: Coastal Bengali monsoon specialty pairing fragrant Gobindobhog khichuri with spiced prawns.

name: Chingri Kochuri (Bengali Spiced Minced Prawn Stuffed Puri)

steps.text: Sauté chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste in mustard oil until golden. Add minced chingri, turmeric, chilli powder, garam masala, salt, and roasted cumin-fennel powder; cook on medium-high until dry and aromatic.
Knead maida with warm ghee and water. Roll into small cups, fill each with a spoonful of cooked prawn puran, seal tightly, and roll evenly without tearing.
Deep-fry in hot oil until puffed and crisp. Serve hot with kasundi (Bengali mustard) and onion-cucumber salad.

notes: An aristocratic Bengali banquet delicacy featuring sweet kucho chingri.

name: Chingri Kosha (Bengali Slow-Cooked Spicy Prawn Masala)

steps.text: Coat prawns with turmeric and salt, sear in smoking mustard oil for 1 minute per side, and set aside.

Temper oil with whole garam masala and a pinch of sugar for color. Caramelize sliced onions, then slow-roast ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, and spice powders with splashes of warm water until dark and glossy.
Add the seared prawns and slit green chillies to the rich masala, cook for 4-5 minutes until well coated, and finish with ghee.

notes: Delicious with luchi, radhaballabhi, parotta, or pulao.

name: Chingri Macher Bora (Bengali Prawn & Coconut Fritters)

steps.text: Coarsely chop or pulse the cleaned prawns so they retain a bite.
Combine minced prawns with grated coconut, chopped onion, green chillies, coriander leaves, turmeric, kalonji, salt, and besan into a firm mixture.
Shape into flat round patties (bora) and shallow-fry in hot mustard oil over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until crisp and golden brown.

notes: Serve hot as a starter with dal-bhaat (lentils and steamed rice) or as an evening snack with tea.

name: Chingri Macher Chop (Bengali Spiced Prawn Croquettes)

steps.text: Sauté onion, ginger, garlic, and chopped prawns with turmeric until cooked. Mix in mashed potatoes, bhaja masala, garam masala, green chillies, and coriander; cool completely.
Shape mixture into oval croquettes, roll in dry flour, dip in beaten egg or cornflour slurry, and coat generously in breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil until deep golden brown and crunchy. Serve with kasundi and onion-cucumber salad.

notes: A classic Kolkata telebhaja / cabin snack.

name: Chingri Macher Jhol (Light Homestyle Bengali Prawn Broth)

steps.text: Lightly fry seasoned prawns in mustard oil and set aside. Fry potato wedges for 3 minutes.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, cook ginger paste, cumin-coriander powder, and tomato, then add warm water and potatoes.
Once potatoes are tender, add prawns and fresh coriander leaves; simmer gently for 5 minutes.

notes: Comforting, low-spice everyday Bengali prawn jhol.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Bata (Bengali Smoky Mashed Prawn Head Bharta)

ingredients.name: Prawn Heads (with Inner Meat and Ghilu/roe)

steps.section: Roast prawn heads, garlic and chillies
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, fry dry red chillies and nigella seeds, then pan-roast garlic cloves, sliced onion, and turmeric-salted prawn heads until cooked through and smoky.
Grind the roasted prawn heads, garlic, onions, dry red chillies, green chillies, and fresh coriander on a shil-nora (stone grinder) or food processor with zero water.
Season with salt, drizzle 1 tbsp pungent raw mustard oil on top, and serve with steaming hot white rice.

notes: One of Bengal's most prized zero-waste bata/bharta delicacies.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Diye Aloo Potol Dalna (Pointed Gourd & Potato Curry with Prawn Heads)

steps.section: Fry potol, potatoes and prawn heads
steps.text: Fry potol halves and potato wedges in mustard oil until golden and remove. Fry seasoned prawn heads until golden and crush slightly.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, fry chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste, and cook tomato with spice powders.
Add fried potol, potatoes, prawn heads, and warm water; simmer covered for 7 minutes until tender and finish with ghee and garam masala.

notes: Infuses everyday Aloo Potol Dalna with rich prawn head flavor.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Diye Bandhakopi Ghonto (Bengali Cabbage with Prawn Heads)

steps.text: Fry seasoned prawn heads in mustard oil, crush into bite-sized pieces, and set aside. Fry cubed potatoes until golden.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, cook ginger paste, tomato, and spices, then add shredded cabbage, potatoes, and salt; cover and cook until soft.

steps.section: Fold in prawn heads and peas
steps.text: Add green peas, crushed prawn heads, sugar, ghee, and garam masala; cook uncovered for 5 minutes.

notes: Hearty winter Bengali cabbage ghonto flavored with fried prawn heads.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Diye Chalkumro Ghonto (Ash Gourd with Prawn Heads)

ingredients.name: Fresh Grated Coconut or Mustard Paste

steps.text: Season cleaned prawn heads with salt and turmeric, fry in mustard oil until golden, and crush coarsely.
Temper oil with bay leaf, nigella seeds, and slit green chillies; add julienned ash gourd, turmeric, and salt, and cook covered until soft.

steps.section: Finish with prawn heads and coconut
steps.text: Stir in the crushed prawn heads, grated coconut, and a pinch of sugar; cook uncovered for 4 minutes until thick.

notes: Cooling summer gourd dish enriched with prawn heads.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Diye Kochu Shak (Colocasia Greens with Prawn Heads)

steps.section: Blanch kochu shak and fry prawn heads
steps.text: Boil chopped colocasia stems with salt until tender, drain well, and mash. Fry seasoned prawn heads in mustard oil until crisp and crush coarsely.

steps.section: Temper with garlic and kalo jeere
steps.text: Temper mustard oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, nigella seeds, crushed garlic, and slit green chillies.
Add mashed kochu shak, turmeric, salt, sugar, and crushed prawn heads; stir-cook over medium flame until moisture evaporates and finish with lemon juice.

notes: Traditional Bengali monsoon delicacy.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Diye Kochur Loti (Taro Stolons with Crushed Prawn Heads)

steps.section: Blanch kochur loti and fry prawn heads
steps.text: Blanch cleaned taro stolons in salted turmeric water for 2 minutes and drain. Fry seasoned prawn heads in mustard oil and crush coarsely.
Temper oil with nigella seeds, fry sliced onion and garlic paste with turmeric and chilli powder.

steps.section: Braise with prawn heads and mustard-coconut
steps.text: Add blanched kochur loti, crushed prawn heads, mustard paste, grated coconut, and green chillies; cook covered on low heat for 8 minutes until tender.

notes: Bold, garlicky East Bengali preparation using crushed prawn heads.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Diye Kumro Chorchori (Sweet Red Pumpkin with Prawn Heads)

steps.text: Fry turmeric-salted prawn heads in mustard oil, crush coarsely, and set aside.
Temper oil with panch phoron and dry red chilli, sauté sliced onion, and add pumpkin and potato cubes with turmeric and salt.
Add crushed prawn heads, slit green chillies, and a splash of water; cover and cook until pumpkin is soft and slightly mashed. Garnish with coriander.

notes: Sweet red pumpkin balances the savory depth of fried prawn heads.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Diye Lau Ghonto (Bottle Gourd with Crushed Prawn Heads)

steps.text: Fry turmeric-salted prawn heads in mustard oil until aromatic and golden, crush lightly to release the inner ghilu, and remove.
Temper oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste and cumin-coriander powder, then add finely chopped bottle gourd and salt; cover and cook until soft.
Stir in the fried prawn heads, slit green chillies, and a pinch of sugar; cook until excess liquid reduces and finish with chopped coriander and ghee.

notes: Delicate bottle gourd absorbs the rich scampi flavor of jumbo prawn heads.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Diye Mochar Ghonto (Banana Blossom with Prawn Heads)

steps.section: Boil mocha and fry prawn heads
steps.text: Boil chopped banana blossom with turmeric and salt, drain and mash lightly. Fry seasoned prawn heads and potato cubes in mustard oil.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste, cumin-coriander powder, grated coconut, and fried potatoes.
Add boiled banana blossom, crushed fried prawn heads, salt, and sugar; cook until cohesive and finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Rich, aromatic Bengali banana blossom ghonto.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Diye Moong Dal (Roasted Moong Dal with Prawn Heads)

ingredients.name: Jumbo Prawn Heads (Golda Chingri Matha) or Small Prawns

steps.text: Dry-roast sona moong dal until golden and aromatic, wash thoroughly, and boil with salt and turmeric until soft but intact.
Heat mustard oil, temper with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and cumin seeds. Fry chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and seasoned prawn heads, crushing them slightly to release flavor.

steps.section: Simmer dal and finish with ghee
steps.text: Pour the boiled moong dal into the pan, simmer together for 5 minutes with a pinch of sugar, and finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Zero-waste Bengali delicacy that turns golda chingri heads into a rich, aromatic dal.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Diye Muri Ghonto (Gobindobhog Rice & Prawn Head Medley)

steps.section: Fry prawn heads, potatoes and rice
steps.text: Fry cubed potatoes in mustard oil and set aside. Fry seasoned prawn heads until golden, crushing them slightly. Lightly toast Gobindobhog rice, cashews, and raisins in 1 tsp ghee.
Temper oil with bay leaf and whole garam masala, brown chopped onion, and cook ginger-garlic paste, tomato, cumin, coriander, and turmeric.

steps.section: Simmer rice, potatoes and prawn heads
steps.text: Add toasted rice, fried potatoes, crushed prawn heads, and 1.25 cups warm water; cover and cook on low heat until rice and potatoes are tender. Finish with ghee, sugar, and garam masala.

notes: A royal prawn-head version of traditional Bengali Muri Ghonto.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Diye Pui Shak Chorchori (Malabar Spinach & Pumpkin with Prawn Heads)

steps.text: Season cleaned prawn heads with salt and turmeric, fry in hot mustard oil until crisp, crush coarsely with the spatula, and set aside.
Temper oil with panch phoron and dry red chilli, fry potato and pumpkin cubes, then add pui shak stems and leaves, ginger paste, turmeric, and salt; cover and cook until tender.

steps.section: Fold in prawn heads and mustard
steps.text: Add the crushed fried prawn heads, mustard paste, slit green chillies, and a pinch of sugar; cook uncovered for 5 minutes until thick.

notes: Classic Bengali household way to use every bit of prawn head flavor in leafy green chorchori.

name: Chingri Macher Matha Kosha (Bengali Spicy Prawn Head Masala)

ingredients.name: Jumbo Prawn Heads (Golda Chingri Matha, Cleaned with Ghilu Intact)

steps.text: Season cleaned jumbo prawn heads with salt and turmeric and fry in hot mustard oil for 3-4 minutes, pressing lightly so the rich head fat flavors the oil.
Temper oil with whole garam masala, brown sliced onions, and slow-cook ginger-garlic paste, chopped tomato, and spice powders until oil separates.
Return the prawn heads with a splash of warm water, cook covered for 5 minutes until coated in thick masala, and finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Celebratory Bengali dish where the creamy orange ghilu inside golda chingri heads enriches the kosha gravy.

name: Chingri Malai Curry

steps.text: Clean prawns and lightly season with salt and turmeric.
Lightly fry prawns, remove, then cook onion and ginger paste with spices.
Add coconut milk and a little water. Return prawns and simmer gently until just cooked.

name: Chingri Mathar Chop (Bengali Spiced Prawn Head & Potato Croquettes)

steps.text: Sauté minced onion, ginger, garlic, and crushed prawn heads in mustard oil with turmeric and chilli powder until cooked and dry. Fold in mashed potatoes, bhaja masala, garam masala, and coriander.
Shape cooled mixture into oval croquettes, dip in cornflour slurry, and coat generously in breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot oil until deep golden brown and serve with kasundi and onion-cucumber salad.

notes: Rich, savory Bengali chop infused with the deep flavor of prawn head roe (ghilu).

name: Chingri Paturi (Banana Leaf Wrapped Mustard Prawns)

steps.text: Grind mustard seeds, poppy seeds, grated coconut, and 2 green chillies into a thick, smooth paste. Mix with turmeric, salt, raw mustard oil, and cleaned prawns.
Spoon marinated prawns onto oiled, flame-softened banana leaf squares, top each parcel with a slit green chilli, and fold and tie securely with cotton thread.
Cook the banana leaf parcels in a lightly oiled covered skillet on low heat for 7-8 minutes per side until the leaves char and the aroma blooms.

notes: Wilting the banana leaves briefly over an open flame makes them pliable so they fold without tearing.

name: Chingri Porota (Bengali Spiced Small Prawn & Onion Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Sauté onions and ginger-garlic in mustard oil, add minced prawns, turmeric, cumin, garam masala, chillies, and salt; stir-fry until thoroughly cooked and completely dry.
Wrap the savory chingri filling in dough balls, seal edges, and roll into flatbreads.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until blistered and golden. Serve warm with kasundi and cucumber salad.

notes: A coastal and riverine Bengali delicacy celebrating small sweet prawns encased in flaky paratha.

name: Chingri Posto (Prawns in Bengali Poppy Seed Paste)

steps.text: Soak white poppy seeds in warm water for 20 minutes, then grind with 2 green chillies and a splash of water into a creamy paste.
Lightly sear turmeric-salted prawns in mustard oil for 1 minute. Temper the oil with nigella seeds and optional sliced onion until translucent.
Stir in the poppy seed paste, warm water, salt, and prawns. Simmer on low heat for 5 minutes and finish with raw mustard oil and slit green chillies.

notes: Keep spices minimal so the nutty sweetness of posto and mustard oil shines through.

name: Chingri Pulao (Bengali Gobindobhog Prawn Pilaf)

steps.text: Wash and drain rice. Lightly fry seasoned prawns and set aside; fry cashews and raisins in ghee.
Temper ghee with bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves. Cook onion-ginger paste, then gently roast the drained rice for 2 minutes.

steps.section: Simmer with coconut milk and prawns
steps.text: Add coconut milk, warm water, salt, and a touch of sugar. When rice is 80% done, fold in the prawns, fried cashews, raisins, and green chillies; cover on low heat until fluffy.

notes: Fragrant Bengali one-pot prawn pilaf cooked with coconut milk and Gobindobhog rice.

name: Chini Porota (Bengali Sweet Sugar-Stuffed Layered Paratha)

steps.text: Knead flour with 1 tsp ghee, a pinch of salt, and warm water or milk into a soft dough.
Roll into a circle, brush with ghee, sprinkle evenly with sugar and cardamom powder, fold into a triangle or square parcel sealing the edges well, and roll out gently.
Cook on a medium-hot tawa with ghee until the sugar inside melts into a caramelized syrup and the outside turns golden and crisp.

notes: Nostalgic childhood favorite across Bengali and Indian households.

name: Chira Bhaja Diye Muri Makha (Crispy Flattened Rice & Puffed Rice Mix)

steps.text: Heat oil in a kadhai, fry peanuts, curry leaves, and slit green chillies until crisp, then add dry thick chira and roast on medium-low heat for 5 minutes until puffed and crunchy. Cool slightly.
Combine the crisp chira bhaja with puffed rice, chopped onion, black salt, and roasted cumin powder.

notes: Two-texture Bengali tiffin combining crunchy pan-roasted chira with light muri.

name: Chirer Moa (Crispy Fried Flattened Rice & Jaggery Balls)

steps.section: Roast or flash-fry chira until crisp and puffed
steps.text: Dry-roast or flash-fry flattened rice in a strainer until light, airy, and crunchy; drain thoroughly.

steps.section: Cook jaggery to sticky thread stage
steps.text: Melt jaggery with 2 tbsp water and cardamom over low flame until frothy and reaches a two-thread consistency.

steps.section: Coat crispy chira and shape into balls
steps.text: Fold the crispy chira into the hot jaggery syrup and shape into round moas with water-dampened or ghee-greased hands.

notes: Classic Bengali puffed flattened-rice sweet ball alongside Murir Moa and Khoier Moa.

name: Chirer Polao

steps.text: Wash, chop and measure the ingredients. Soak or ferment the base if the recipe requires it.
Heat oil, add mustard or cumin seeds, onion, chilli and vegetables.
Add the main ingredient and the required water or batter; cook until tender and serve hot.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Chitoi Pitha (Porous Bengali Stovetop Rice-Flour Pancakes)

ingredients.name: Baking Powder (or Eno, Optional for Pores)

steps.text: Whisk fine rice flour, salt, and lukewarm water by hand until completely lump-free and pouring-consistency; rest 15 minutes, then stir in baking powder.

steps.section: Cook covered on hot heavy pan
steps.text: Heat a lightly greased appam pan or small heavy cast-iron kadhai. Pour a ladle of batter, immediately cover tightly with a lid, and cook on medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes until puffed, porous, and crisp underneath.

notes: Serve hot with nolen gur, bhapa dim, or spicy dhonepata-shorshe bharta.

name: Chocolate Barfi

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Chocolate Milkshake

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Cholar Dal Bengali Style

steps.text: Rinse the lentils or legumes. Pressure-cook or simmer with water and turmeric until soft.
Heat oil or ghee; add cumin, garlic, onion and tomato and cook until fragrant.
Mix the tempering into the cooked dal, adjust water and salt, and simmer briefly.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Cholar Dal Bhaja Muri Makha (Crunchy Fried Chana Dal & Puffed Rice Tiffin)

steps.text: Mix chopped onion, cucumber, deseeded tomato, green chilli, coriander, black salt, and mustard oil in a bowl.

steps.section: Fold in muri and fried chana dal
steps.text: Add crisp puffed rice and spiced fried chana dal, drizzle with lemon juice, toss well, and serve.

notes: High-crunch protein-rich evening tiffin.

name: Cholar Daler Kochuri (Bengali Spiced Bengal Gram / Chana Dal Stuffed Puri)

steps.section: Grind and sauté cholar dal puran
steps.text: Pulse boiled chana dal in a grinder to a coarse paste. Sauté in ghee with hing, kalo jeere, ginger-green chilli paste, roasted bhaja masala, salt, and sugar until the paste leaves the pan.
Knead maida with 2 tbsp ghee and water into a smooth dough. Shape into balls, make an indentation, fill with dal paste, pinch close, and roll into smooth puris.
Fry in hot oil until fully puffed and golden crisp. Serve warm with hing aloor dum or bandhakopir torkari.

notes: The hearty Bengal gram cousin of Radhaballabhi, popular for Sunday winter breakfasts.

name: Choshir Payesh / Chushi Pitha (Hand-Rolled Rice-Flour Pearls in Nolen Gur Milk)

steps.text: Boil 1 cup water with a pinch of salt and ghee, stir in rice flour, cover 5 minutes, and knead smooth. Pinch tiny rice-grain-sized bits and roll between palms into tapered 1/2-inch pearls; dry on a plate dusted with rice flour.

steps.section: Simmer in thickened milk and gur
steps.text: Boil milk with bay leaf and cardamom until reduced by a quarter. Drop in the choshi pearls gently and simmer 10 minutes until cooked and thickened. Turn off heat, wait 2 minutes, and stir in nolen gur.

notes: Adding nolen gur off the heat prevents the milk from curdling.

name: Churmur (Kolkata Street-Style Crushed Phuchka & Spiced Potato Chaat)

steps.section: Toss diced potatoes with spices and tamarind
steps.text: In a deep bowl (or sal-leaf dona), mix cubed boiled potatoes, boiled kala chana, chopped onion, cucumber, green chillies, coriander, bhaja masala, bitnoon, and tangy tetul jol.

steps.section: Fold in crushed phuchkas and serve
steps.text: Crush crisp phuchka shells directly into the bowl, squeeze fresh Gondhoraj lemon juice, toss quickly so the shells stay crunchy, and serve immediately.

notes: No Kolkata phuchka outing is complete without a bowl of tangy, crunchy Churmur served in a sal-leaf bowl.

name: Churmure / Murmura Laddoo (Crispy Puffed Rice & Jaggery Laddoo)

steps.section: Crisp murmura and boil jaggery syrup
steps.text: Dry-roast puffed rice 2 minutes in a wide kadhai until extra crisp; set aside. Melt jaggery with 2 tbsp water and ghee in the kadhai, boiling 4–5 minutes until a drop forms a firm ball in cold water.

steps.section: Toss and shape quickly with wet palms
steps.text: Turn off heat, fold in crisp murmura and spice quickly until coated. Dip palms lightly in water and press into round laddoos while still warm.

notes: Work swiftly while the jaggery-coated murmura is warm so the laddoos hold together cleanly.

name: Classic Baked Macaroni and Cheese (Creamy Cheddar & Crispy Breadcrumb Mac & Cheese)

ingredients.name: Panko Breadcrumbs Toasted in 1 Tbsp Butter

steps.text: Cook macaroni in boiling salted water for 6 minutes until al dente. Drain and rinse briefly under warm water.

Melt butter in a saucepan, whisk in flour and cook roux for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in warm milk, simmering until thickened. Stir in mustard, nutmeg, pepper, and remove from heat before melting in shredded cheeses.
Fold boiled macaroni into the velvety cheese sauce. Pour into a buttered baking dish, scatter buttered panko breadcrumbs on top, and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling.

notes: Always shred cheese from blocks; pre-shredded cheeses contain anti-caking starches that prevent a silky, smooth melt.

name: Classic Chocolate Pudding (Silky Dark Chocolate Stovetop Custard Pudding)

steps.text: In a heavy saucepan, whisk together sugar, sifted cocoa powder, cornflour, and salt. Gradually whisk in cold whole milk until smooth with no lumps.

Heat saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly with a silicone spatula or whisk, scraping bottom and corners. Bring to a gentle boil and simmer for 2 minutes as it thickens into a glossy, velvety custard.

Remove from heat, immediately add chopped dark chocolate, butter, and vanilla extract. Whisk vigorously until the chocolate melts completely and the pudding is mirror-glossy. Pour into dessert bowls and chill for at least 2 hours.

notes: Real stovetop custard pudding with deep cocoa depth, velvety texture, and no artificial pudding mixes.

name: Classic Crispy Hashbrowns (Diner-Style Pan-Fried Shredded Potatoes)

steps.text: Grate potatoes on the large holes of a box grater, rinse in cold water to remove surface starch, and wring dry in a clean kitchen cloth.

Heat oil and butter in a wide skillet over medium heat. Spread shredded potatoes in an even 1/2-inch layer, season with salt and pepper, and cook undisturbed for 7 minutes until crisp brown underneath. Flip in sections or as one cake and cook 6 minutes more.

notes: Avoid stirring while browning so the bottom forms a crisp diner-style crust.

name: Classic Italian Minestrone Soup (Hearty Bean, Ditalini, Zucchini & Tomato Broth with Pesto)

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a soup pot, saute onions, carrots, and celery for 6 minutes. Add garlic, green beans, and zucchini, cooking for 3 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, bay leaf, and oregano. Bring to a boil, lower heat, and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Stir in cannellini beans, kale, and ditalini pasta. Simmer for 8 minutes until pasta is tender. Ladle into bowls and crown with a dollop of fresh basil pesto and grated Parmesan.

notes: Topping each warm bowl with a spoonful of fresh Genovese basil pesto elevates the broth with herbal brightness.

name: Classic Milk Tea

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Classic Minestrone Pasta (Hearty Ditalini Pasta with White Beans & Vegetables)

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a heavy Dutch oven, saute onions, carrots, and celery for 5 minutes until softened. Add garlic and diced zucchini, cooking for 2 more minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, cannellini beans, and Parmesan rind. Simmer on medium heat for 12 minutes to develop deep flavors.

Stir in ditalini pasta and cook directly in the simmering broth for 8 minutes until al dente. Fold in spinach until wilted, remove cheese rind, and serve with grated Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

notes: A rustic Italian pasta-stew; cooking the small ditalini directly in the rich tomato-bean broth yields concentrated, heartwarming flavor.

name: Classic Sooji Malai Toast / Rava Malai Bread Sandwich (Creamy Semolina & Veggie Pan Toast)

steps.text: Whisk fresh malai with sooji and milk into a thick paste, fold in chopped onion, tomato, capsicum, green chilli, coriander, black pepper, and salt, and rest 10 minutes.

Spread generously on bread slices. Place malai-side down on a warm tawa (no extra oil needed as malai releases ghee), cook 3–4 minutes on low heat until golden, flip and toast 2 minutes, then dust with chaat masala.

notes: Beloved North Indian home breakfast toast; malai creates a rich buttery crunch.

name: Classic Spaghetti Aglio e Olio (Garlic, Olive Oil & Red Pepper Flakes Spaghetti)

steps.text: Drop spaghetti into a pot of rapidly boiling salted water and cook for 8-9 minutes until firm to the bite. Reserve 0.5 cup of starchy pasta water before draining.

In a wide skillet, warm olive oil over gentle medium-low heat. Add sliced garlic and cook slowly for 2-3 minutes until pale straw golden (never burnt). Add red pepper flakes and remove briefly from heat.

Add drained spaghetti, reserved pasta water, and chopped fresh parsley to the pan. Toss vigorously over medium heat for 1 minute until a glistening, emulsified sauce coats the pasta. Serve immediately.

notes: The pure essence of Neapolitan cuisine; the slow infusion of garlic without browning preserves its sweet, fragrant aroma.

name: Clear Vegetable Wonton Soup (Delicate Sesame Ginger Broth with Steamed Vegetable Dumplings)

steps.text: In a pot, simmer vegetable broth with sliced ginger, crushed garlic, and white pepper for 10 minutes to extract aromatic oils. Strain out ginger slices.
Bring seasoned broth to a gentle simmer with soy sauce. Drop in vegetable wontons and simmer for 4 minutes until they float. Add bok choy for 1 minute until crisp-tender.
Ladle wontons, greens, and clear steaming broth into deep bowls. Finish with toasted sesame oil and scattered spring onions.

notes: Light, clean, and restorative broth showcasing plump, delicate dumplings in steaming herbal broth.

name: Club Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

steps.section: Fry cashews and temper whole spices
steps.text: Heat ghee in a heavy pot, fry cashews and raisins until golden and set aside. Temper bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, star anise, and fennel seeds.

steps.section: Saute onions, green chillies, and mint
steps.text: Add sliced onions, slit green chillies, ginger-garlic paste, and mint leaves; saute until onions turn soft and translucent without browning too dark.
Pour coconut milk, water, and salt, bring to a gentle simmer, fold in drained rice, and cook covered on low heat for 12–14 minutes. Garnish with fried cashews and raisins.

notes: Mildly spiced, silky South Indian coconut milk rice that pairs wonderfully with vegetable kurma, mushroom masala, or chicken curry.

name: Coffee Caramel Pudding / Espresso Caramel Custard (Rich Coffee-Infused Steamed Caramel Pudding)

ingredients.name: Instant Espresso Powder or Strong Dark Roast Decoction

steps.text: In a small pan, heat sugar and water on medium heat until golden amber. Swirl without stirring, then pour immediately into a 6-inch pudding tin, coating the base evenly. Let set firm.

Dissolve espresso powder and custard powder in 0.5 cup milk. Heat remaining milk, condensed milk, and fresh cream in a saucepan. Whisk in the coffee custard slurry and simmer on low heat for 3 minutes until thickened and silky smooth.

Pour warm coffee custard into the caramel-lined tin. Cover tightly with aluminium foil and steam in a steamer for 25 minutes. Cool, refrigerate for 3 hours, then invert onto a serving platter so the glossy dark coffee caramel pools over the pudding.

notes: An irresistible dessert for coffee lovers combining the bittersweet notes of espresso with rich golden caramel and velvety milk custard.

name: Corn Paratha / Makai Paratha (Spiced Sweet Corn & Coriander Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Sauté crushed sweet corn with ginger, chillies, ajwain, chaat masala, and amchur for 4 minutes; stir in roasted besan and salt until moisture is absorbed.
Place corn filling inside wheat dough rounds, seal neatly, and roll out with even strokes.
Cook on a hot griddle with ghee until crisp and golden brown. Serve with tomato chutney or dahi.

notes: Naturally sweet, juicy, and spiced corn stuffed flatbread loved across Indian homes.

name: Cornflakes Chivda / Khatta Meetha Cornflakes Mixture

steps.section: Temper nuts, dry coconut, and curry leaves
steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide kadai, crackle mustard seeds and curry leaves, and roast peanuts, thin dry coconut slices, cashews, sesame seeds, and raisins until golden.
Lower the flame and stir in turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli powder, amchur, and black salt.

steps.section: Fold in crisp cornflakes and powdered sugar
steps.text: Gently toss in the cornflakes and powdered sugar over low heat for 2 minutes until evenly coated and crunchy.

notes: Light, low-oil sweet-and-tangy cornflakes namkeen studded with dry fruits.

name: Country Chicken Bhuna

steps.text: Mix chicken with salt, turmeric and a little yogurt or spice; rest if time allows.
Sauté onion until golden, add ginger-garlic and spices, then tomato or yogurt.
Add chicken and a little water; cover and cook until fully cooked and tender.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.
