name: Elaneer Payasam / Tender Coconut Kheer (Creamy Tender Coconut Pulp & Coconut Milk Pudding)

steps.text: Boil full-fat milk with condensed milk and cardamom on medium flame for 8 minutes until slightly thickened; remove from heat and let cool completely to room temperature.
Puree half of the tender coconut pulp with coconut water until creamy, keeping the other half as small tender bites for texture.
Whisk thick coconut milk, pureed coconut pulp, and chopped coconut bites into the cooled milk. Chill for at least 2 hours and serve cold.

notes: A heavenly, refreshing South Indian coastal dessert made with pure tender coconut and aromatic cardamom.

name: Elo Jhelo / Elojhelo (Bengali Ribbon-Twisted Crispy Sweet Pastry in Syrup)

steps.section: Cut slit strips and fold into tangled bows
steps.text: Knead maida, ghee, pinch of salt, and kalonji into a firm dough; roll into rectangles, cut multiple parallel vertical slits leaving the borders intact, and pull one end through the center to form a tangled ribbon ('elo-jhelo').
Deep-fry on medium-low heat until every ribbon fold is crisp and golden.
Dip into warm single-thread sugar syrup for 1–2 minutes and drain.

notes: Traditional Bengali home-made festive sweet prepared for Bijoya Dashami and weddings.

name: Enduri Pitha / Haladi Patra Pitha (Odia Turmeric-Leaf Steamed Coconut-Chhena Cakes)

steps.text: Cook grated coconut, chhena, jaggery, and cardamom in a pan for 5 minutes until thick; cool. Whisk rice flour, suji, salt, and warm water into a thick spreadable batter.

steps.section: Spread on turmeric leaves and steam
steps.text: Spread 2 tbsp batter along the center of a washed turmeric leaf, place 1 tbsp coconut-chhena filling, fold the leaf in half, and steam over boiling water for 12–15 minutes until firm and fragrant.

notes: Turmeric leaves impart an unmistakable earthy aroma during steaming.

name: Espresso

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Falafel Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Falooda

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Fettuccine Alfredo (Rich Butter & Parmesan Cream Sauce Pasta)

ingredients.name: Heavy Dairy Cream (or Classic Butter-water Emulsion)

steps.text: Boil fettuccine in salted water until perfectly al dente (about 8-9 minutes). Reserve 0.5 cup hot pasta water.
In a wide deep pan, melt butter gently over medium-low heat. Pour in heavy cream and nutmeg, bringing to a gentle simmer for 1-2 minutes.

Transfer hot fettuccine into the pan, turn off heat, and add freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano in two additions with splashes of pasta water. Toss rapidly until the cheese melts into a luxurious, clingy glaze.

notes: True Alfredo is an emulsion of rich cultured butter and aged Parmigiano-Reggiano with starchy pasta water coating broad fettuccine ribbons.

name: Filter Coffee

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Fish Egg Bhurji (Macher Dimer Jhuri Bhaja / Spiced Scrambled Fish Roe)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil in a pan and fry finely chopped onions, minced garlic, ginger, and green chillies until golden.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, cumin, red chilli powder, and salt, then tip in the mashed fish eggs and stir-fry continuously on medium-low heat.
Keep stirring until the roe separates into golden, savory granules (jhuri). Finish with garam masala, lemon juice, and fresh coriander.

notes: Delicious scrambled fish roe bhurji that can be eaten with hot rice, roti, or buttered toast.

name: Fish Egg Curry (Homestyle Indian Macher Dimer Curry)

steps.text: Simmer the fish roe sacs gently in salted turmeric water for 5-6 minutes until firm, cool slightly, cut into bite-sized cubes, and lightly sear in oil.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and bay leaf, brown the chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste, then cook tomatoes and spice powders until oil separates.
Add warm water to form a smooth gravy, add the seared fish egg cubes, simmer gently for 6 minutes, and finish with garam masala and coriander leaves.

notes: Poaching and cubing the roe allows it to hold its shape like paneer cubes in the curry.

name: Fish Egg Fritter Curry (Macher Dimer Borar Jhol)

steps.section: Make and fry fish egg boras
steps.text: Mix fish eggs with half the chopped onion, chopped green chilli, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry small boras in mustard oil until golden and set aside.
In the remaining oil, temper with bay leaf and cumin seeds, fry potato wedges and remaining onion, then cook ginger paste, tomato, turmeric, cumin, and coriander powder.
Pour in warm water, cover and cook until potatoes are tender, then drop in the fried fish egg boras and simmer for 4-5 minutes so they soak up the gravy. Finish with garam masala.

notes: Quintessential Bengali homestyle fish egg fritter curry served with steamed rice.

name: Fish Egg Fritters (Macher Dimer Bora)

ingredients.name: Fish Eggs / Fish Roe (Rohu or Katla Macher Dim)

steps.text: Wash the fish roe gently, peel off the thin outer membrane, and mash the eggs in a bowl so no tough lumps remain.
Add finely chopped onion, green chillies, coriander leaves, nigella seeds, turmeric, salt, besan, and rice flour; whisk vigorously for 2 minutes to aerate.
Heat mustard oil in a pan over medium-low flame, drop spoonfuls of the mixture, and fry slowly on both sides until crisp outside and cooked through inside.

notes: Fry on medium-low heat and cover briefly if needed, as fish eggs pop slightly in hot oil.

name: Fish Egg Masala (Macher Dimer Kosha / Spicy Fish Roe Masala)

steps.text: Steam or poach the fish roe with salt and turmeric until firm, cut into thick squares, and sear in hot mustard oil until golden.
Temper oil with whole garam masala, caramelize sliced onions, and slow-roast ginger-garlic paste, chopped tomato, and spice powders with splashes of water until dark and glossy.
Add the fried fish roe pieces and a splash of warm water, cook for 5 minutes until coated in thick masala, and finish with garam masala.

notes: Rich, spicy fish egg masala that pairs great with steamed rice, roti, or paratha.

name: Fish Egg Pakora (Crispy Macher Dimer Pakora)

steps.text: Combine cleaned fish eggs with sliced onion, ginger-garlic paste, chopped green chillies, coriander, ajwain, turmeric, chilli powder, lemon juice, salt, besan, and cornflour.
Drop small bite-sized portions into medium-hot oil and fry for 4-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden brown and crunchy.
Drain on paper towels, dust with chaat masala, and serve hot with kasundi or mint-coriander chutney.

notes: Crunchy evening snack that pairs wonderfully with masala chai or as a starter with dal-rice.

name: Fish Egg Potato Curry (Aloo Diye Macher Dimer Jhol)

steps.text: Season fish roe with salt and turmeric, sear whole or in thick slabs in mustard oil until firm, and cut into pieces. Fry potato wedges in the same oil.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and bay leaf, fry chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste, then cook tomato and spice powders.
Add potatoes and warm water; cook until tender, then add the fish roe pieces, simmer 5 minutes, and garnish with garam masala and coriander.

notes: Classic homestyle fish egg and potato curry.

name: Fish Finger Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Fish Momo (Bhetki / Boneless Fish, Ginger & Coriander Steamed Dumplings)

ingredients.name: Boneless Bhetki or White Fish Fillet (Finely Minced By Knife)

steps.text: Finely chop boneless fish fillets with a knife, then mix with onion, green chilli, coriander, ginger, garlic, lime juice, black pepper, oil, and salt.
Wrap 1 tbsp fish filling in thin maida circles, pleat tightly, and steam over boiling water for 11–12 minutes.

notes: Delicate Bengali-Himalayan fusion; serve with tomato-chilli dip or kasundi.

name: Fish Roe Fry

steps.text: Gently clean fish roe and season with salt and turmeric.
Heat oil, sauté onion and chilli, add roe carefully and cook through while breaking it into small pieces.

name: Fish Tikka Kathi Roll (Kolkata Street-Style Bhetki Fish Roll)

steps.text: Marinate boneless Bhetki cubes with lemon juice, ginger-garlic-chilli paste, yogurt, kasundi, garam masala, and salt. Sear on a hot tawa in mustard oil until flaky and golden.
Lay the smoky Bhetki tikka pieces over crisp laccha parathas, top with onion rings, cucumber, coriander, chaat masala, and a squeeze of lime, and roll tightly.

notes: Delicate Kolkata Bhetki fish tikka infused with kasundi and wrapped in a crisp kathi roll.

name: Flat White

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: French Onion Soup (Rich Caramelized Onion & Herb Broth with Crusty Cheesy Baguette)

ingredients.name: Rich Beef or Dark Vegetable Broth
White Wine or Apple Cider Vinegar

steps.text: Melt butter in a heavy Dutch oven. Add sliced onions with a pinch of salt and cook on medium-low heat for 35-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and sweet.
Dust onions with flour and cook for 1 minute. Deglaze pot with white wine or vinegar, scraping browned bits. Add broth, thyme, and bay leaf. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Ladle hot soup into oven-safe crocks. Place toasted baguette slices on top, smother generously with Gruyere cheese, and broil in the oven for 3-4 minutes until bubbling and blistered brown.

notes: Patience is key; slowly cooking onions over low heat until natural sugars caramelize produces the unmistakable rich amber broth.

name: French Toast Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Fresh Orange Juice

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Fried Veg Momo (Golden Crispy Deep-Fried Cabbage & Carrot Dumplings)

steps.text: Squeeze water from grated cabbage and carrot, toss with onion, spring onion, ginger, garlic, green chilli, soy sauce, pepper, and salt. Roll thin maida circles, fill, and seal edges firmly.
Fry in medium-hot oil in batches for 5–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until crisp and golden brown all over.

notes: Keep oil at medium heat so the pleated wrapper cooks crisp without blistering.

name: Fulkopir Datta Aloo Jhol / Patla Torkari (Light Homestyle Cauliflower Stem & Potato Curry)

steps.section: Sauté fulkopir datta and potatoes with ginger-cumin spices
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with cumin seeds and bay leaf, sauté potatoes and peeled cauliflower stems for 4 minutes, then add ginger paste, chopped tomato, turmeric, cumin, coriander powder, and salt.

steps.section: Simmer in light broth and garnish
steps.text: Add 1.5 cups warm water, cover and simmer until the fulkopir datta and potatoes are fork-tender, and finish with slit green chillies and fresh coriander leaves.

notes: Light, soothing everyday Bengali jhol using tender cauliflower stems and potatoes.

name: Fulkopir Datta Aloo Kumro Torkari (Cauliflower Stem, Sweet Pumpkin & Potato Panch-Phoron Curry)

steps.section: Temper and simmer fulkopir datta with pumpkin and potato
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle panch phoron, bay leaf, and dry red chilli, add grated ginger, potatoes, and fulkopir datta; sauté 4 minutes, then add pumpkin, turmeric, cumin, salt, and warm water to cover and cook until tender.

steps.section: Mash a few pumpkin cubes and garnish
steps.text: Lightly mash a few pumpkin pieces to thicken the gravy, balance with a pinch of sugar, and garnish with chopped coriander leaves.

notes: Great accompaniment to गरम luchi, paratha, roti, or dal-chawal.

name: Fulkopir Datta Bharta / Phulkopir Data Bata (Spiced Mashed Cauliflower Stem & Leaf Paste with Mustard Oil)

steps.section: Boil and grind the fulkopir datta
steps.text: Blanch or steam the chopped cauliflower stems until soft, drain thoroughly, and grind into a coarse paste with green chillies and half the garlic.

steps.section: Temper and roast paste in mustard oil until dry
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle kalo jeere, dry red chillies, remaining garlic, and onion until golden, then add the ground fulkopir datta paste and salt; stir continuously on medium flame until all moisture evaporates and oil separates.

notes: Earthy, smoky Bangal-style Fulkopir Datta Bata served as the first course with hot steamed rice.

name: Fulkopir Datta Bora / Pakora (Crispy Spiced Cauliflower Stem & Gram Flour Fritters)

ingredients.name: Rice Flour (Chaler Guro) for Extra Crunch

steps.text: Toss finely julienned (or lightly steamed) cauliflower stems with salt, turmeric, chilli powder, kalo jeere, posto, besan, and rice flour, sprinkling just enough water to bind into tight clusters.
Drop spoonfuls into medium-hot mustard oil and fry on both sides until crisp and golden brown; serve hot with kasundi or dal-rice.

notes: Crispy zero-waste Bengali bora made from sweet, tender cauliflower stalks.

name: Fulkopir Datta Bori Begun Chorchori (Cauliflower Stem, Eggplant & Fried Lentil Dumpling Medley)

steps.text: Fry the lentil dumplings (bori) in hot mustard oil until golden brown, crush lightly, and set aside.

steps.section: Braise vegetables and fold in crispy bori
steps.text: Temper the oil with panch phoron, cook fulkopir datta and potatoes until nearly soft, add eggplant and mustard paste, cook until thick, and top with crushed fried bori before serving.

notes: Pure vegetarian (niramish) winter chorchori with crunchy fried bori.

name: Fulkopir Datta Chingri Chorchori (Cauliflower Stem, Potato & Prawn Dry Curry)

steps.text: Toss prawns with a pinch of turmeric and salt, flash-fry in hot mustard oil for 1–2 minutes, and set aside.

steps.section: Cook fulkopir datta, potatoes, and prawns together
steps.text: Temper oil with panch phoron and sliced onion, add ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, cumin, fulkopir datta, and potatoes; cover until tender, then fold in brinjal, fried prawns, and mustard paste, cooking until dry and well-coated.

notes: Sweet kucho chingri elevates humble cauliflower stems into a prized Bengali lunch dish.

name: Fulkopir Datta Chorchori / Phulkopir Data Chorchori (Bengali Cauliflower Stem, Potato, Brinjal & Mustard Medley)

steps.section: Prep the fulkopir datta and vegetables
steps.text: Peel the tough outer skin off the thick cauliflower stems (fulkopir datta) and slice into finger-length batons along with any tender inner leaves. Cut potatoes, pumpkin, and brinjal into similar sizes.

steps.section: Temper with panch phoron and braise stems
steps.text: Heat mustard oil in a kadai, crackle panch phoron and dry red chilli, add potatoes and fulkopir datta with turmeric and salt, and sauté covered with a splash of water until 75% tender.

steps.section: Add brinjal, pumpkin, and mustard paste
steps.text: Add pumpkin and brinjal pieces, cook until soft, then stir in mustard paste, slit green chillies, a pinch of sugar, and a raw mustard oil drizzle; cook for 3 minutes until mushy (ga-makha).

notes: Classic zero-waste Bengali winter delicacy using tender cauliflower stems (fulkopir datta) in a mustard-laced chorchori.

name: Fulkopir Datta Diye Masoor Dal (Red Lentil Dal Cooked with Tender Cauliflower Stems)

steps.section: Boil masoor dal with fulkopir datta
steps.text: Simmer washed masoor dal with turmeric, salt, and peeled cauliflower stem pieces until the lentils are creamy and the stems are tender yet hold their shape.

steps.section: Temper with kalo jeere, tomato, and coriander
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle kalo jeere, dry red chilli, and green chillies, sauté chopped tomato until soft, pour the boiled dal over, simmer 3 minutes, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Comforting everyday Bengali winter masoor dal infused with the sweetness of cauliflower stems.

name: Fulkopir Datta Diye Motor Dal (Yellow Split Pea Dal with Cauliflower Stems & Coconut)

ingredients.name: Fresh Coconut Bits or Grated Coconut

steps.section: Pressure-cook motor dal and add fulkopir datta
steps.text: Boil motor dal until soft, then simmer with peeled cauliflower stems, turmeric, and salt until the stems are tender.

steps.section: Temper with cumin, ginger, and coconut
steps.text: Heat mustard oil and a spoon of ghee, crackle cumin seeds, bay leaf, and red chilli, fry coconut bits and grated ginger, pour in the dal, and simmer 3 minutes.

notes: Nutty, aromatic Bengali winter motor dal with tender fulkopir datta.

name: Fulkopir Datta Fry / Fulkopir Data Bhaja (Crispy Mustard-Tempered Cauliflower Stem & Potato Stir-Fry)

steps.section: Stir-fry julienned fulkopir datta and potatoes
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with kalo jeere and green chillies, add thinly julienned cauliflower stems and potatoes with turmeric and salt, and stir-fry on medium flame until tender and golden.
Sprinkle white poppy seeds (posto) and toss on high heat for 2 minutes until nutty and crisp.

notes: Quick, crunchy side fry (bhaja) to serve alongside dal and steamed rice.

name: Fulkopir Datta Macher Dimer Chorchori (Cauliflower Stem, Potato & Fish Roe Scramble Curry)

ingredients.name: Fresh Fish Roe / Fish Eggs (Macher Dim)

steps.text: Season fish eggs with turmeric and salt, pan-fry in hot mustard oil while breaking into coarse nuggets, and set aside.

steps.section: Cook fulkopir datta and toss with fish roe
steps.text: Temper oil with panch phoron, sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste, add cauliflower stems, potato strips, and spices; cook covered until tender, then fold in the fried fish roe and cook 3 minutes until well combined.

notes: Hearty Bengali homestyle dish combining tender fulkopir datta with savory macher dim.

name: Fulkopir Datta Macher Matha Diye Chorchori (Cauliflower Stem & Potato Medley with Fish Head)

ingredients.name: Rohu or Katla Fish Head (Macher Matha)

steps.section: Crisp-fry and break the fish head
steps.text: Marinate fish head pieces with turmeric and salt, fry in smoking mustard oil until crisp and golden, break into bite-sized chunks with the spatula, and set aside.

steps.section: Braise fulkopir datta with spices and fish head
steps.text: Temper oil with panch phoron, sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste, add fulkopir datta, potatoes, pumpkin, brinjal, and spice powders; cook covered until tender, fold in the fried fish head chunks, and finish with garam masala.

notes: Rich, rustic Bengali Macher Matha Diye Fulkopir Datta Chorchori.

name: Fulkopir Datta Mulo Begun Bori Ghonto (Cauliflower Stem, Radish, Brinjal & Bori Winter Medley)

steps.section: Cook fulkopir datta and radish together
steps.text: Temper mustard oil with panch phoron, add fulkopir datta, radish (mulo), and potatoes with ginger, cumin-coriander, turmeric, and salt; cover and braise until soft.
Add brinjal cubes and crushed fried bori, cook until thick and mushy (ghonto consistency), and balance with a pinch of sugar.

notes: Traditional winter vegetable ghonto combining cauliflower stems and white radish.

name: Fulkopir Datta Narkel Diye Chorchori (Niramish Cauliflower Stem & Grated Coconut Medley)

steps.section: Braise stems with ginger and panch phoron
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle panch phoron, red chilli, and bay leaf, add ginger paste, fulkopir datta, potatoes, and pumpkin with turmeric and salt, and cook covered until soft.

steps.section: Fold in fresh grated coconut and roasted cumin
steps.text: Stir in fresh grated coconut, roasted cumin powder, a pinch of sugar, and 1 tsp ghee; cook 3 minutes until fragrant.

notes: Traditional niramish (no-onion, no-garlic) cauliflower stem curry enriched with fresh grated coconut.

name: Fulkopir Datta Palong Shak Chorchori (Cauliflower Stem, Spinach & Winter Vegetable Chorchori)

steps.section: Cook fulkopir datta and root vegetables
steps.text: Fry bori and set aside. Temper oil with panch phoron and red chilli, add grated ginger, fulkopir datta, potato, and pumpkin with turmeric and salt; cook until nearly tender.

steps.section: Wilting spinach and finishing with bori
steps.text: Add brinjal and chopped palong shak, cook uncovered until the greens wilt and moisture reduces, and top with crushed fried bori.

notes: Nutrient-rich Bengali Palong-Fulkopir Datta Chorchori.

name: Fulkopir Datta Posto / Phulkopir Data Posto (Cauliflower Stem & Potato in Poppy Seed Paste)

steps.section: Sauté fulkopir datta and potato batons
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with kalo jeere and dry red chilli, add cauliflower stem batons and potato batons with salt, and stir-fry covered on low-medium flame until tender.
Add the ground poppy seed-green chilli paste with 3 tbsp water, toss gently for 3–4 minutes until the posto coats the stems, and finish with 1 tsp raw mustard oil.

notes: Nutty, creamy Bengali posto dish celebrating the sweet crunch of tender cauliflower stems.

name: Fulkopir Datta Shorshe / Shorshe Bata Diye Fulkopir Data (Cauliflower Stem in Mustard Gravy)

ingredients.name: Yellow Mustard Seeds Ground with Green Chillies

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with kalo jeere, add fulkopir datta and potato wedges with turmeric, salt, and a splash of water; cover and cook until tender.
Pour in strained or smooth mustard paste and slit green chillies, simmer for 3 minutes until thick and clinging, and drizzle raw mustard oil before serving with hot rice.

notes: Pungent shorshe-bata preparation that pairs wonderfully with steamed white rice.

name: Fulkopir Datta Shorshe Posto Chorchori (Cauliflower Stem in Mustard & Poppy Seed Paste)

ingredients.name: Yellow Mustard Seeds Ground Together with Green Chillies

steps.section: Braise fulkopir datta and potato batons
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with kalo jeere, add cauliflower stems and potatoes with turmeric and salt, and cook covered with a splash of water until tender.
Stir in the combined mustard-poppy seed paste, slit green chillies, and a pinch of sugar, simmer 3–4 minutes until thick, and finish with raw mustard oil.

notes: Balances the nutty creaminess of posto with the sharp zing of yellow mustard.

name: Fulkopir Datta Shutki Chorchori (Bengali Cauliflower Stem, Potato & Dried Fish Spicy Medley)

steps.section: Roast cleaned shutki with garlic and onion
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, fry cleaned shutki with crushed garlic and sliced onion until fragrant and golden.

steps.section: Braise fulkopir datta, potato, and brinjal
steps.text: Add fulkopir datta, potatoes, brinjal, turmeric, red chilli powder, and salt; cover and cook on low-medium heat until the stems are tender and coated in spicy garlic-shutki oil.

notes: Bold, garlicky Bangal-style shutki chorchori where fibrous cauliflower stems soak up the savory flavors.

name: Fulkopir Datta Sim Aloo Chorchori (Winter Cauliflower Stem, Flat Bean & New Potato Chorchori)

steps.section: Sauté winter vegetables with panch phoron
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle panch phoron, add fulkopir datta, new potatoes, and flat beans (sim) with turmeric and salt; cover and cook until tender.

steps.section: Simmer with tomato, mustard paste, and coriander
steps.text: Add tomato wedges, mustard paste, and green chillies, cook 4 minutes until coated, and finish with fresh winter coriander leaves.

notes: Quintessential Bengali winter afternoon chorchori with notun aloo, sim, and fulkopir datta.

name: Fulwadi (Crispy Spiced Coarse Besan, Curd, Sesame & Coriander Seed Namkeen Logs)

steps.section: Whisk spiced curd-oil batter with coarse besan
steps.text: Whisk sour curd, 3 tbsp hot oil, sugar, and baking soda until frothy, then fold in coarse besan, crushed coriander, fennel, sesame seeds, chilli powder, and salt into a thick batter.

steps.section: Pipe short logs into hot oil
steps.text: Pipe or press 1.5-inch cylindrical fingers into medium-hot oil.

steps.section: Fry until deep golden and porous-crunchy
steps.text: Fry on medium-low heat for 6–7 minutes until deep golden-brown, crisp on the outside, and airy inside.

notes: Crunchy, spice-studded savory gram-flour logs bursting with whole coriander and sesame seeds.

name: Gajak

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Gajar Beans Fry (Crispy Carrot & French Beans Stir-Fry with Panch Phoron)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle panch phoron and green chillies, add carrot and bean batons with turmeric and salt, and stir-fry on medium-high heat so they stay bright and crisp-tender.

steps.section: Finish with bhaja masala or crushed peanuts
steps.text: Toss with roasted bhaja masala or crushed peanuts and serve hot.

notes: Colorful, nutritious everyday vegetable fry.

name: Gajar Ka Halwa

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Gajar Laddoo (Slow-Simmered Grated Carrot, Khoya & Coconut Laddoo)

steps.text: Saute finely grated carrots in ghee on medium heat for 10–12 minutes until tender and moisture evaporates.

steps.section: Fold in sugar, khoya, and roll
steps.text: Add sugar and cook 5 minutes until glossy and dry; mix in grated khoya, coconut, cardamom, and cashews, cooking 4 minutes until mixture binds together. Cool slightly and shape into laddoos.

notes: All the richness of gajar halwa in convenient hand-rolled laddoos.

name: Gajar Paratha (Spiced Grated Red Carrot & Green Chilli Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Sauté grated carrots lightly with ginger, chillies, ajwain, and cumin for 3 minutes to remove raw water; mix in mashed potato, amchur, and salt.
Enclose carrot mixture in dough balls, seal edges, and roll out with light pressure.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee on both sides until crisp and golden brown. Serve with fresh dahi and pickle.

notes: A delicious winter specialty celebrating sweet seasonal red carrots.

name: Gajor Bharta (Spiced Carrot Mash)

steps.text: Peel and slice carrots, then steam or boil until fork-tender and drain.
Heat mustard oil, crackle nigella seeds, fry garlic, onion, and green chillies, and toss in the boiled carrots.
Mash into a coarse bharta, season with salt and fresh coriander, and serve warm.

notes: Nutritious, colourful side dish for lunch or dinner.

name: Garlic Bread

steps.text: Wash, chop or mash ingredients and mix with seasoning.
Spread garlic butter on bread and toast or bake until crisp.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

name: Garlic Butter Naan (Restaurant-Style Tawa Garlic Naan)

steps.text: Knead maida, yogurt, baking powder, baking soda, sugar, salt, and warm water into a soft dough; rest covered for 30-45 minutes.
Roll into teardrop shapes, press minced garlic, kalonji, and chopped coriander on top, and brush the underside with water.
Stick the wet side onto a hot iron tawa (not non-stick). Once bubbles rise, invert the tawa directly over the gas flame until charred spots appear, then brush with melted garlic butter.

notes: Sticking the water-brushed underside to a hot iron tawa replicates tandoor char at home.

name: Garlic Butter Prawn Pasta (Spaghetti Aglio e Olio with Prawns)

steps.text: Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente; reserve 1/2 cup starchy pasta cooking water before draining.
Heat olive oil and butter in a wide pan, gently toast sliced garlic and chilli flakes, and sear seasoned prawns for 2 minutes per side until pink.
Add drained pasta, reserved pasta water, lemon juice, and parsley; toss vigorously over medium heat until coated in a glossy garlic-butter glaze.

notes: Quick 25-minute weeknight dinner; top with grated Parmesan or extra herbs if desired.

name: Garlic Butter Toast

steps.text: Toast bread in a toaster or pan if making toast; leave soft for plain bread.
Spread garlic butter evenly over the bread and serve.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

name: Garlic Herb Potato Rösti (Swiss-Style Crisp Skillet Potato Cake)

steps.text: Toss coarsely grated parboiled potatoes gently with minced garlic, herbs, salt, and black pepper.
Melt butter/oil in a skillet, press the potato mixture into a flat round cake, and cook on medium-low heat for 8–9 minutes per side (using a plate to flip cleanly) until deeply golden and crisp.

notes: Brief parboiling gives a tender interior and crisp buttery exterior.

name: Garlic Herb Sooji Bread Sandwich (Tawa-Crisped Garlic-Butter Semolina Toast)

steps.text: Combine sooji, curd/milk, minced garlic, half the softened butter, oregano, chilli flakes, coriander, capsicum, corn, and salt; rest 8 minutes.
Spread on bread slices and toast topping-side down in butter on a low-medium tawa until golden and fragrant, then crisp the underside.

notes: Garlic-bread flavour with a crunchy toasted semolina crust.

name: Garlic Lachha Paratha (Crispy Garlic & Butter Layered Paratha)

steps.text: Mash softened butter with finely minced garlic, chopped coriander, and chilli flakes.
Roll dough thin, spread with garlic butter, dust with dry flour, pleat like a paper fan, coil into a spiral, and roll gently.
Cook on a hot tawa until golden and crisp, then gently scrunch to separate the garlicky flaky layers.

notes: Restaurant-style garlic lachha paratha great with paneer, chicken, or prawn curries.

name: Garlic Mushroom Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Garlic Pepper Masala Rice / Poondu Milagu Sadam (Chettinad Crushed Black Pepper, Roasted Garlic, Ghee & Curry Leaf Rice)

steps.section: Slow-roast garlic and lentils in gingelly oil
steps.text: Heat sesame oil and ghee in a kadai, crackle mustard seeds, chana dal, urad dal, cashews, dried red chillies, hing, and curry leaves. Add sliced garlic cloves and slow-roast until golden and fragrant.

steps.section: Bloom crushed black pepper and cumin
steps.text: Lower heat, stir in coarsely crushed black pepper, cumin, turmeric, and salt for 30 seconds so the pepper oils bloom without burning.
Toss in cooled rice gently until coated in the aromatic garlic-pepper tempering. Serve warm with appalam or onion raita.

notes: Warming South Indian comfort rice packed with roasted garlic and freshly cracked black pepper.

name: Garlic Potato Bharta

steps.text: Boil potatoes until tender, peel, and mash smoothly while warm.
Heat oil or ghee in a small pan and fry sliced garlic and chillies over low heat until golden and nutty.
Pour the golden garlic and infused oil over the mashed potatoes, add chopped onion, salt, and coriander, and mix thoroughly.

notes: Slowly frying the garlic until golden infuses the oil and removes raw pungency.

name: Garlic Prawns (Indo-Chinese Hot Garlic Sauce Prawns)

steps.text: Coat prawns lightly in cornflour, salt, and white pepper; sear in hot oil until crisp and golden, then set aside.
Sauté minced garlic and spring onion whites until golden and aromatic. Stir in chilli paste, ketchup, soy sauce, vinegar, and 1/2 cup water.
Thicken with cornflour slurry, return the prawns to the wok, and garnish with spring onion greens.

notes: Pairs wonderfully with vegetable or egg fried rice and hakka noodles.

name: Gatte ki Kadhi (Marwari Spiced Buttermilk Gravy with Soft Gram Flour Dumplings)

steps.section: Poach and slice soft besan gattas
steps.text: Knead 1 cup besan with 1 tbsp ghee, 2 tbsp curd, ajwain, turmeric, chilli powder, and salt into logs. Boil in water for 10 minutes, drain (saving the water), and slice into rounds.

Whisk 3 tbsp besan smoothly into sour buttermilk with turmeric, salt, and reserved poaching water. Simmer on medium-low heat for 12–15 minutes while stirring until creamy and raw besan aroma disappears.

steps.section: Add gattas and pour smoky ghee tadka
steps.text: Simmer the sliced gattas in the kadhi for 4 minutes, then pour a sizzling ghee tempering of mustard, cumin, methi dana, hing, curry leaves, and Kashmiri red chilli over the top.

notes: Combines the tangy comfort of Rajasthani kadhi with tender poached besan gattas.

name: Ghoti Gorom (Kolkata Street-Style Warm Spiced Chanachur & Raw Mango Mix)

ingredients.name: Raw Green Mango (Kacha Aam) or Cucumber

steps.section: Toss warm chanachur with raw mango and onion
steps.text: Toss warm jhuribhaja/chanachur with finely chopped onion, tart raw mango bits, green chillies, coriander, bitnoon, bhaja masala, lemon juice, and a few drops of mustard oil.

notes: Named after the brass vessel (ghoti) with hot charcoal inside that street vendors carry along the Ganges ghats and Maidan.

name: Ghugni Chaat (Kolkata Street-Style Spiced Yellow Pea Curry with Tamarind & Sev)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with bay leaf and cumin, sauté onions, ginger-garlic, tomatoes, potato cubes, and spices, then add boiled yellow peas with cooking liquid and simmer until thick and glossy.
Ladle hot ghugni into bowls and top with chopped raw onion, green chillies, coriander leaves, a drizzle of tangy tamarind water, bhaja masala, bitnoon, lemon juice, and crunchy sev.

notes: Served steaming hot across Kolkata streets, railway stations, and evening tea stalls.

name: Ghugni Muri Makha (Spiced Yellow Pea Ghugni & Crisp Puffed Rice)

steps.text: Pressure-cook soaked yellow peas with turmeric and salt for 3–4 whistles until tender. In a kadhai, heat mustard oil, saute half the onion, ginger, tomato, and cumin, then simmer with the cooked peas for 8 minutes.

steps.section: Top with crisp muri and garnishes
steps.text: Ladle hot ghugni into bowls, top generously with crisp puffed rice, raw chopped onion, green chillies, coriander, bhaja masala, black salt, and tamarind water.

notes: Kolkata street-style ghugni-muri tiffin; add muri just before eating for crunch.

name: Ginger Tea

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Goan Fish Roe Curry (Gabhache Hooman / Coconut Kokum Fish Egg Curry)

steps.text: Grind grated coconut, Kashmiri red chillies, coriander seeds, turmeric, garlic, and tamarind with water into a smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil, sauté chopped onion and green chillies until soft, add the ground coconut paste and water, and bring to a simmer.
Slide in the cleaned fish roe pieces and kokum petals, season with salt, and simmer gently for 7 minutes until the roe is cooked through.

notes: Authentic Goan Gabhache Hooman served with steamed parboiled rice.

name: Goan Prawn Curry (Ambotik / Coconut Kokum Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Kokum Petals or Raw Mango Slices

steps.text: Grind grated coconut, Kashmiri red chillies, coriander seeds, cumin, turmeric, garlic, and tamarind with warm water into a silky orange-red paste.
Heat coconut oil, fry chopped onion and slit green chillies until translucent, then pour in the ground masala paste and water; simmer for 6 minutes.
Add cleaned prawns, kokum petals, and salt; simmer gently for 5-6 minutes until the prawns curl and are cooked through.

notes: Authentic coastal Goan curry best enjoyed with steamed red or parboiled rice.

name: Gobi Aloo Hashbrowns (Crispy Grated Cauliflower & Potato Patties)

steps.text: Wring grated potato and grated cauliflower together in a cloth to remove moisture, then mix with cornflour, ginger, green chilli, cumin, turmeric, and salt.
Shape into flat discs and shallow-fry on a hot oiled tawa for 6 minutes per side until crisp and golden.

notes: Lighter vegetable-packed hashbrown variation using hand-grated cauliflower.

name: Gobi Bharta (Roasted Cauliflower / Phulkopi Mash)

steps.text: Wash cauliflower florets in warm salted water, steam or parboil until tender, and lightly char in a pan.
Heat mustard oil, sauté onion, ginger, garlic, and green chilli until golden, then cook chopped tomato and turmeric until soft.
Mash the cauliflower into the pan, season with salt, cook together for 3–4 minutes, and finish with fresh coriander.

notes: For a Bengali Phulkopi Bharta variation, skip the tomato and mash boiled florets directly with raw mustard oil, roasted red chilli, onion, and coriander.

name: Gobi Bhurji Roll (Finely Grated Spiced Cauliflower Keema Kathi Roll)

steps.text: Heat oil in a kadhai, crackle cumin seeds, and saute chopped onion, ginger, and green chilli until golden. Add chopped tomato, spices, and salt; cook 3 minutes, then fold in hand-grated cauliflower and peas and stir-fry briskly for 8 minutes until dry and crumbly.
Toss the gobi bhurji with chopped coriander and lemon juice. Spoon onto warm tawa parathas and roll tightly.

notes: Box-grating cauliflower creates a quick keema-like texture with zero blender or food processor.

name: Gobi Cheese Roll (Melted Cheese & Spiced Cauliflower Frankie Roll)

steps.text: Saute chopped onion and garlic in butter/oil until soft, add chopped cauliflower, chilli powder, turmeric, frankie masala, and salt, and cook 10–12 minutes until tender and dry.

steps.section: Melt cheese on tawa and roll
steps.text: Warm each paratha on a tawa, spread the hot gobi filling down the center, scatter grated cheese generously so it melts from the heat, add cabbage, onion, and lemon juice, and roll up.

notes: Hot cauliflower filling melts the hand-grated cheese naturally inside the roll.

name: Gobi Corn Roll (Spiced Cauliflower & Sweet Corn Masala Wrap)

steps.text: Heat butter or oil in a pan and stir-fry small cauliflower florets with salt and pepper for 8 minutes until tender-crisp. Add capsicum, boiled sweet corn, cumin, chaat masala, and oregano; toss 3 minutes.
Finish with lemon juice and chopped coriander, spoon onto warm tawa parathas, and roll tightly.

notes: Mild, kid-friendly wrap with natural sweetness from corn and crunch from cauliflower.

name: Gobi Kebab Roll (Pan-Seared Grated Cauliflower Tikki Kathi Roll)

steps.text: Squeeze excess moisture from grated cauliflower by hand, then mix with mashed potato, dry-roasted besan, ginger, green chilli, coriander, spices, and salt. Shape into 4 oblong kebabs and pan-sear on an oiled tawa for 8 minutes until crisp and brown on all sides.
Place 2 hot gobi kebabs on each warm paratha, top with onion rings and lemon juice, and roll firmly.

notes: Hand-squeezing the grated cauliflower keeps the kebab mixture firm without needing a grinder.

name: Gobi Manchurian Roll (Street-Style Cauliflower Manchurian Frankie)

steps.text: Coat parboiled cauliflower florets in a thick batter of cornflour, maida, salt, and pepper, then fry in hot oil until crisp.

steps.section: Glaze in Manchurian sauce and roll
steps.text: Saute minced garlic, ginger, and green chilli in 1 tbsp oil; add soy sauce, ketchup, chilli sauce, vinegar, and 2 tbsp water. Toss in fried gobi until coated in a thick glaze, then roll inside warm parathas with shredded cabbage and spring onion.

notes: Keep the Manchurian glaze thick rather than soupy so the wrap holds cleanly.

name: Gobi Matar Roll (Spiced Cauliflower & Green Peas Masala Paratha Roll)

steps.text: Crackle cumin seeds in hot oil, saute ginger and green chilli, and add cauliflower florets, green peas, turmeric, cumin, coriander, and salt. Cover and cook 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and dry.
Sprinkle garam masala and amchur over the hot filling, spoon onto warm parathas with sliced onion and lemon juice, and roll up.

notes: Great winter tiffin roll using fresh seasonal phulkopi and motorshuti.

name: Gobi Paneer Roll (Spiced Cauliflower & Crumbled Paneer Kathi Roll)

steps.text: Roast chopped cauliflower in hot oil with ginger, garlic, turmeric, chilli, and salt for 8 minutes. Add capsicum, onion, paneer, garam masala, and kasuri methi; saute 4 minutes until aromatic and lightly seared.
Warm parathas on a tawa, fill with the gobi-paneer mixture, sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice, and roll tightly.

notes: Combining roasted cauliflower with paneer adds protein while keeping the roll hearty.

name: Gobi Paratha

steps.text: Mix flour and salt; add water gradually and knead to a soft dough. Rest covered.
Divide into portions and roll or shape according to the bread style.
Cook on a hot tawa or fry as appropriate, turning until cooked and golden.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Gobi Roll (Kolkata Street-Style Spiced Cauliflower Kathi Roll)

steps.text: Heat oil in a wide pan or tawa, add cauliflower florets, grated ginger, garlic, turmeric, chilli powder, cumin, coriander, and salt. Roast on medium-high heat for 12 minutes, tossing often, until tender inside with crisp charred edges.

steps.section: Wrap in flaky Kolkata laccha paratha
steps.text: Toast laccha parathas on a hot tawa until crisp and flaky. Spoon the roasted spiced gobi down the center, top with raw sliced onion, green chillies, chaat masala, black salt, and lemon juice, and roll tightly in paper.

notes: Pure vegetarian Kolkata street-style kathi roll; dry high-heat roasting gives authentic smoky flavour.

name: Gobi Tikka Roll (Tawa-Roasted Spiced Cauliflower & Curd Kathi Roll)

steps.text: Whisk thick curd, roasted besan, mustard oil, ginger, garlic, spices, kasuri methi, and salt in a bowl. Coat parboiled cauliflower florets and pan-roast on a hot oiled tawa for 10–12 minutes until charred and smoky.
Arrange hot gobi tikka pieces down the middle of crisp warm parathas, top with onion rings and fresh lemon juice, and roll up.

notes: Roasted besan helps the spiced curd marinade cling to the cauliflower on a flat tawa.

name: Gobindobhog Rice

steps.text: Wash rice until the water runs mostly clear; soak briefly if appropriate.
Heat ghee or oil, add spices and vegetables if using, and stir until fragrant.
Add rice and measured water, cover and cook until tender. Rest briefly before serving.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Godhuma Bonda / Whole Wheat Flour Mysore Bonda (Healthy Atta, Rice Flour, Sour Curd & Onion-Herb Fritters)

steps.section: Whip atta, rice flour, and curd batter
steps.text: Combine whole wheat flour, rice flour, sour curd, cumin, ajwain, salt, and 1/3 cup water. Beat vigorously by hand for 4–5 minutes to aerate, then rest covered for 20 minutes.
Stir in finely chopped onion, grated ginger, green chillies, curry leaves, coriander, and baking soda.
Drop round portions into medium-hot oil with wet fingers and fry on medium heat until deep golden and cooked through.

notes: Maida-free whole-wheat variation of Mysore Bonda with a nutty aroma and light, airy crumb.

name: Gokul Pithe

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Golda Chingri Malaikari (Jumbo River Prawn Coconut Milk Curry)

steps.text: Devein jumbo golda prawns while keeping the head and tail shell intact for flavor. Rub with salt and turmeric, sear lightly in mustard oil for 2 minutes, and remove.
Temper oil with bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Cook onion and ginger paste with turmeric and Kashmiri chilli powder until oil separates.
Pour in coconut milk and a splash of warm water, add prawns, slit green chillies, salt, and a pinch of sugar. Simmer covered for 8 minutes and finish with ghee and garam masala.

notes: Keeping the head and tail shell intact infuses the coconut milk gravy with deep scampi flavor.

name: Golden Fried Prawns (Crispy Batter-Fried Prawns)

steps.text: Make a shallow slit along the back of each prawn to butterfly it flat, pat dry, and season with salt, white pepper, and ginger-garlic juice.
Whisk flour, cornflour, baking powder, salt, 1 tsp oil, and ice-cold water into a smooth batter.
Hold each prawn by the tail, dip into the batter, and deep-fry in medium-hot oil for 3 minutes until puffed, golden, and crisp.

notes: Serve hot with sweet chilli dipping sauce or hot garlic sauce.

name: Gond ke Laddoo (Edible Gum, Whole Wheat, Nuts & Jaggery Winter Laddoo)

steps.section: Puff gond and roast wheat flour
steps.text: Fry gond crystals in 3 tbsp hot ghee in small batches on low-medium heat until they puff up crisp; drain and crush coarsely with the flat bottom of a steel katori/bowl. In remaining ghee, slow-roast atta for 12–14 minutes until golden and fragrant.
Mix crushed puffed gond, chopped nuts, sonth, and cardamom into the hot roasted atta. Turn off heat, stir in grated jaggery until melted, and roll into round laddoos while warm.

notes: Crushing puffed gond with a steel katori gives classic crunchy pockets without a mixer.

name: Gondhoraj Chicken Momo (Kolkata-Style Aromatic Gondhoraj Lime Steamed Chicken Dumplings)

steps.text: Mix minced chicken with grated Gondhoraj zest, juice, shredded lime leaves, finely chopped onion, ginger, green chilli, black pepper, softened butter, and salt.
Fill thin maida discs, pleat tightly, and steam for 14–15 minutes over boiling water (place a Gondhoraj leaf in the steaming water for extra aroma).

notes: Kolkata favourite; grate only the green outer zest of Gondhoraj lime to avoid bitterness.

name: Gondhoraj Lebu Sharbat

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Gongura Royyalu (Andhra Sorrel Leaves & Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Sauté gongura leaves with 2 green chillies and a little oil until wilted and soft, then mash into a coarse tangy paste.
Heat oil, temper with mustard, fenugreek, crushed garlic, dry red chillies, and curry leaves. Fry chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste, then cook prawns with spice powders.
Stir in the mashed gongura paste and a splash of water; simmer for 6 minutes until oil floats to the top.

notes: Signature Andhra delicacy pairing the natural tang of sorrel leaves with sweet, juicy prawns.

name: Goyna Bori Bhaja (Crispy Fried Medinipur Ornamental Filigree Lentil Dumplings with Poppy Seeds)

ingredients.name: Medinipur Goyna Bori / Nakshi Bori (Ornamental Poppy-crusted Urad Dal Dumplings)
Mustard Oil or Ghee-mustard Oil Blend

steps.text: Heat mustard oil (or half mustard oil and half gama/cow ghee) in a flat pan until hot, then lower the flame so the delicate filigree patterns do not scorch.

steps.section: Baste and fry Goyna Bori gently
steps.text: Slide 2-3 Goyna Bori in at a time, spoon warm oil over the top, and flip gently after 45 seconds until pale golden and crisp; drain on paper towels.

notes: A GI-tagged culinary art form from Purba and Paschim Medinipur, shaped like traditional Bengali jewelry and eaten whole as a crunchy accompaniment to steamed rice and dal.

name: Green Chilli & Coriander Masala Hashbrowns (Desi Tawa Aloo Rösti)

steps.text: Combine well-dried grated potatoes with green chillies, coriander, cornflour, amchur, garam masala, and salt.
Cook flat patties in hot oil on a tawa for 6–7 minutes per side until crisp and speckled golden.

notes: Bright, tangy street-style flavours; serve with tomato ketchup or curd.

name: Green Chilli Omelette

steps.text: Beat eggs with salt, pepper and optional milk or water; prepare the listed variation ingredients.
Heat butter or oil in a pan. Add vegetables first if needed, pour in eggs and cook gently; fold when set.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Grilled Lemon Herb Prawns

steps.text: Toss prawns with olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, minced garlic, herbs, paprika, black pepper, and salt; marinate for 10-15 minutes.
Thread onto skewers or place on a hot grill pan and sear for 2-3 minutes per side until lightly charred and opaque.
Sprinkle with fresh parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

notes: High-protein, low-oil grilled seafood dish great for light dinners or salads.

name: Grilled Tomato Cheese Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and slice vegetables or prepare the listed filling.
Spread butter or condiment on bread, add filling and season lightly. Serve fresh or grill until crisp.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

name: Gujarati Fafda (Crisp Carom-Spiced Gram Flour Strips with Fried Green Chillies)

steps.section: Knead elastic besan dough with soda-oil water
steps.text: Dissolve salt, hing, and baking soda in warm water with 2 tbsp oil, add to besan, turmeric, and ajwain, and knead for 8 minutes into a smooth, stretchy dough.

steps.section: Pull thin strips on a wooden board with the heel of your palm
steps.text: Place a small log of dough on a greased wooden board, press with the base of your palm and slide forward in one stroke to form a thin ribbon strip, then lift off with a flat knife.

steps.section: Fry on medium-low flame with salted green chillies
steps.text: Fry the fafda strips on medium-low heat until crisp without browning, and serve with fried salted green chillies and jalebi.

notes: Iconic crunchy gram-flour strips traditionally paired with hot jalebi and fried green chillies.

name: Gujarati Kadhi (Sweet-Tangy Ginger, Green Chilli & Curry Leaf Tempered Buttermilk-Besan Gravy)

steps.text: Blend sour curd, besan, ginger-green chilli paste, jaggery, salt, and 2.5 cups water using a hand churner (mathani) until completely smooth.
Bring the mixture to a gentle boil over medium heat while stirring so it does not curdle, then simmer for 12–15 minutes until lightly thickened and glossy.
Heat ghee in a tadka pan, crackle mustard, cumin, fenugreek seeds, cloves, cinnamon, dried red chillies, curry leaves, and hing. Pour into the simmering kadhi and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Traditionally kept pale ivory-white (without turmeric) to showcase the delicate balance of sour curd, sweet jaggery, and green chilli heat.

name: Gujarati Khandvi / Dahivadi / Suralichi Vadi (Silky Rolled Gram Flour & Buttermilk Pinwheels with Coconut & Mustard Tadka)

ingredients.name: Sour Curd (1 Cup) Whisked with Water

steps.section: Whisk and slow-cook smooth besan-buttermilk paste
steps.text: Whisk sifted besan with sour buttermilk, ginger-chilli paste, turmeric, hing, and salt, then strain into a heavy non-stick pan. Cook over medium-low heat while stirring continuously for 10–12 minutes until thick, glossy, and a small dab spread on a plate peels off cleanly when cool.

steps.section: Spread paper-thin and roll into pinwheels
steps.text: Working quickly while hot, spread the cooked paste in paper-thin layers across the back of greased steel thalis or a marble slab using a flat spatula. Cool 5 minutes, sprinkle a little coconut and coriander, slice into 2-inch ribbons, and roll each strip into tight, delicate cylinders.
Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, white sesame seeds, curry leaves, and slit green chillies, and spoon over the arranged khandvi rolls. Garnish with fresh grated coconut and coriander.

notes: Maintaining a strict 1:3 ratio of besan to sour buttermilk liquid guarantees melt-in-the-mouth rolls that peel effortlessly.

name: Gujarati Papad Churi / Marwari Papad Churi (Crushed Roasted Papad Tossed with Ghee, Sev, Onion, Coriander & Chaat Masala)

ingredients.name: Crispy Nylon Sev or Bikaneri Bhujia

steps.section: Roast and crush papads into flaky shards
steps.text: Roast papads over an open flame or tawa until crisp and blistered, cool for 1 minute, and crush by hand in a mixing bowl into bite-sized flakes.

steps.section: Toss with warm ghee and spices
steps.text: Drizzle warm melted desi ghee over the crushed papad and toss with Kashmiri red chilli powder, roasted cumin powder, chaat masala, and black salt so the spices cling to every shard.

steps.section: Fold in onions, bhujia, and lemon
steps.text: Add finely chopped onion, tomato, green chillies, fresh coriander, crunchy bhujia/sev, and lemon juice right before serving.

notes: Signature Gujarati/Marwari restaurant accompaniment and crunchy evening snack.

name: Gujarati Vaghareli Khichdi (Spiced Tuvar-Moong Dal Khichdi with Garlic-Curry Leaf Tempering)

ingredients.name: Garlic with Red Chilli Powder (Lasan Ni Chutney Paste)

steps.text: Heat peanut oil and ghee in a pressure cooker. Crackle mustard and cumin seeds, hing, curry leaves, cinnamon, and cloves. Add crushed chilli-garlic paste and saute for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add diced potatoes, carrots, green peas, turmeric, and dhana jeeru. Stir in washed rice and dals, coating well in the spiced oil.
Add 4 cups warm water and salt. Pressure-cook for 3 whistles until soft and comforting. Top with fresh coriander and a dollop of ghee; serve with Gujarati Kadhi.

notes: Kathiawadi evening staple renowned for its fiery garlic-chilli vaghar (tempering) and pairing with sweet-tangy Gujarati kadhi.

name: Gujiya / Mawa Karanji (Crispy Flaky Maida Dumplings Stuffed with Roasted Khoya, Coconut & Nuts)

steps.text: Roast mawa until fragrant and lightly pink. Cool completely, then blend with toasted coconut, powdered sugar, chironji, chopped cashews, raisins, and cardamom powder.

Rub 4 tbsp ghee into maida until it holds shape, knead with cold water into a stiff dough. Roll into small discs, place stuffing in center, moisten edges with water, fold into half-moons, and flute the edges with a gujiya mould or fork.
Slide into medium-hot ghee and fry on low flame for 10-12 minutes until blister-free, crisp, and pale golden.

notes: The quintessential festive Holi and Diwali sweet dumpling celebrated across North India and Maharashtra.

name: Gulab Jamun

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Gulgule / Pua (Traditional Soft Sweet Jaggery & Fennel Fritters)

steps.text: Melt jaggery in warm water and strain out impurities. Whisk the jaggery syrup into whole wheat flour with crushed fennel seeds and cardamom into a thick, dropping-consistency batter; rest 15 minutes.
Heat oil on medium flame. Scoop spoonfuls or hand dollops of batter into the hot oil; they will puff up into round balls.
Fry gently, turning regularly until the exterior is crisp and dark caramel brown and the interior is soft and spongy. Drain and serve warm.

notes: A nostalgic rainy-day and festive North Indian sweet fritter with rich jaggery-fennel flavor.

name: Gundruk Sadeko (Nepali Fermented Leaf & Mustard Oil Salad)

steps.text: Soak dried gundruk in warm water for 10 minutes until soft, drain and squeeze out all excess moisture thoroughly, and chop coarsely.
In a bowl, mix squeezed gundruk with sliced onion, tomato, crushed garlic, minced ginger, green chillies, cilantro, roasted cumin, timur, and salt.
Drizzle generously with raw mustard oil and lemon juice, massage gently with hands to infuse flavors, and serve as an earthy, tangy side dish with dal-bhat.

notes: Nepal's national dish ingredient: naturally sour fermented greens tossed with raw mustard oil and pungent Himalayan timur.

name: Gur Paratha / Jaggery Paratha (Winter Jaggery, Fennel & Ghee Stuffed Sweet Paratha)

steps.text: Combine grated jaggery with crushed fennel seeds, cardamom powder, and sesame seeds.

steps.section: Stuff into dough and seal carefully
steps.text: Place jaggery mixture inside a rolled dough circle, pinch all edges tightly so sugar does not leak out, and roll gently.

steps.section: Roast with desi ghee on low flame
steps.text: Cook on low flame with generous ghee until the paratha puffs and the jaggery inside turns into molten caramel. Serve warm.

notes: A comforting Punjabi winter sweet flatbread that warms the body.

name: Gurer Kalakand (Nolen Gur Infused Granular Bengali Milk Cake)

ingredients.name: Patali Gur / Nolen Gur (Date Palm Jaggery)

steps.text: Combine crumbled chhena, milk, and condensed milk in a heavy pan and cook on medium flame, stirring until thick and grainy.
Lower the flame, add grated Nolen Gur and cardamom powder, and cook for 5–6 minutes until the mixture turns caramel-hued and leaves the pan sides.

steps.section: Set in greased tray and slice into squares
steps.text: Spread into a ghee-lined tray, scatter chopped pistachios on top, cool for 1 hour, and cut into squares.

notes: Moist, granular Bengali winter milk cake perfumed with smoky date-palm jaggery.

name: Gurer Narkel Naru (Bengali Date Palm Jaggery & Grated Coconut Ladoo)

ingredients.name: Patali Gur or Sugarcane Jaggery (Akher Gur)

steps.section: Knead grated coconut and jaggery together
steps.text: Massage freshly grated coconut and crushed jaggery together in a heavy pan for 5 minutes until juicy.

steps.section: Cook over low heat until sticky (pak)
steps.text: Cook on low flame, stirring continuously for 15–18 minutes until the moisture evaporates and the coconut-jaggery mixture turns glossy and sticky.

steps.section: Roll warm mixture into smooth naru balls
steps.text: Stir in cardamom powder, grease palms with ghee, and quickly roll warm spoonfuls into smooth bite-sized balls.

notes: Quintessential Lakshmi Puja and Bijoya Dashami home-made Bengali coconut sweet.

name: Hara Bhara Kebab

steps.text: Wash, chop or mash ingredients and mix with seasoning.
Mash the cooked greens, peas and potato with spices, shape patties and shallow-fry.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

name: Hara Bhara Spinach & Pea Sooji Sandwich (No-Bread Palak-Matar Semolina Tawa Sandwich)

steps.section: Fold palak and mashed peas into sooji batter
steps.text: Whisk sooji, curd, salt, and 1/2 cup water; rest 10 minutes. Fold in finely chopped spinach, fork-mashed peas, ginger, green chilli, chaat masala, and baking soda.

steps.section: Cook covered and slice into sandwiches
steps.text: Pour into a greased pan or sandwich maker, cook covered on low heat 4–5 minutes per side until crisp green-gold, and cut into triangles.

notes: Iron-rich green breakfast sandwich with zero bread or blender.

name: Harey Chane O Palang Shaker Khichuri / Palak Dal Khichdi (Spinach, Green Chickpea & Garlic-Ghee Khichdi)

ingredients.name: Green Peas or Tender Green Chickpeas (Hara Chana)

steps.section: Pressure-cook rice, moong dal, and green peas
steps.text: Wash rice and moong dal, then pressure-cook with green peas/hara chana, 4 cups water, turmeric, and salt for 3 whistles until soft.

steps.section: Saute aromatics and fold spinach puree
steps.text: Heat 1.5 tbsp ghee in a pan, saute chopped onions, ginger, and tomatoes until soft. Add vibrant blanched spinach puree and cook for 3 minutes, then fold in the cooked khichdi and garam masala.
Heat remaining 1.5 tbsp ghee, fry sliced garlic, cumin seeds, hing, and whole dry red chillies until crisp and golden, and pour over the emerald-green Palak Khichdi.

notes: Iron-rich, vibrant emerald-green spinach khichdi elevated with smoky browned garlic flakes.

name: Hariyali Paneer Tikka (Mint, Coriander & Hung-Curd Marinated Grilled Paneer Skewers)

ingredients.name: Green Chillies (3) Ground to a Paste

steps.section: Marinate paneer and vegetables in mint-coriander hung curd
steps.text: Whisk hung curd, roasted besan, mint-coriander-green chilli paste, ginger-garlic paste, roasted cumin, chaat masala, black salt, lemon juice, and 1 tbsp smoky mustard oil; coat paneer, capsicum, and onions and rest 15 minutes.

steps.section: Skewer and char-roast on tawa or oven
steps.text: Thread onto skewers and grill in a hot oven or sear on a cast-iron tawa basting with butter until charred spots appear; dust with chaat masala and lemon juice.

notes: Fresh mint, coriander, and black salt give Hariyali Paneer Tikka a zesty herbal punch.

name: Hashbrown Toast / Golden Rectangular Potato Patties (Tawa-Crisped)

ingredients.name: Onion Powder or Finely Grated Onion

steps.text: Steam or boil grated potatoes briefly for 3 minutes, drain and press dry, then mix with cornflour, grated onion, salt, and pepper. Press into 4 neat rectangular patties by hand.
Shallow-fry in hot oil for 5–6 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp outside, tender inside.

notes: Classic fast-food style rectangular hashbrown patties made entirely on the stovetop without freezing.

steps.text: Toss grated sweet potato with cornflour, spring onion, oregano, black pepper, and salt.
Cook thin patties in a lightly oiled skillet on medium-low heat for 5–6 minutes per side until caramelised and crisp.

notes: Cook on medium-low heat so the natural sugars caramelise without scorching.

name: Hinger Aloor Torkari (Kolkata Club Kachori Style Asafoetida Potato Curry)

steps.section: Bloom hing and spices in oil
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle dry red chilli and panch phoron/cumin, and add hing and ginger-green chilli paste so the aroma blooms.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, coriander, and red chilli powder; cook until soft and pulpy.
Add boiled cubed/crushed potatoes and warm water; simmer for 8-10 minutes until thick. Finish with bhaja masala, coriander leaves, and a topping of crispy sev.

notes: Famous Bura Bazar / Kolkata morning breakfast potato curry served with Hinger Kochuri or Club Kachori.

name: Hinger Kochuri (Kolkata Club Kachori Style Asafoetida Puri)

steps.text: Sauté ground urad dal (or sattu) in oil with a generous dose of hing, ginger-green chilli paste, roasted fennel-cumin powder, salt, and a pinch of sugar until dry.
Knead maida and sooji with melted ghee, salt, and water. Stuff small dough balls with the hing mixture and roll into crisp puris.
Fry in medium-hot oil until golden and crisp. Serve with spicy street-style potato curry (aloor torkari).

notes: Famous North Kolkata sweet-shop morning breakfast kochuri.

name: Homemade Rice Flour Papad / Chawal ke Khichiya Papad (Manual Steamed Rice Flour, Cumin & Green Chilli Sun-Dried Crisps)

ingredients.name: Green Chillies or Red Chilli Flakes

steps.section: Boil spiced water and steam rice flour dough (khichiya)
steps.text: Bring 2 cups water to a rolling boil with cumin seeds, ajwain, minced green chillies/chilli flakes, papad khar/baking soda, and salt. Stir in 1 cup rice flour continuously on low heat until it forms a lump-free mass, then cover and steam on lowest flame for 6–7 minutes.

steps.section: Knead warm dough and press between greased sheets
steps.text: Transfer the warm dough to a greased plate, knead for 5 minutes with a little oil until smooth and elastic, roll into lemon-sized balls, and press each ball flat between two oiled plastic sheets using a flat-bottomed steel bowl or rolling pin.
Dry the thin discs in bright sunlight for 1–2 days until translucent and brittle. Store in an airtight jar and deep-fry in hot oil for 3 seconds whenever needed—they puff up to triple their size.

notes: Manual stovetop khichiya method requiring only a pot, greased sheet, and flat bowl—zero blender or special press needed.

name: Homestyle Masala Rice / Veg Masala Chawal (One-Pot Onion, Tomato, Carrot, Peas & Garam Masala Spiced Basmati Rice)

steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker or kadai, crackle cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, and cardamom, then saute onion, grated ginger, garlic, and green chillies until golden. Add chopped tomato and ground spices and cook until soft.

steps.section: Fold in vegetables and soaked rice
steps.text: Toss diced carrot, green peas, potato, and drained basmati rice into the masala for 2 minutes.
Add 2.75 cups hot water and salt; pressure cook for 1–2 whistles (or simmer covered 12–15 minutes), rest 5 minutes, fluff with fresh coriander, and serve with yogurt or cucumber salad.

notes: Everyday comfort one-pot masala rice built for quick manual prep with a knife, grater, and pressure cooker.

name: Honey Butter Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and slice vegetables or prepare the listed filling.
Spread butter or condiment on bread, add filling and season lightly. Serve fresh or grill until crisp.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

name: Hong Kong Style Veg Chowmin / Chowmein (Spicy Star-Anise, Chilli & Roasted Cashew Noodles)

steps.section: Fry cashews and dry red chillies
steps.text: Heat oil in a wok, fry whole dry red chillies and cashew nuts until golden, then add minced garlic and ginger.

steps.section: Stir-fry colorful vegetables on high flame
steps.text: Add carrots, baby corn, bell peppers, and cabbage and stir-fry on high heat for 3 minutes.

steps.section: Toss noodles in sweet-spicy Hong Kong glaze
steps.text: Add boiled chowmin, soy sauce, chilli paste, ketchup, vinegar, and a tiny pinch of Chinese five-spice; toss on high flame and top with spring onions.

notes: Restaurant-style Hong Kong Veg Chowmin studded with roasted cashews and bell peppers.

name: Hong Kong Style Veg Fried Rice (Spicy Chilli-Garlic, Cashew, Star-Anise & Bell Pepper Fried Rice)

steps.section: Toast cashews and dry red chillies in garlic oil
steps.text: Fry cashews, dry red chillies, minced garlic, and ginger in hot oil for 1 minute until fragrant.
Toss in diced carrots, beans, baby corn, sweet corn, and bell peppers and stir-fry on high flame for 3 minutes.

steps.section: Coat chilled rice in Hong Kong spice glaze
steps.text: Add chilled rice, soy sauce, red chilli paste, ketchup, vinegar, and a pinch of five-spice; toss on high heat for 3 minutes and garnish with spring onion greens.

notes: Vibrant, nutty, and mildly sweet-spicy Hong Kong Style Veg Fried Rice.

name: Hyderabadi Bagara Rice / Baghara Chawal (Shahi Jeera, Caramelized Onion, Mint & Ghee Tempered Spiced Rice)

steps.section: Temper shahi jeera and brown onions
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot, crackle shahi jeera, bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves, and green cardamom, then saute sliced onions until golden brown.

steps.section: Saute ginger-garlic, chillies, and fresh herbs
steps.text: Add ginger-garlic paste and slit green chillies; saute 2 minutes, then stir in torn mint and coriander leaves until aromatic.
Add 3.5 cups hot water and salt, bring to a boil, fold in drained basmati rice, cover tightly, and simmer on low flame for 12–14 minutes until every grain is separate and fragrant.

notes: Hyderabadi and Telangana staple spiced rice served alongside Mirchi ka Salan, Baghara Baingan, or Dalcha.

name: Hyderabadi Khatti Dal Khichdi / Keema Khichdi (Nizami Saffron, Mint & Chana-Masoor Dal Pilaf Khichdi)

ingredients.name: Whole Spices (Shahi Jeera, Cinnamon, Cardamom, Cloves, Bay Leaf)

steps.section: Fry birista onions and whole spices
steps.text: Heat ghee in a heavy pot, temper shahi jeera, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and bay leaf. Add sliced onions and fry until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, slit green chillies, fresh mint, and coriander. Add drained Basmati rice and soaked lentils, sauteing gently for 3 minutes.
Add 3.5 cups hot water and salt. Bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on low dum heat for 12 minutes. Traditionally served with tangy tamarind Khatta or Til ka Khatta.

notes: Classic Hyderabadi breakfast and brunch specialty scented with mint, shahi jeera, and caramelized onions.

name: Hyderabadi Paneer (Cottage Cheese in Tangy Mint, Coriander, Fried Onion & Yogurt Green Gravy)

steps.section: Blend birista, mint, coriander, cashews and yogurt into green paste
steps.text: Sear paneer pieces until golden; blend crispy fried onions, fresh coriander, mint leaves, green chillies, soaked cashews, and yogurt into a smooth emerald-green paste.

steps.section: Braise green masala with whole spices and add paneer
steps.text: Temper oil-ghee with shahi jeera, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon, sauté ginger-garlic paste, add the green birista-herb-yogurt paste and spices, cook until oil separates, and simmer with paneer for 4 minutes.

notes: Caramelized fried onions blended with fresh mint and coriander create a uniquely rich, tangy green gravy.

name: Iced Americano

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.
