name: Idli

steps.text: Wash, chop and measure the ingredients. Soak or ferment the base if the recipe requires it.
Heat oil, add mustard or cumin seeds, onion, chilli and vegetables.
Add the main ingredient and the required water or batter; cook until tender and serve hot.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Ilish Begun Bori Jhol (Hilsa Fish, Eggplant & Fried Lentil Dumpling Kalo-Jeere Light Broth)

steps.section: Fry bori, eggplant and lightly sear Hilsa
steps.text: In smoking mustard oil, fry the bori until golden-red and remove; lightly pan-fry the eggplant wedges and lightly sear the Hilsa steaks for 1 minute per side.

Temper the remaining ilish-scented mustard oil with kalo jeere and slit green chillies, add turmeric, chilli powder, and 1.5 cups warm water; once boiling, add Hilsa, fried bori, and eggplant and simmer 5 minutes.

notes: No onion, garlic, or heavy spices are used so the delicate aroma of Hilsa and fried bori shines through.

name: Ilish Macher Dimer Bora (Hilsa Fish Egg Fritters)

steps.text: Wash the Hilsa roe lobes very gently without breaking the sac, pat dry, and rub evenly with salt, turmeric, and a pinch of red chilli powder.
Heat mustard oil in a skillet until lightly smoking, lower the flame, and fry the Hilsa roe with slit green chillies for 4-5 minutes per side covered until golden and firm.

steps.section: Slice and serve with fragrant oil
steps.text: Cut into thick slices and serve immediately over steaming hot plain rice drizzled with the aromatic Hilsa-infused frying oil.

notes: Keep spices minimal for Hilsa roe so its prized, buttery monsoon flavor takes center stage.

name: Ilish Macher Dimer Jhal (Hilsa Fish Roe Mustard-Tomato Gravy)

steps.text: Rub Hilsa roe lobes gently with salt and turmeric and sear lightly in hot mustard oil for 2 minutes per side.
Temper the Hilsa-scented oil with nigella seeds and green chillies, sauté grated tomato and turmeric, and stir in mustard paste with warm water.
Return the Hilsa roe lobes to the pan, simmer covered for 5-6 minutes, and finish with a drizzle of raw mustard oil.

notes: Delicate monsoon Hilsa roe curry best enjoyed with plain steamed rice.

name: Ilish Macher Dimer Tok (Hilsa Roe in Tangy Tamarind Gravy)

steps.text: Season Hilsa roe with salt and turmeric, shallow-fry in mustard oil for 3 minutes per side, and slice into thick pieces.
Temper oil with panch phoron and dry red chilli, pour in tamarind water, turmeric, salt, mustard paste, and jaggery, and boil for 4 minutes.
Add the fried Hilsa roe slices and simmer gently for 4 minutes.

notes: Traditional East Bengali (Bangal) heirloom recipe pairing rich Hilsa roe with tangy tamarind.

name: Ilish Macher Khichuri (Bengali Monsoon Hilsa Fish & Mustard Oil Khichuri)

ingredients.name: Pungent Mustard Oil (Plus Oil From Frying Ilish)

steps.section: Lightly sear Ilish in mustard oil
steps.text: Rub Hilsa steaks with salt and turmeric. Sear very lightly (60 seconds per side) in smoking mustard oil to release the prized Ilish tel (aromatic Hilsa oil), then remove fish carefully.

In the remaining Hilsa mustard oil, temper kalo jeere (nigella seeds) and green chillies. Add ginger paste, turmeric, washed Gobindobhog rice, and lentils. Stir-fry for 3 minutes, add 4 cups hot water, and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Gently place the seared Hilsa steaks and any reserved fish oil on top of the nearly-cooked khichuri, add whole slit green chillies, cover tightly, and steam on low heat for 6-7 minutes.

notes: The ultimate Bengali monsoon celebration: fragrant Gobindobhog khichuri infused with pungent mustard oil and delicate Hilsa roe/steaks.

name: Ilish Macher Matha Diye Khichuri (Bengali Hilsa Fish Head & Roasted Moong Dal Khichuri)

steps.text: Coat Hilsa fish heads with turmeric and salt, fry in hot mustard oil until crisp and golden brown, and crush them lightly with a spatula into savory chunks.
In the same aromatic fish oil, temper bay leaves, dry red chillies, and panch phoron. Add ginger paste, cumin, turmeric, roasted moong dal, and Gobindobhog rice. Pour 4.5 cups hot water and simmer.

steps.section: Fold crushed fish heads and vegetables
steps.text: Add the crushed fried Hilsa heads, fried potato and pumpkin cubes, and slit green chillies. Simmer covered for 10 minutes until the fish head flavors permeate every spoonful.

notes: Nothing goes to waste in a Bengali kitchen; crispy Hilsa heads impart deep coastal umami to roasted moong dal khichuri.

name: Imarti

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Indian-Style Besan Aloo Hashbrowns (Gram-Flour Bound Grated Potato Pancakes)

steps.text: Mix dried grated potatoes with besan, rice flour, ajwain, turmeric, chilli powder, green chilli, and salt (add 1 tbsp water only if needed to bind).
Cook thin patties on an oiled tawa for 5–6 minutes per side until nutty and crunchy.

notes: Besan and ajwain add warm Indian pakora notes to crisp grated-potato hashbrowns.

name: Instant Black Coffee

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.

Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

name: Instant Breadless Sooji Sandwich (Tawa-Toasted Fluffy Curd & Semolina Triangle Sandwich)

ingredients.name: Eno Fruit Salt or Baking Soda

steps.text: Mix sooji, curd, chopped vegetables, green chilli, coriander, salt, and 1/2 cup water into a thick batter; rest 10 minutes. Stir in eno/baking soda just before cooking.

steps.section: Crisp in pan or sandwich maker
steps.text: Heat oil (and optional mustard-curry leaf tadka) in a small pan or sandwich toaster. Pour batter, cover, and cook 4 minutes per side on low heat until golden and spongy inside. Cut into sandwich triangles.

notes: Classic no-bread suji sandwich—crispy outside, soft and fluffy inside.

name: Instant Rava Bonda / Suji Curd Bonda (Crispy Semolina, Rice Flour, Yogurt, Onion & Cashew Round Fritters)

steps.section: Soak suji in curd to hydrate
steps.text: Mix semolina, rice flour, maida, sour curd, salt, and 1/4 cup water in a bowl. Cover and rest for 15 minutes so the rava swells and softens.

steps.section: Beat in aromatics and baking soda
steps.text: Add finely chopped onion, grated carrot, cashews, ginger, green chillies, curry leaves, coriander, cumin, pepper, hing, and baking soda; beat by hand for 2 minutes into a dropping-consistency batter.
Drop small round spoonfuls into medium-hot oil and fry until crunchy golden on the outside and soft inside. Serve hot with coconut chutney.

notes: Ready in 25 minutes with zero fermentation—semolina gives an extra crunchy exterior.

name: Instant Rava Medu Vada / Crispy Suji-Curd Donut Vada (Spiced Semolina, Sour Curd, Ginger, Pepper & Curry Leaf Vadas)

steps.section: Cook rava-curd dough or soak thick batter
steps.text: Whisk sour curd and 3/4 cup water in a pan, add cumin, crushed pepper, hing, ginger, green chillies, curry leaves, and salt; bring to a simmer, stir in rava and rice flour on low flame for 2–3 minutes until it forms a soft dough ball, and cool slightly.

steps.section: Knead with onion and shape donut vadas
steps.text: Knead the warm dough with finely chopped onion, coriander, baking soda, and 1 tsp oil until smooth. Grease palms, shape into flattened rounds, and poke a neat hole in the center with a wet finger.
Slide the vadas into medium-hot oil and fry on medium heat until crisp and golden brown on both sides. Serve hot with sambar and coconut chutney.

notes: Gives the authentic donut shape, pepper-curry leaf aroma, and crunch of Medu Vada in 30 minutes with zero dal soaking or grinding.

name: Irish-Style Coffee (Non-alcoholic)

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.

name: Jaljeera

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Jam Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Jeera Aloo (Cumin & Herb Tossed Spiced Potatoes)

steps.text: Heat ghee or oil in a wide pan, add cumin seeds, crushed coriander seeds, hing, ginger, and green chillies; let them sizzle without burning.
Add boiled potato cubes, turmeric, red chilli flakes, amchur, and salt; toss on medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes until golden and crusted with cumin.
Sprinkle crushed kasuri methi and fresh coriander leaves and serve hot.

notes: Chill boiled potatoes for 30 minutes before cubing so they hold their shape and crisp up nicely.

name: Jeera Rice

steps.text: Wash rice until the water runs mostly clear; soak briefly if appropriate.
Heat ghee or oil, add spices and vegetables if using, and stir until fragrant.
Add rice and measured water, cover and cook until tender. Rest briefly before serving.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Jhal Chanachur (Extra-Spicy Bengali Green Chilli & Black Salt Mixture)

ingredients.name: Gram Flour (Besan) Infused with Green Chilli-ginger Paste

steps.section: Prepare green-chilli spiced sev and gathiya
steps.text: Mix besan with strained green chilli-ginger juice, salt, and hot oil; press through a sev press into hot oil and fry until fiery and crisp.

steps.section: Fry lentils, peanuts, and crisp green chillies
steps.text: Fry peanuts, soaked chana dal, curry leaves, and slit green chillies until completely moisture-free and crunchy.

steps.section: Toss with pungent black salt and pepper masala
steps.text: Mix all components with black salt, freshly ground black pepper, dry ginger powder, and red chilli powder.

notes: Fiery Bengali jhal chanachur ideal for rainy-day chai or mixing into spicy jhalmuri.

name: Jhinge Aloo Bori Posto (Ridge Gourd, Potato & Fried Lentil Dumplings in Poppy Seed Paste)

steps.section: Fry bori and sauté potatoes and jhinge
steps.text: Fry the bori in mustard oil until crisp and golden, then remove; temper oil with kalo jeere, fry potato cubes for 4 minutes, then add ridge gourd cubes and cook until softened.

steps.section: Fold in posto bata and fried bori
steps.text: Stir in freshly ground poppy-green chilli paste, salt, and ¼ cup water, add the fried bori, and simmer for 3-4 minutes until the posto coats the vegetables and bori.

notes: The fried bori soak up the sweet juices released by the ridge gourd and poppy seed paste.

name: Jhinge Aloo Chingri (Ridge Gourd, Potato & Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Lightly fry turmeric-salted prawns in mustard oil and remove. Fry potato wedges until golden.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and green chillies, add ridge gourd, cumin-ginger paste, and turmeric; sauté for 4 minutes.
Add warm water and salt, cook covered until potatoes and ridge gourd are soft, then add prawns and simmer for 4 minutes.

notes: A soothing, light Bengali summer lunch curry (jhol) that is easy to digest.

name: Jhinge Aloo Diye Macher Dimer Borar Jhol (Ridge Gourd, Potato & Fish Egg Fritter Curry)

steps.text: Mix fish eggs with chopped onion, green chilli, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry small fritters in mustard oil and set aside.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies, fry potato wedges, then add ridge gourd, ginger-cumin paste, turmeric, and warm water.
Once vegetables are soft, add the fried fish egg boras and simmer gently for 4-5 minutes.

notes: Light, cooling Bengali summer jhol.

name: Jhinge Bharta (Ridge Gourd / Turai Mash)

steps.text: Scrape the sharp ridges, peel lightly, and chop the ridge gourd (and clean peels if tender) into pieces.
Heat mustard oil, add kalo jeere, garlic, and green chillies, then add the ridge gourd and cook until tender and dry.
Grind or mash the cooked mixture with chopped onion, salt, and a few drops of raw mustard oil.

notes: Both the flesh and the tender ridged peel of jhinge make a delicious bharta.

name: Jhinge Fry / Jhinge Posto Bhaja (Bengali Ridge Gourd Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: White Poppy Seeds (Posto) or Roasted Peanuts

steps.section: Stir-fry ridge gourd over high heat
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with kalo jeere and green chillies, add jhinge pieces, turmeric, and salt, and cook uncovered on high heat until the released moisture evaporates and the gourd caramelizes.
Sprinkle poppy seeds (posto) or crushed peanuts and toss for 2 minutes until toasted.

notes: Light, cooling Bengali summer stir-fry.

name: Jhinger Bora / Jhinge Fritters (Crispy Ridge Gourd Fritters in Poppy-Rice Batter)

steps.section: Slice tender jhinge and pat dry
steps.text: Scrape the sharp ridges off the ridge gourd, slice into thin 3-inch planks, and pat dry; salt only right before dipping so the gourd does not get watery.

steps.section: Dip in thick posto-rice batter and fry
steps.text: Coat each slice in a thick batter of besan, rice flour, poppy seeds, kalo jeere, turmeric, and green chilli paste, and fry immediately in hot mustard oil until golden and crisp.

notes: Known as Janhi Bara in Odisha and Jhinger Bora in Bengal; best eaten fresh off the kadai.

name: Jhuri Aloo Bhaja (Bengali Crispy Matchstick Fried Potatoes with Peanuts)

steps.text: Rinse finely julienned potatoes in cold water 3-4 times until the water runs completely clear to remove starch, then spread on a kitchen towel until bone-dry.
Fry raw peanuts, dry red chillies, and curry leaves in hot oil until crisp; drain and set aside.
Fry the dry potato matchsticks in batches in hot oil until golden and crunchy. Drain on paper towels and toss with fried peanuts, curry leaves, and black salt.

notes: Do not salt the potatoes before frying so they turn out ultra-crispy.

name: Jhuri Aloor Bora / Crispy Shredded Potato Laccha Pakora (Spiced Potato Nest Fritters)

steps.section: Rinse potato strands and bind lightly with flour
steps.text: Rinse grated potato strands twice in cold water, squeeze dry in a towel, and toss with green chillies, ginger, coriander, kalo jeere, chilli flakes, salt, besan, and cornflour/rice flour without adding water.

steps.section: Drop loose lacy clusters into hot oil
steps.text: Drop loose bird's-nest clusters into hot oil without compacting them and fry on medium flame until every potato strand is golden and ultra-crunchy.

notes: Minimal flour and zero added water create a lacy, crackly potato texture.

name: Jibe Goja / Jibhe Goja (Crisp Sugar-Glazed Tongue-Shaped Bengali Sweet Pastry)

steps.section: Roll oval pastries and score the center
steps.text: Knead a firm maida-ghee dough, divide into small balls, roll into thin elongated oval shapes resembling a tongue ('jibhe'), and make 3–4 parallel knife slits down the middle without cutting the ends.
Deep-fry the ovals on medium-low heat until crisp and light golden.
Dip the crisp fried pastries in warm single-thread sugar syrup for 2 minutes and drain on a wire rack.

notes: Classic Bengali fair ('mela') and Rathayatra sweet pastry prized for its delicate crispness.

name: Jodhpur Mirchi Bread Pakora (Stuffed Green Chilli & Spiced Potato Bread Fritters)

ingredients.name: Mild Thick Green Chillies (Bhavnagri, Deseeded & Chopped)

steps.text: Temper hing, crushed coriander seeds, and fennel in 1 tsp oil; toss in chopped mild green chillies for 2 minutes, then mash in potatoes, amchur, black salt, and salt.

steps.section: Stuff, coat in besan, and fry
steps.text: Stuff between bread slices, slice into triangles, dip in ajwain-turmeric besan batter, and fry until puffed and golden.

notes: Inspired by Jodhpur's iconic mirchi vada combined with crispy bread pakora.

name: Jolbhora Sandesh

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

name: Joynagarer Moa (Winter Kanakchur Khoi & Nolen Gur Sweet Balls with Ghee & Cashews)

ingredients.name: Liquid Nolen Gur (Date Palm Jaggery / Jhola Gur)

steps.section: Simmer Nolen Gur to light binding consistency
steps.text: Warm liquid Nolen Gur in a pan for 3–4 minutes with cardamom powder and 1 tbsp ghee until fragrant and lightly syrupy.

steps.section: Fold in khoi and grated khoya
steps.text: Toss clean Kanakchur khoi with the warm Nolen Gur and half the grated khoya, coating gently without crushing the delicate puffed grains, and rest for 1 hour to soften.

steps.section: Shape soft balls and garnish with khoya & nuts
steps.text: Grease palms with cow ghee, shape into round moas, and crown each with a pinch of grated khoya, a cashew half, pistachio, and raisin.

notes: GI-tagged South 24 Parganas winter delicacy prized for its melt-in-the-mouth texture and Nolen Gur aroma.

name: Kabuli Chana Bengali Style

steps.text: Rinse the lentils or legumes. Pressure-cook or simmer with water and turmeric until soft.
Heat oil or ghee; add cumin, garlic, onion and tomato and cook until fragrant.
Mix the tempering into the cooked dal, adjust water and salt, and simmer briefly.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Kacha Aam Diye Macher Dimer Tok (Raw Mango & Fish Egg Sour Curry)

steps.text: Beat fish roe with besan, salt, and turmeric; fry small golden fritters in mustard oil.

steps.section: Cook raw mango in mustard broth
steps.text: Temper oil with mustard seeds and dry red chilli, sauté green mango wedges with turmeric and salt, then add water and cook until mango softens.

steps.section: Simmer with mustard paste and boras
steps.text: Stir in mustard paste, sugar, and fried fish egg boras; simmer for 4 minutes and serve warm or at room temperature.

notes: A beloved Bengali summer afternoon dish using fresh tart green mangoes.

name: Kacha Chola Muri Makha (Soaked Black Chickpea, Coconut & Ginger Puffed Rice)

steps.text: In a bowl, toss drained soaked kala chana with finely diced fresh coconut, minced ginger, green chilli, chopped onion, black salt, roasted cumin powder, and mustard oil.
Add puffed rice and toss briskly until evenly coated. Serve immediately.

notes: Wholesome no-cook morning tiffin popular across Bengal.

name: Kacha Golla

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Kacha Kola Bharta (Raw Banana / Plantain Mash)

steps.text: Wash raw green bananas, cut in halves with skin on, and boil or pressure-cook until fork-tender.
Peel the warm bananas (reserve the skins for Kanchkola Khosa Bharta if desired) and mash immediately while hot so no lumps form.
Mix in chopped onion, grated ginger, crushed chillies, fresh coriander, salt, and mustard oil or ghee.

notes: Always mash raw bananas while still hot, as they firm up quickly on cooling.

name: Kacha Peper Bora / Raw Papaya Fritters (Crispy Grated Green Papaya & Coconut Fritters)

ingredients.name: Besan (Gram Flour) or Soaked Cholar Dal Paste

steps.section: Squeeze grated raw papaya and bind with coconut and flours
steps.text: Salt the grated raw papaya lightly for 5 minutes, squeeze out excess moisture, and mix with besan/dal paste, rice flour, grated coconut, poppy seeds, kalo jeere, ginger, and green chillies.

steps.section: Shallow-fry golden patties in mustard oil
steps.text: Shape into small flat medallions and shallow-fry in hot mustard oil over medium heat until golden and crisp.

notes: Turns humble everyday green papaya into a nutty, coconut-scented Bengali starter.

name: Kacha Tomato Bharta (Green Tomato Mash)

steps.text: Halve green tomatoes and pan-roast with garlic cloves and green chillies in a few drops of mustard oil until blistered and soft.
Mash the roasted green tomatoes, garlic, and chillies into a tangy coarse paste.
Fold in chopped onion, optional mustard paste, fresh coriander, salt, and raw mustard oil.

notes: Tangy and vibrant winter relish.

name: Kachu Fry / Mukhi Kochu Bhaja (Crispy Taro Root / Arbi Tawa Fry)

steps.text: Boil taro roots until just fork-tender (do not overcook), peel, slice into thick discs, and coat with turmeric, chilli, coriander, amchur, rice flour, and salt.
Heat mustard oil with ajwain/radhuni and dry red chilli, and shallow-fry the taro slices until crisp and golden brown on both sides.

notes: Crispy outside and creamy inside—finish with a squeeze of lemon juice.

name: Kadai Paneer (Wok-Tossed Paneer & Bell Peppers in Freshly Pounded Coriander-Chilli Kadai Masala)

steps.section: Dry-roast and coarsely pound Kadai Masala
steps.text: Dry-roast whole coriander seeds, cumin, black peppercorns, and dry red chillies until aromatic, then crush coarsely in a mortar and pestle; toss paneer, capsicum, and onion petals on high heat for 2 minutes and set aside.

steps.section: Cook onion-tomato masala and toss with paneer and capsicum
steps.text: Sauté finely chopped onions, ginger-garlic paste, and tomato puree until thick, stir in two-thirds of the pounded kadai masala, fold in the seared paneer, capsicum, and onion petals, and top with ginger juliennes, kasuri methi, and remaining kadai masala.

notes: Freshly pounded coriander seeds and dry red chillies give Kadai Paneer its signature smoky crunch.

name: Kadai Prawns (Prawns with Bell Peppers & Kadai Masala)

ingredients.name: Kadai Masala (Roasted Coriander Seeds, Dry Red Chillies, Cumin)

steps.section: Pound kadai spice and toss peppers
steps.text: Dry-roast coriander seeds, cumin, and whole red chillies; crush coarsely. Quickly toss cubed onion petals and bell peppers in hot oil for 2 minutes and set aside.
Sauté finely chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste until golden, add tomatoes and crushed kadai masala, and cook until oil separates.
Add prawns, sautéed bell peppers, and onion petals; cook for 5-6 minutes until prawns are tender. Finish with crushed kasuri methi and ginger juliennes.

notes: Serve hot with garlic naan, tandoori roti, or jeera rice.

name: Kaju Ghee Rice / Nei Choru (Malabar-Style Ghee-Roasted Cashews, Golden Raisins, Crispy Shallots & Whole Spice Rice)

steps.section: Crisp-fry cashews, raisins, and shallots in ghee
steps.text: Heat desi ghee in a heavy pot, fry cashews golden, plump the raisins, and crisp-fry half the sliced shallots until deep brown; reserve for garnish.

steps.section: Toast rice in whole-spice infused ghee
steps.text: Temper cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, star anise, mace, and bay leaf in the remaining ghee, saute remaining shallots and ginger-garlic-chillies, then toast drained rice for 2–3 minutes.
Pour 3.5 cups hot water with salt, cover tightly, and simmer 12 minutes until fluffy. Top with crispy fried shallots, cashews, and raisins.

notes: Kerala and coastal Karnataka festive Ghee Rice (Nei Choru), best paired with spicy roasted curries or kurma.

name: Kaju Katli

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Kaju Pista Roll (Cashew Marzipan Roll Stuffed with Pistachio Fudge)

steps.section: Cook cashew and pistachio fudges separately
steps.text: Boil sugar and water to 1-thread syrup; mix 3/4 of the syrup with cashew powder and 1/4 with pistachio powder and cardamom, cooking each on low flame with a tsp of ghee into smooth pliable doughs.

steps.section: Roll cashew sheet and pistachio cylinder
steps.text: Roll the warm cashew dough between parchment sheets into a thin rectangle and roll the green pistachio dough into tight cylindrical logs.

steps.section: Wrap, roll tight, and slice into cylinders
steps.text: Wrap the cashew sheet tightly around the pistachio log, roll until seamless, and slice into 1.5-inch Kaju Pista Rolls.

notes: Showstopping Diwali and festive confection pairing smooth cashew katli with vibrant pistachio filling.

name: Kaju Rose Laddoo (Hand-Crushed Cashew, Gulkand & Rosewater Laddoo)

ingredients.name: Cashews (Finely Chopped & Crushed with Rolling Pin)

steps.text: Warm ghee in a pan on very low heat and toast finely chopped/crushed cashews and desiccated coconut for 3 minutes without browning.
Stir in powdered sugar (or condensed milk), gulkand, cardamom, and rosewater on low heat for 3 minutes until cohesive. Cool slightly and roll into fragrant laddoos.

notes: Festive rose-scented mithai with a chewy gulkand-cashew bite.

name: Kakra Pitha (Crispy Odia Semolina & Coconut-Jaggery Stuffed Fried Fritters)

steps.section: Make suji dough and coconut-fennel stuffing
steps.text: Cook grated coconut with half the jaggery, fennel, and cardamom for 6 minutes until sticky. Boil 2 cups water with remaining sugar/jaggery and ghee, slowly whisk in suji while stirring briskly until a smooth soft dough forms; cool slightly and knead.
Form greased-hand cups from the suji dough, stuff with coconut pur, seal into smooth flat rounds, and fry on medium heat until crisp and golden brown.

notes: Crisp outside and soft inside; stays tender even after cooling.

name: Kakro Chaukani / Cucumber Chukauni (Refreshing Nepali Cucumber & Spiced Yogurt Salad)

steps.text: Fold diced cucumber, boiled potato, onion, green chillies, and coriander into whisked thick curd; season with roasted cumin, salt, and lemon juice.
Heat mustard oil in a ladle, brown fenugreek seeds until dark, stir in turmeric and red chilli powder, and immediately pour sizzling over the yogurt salad.
Mix well so the golden oil streaks through the cool yogurt. Serve chilled as a refreshing summer lunch accompaniment.

notes: Cooling, crunchy cucumber variation of traditional Chukauni, perfect for warm weather meals.

name: Kakro ko Achar (Nepali Spiced Cucumber & Roasted Sesame Salad)

steps.text: Place diced cucumber in a bowl with ground roasted sesame powder, green chillies, salt, and fresh lemon juice.
Heat mustard oil until smoking, add fenugreek seeds and fry until dark brown. Take off heat, add turmeric powder, and pour sizzling over the cucumbers.
Toss thoroughly to coat every cucumber piece in the nutty sesame dressing. Serve fresh with dal-bhat or sel roti.

notes: Beloved Nepali quick instant pickle salad showcasing the rich, nutty aroma of roasted sesame paste and crunchy cucumbers.

name: Kakrol Bharta (Spiny Gourd Mash)

steps.text: Wash kakrol thoroughly, lightly scrape the spiny skin, and cut into thick slices or cubes.
Boil or steam kakrol slices with a pinch of salt and turmeric until tender, drain well, and sear in mustard oil with nigella seeds, garlic, and green chillies.
Mash or grind the cooked kakrol mixture into a smooth bharta, fold in finely chopped onion and a drizzle of raw mustard oil, and serve warm.

notes: Remove hard seeds if the kakrol is over-ripe before mashing.

name: Kakrol Fry / Kakrol Bhaja (Bengali Crispy Spiny Gourd / Teasle Gourd Pan-Fry)

steps.section: Slice and par-blanch or salt kakrol discs
steps.text: Wash the spiny gourds gently, slice into even round discs, and rub with turmeric powder, red chilli powder, salt, and a light dusting of rice flour.
Heat mustard oil in a wide pan, arrange the kakrol discs in a single layer, and fry on medium heat for 4-5 minutes per side until crisp on the edges and soft in the center.

notes: Classic monsoon Bengali Kakrol Fry—pairs wonderfully with masoor dal and steamed rice.

name: Kakroler Bora / Kakrol Fritters (Crispy Batter-Fried Spiny Gourd / Teasle Gourd Fritters)

steps.text: Lightly scrape the spiny outer skin of the kakrol, slice into even rounds, rub with salt and turmeric, and rest for 8 minutes (or steam for 2 minutes) so the interior cooks evenly.

steps.section: Dip in posto-studded batter and fry
steps.text: Whisk besan, rice flour, poppy seeds, kalo jeere, green chilli paste, turmeric, and water into a thick batter; coat each kakrol slice and deep-fry in mustard oil until nutty and crisp.

notes: The poppy seeds in the batter toast in the hot mustard oil, giving Kakroler Bora an unmistakable crunch.

name: Kala Chana Bengali Style

steps.text: Rinse the lentils or legumes. Pressure-cook or simmer with water and turmeric until soft.
Heat oil or ghee; add cumin, garlic, onion and tomato and cook until fragrant.
Mix the tempering into the cooked dal, adjust water and salt, and simmer briefly.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Kalo Jeere O Rosun Kochuri (Bengali Fragrant Garlic & Nigella Seed Stuffed Kochuri)

steps.text: Warm mustard oil in a pan, toss in kalo jeere and minced garlic, sautéing on low flame until fragrant. Stir in roasted besan, chopped chillies, lemon juice, and salt, creating a damp, flavorful stuffing.
Knead maida with ghee, salt, and water. Form lemon-sized balls, stuff with the garlic-kalo jeere mixture, seal securely, and roll out.
Fry in medium-hot oil until puffed with a delightfully crunchy exterior. Serve with bhanga aloor torkari.

notes: A pungent, immune-boosting traditional winter specialty celebrated for its distinct garlic-nigella aroma.

name: Kanchkola Bori Jhol (Raw Plantain, Potato & Fried Lentil Dumpling Digestive Broth)

steps.section: Soak raw banana in turmeric water and fry bori
steps.text: Soak cut kanchkola in turmeric water to prevent blackening; fry the bori in mustard oil until golden and set aside.

steps.section: Simmer light cumin-radhuni broth with bori
steps.text: Temper oil with cumin, radhuni, and bay leaf, sauté potatoes and kanchkola with ginger, cumin-coriander powder, and turmeric, add 2 cups warm water, and simmer with fried bori until tender; finish with 1 tsp ghee.

notes: Light, wholesome, and soothing on the stomach, ideal for everyday Bengali lunches.

name: Kanchkola Fry / Kacha Kola Bhaja (Bengali Crispy Raw Banana / Plantain Fry)

steps.section: Soak in turmeric water and coat with spices
steps.text: Soak sliced raw banana in turmeric water for 5 minutes to prevent darkening, drain, and toss with turmeric, chilli powder, cumin, pepper, rice flour, and salt.
Shallow-fry in hot mustard oil over medium flame for 4-5 minutes per side until crisp outside and fluffy inside.

notes: Crunchy, savory raw banana fry that pairs with dal-chawal or sambar-rice.

name: Kanchkola Khosa Bharta (Raw Banana Peel Mash)

steps.text: Boil clean raw banana peels in water with a pinch of turmeric and salt until completely tender, then drain.
Grind the boiled peels with garlic cloves and green chillies into a smooth paste.
Heat mustard oil, crackle nigella seeds, add the ground paste and salt, and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until dark, glossy, and aromatic.

notes: Rich in iron and fibre; a staple Bengali comfort dish.

name: Kanchkolar Bora / Raw Banana Fritters (Crispy Plantain Slices & Spiced Mashed Plantain Fritters)

steps.section: Soak peeled raw banana slices in turmeric water
steps.text: Slice peeled green plantains into thin lengthwise planks or diagonal ovals, soak in turmeric-salted water for 5 minutes to prevent darkening, and pat dry.

steps.section: Coat in spiced besan-rice batter and fry
steps.text: Dip each slice into a smooth batter of besan, rice flour, kalo jeere, ajwain, turmeric, red chilli, black pepper, and salt, and deep-fry in hot oil until puffed and crisp.

notes: Also known as Vazhakkai Bajji in South India and Kanchkolar Beguni in Bengali homes.

name: Karachi Halwa / Bombay Ice Halwa (Glossy Cornflour, Ghee & Cashew Jelly Sweet)

steps.section: Dissolve cornflour and cook with sugar syrup
steps.text: Whisk cornflour with 1.5 cups water until lump-free; boil sugar with 0.75 cup water and lemon juice, then slowly stir in the cornflour slurry over low flame.

steps.section: Incorporate ghee spoon by spoon until glossy and translucent
steps.text: Cook on low-medium flame for 20 minutes, adding 1 tbsp ghee at a time while stirring until the halwa turns translucent, chewy, and pulls away from the pan.

steps.section: Fold in nuts and set into jewel-like squares
steps.text: Mix in cardamom, saffron tint, cashews, and melon seeds, pour into a greased square tin, cool completely, and cut into jewel-bright squares.

notes: Chewy, jewel-toned translucent halwa studded with crunchy cashews and melon seeds.

name: Karela Bharta (Bitter Gourd Mash)

ingredients.name: Green Chilli or Roasted Red Chilli

steps.text: Wash and slice karela thinly, rub with 1/2 tsp salt and turmeric, rest for 10 minutes, and squeeze out excess bitter juice.
Heat mustard oil in a pan and fry or steam-fry the karela slices with garlic on medium-low heat until tender and lightly browned.
Coarsely mash or pound the cooked karela with finely chopped onion, crushed chilli, salt, and a drizzle of raw mustard oil.

notes: Salting and resting karela before cooking mellows the bitterness while keeping its digestive benefits.

name: Karela Nimki / Karela Mathri (Crisp Accordion-Pleated Spiced Savory Pastry)

steps.section: Roll small ovals and cut parallel center slits
steps.text: Knead a firm maida-ghee dough with kalonji, ajwain, and salt; roll small balls into thin ovals and make closely spaced parallel knife slits down the center without cutting the outer rim.

steps.section: Roll and pinch ends into bitter-gourd (karela) shape
steps.text: Roll each slit oval lengthwise from one side to the other and pinch both pointed ends together so the middle fans out like a karela.

steps.section: Deep-fry on low-medium flame until crisp
steps.text: Fry in medium-low oil until every pleated strip turns golden and crunchy.

notes: Decorative accordion-pleated Bengali/Bihari nimki that stays extra crunchy due to its separated strips.

name: Karela Paratha (Spiced Sautéed Bitter Gourd & Amchur Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Salt grated karela, rest 10 minutes, squeeze out bitter juice. Sauté onions, ginger, and karela in mustard oil with fennel powder, amchur, cumin, and turmeric until dry and caramelized.
Enclose karela stuffing in whole wheat dough balls and roll into even rounds.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until crisp and spotted with golden brown blisters. Serve with cool curd.

notes: A therapeutic, tangy-sweet-bitter flatbread beloved in Gujarati and Rajasthani cooking.

name: Karnataka Vangi Bath (Spiced Brinjal / Eggplant, Tamarind & Roasted Vangi Bath Powder Masala Rice)

ingredients.name: Cooled Sona Masoori or Basmati Rice
Tender Purple Brinjal / Eggplant (Thinly Sliced Lengthwise)
Vangi Bath Masala Powder (Coriander, Chana-urad Dal, Cinnamon, Cloves, Dry Coconut & Red Chilli)
Sesame Oil or Groundnut Oil + 1 Tbsp Ghee

steps.text: Heat oil in a wide kadai, crackle mustard seeds, chana dal, urad dal, peanuts, cashews, hing, and curry leaves until golden.

steps.section: Cook brinjal in tangy tamarind and Vangi Bath masala
steps.text: Add sliced brinjal, turmeric, and salt; saute until tender. Stir in tamarind pulp, pinch of jaggery, and Vangi Bath powder, cooking 3–4 minutes until aromatic and glossy.
Turn off heat, gently fold in cooled, fluffy rice with 1 tbsp desi ghee and chopped fresh coriander until every grain is coated in spiced masala.

notes: Beloved Karnataka breakfast and lunchbox masala rice; using slightly cooled, separated rice keeps the grains intact.

name: Kasha Aloor Dum (Bengali Spicy Slow-Braised Onion-Garlic Potato Dum)

steps.text: Parboil halved potatoes with salt and turmeric for 5 minutes, drain, and fry in hot mustard oil until golden-crusted.
Temper oil with bay leaf, whole garam masala, and a pinch of sugar. Caramelize onions, then slow-braise ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and spices with splashes of warm water until dark and glossy.
Add the fried potatoes and a cup of warm water, cover and cook on low flame until the thick masala coats the potatoes, and finish with ghee.

notes: Rich, meaty-style Bengali kosha gravy for potatoes.

name: Kashmiri Dum Aloo (Fennel & Yogurt Spiced Baby Potato Curry)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri Red Chilli Powder (Dissolved in Water)

steps.text: Prick parboiled baby potatoes thoroughly with a fork or toothpick and fry in hot mustard oil until a golden-brown skin forms all around.
Whisk yogurt with Kashmiri red chilli paste, fennel powder (saunf), and dry ginger powder (sonth). Temper 2 tbsp oil with cloves, black cardamom, cinnamon, and hing.
Stir the spiced yogurt into the pan on low flame until boiling, add the fried baby potatoes and salt, and simmer covered on low heat for 10 minutes so the potatoes soak up the gravy.

notes: Authentic Kashmiri Pandit recipe made without onion, garlic, or tomatoes.

name: Kashmiri Kahwa

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Kashmiri Noon Chai

name: Kashmiri Pulao

steps.text: Wash rice until the water runs mostly clear; soak briefly if appropriate.
Heat ghee or oil, add spices and vegetables if using, and stir until fragrant.
Add rice and measured water, cover and cook until tender. Rest briefly before serving.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Kasundi Aloo Bread Pakora (Bengali Mustard-Sauce & Spiced Potato Bread Fritters)

steps.text: Spread a thin layer of kasundi on the inside of each bread slice, layer with mashed potato seasoned with onion, green chillies, bhaja masala, and salt, close, and cut diagonally.

steps.section: Dip in kalonji besan batter and fry
steps.text: Coat each triangle in besan-rice flour batter spiced with kalonji, turmeric, and salt, then fry until golden and crisp.

notes: Kasundi inside the sandwich adds a punchy Bengali mustard zing to every bite.

name: Kasundi Muri Makha (Bengali Mustard Sauce & Crisp Puffed Rice Tiffin)

steps.text: Toss chopped onion, cucumber, deseeded tomato, green chillies, coriander, and black salt with Bengali kasundi in a mixing bowl.
Fold in puffed rice, roasted peanuts, and chanachur, toss lightly, and serve right away.

notes: Tangy, pungent kasundi gives instant zing without needing extra oil.

name: Kasundi Paratha (Bengali Pungent Mustard Paste & Herb Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Combine mashed potato with kasundi mustard paste, kalo jeere, chopped chillies, fresh coriander, roasted cumin, and salt.
Fill wheat dough balls with the tangy mustard stuffing and roll into medium circles.
Cook with mustard oil or ghee on high heat until blistered and crunchy. Serve with tea or plain yogurt.

notes: An exhilaratingly pungent Bengali paratha featuring traditional Queen of Mustards, Kasundi.

steps.text: Clean fish and season lightly with salt and turmeric.
Heat oil and lightly fry or sear fish; set aside.
Cook potato, tomato and spices, add water, then return fish and simmer gently until cooked through.

name: Keema Paratha (Spiced Minced Meat Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Sauté chopped onion, ginger-garlic, and green chillies in 1 tbsp oil, add minced meat and spice powders, and cook until completely dry. Stir in mint and coriander and cool completely.
Fill soft dough balls with the cooled dry keema mixture, seal tightly, and roll into parathas.
Roast on a hot tawa with ghee until crisp and golden brown on both sides. Serve with mint raita.

notes: Make sure the cooked keema has zero moisture and is completely cool before stuffing.

name: Keerai Bonda / Palak Mysore Bonda (Spiced Spinach, Sour Curd, Gram Flour & Rice Flour Crispy Round Fritters)

steps.section: Beat curd-flour base and fold in greens
steps.text: Beat besan, maida, rice flour, sour curd, cumin, pepper, hing, and salt with a splash of water for 3 minutes until fluffy. Fold in finely shredded greens, chopped onion, ginger, green chillies, and baking soda.
Drop round spoonfuls into medium-hot oil and fry on medium heat for 4–5 minutes until crisp and golden brown.
Serve piping hot with coconut chutney or mint chutney.

notes: Combines the airy sour-curd crumb of Mysore Bonda with iron-rich leafy greens.

name: Kerala Chemmeen Roast (Nadan Spicy Prawn Fry)

steps.text: Cook cleaned prawns with turmeric, half the chilli powder, salt, curry leaves, and soaked kudampuli in a little water for 4 minutes.
Heat coconut oil in a heavy pan, add extra curry leaves, crushed ginger-garlic, and sliced shallots; sauté until deep golden brown.
Add chopped tomato, remaining chilli, fennel, and black pepper powder, then tip in the prawns and roast on medium-low heat until dark and richly coated.

notes: Coconut oil, shallots, and fresh curry leaves give this Kerala toddy-shop classic its signature aroma.

name: Kerala Fish Roe Roast (Meen Mutta Roast with Shallots & Curry Leaves)

steps.text: Heat coconut oil in a heavy pan, splutter curry leaves, and sauté crushed ginger-garlic and sliced shallots until golden brown.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli, fennel, and black pepper powder; cook until thick and oil separates.
Add the fish roe (whole slices or coarse chunks), cover on low heat for 5 minutes until cooked, then stir-roast with extra curry leaves and lemon juice.

notes: Spicy, aromatic Kerala toddy-shop style Meen Mutta Roast.

name: Kerala Pazham Bonda / KaiVada (Sweet Ripe Banana, Jaggery, Coconut, Cardamom & Rice-Flour Fritters)

ingredients.name: Ripe Nendran or Robusta Bananas (Mashed By Hand)
Jaggery (Melted in 1/4 Cup Warm Water & Strained)
Tiny Coconut Bites (Thenga Kothu, Fried in Ghee)

steps.section: Mash bananas with jaggery syrup and spices
steps.text: Mash ripe bananas thoroughly in a bowl, then mix in warm strained jaggery syrup, ghee-fried coconut bits, grated coconut, sesame seeds, cardamom powder, dry ginger powder, baking soda, and a pinch of salt.

steps.section: Fold in flour to form thick batter
steps.text: Fold in wheat flour/maida and rice flour, beating by hand for 2 minutes into a thick, scoopable bonda batter.

steps.section: Fry in coconut oil until caramelized
steps.text: Drop round spoonfuls into medium-low coconut oil and fry slowly until deep mahogany-golden outside and soft and fragrant inside.

notes: Kerala tea-shop classic ('Pazham Bonda' / 'Unniyappam-style bonda') made without any grinder.

name: Kerala Prawn Moilee (Chemmeen Molee in Coconut Milk)

steps.text: Toss prawns with turmeric, black pepper, lemon juice, and salt for 10 minutes.

steps.section: Sauté aromatics and simmer in thin milk
steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds, cloves, cinnamon, and curry leaves. Soften sliced onion, ginger, garlic, and green chillies without browning, add thin coconut milk and prawns, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add tomato slices and thick coconut milk, warm gently for 2 minutes without boiling rigorously, and remove from heat.

notes: Delicate, mildly spiced Syrian Christian Kerala stew best served with appam, idiyappam, or steamed rice.

name: Kesar Barfi

Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Khaja (Digha / Puri Style Multi-Layered Crispy Ghee Pastry in Sugar Syrup)

steps.section: Roll thin sheets and coil with ghee-rice flour paste
steps.text: Roll stiff maida dough into 5 paper-thin rotis, brush each layer with a paste of ghee and rice flour, stack and roll tightly into a log, slice into 1-inch pieces, and roll lightly lengthwise.

steps.section: Deep-fry on low flame so layers puff open
steps.text: Fry the khaja pieces in low-temperature oil, splashing hot oil over the top until the concentric layers separate and turn golden-crisp.

steps.section: Dip briefly in warm cardamom syrup
steps.text: Submerge warm khajas in 1-thread cardamom sugar syrup for 2 minutes and drain so the layers remain crisp yet juicy.

notes: Iconic multi-layered sweet pastry beloved in coastal Bengal (Digha) and Puri Jagannath Dham.

name: Khaman Dhokla / Nylon Khaman (Fluffy Steamed Gram Flour Sponge Cake with Mustard, Sesame & Green Chilli Tempering)

ingredients.name: Citric Acid (Nimbu Phool) or Fresh Lemon Juice

steps.text: Dissolve sugar, salt, citric acid/lemon juice, ginger-chilli paste, turmeric, and 2 tbsp oil in 1 cup water. Whisk in sifted besan and suji for 4–5 minutes until silky and ribbon-like; rest 10 minutes.

steps.section: Activate with fruit salt and steam
steps.text: Bring a steamer to a rolling boil. Whisk fruit salt with 1 tbsp water into the batter until frothy, pour immediately into a greased thali, and steam on high heat for 15 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.

Heat 1.5 tbsp oil, crackle mustard seeds, sesame seeds, hing, curry leaves, and slit green chillies, then add 1/2 cup water and 1 tbsp sugar and boil 1 minute. Cut the warm khaman into squares, spoon the warm tempering syrup evenly so the sponge turns juicy, and garnish with fresh coconut and coriander.

notes: Keep turmeric to a tiny pinch (1/4 tsp) so it never reacts with the leavening agent to form red spots.

name: Khara Shankarpali / Salted Diamond Biscuits (Crisp Cumin & Pepper Tea-Time Crackers)

steps.section: Pour sizzling ghee over flour and knead stiff dough
steps.text: Pour hot melted ghee over maida, rava, cumin, ajwain, crushed black pepper, and salt; rub thoroughly and knead with water into a stiff dough.

steps.section: Roll thick sheet and cut into squares or diamonds
steps.text: Roll dough to a 0.25-inch thickness and cut with a fluted cutter or knife into 1-inch squares.

steps.section: Fry on low flame until flaky and biscuit-crisp
steps.text: Deep-fry over low-medium heat for 10–12 minutes until pale golden and flaky like shortbread biscuits.

notes: Melt-in-the-mouth savory diamond biscuits seasoned with cumin and black pepper.

name: Khasta Dal Kachori (Flaky Moong Dal Stuffed Puri)

steps.text: Sauté hing, crushed fennel, coriander, cumin, and besan in 1 tbsp oil, add coarse moong dal, red chilli, amchur, and salt, and roast until dry and crumbly.

steps.section: Knead flaky moyan dough and stuff
steps.text: Rub 4 tbsp melted ghee into maida until breadcrumb-like, knead with cold water, stuff with dal balls, and flatten gently with your palm.
Slide into warm (low-medium) oil and fry slowly for 10-12 minutes until puffed, golden, and shatteringly flaky (khasta).

notes: Frying on low heat is the secret to a crisp, blister-free khasta kachori.

name: Khasta Goja / Bengali Belgrami (Crispy Multi-Layered Deep-Fried Maida Pastry in Sugar Glaze)

steps.text: Rub ghee into maida with baking soda and salt until crumbly. Add cold water to gently bring dough together without over-kneading. Roll into a thick sheet, cut in half, stack on top, and roll again (repeat 4 times to build flaky layers).
Cut the layered dough into 2-inch rectangular blocks. Slide into medium-low heat oil and fry slowly for 15 minutes until puffed and thoroughly crisp.
Boil sugar and water to a heavy 2-string syrup with cardamom. Toss the hot fried gojas in the syrup off heat until a frosted white sugar crust crystallizes on the surface.

notes: Classic Bengali sweet-shop dry pastry celebrated for its flaky interior and crunchy frosted sugar shell.

name: Kheer (Vermicelli)

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.

name: Kheer Kadam / Raskadam (Mini Rasgulla Encased in Roasted Khoya Sphere)

ingredients.name: Mini Sponge Rasgullas (or Nolen Gur Rasgullas)
Poppy Seeds (Posto) or Dry Khoya Crumbs

steps.text: Gently press excess syrup out of the mini rasgullas and rest them on a sieve for 15 minutes so they remain juicy inside but dry on the surface.
Cook grated khoya with powdered sugar and cardamom over low flame for 6–8 minutes until smooth and firm, then cool completely.

steps.section: Wrap each mini rasgulla in khoya and coat
steps.text: Flatten portions of khoya dough, encase one mini rasgulla inside each, roll into smooth balls, and coat in roasted poppy seeds or dry khoya crumbs.

notes: Iconic Bengali dual-textured sweet revealing a juicy mini rasgulla inside a rich khoya shell.

name: Kheer Patisapta (Bengali Thin Crepes Filled with Thickened Milk Khoya & Nolen Gur)

steps.section: Prepare smooth crepe batter and kheer filling
steps.text: Whisk maida, suji, rice flour, 2 tbsp nolen gur, and milk into a thin lump-free batter; rest 20 minutes. Simmer grated khoya with remaining nolen gur and cardamom for 5 minutes until thick and creamy.
Spread a thin ladle of batter on a lightly ghee-brushed non-stick tawa, cook 1 minute on low heat, place a line of kheer filling along one edge, and roll neatly.

notes: Keep tawa temperature low so the crepes stay pale, soft, and never stick.

name: Kheer Puli Pithe (Bengali Rice Dumplings Stuffed with Coconut in Thickened Gur Milk)

steps.section: Prepare coconut-gur pur and rice-flour dough
steps.text: Cook grated coconut, khoya, and Nolen Gur into a sticky filling; knead rice flour with boiling salted water into a soft, smooth dough.
Shape small dough discs, fill with coconut-khoya pur, and pinch the edges into pleated half-moon dumplings.

steps.section: Simmer dumplings in Nolen Gur thickened milk
steps.text: Reduce milk with cardamom and bay leaf to a creamy kheer, gently simmer the puli dumplings for 10 minutes until they float, and stir in Nolen Gur off the heat.

notes: Beloved Poush Sankranti winter pithe simmered in aromatic date-palm jaggery milk.

name: Khosa-Soho Aloor Torkari (Kolkata Kochuri-Shop Skin-On Potato Curry)

ingredients.name: Black Chickpeas (Kala Chana, Soaked) or Green Peas

steps.text: Heat mustard oil until smoking, then temper with whole dry red chillies, panch phoron, and a generous pinch of hing.
Add scrubbed skin-on potato cubes, soaked kala chana, ginger-green chilli paste, turmeric, and salt; stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Add warm water, cover and cook until potatoes are soft, lightly mash a few pieces into the gravy, and finish with a pinch of sugar and roasted bhaja masala.

notes: Authentic Kolkata street-corner kochuri and petai porota accompaniment.

name: Khoya Paratha / Mawa Paratha (Sweet Mawa, Cardamom & Nut Stuffed Rich Paratha)

steps.text: Roast mawa on low flame for 4 minutes until warm, mix with powdered sugar, cardamom, nutmeg, and crushed nuts; let cool.
Place portions of mawa stuffing inside dough balls, seal edges securely, and roll gently.
Cook on a hot tawa with generous ghee on low-medium flame until golden, crisp, and fragrant. Serve as a dessert or festive treat.

notes: A royal North Indian festive delicacy reminiscent of stuffed sweet peda in paratha form.

name: Khuska / Kuska (South Indian Plain Biryani Rice — Fragrant Seeraga Samba / Basmati Rice with Whole Spices, Mint & Curd)

ingredients.name: Seeraga Samba Rice or Aged Basmati Rice

steps.section: Caramelize onions and bloom whole spices
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or pressure cooker, temper bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, star anise, and fennel seeds, then fry thinly sliced onions until deep golden brown.

steps.section: Saute ginger-garlic, herbs, tomato, and curd
steps.text: Add ginger-garlic paste and slit green chillies and cook 2 minutes until raw smell fades. Stir in chopped mint, coriander, tomato, red chilli powder, turmeric, and biryani masala until soft, then lower heat and whisk in curd until oil separates.

steps.section: Dum-cook soaked rice to fluffy perfection
steps.text: Pour in 3.5 cups hot water and salt, bring to a rolling boil, fold in drained soaked rice gently, and cook covered on low dum for 12–14 minutes (or 1 whistle on medium flame) followed by 5 minutes rest before fluffing with a fork. Serve hot with salna, kurma, or onion raita.

notes: Classic South Indian 'plain biryani' (Kuska) prized for its rich, aromatic masala rice grains without any meat.

name: Kochu Patar Bora (Steamed & Pan-Fried Spiced Taro / Colocasia Leaf Rolls)

ingredients.name: Tamarind Pulp or Lemon Juice (to Neutralize Itchiness)
Yellow Mustard-poppy Paste or Roasted Cumin-coriander Spice Mix

steps.section: Layer taro leaves with tangy spiced paste and steam
steps.text: Spread a thick paste of besan, rice flour, tamarind pulp, mustard-poppy paste, green chilli, turmeric, and salt over taro leaves, roll into a tight log, and steam for 12 minutes.

steps.section: Slice and shallow-fry with sesame and kalo jeere
steps.text: Cool the steamed roll, slice into 1/2-inch pinwheels, and shallow-fry in hot mustard oil tempered with sesame and kalo jeere until crisp on both faces.

notes: Tamarind or lemon is essential when cooking kochu pata to neutralize calcium oxalate crystals.

name: Kochu Shak Chingri (Colocasia Stems & Greens with Prawns)

steps.text: Boil chopped colocasia stems with salt until soft, then drain thoroughly and mash coarsely.
Lightly fry seasoned prawns in mustard oil. Temper the oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, nigella seeds, crushed garlic, and green chillies.
Add mashed kochu shak, turmeric, salt, sugar, grated coconut, and fried prawns. Cook on medium heat, stirring continuously, until all moisture evaporates. Finish with lemon juice.

notes: Adding a squeeze of lemon juice at the end balances the earthy taro greens.

name: Kochu Shak Diye Macher Dim (Colocasia Greens with Fish Eggs)

steps.section: Boil kochu shak and fry roe
steps.text: Boil chopped colocasia stems with salt until soft, drain thoroughly, and mash. Fry seasoned fish roe in mustard oil until golden and crumble coarsely.

steps.section: Temper with garlic and kalo jeere
steps.text: Temper mustard oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, nigella seeds, crushed garlic, and green chillies.
Add mashed kochu shak, turmeric, salt, sugar, and crumbled fried fish roe; stir-cook until moisture dries up completely and finish with lemon juice.

notes: Rich, garlicky taro greens elevated with savory fried fish roe granules.

name: Kochur Loti Chingri (Taro Stolons with Prawns)

steps.text: Briefly blanch cleaned taro stolons in salted turmeric water for 2 minutes and drain well.
Heat mustard oil, temper with nigella seeds, fry sliced onion, garlic paste, and seasoned prawns with turmeric and chilli powder.
Add blanched kochur loti, mustard paste, grated coconut, and slit green chillies. Cook covered on low heat until tender and lightly caramelized.

notes: A prized East Bengali (Bangal) delicacy celebrated for its bold garlic, mustard, and prawn flavors.

name: Kochur Mukhi Bharta (Taro Root / Arbi Mash)

ingredients.name: Kochur Mukhi / Gathi Kochu / Arbi (Taro Root)

steps.text: Wash taro roots and boil or pressure-cook with skins on until soft, then cool slightly and slip off the skins.
Mash the peeled taro roots smoothly with chopped onion, crushed roasted garlic and chillies, lemon juice, salt, and mustard oil.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve warm with steamed rice and dal.

notes: Creamy texture that pairs wonderfully with plain masoor or moong dal.

name: Koi Phulkopi Bori Jhol (Climbing Perch, Winter Cauliflower & Fried Bori Light Curry)

steps.section: Fry bori, cauliflower and koi fish
steps.text: Fry the bori in mustard oil until golden and remove; golden-roast the cauliflower florets and potato wedges, then fry the scored koi fish until golden brown.

steps.section: Simmer winter jhol and finish with bhaja moshla
steps.text: Temper oil with whole cumin and bay leaf, cook ginger paste, turmeric, and cumin powder, add 2 cups warm water, potatoes, cauliflower, koi fish, and fried bori, and simmer until tender; sprinkle roasted cumin-coriander powder.

notes: One of Bengal's most celebrated winter fish curries combining Koi mach, fresh phulkopi, and bori.

name: Kokum Sharbat

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Kolkata Cabin-Style Fish Fry (Crumb-Fried Bhetki Fillet with Kasundi)

ingredients.name: Boneless Kolkata Bhetki Fish Fillets (Thin Rectangular Fillets)

steps.section: Marinate Bhetki fillets in green herb paste
steps.text: Marinate Bhetki fillets first with lemon juice, salt, and black pepper, then coat in a vibrant paste of coriander, mint, green chillies, ginger, and garlic for 20 minutes.

steps.section: Double-crumb coat into classic diamond shape
steps.text: Dust each fillet with cornflour, dip in beaten egg, press firmly in biscuit crumbs, dip in egg a second time, and coat again in crumbs, shaping the edges neatly with a flat knife.

steps.section: Deep-fry golden and serve with kasundi
steps.text: Deep-fry in medium-hot oil until crisp and golden brown. Serve hot with pungent Bengali kasundi and thinly sliced onion-cucumber salad.

notes: The crown jewel of College Street and Golpark cabins—double-crumbed Bhetki Fish Fry.

name: Kolkata Chicken Kabiraji Cutlet (Crispy Spun Egg-Net Coated Chicken Cutlet)

steps.section: Shape and crumb-coat spiced chicken cutlets
steps.text: Mix minced chicken with ginger-garlic, onion, mint, coriander, green chilli, black pepper, garam masala, and salt. Shape into flat rectangular cutlets and coat in breadcrumbs.

steps.section: Wrap in lacy fried egg web
steps.text: Whisk eggs with a pinch of cornflour and water; drizzle from your fingertips over hot oil to form a lacy golden egg net, place the fried cutlet at the edge, and roll it up inside the crisp egg web.

notes: Famous North Kolkata heritage cabin delicacy derived from the 'Coverage' cutlet.

name: Kolkata Hing-er Kachori & Aloor Torkari (Club Kachori with Spiced Potato Curry)

ingredients.name: Potatoes (with Skin) for Street-style Aloor Torkari

steps.text: Temper mustard oil with panch phoron, dry red chillies, and hing; add cubed skin-on potatoes, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli, water, and black salt, simmering into a thick, tangy gravy.

steps.section: Stuff and fry crisp hing-er kachoris
steps.text: Stuff maida dough balls with spiced hing-urad dal paste (or knead into club kachori dough), roll into small discs, and deep-fry until puffed and crisp. Serve hot with the potato curry and bhujia.

notes: Burrabazar and Sovabazar's iconic morning street breakfast.

name: Kolkata Jhalmuri (Spiced Puffed Rice with Chanachur, Coconut & Mustard Oil)

ingredients.name: Pungent Raw Mustard Oil (Kacha Shorsher Tel)

steps.section: Combine muri and fresh crunchy mix-ins
steps.text: In a large mixing tin, combine puffed rice, chanachur, diced boiled potato, sprouted kala chana, chopped onion, cucumber, green chillies, coriander, and coconut slivers.

steps.section: Toss with bhaja masala and raw mustard oil
steps.text: Sprinkle jhalmuri bhaja masala, bitnoon, lemon juice, and pungent raw mustard oil. Shake and toss vigorously for 30 seconds and serve in paper cones (thonga).

notes: The unmistakable aroma of raw mustard oil and roasted bhaja masala defines authentic Kolkata Jhalmuri.

name: Kolkata Mutton Mughlai Paratha (Crispy Golden Deep-Fried Paratha Stuffed with Spiced Mutton Mince & Egg)

steps.section: Mix egg and mutton keema filling
steps.text: Beat eggs with chopped onion, green chillies, ginger, cooked dry mutton keema, biscuit crumbs, garam masala, black pepper, and salt.

steps.section: Stretch thin and fold envelope parcel
steps.text: Roll maida dough into a large thin translucent square on an oiled board, pour the egg-mutton filling in the center, and fold all four edges to make a neat rectangular envelope.
Gently slide into hot oil and fry slowly for 5-6 minutes on each side until puffed, flaky, and golden brown. Cut into squares and serve with aloor dum, salad, and mustard.

notes: The crowning glory of Kolkata cabin dining (such as Mitra Cafe and Anadi Cabin).

name: Kolkata Phuchka (Crisp Semolina Shells with SpicedAloo & Tangy Tetul Jol)

ingredients.name: Bengali Bhaja Masala (Roasted Cumin, Coriander & Dry Red Chilli Powder)

steps.section: Prepare spicy Kolkata phuchka aloo mash
steps.text: Mash boiled potatoes with boiled kala chana, crushed green chillies, chopped coriander, generous bhaja masala, bitnoon, and a splash of tamarind water.
Dissolve tamarind pulp in chilled water with bitnoon, roasted cumin-chilli bhaja masala, grated ginger, crushed green chillies, coriander leaves, and fragrant Gondhoraj lime juice.
Crack the top of each crisp phuchka, stuff with spiced potato mash, dunk into the tangy tetul jol, and serve immediately (finished with a dry 'sukha phuchka'!).

notes: Unlike pani puri elsewhere, authentic Kolkata Phuchka uses zero sweet chutney and relies on smoky bhaja masala, kala chana, bitnoon, and Gondhoraj-scented tetul jol.

name: Kolkata Special Egg Chicken Mughlai Paratha (Double Egg & Spiced Minced Chicken Stuffed Crispy Fried Paratha)

steps.text: Whisk eggs with cooked minced chicken, chopped onion, chillies, biscuit powder, roasted spices, pepper, and salt.
Roll dough very thin, spread chicken-egg filling, fold into a rectangular packet, and seal edges with light pressing.
Shallow fry on medium heat until the envelope is delightfully crisp outside and thoroughly cooked inside. Serve with spicy potato curry.

notes: The ubiquitous Kolkata street-side mughlai paratha stuffed with spicy chicken and whipped eggs.

name: Kolkata Street-Style Egg Chowmein (Wok-Tossed Hakka Noodles with Egg & Salad)

steps.section: Scramble eggs and stir-fry julienned vegetables
steps.text: Heat oil in a smoking-hot wok, scramble the eggs with a pinch of salt and set aside. Stir-fry garlic, green chillies, onions, cabbage, carrot, and capsicum on high flame for 2 minutes so they stay crunchy.

steps.section: Toss noodles on high flame and garnish
steps.text: Add boiled Hakka noodles, scrambled eggs, soy sauce, vinegar, black pepper, and chilli sauce; toss vigorously. Serve hot topped with raw cucumber-onion juliennes, tomato ketchup, green chilli sauce, and a handful of salted peanuts.

notes: Kolkata para-corner Egg Chowmein is famously served with raw cucumber-onion salad and a drizzle of ketchup & chilli sauce on top.

name: Kolkata Style Garam Chanachur (Bengali Spicy Besan Sev, Peanut & Curry Leaf Mixture)

steps.section: Press and fry crisp besan sev and boondi
steps.text: Knead spiced besan and rice flour dough with hot oil and press through a sev maker into hot oil to make crunchy sev and khara boondi.

steps.section: Fry chira, peanuts, lentils, and curry leaves
steps.text: In a mesh strainer, flash-fry thick chira, raw peanuts, cashews, soaked/dried chana dal, and fresh curry leaves until crisp.

steps.section: Toss warm with Bengali chanachur masala
steps.text: Combine all warm fried components in a wide bowl and toss thoroughly with black salt, amchur, roasted cumin-coriander powder, chilli powder, and hing.

notes: Signature Kolkata tea-time and jhalmuri chanachur bursting with smoky spices and curry leaves.

name: Kolkata Telebhaja Platter (Street-Style Beguni, Peyaji & Phuluri)

steps.section: Whisk airy besan batter and onion-peyaji mix
steps.text: Whisk besan, rice flour, kalo jeere, posto, turmeric, chilli powder, salt, and a pinch of soda into an airy batter for beguni and phuluri. Mix sliced onions and green chillies with coarse besan for peyaji.

steps.section: Deep-fry crisp beguni, peyaji and phuluri
steps.text: Dip eggplant slices in batter and fry until puffed into golden begunis; drop small batter balls for fluffy phuluris; and fry lacy onion clusters into crisp peyajis. Sprinkle with bitnoon and serve with muri.

notes: The heart of Kolkata's evening adda—hot telebhaja with puffed rice (muri) and adrak chai.

name: Kolmi no Patio (Parsi Sweet, Sour & Spicy Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Heat oil with curry leaves and fry finely chopped onions until deep golden brown.
Add garlic-cumin-chilli paste and turmeric, sauté for 2 minutes, then add tomatoes and cook down into a thick, jammy masala.

steps.section: Simmer prawns with jaggery and vinegar
steps.text: Add prawns, jaggery, vinegar, and salt; cook for 5-6 minutes until prawns are tender and the sweet-sour-spicy balance comes together.

notes: Traditionally served alongside Parsi yellow dal (Dhan Dar) and steamed rice.

name: Komola Bhog / Kamalabhog (Bengali Orange-Flavored Chhena Rasgulla)

ingredients.name: Drop of Food-grade Orange Extract or Saffron-orange Tint

steps.text: Knead drained chhena with the heel of your palm for 8–10 minutes with suji, fine orange zest, and orange tint until smooth; roll into crack-free balls.
Bring sugar and 4 cups water to a rolling boil, drop in the chhena balls, and cook covered on medium-high heat for 18 minutes until doubled in size.

steps.section: Infuse with fresh orange juice and chill
steps.text: Turn off the heat, stir strained sweet orange juice into the warm syrup, and let the komolabhog soak for 3–4 hours before serving chilled.

notes: Fragrant winter Bengali rasgulla variation infused with real Nagpur/Darjeeling orange flavor.

name: Kora Pak Nolen Gur Sandesh (Firm Winter Date Palm Jaggery Sandesh)

ingredients.name: Patali Gur / Nolen Gur (Crushed Date Palm Jaggery)

steps.section: Grind chhena and patali gur until ultra-smooth
steps.text: Knead or pulse fresh chhena with crushed Patali Gur and 1 tsp rice flour until completely smooth and lump-free.

steps.section: Cook over low flame to kora pak (firm stage)
steps.text: Cook the mixture in a heavy kadai over very low flame, stirring continuously for 15–18 minutes until moisture evaporates and the dough pulls cleanly from the sides.
While still warm, press portions into greased conch or floral sandesh moulds, unmould carefully, and top with pistachio slivers.

notes: Traditional long-keeping firm ('kora pak') Bengali sandesh stamped in intricate wooden or clay moulds.

name: Koraishutir Kochuri (Bengali Green Peas Stuffed Puri)

steps.text: Blend green peas, ginger, and green chillies into a smooth paste. Heat 1 tbsp oil with hing, add the pea paste, roasted cumin-coriander powder, salt, and sugar, and stir-cook until it leaves the sides of the pan.
Knead maida with 2 tbsp ghee, salt, and warm water into a pliable dough. Fill each dough cup with a ball of cooled pea stuffing, seal, and roll gently.
Deep-fry in hot oil until puffed and lightly golden. Serve with notun aloor dum and nolen gurer payesh.

notes: The quintessential Bengali winter breakfast and feast delicacy.

name: Kothimbir Vadi (Maharashtrian Crispy Steamed & Pan-Fried Fresh Coriander, Peanut & Besan Fritter Squares)

ingredients.name: Fresh Coriander Leaves (Washed, Dried & Finely Chopped)

steps.section: Mix coriander-rich besan dough and steam
steps.text: Combine finely chopped coriander leaves, besan, rice flour, crushed peanuts, sesame seeds, ajwain, green chilli-garlic paste, spices, lemon juice, 1 tbsp oil, and minimal water into a thick dough/batter. Pat into a greased tray, top with sesame seeds, and steam on medium-high heat for 15 minutes until firm.
Let the steamed cake cool completely, then slice into neat squares or rectangles.
Shallow-fry the squares in hot groundnut oil with mustard seeds and curry leaves until crisp and golden brown on both sides. Serve with green chutney.

notes: Uses twice the volume of fresh coriander leaves to gram flour so every bite bursts with herbaceous aroma and peanut crunch.

name: Kozhukattai (Sweet)

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Kucho Chingri Bhaja (Crispy Fried Small Shrimps with Onion & Chilli)

steps.text: Wash tiny shrimps thoroughly in a colander, drain completely, and toss with salt and turmeric powder.
Heat mustard oil in a wide pan, add the shrimps, and fry over medium-high heat until moisture evaporates and they turn crisp.
Add sliced onions and green chillies, stir-fry until onions are golden-brown, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Crunchy, savory Bengali starter accompaniment for hot rice and masoor dal.

name: Kucho Nimki (Bengali Crispy Diamond-Cut Kalonji Savory Crackers)

steps.section: Rub shortening into flour and knead stiff dough
steps.text: Rub ghee, salt, sugar, kalonji, and ajwain into maida for 4–5 minutes until it holds a breadcrumb texture, then add minimal water to knead a stiff dough and rest 15 minutes.

steps.section: Roll thin and cut into small diamonds
steps.text: Roll the dough into a thin sheet and slice crosswise with a knife into bite-sized 0.75-inch diamond shapes.
Drop the diamonds into medium-low heat oil and fry slowly, stirring constantly, until evenly golden-brown and crisp; cool and store in an airtight jar.

notes: Quintessential Bengali tea-time and Bijoya Dashami savory snack that stays crisp for weeks.

name: Kulcha

Heat mustard oil in a flat pan and fry the pumpkin slices in a single layer for 3-4 minutes per side until caramelized, golden-charred on the outside, and creamy inside.

steps.section: Clean blossoms and prepare crisp batter
steps.text: Gently rinse pumpkin blossoms, remove the inner stamen, and pat dry. Whisk rice flour, besan, posto, kalo jeere, turmeric, chilli powder, and salt with cold water into a smooth batter.

steps.section: Flatten and shallow-fry until lacy and crisp
steps.text: Dip each blossom in batter, lay flat in hot mustard oil, and fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and paper-crisp.

notes: Delicate, shatteringly crisp Bengali pumpkin flower fry.

name: Kumro Phooler Bora (Bengali Crispy Pumpkin Blossom Fritters)

ingredients.name: Rice Flour (Chaler Guro) or Soaked Ground Gobindobhog Rice Paste

steps.section: Clean and dry pumpkin flowers gently
steps.text: Snip off the spiky green calyx and inner stamen from each pumpkin blossom, rinse gently in cold water, and pat dry on a kitchen towel.

steps.section: Coat in crisp rice-posto batter and fry
steps.text: Fold each blossom flat, dip into a batter of rice flour, besan, poppy seeds, kalo jeere, turmeric, green chilli paste, and salt, and fry in hot mustard oil until lace-crisp.

notes: Using half rice flour and half besan keeps the delicate pumpkin blossoms crisp for longer.

name: Kumro Pui Shak Bori Chorchori (Malabar Spinach, Sweet Red Pumpkin & Bori Panch-Phoron Medley)

ingredients.name: Biulir Daler Bori or Masoor Daler Bori

steps.section: Fry bori and sauté pumpkin, potato and pui stems
steps.text: Fry the bori in mustard oil until crisp and remove; temper oil with panch phoron, dry red chilli, and bay leaf, then sauté potato, pumpkin, and thick pui stems with ginger, turmeric, and cumin.

steps.section: Wilt pui leaves with mustard paste and fold in bori
steps.text: Add chopped pui leaves, salt, and 1 tbsp mustard paste, cover until stems are tender, and fold in the fried bori (half whole, half crushed) and a pinch of sugar.

notes: The sweetness of red pumpkin balances the earthy Malabar spinach and crispy fried lentil dumplings.

name: Kumro Shak Bori Chorchori (Pumpkin Vine Greens, Stems, Potato & Crushed Bori Medley)

ingredients.name: Biulir Daler Bori or Masoor Daler Bori

steps.section: Fry bori and sauté vegetables with panch phoron
steps.text: Fry the bori in mustard oil until golden-brown and set aside; temper oil with panch phoron and dry red chilli, and sauté potato, sweet pumpkin, brinjal, and pumpkin stems.

steps.section: Braise pumpkin greens with mustard-poppy paste and bori
steps.text: Add pumpkin leaves, turmeric, salt, and mustard-poppy paste, cover and cook until tender, and finish with half-crushed fried bori and a pinch of sugar.

notes: Peeling the fibrous outer strings off the pumpkin vine stems ensures a melt-in-the-mouth chorchori.
