name: Kumror Bora / Mishti Kumro Fritters (Crispy Sweet Red Pumpkin Fritters)

steps.text: Cut peeled sweet pumpkin into thin uniform slices and toss with a pinch of salt and turmeric.

steps.section: Dip in rice-besan batter and fry
steps.text: Whisk besan, rice flour, kalo jeere, posto, turmeric, chilli powder, a pinch of sugar, and water into a smooth batter; dip pumpkin slices and fry in medium-hot oil until tender inside and crisp outside.

notes: The sweet, creamy pumpkin interior contrasts beautifully with the savory kalo-jeere crust.

name: Kundru Bharta (Ivy Gourd / Tendli / Telakucha Mash)

steps.text: Wash ivy gourds, trim the ends, and slice into rounds or halves.
Sauté in mustard oil with cumin/nigella seeds, garlic, and green chillies covered over low heat until soft and lightly browned.
Coarsely mash or pulse with chopped onion, salt, and coriander leaves.

notes: Pan-roasting kundru brings out a pleasant nutty flavour.

name: Kundru Fry / Kudri Bhaja (Crispy Ivy Gourd / Tendli Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Lengthwise into Quarters or Thin Rounds

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and dry red chilli, add sliced kundru with turmeric and salt, and stir-fry uncovered until tender and browned at the edges.
Sprinkle Kashmiri chilli, coriander, and roasted cumin powder and toss on high heat for 2 minutes.

notes: Slicing kundru thin and cooking uncovered keeps it crisp rather than soggy.

name: Kundrur Bora / Tendli Pakora (Crispy Batter-Fried Ivy Gourd Fritters)

steps.section: Toss lengthwise kundru strips with spices and flours
steps.text: Toss sliced ivy gourd with ginger-chilli paste, turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli, cumin, salt, besan, rice flour, and sesame/poppy seeds, sprinkling a little water so the dry batter coats each strip.
Scatter the coated kundru strips into hot oil and fry over medium-high flame until crisp; toss with chaat masala before serving.

notes: Makes an addictive crunchy side dish for dal-chawal or khichdi.

name: Kurkure Posto Aloo Bhaja (Bengali Poppy Seed Crusted Crispy Potatoes)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with dry red chillies and nigella seeds, and fry cubed potatoes with turmeric and salt until golden and tender.
Sprinkle whole white poppy seeds (posto) and slit green chillies over the potatoes and stir-fry on medium-high flame for 3-4 minutes until the posto toasts nutty and crunchy.

notes: Toasted poppy seeds form a crunchy, nutty crust around the fried potatoes.

name: Kurkure Veg Momo (Extra-Crunchy Crushed Cornflakes-Coated Fried Momos)

steps.section: Batter-dip and coat in crushed cornflakes
steps.text: Whisk maida, cornflour, chilli powder, garlic powder, salt, and water into a smooth slurry. Dip each steamed momo into the slurry, then roll thoroughly in hand-crushed cornflakes.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil for 3–4 minutes until golden and crackling crisp. Dust with chaat masala and serve hot.

notes: Crush cornflakes inside a clean bag with a rolling pin—no grinder needed.

name: Kurkuri Besan Bhindi / Rajasthani Besan Wali Bhindi (Crispy Gram Flour & Fennel-Spiced Okra Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Tender Okra (Bhindi, Washed, Wiped Dry & Slit Lengthwise)

steps.section: Toss dry slit okra with spices and lemon
steps.text: Toss julienned/slit okra with turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder, crushed fennel, amchur, lemon juice, and salt.

steps.section: Coat with besan and rice flour
steps.text: Sprinkle roasted besan and rice flour over the spiced okra and toss gently so a light, even crust adheres to every piece.
Heat mustard oil in a wide cast-iron kadai, temper ajwain and hing, and sear the besan-coated bhindi in batches over medium-high flame for 10–12 minutes until golden and crunchy.

notes: Wiping the okra completely dry before slicing and adding salt just before pan-roasting keeps the bhindi super crisp and non-sticky.

name: Kurkuri Bhindi Fry (Spiced Gram-Flour Crusted Crispy Okra Fry)

steps.section: Julienne okra and toss in dry spice-flour coating
steps.text: Slice okra into thin lengthwise strips, toss with lemon juice, spices, besan, and rice flour just before frying.
Fry in batches in hot oil until crisp and golden; finish with a sprinkle of chaat masala.

notes: Ultra-crunchy restaurant-style Kurkuri Bhindi Fry.

name: Labanga Latika / Lavang Latika (Traditional Bengali Clove-Sealed Crisp Mawa Pastry in Sugar Syrup)

steps.text: Roast mawa with grated coconut, powdered sugar, cardamom powder, and chopped cashews until fragrant and thick; let cool completely.

steps.section: Fold pastry parcels and pin with whole clove
steps.text: Knead maida with melted ghee and cold water into a smooth dough. Roll into small thin squares, place stuffing in center, fold all 4 corners like an envelope, and pierce through the center with a whole clove to lock the parcel.

steps.section: Deep fry and soak in syrup
steps.text: Fry in medium-low ghee for 10-12 minutes until golden brown and flaky. Drop immediately into warm 1-string cardamom sugar syrup for 5 minutes.

notes: An iconic heirloom Bengali pastry where the whole clove infuses an intoxicating spicy aroma into the sweet mawa parcel.

name: Lal Shak Bori Bhaja (Red Amaranth Greens Stir-Fried with Crushed Crispy Bori & Peanuts)

ingredients.name: Biulir Daler Bori or Masoor Daler Bori

steps.section: Fry bori and peanuts and crush bori coarsely
steps.text: Fry the bori (and peanuts if using) in mustard oil until crisp and golden, remove, and coarsely crush the fried bori.

steps.section: Stir-fry lal shak with kalo jeere and top with crushed bori
steps.text: Temper oil with dry red chilli and kalo jeere, add chopped lal shak and salt, cook until wilted and dry, and toss with crushed fried bori and toasted poppy seeds right before serving.

notes: An everyday Bengali first-course shak dish where crispy crushed bori adds irresistible texture.

name: Lau Bharta (Bottle Gourd Mash)

steps.text: Peel the bottle gourd, remove any large seeds, and grate or chop finely.
Simmer the bottle gourd covered in its own juices with a pinch of salt until soft, then uncover and cook until excess water evaporates.
Heat mustard oil, temper with nigella seeds, garlic, onion, and green chillies, add the cooked gourd, and mash on the pan until cohesive. Garnish with coriander.

notes: Light, cooling, and easy to digest.

name: Lau Bori Ghonto (Bengali Bottle Gourd Mash with Crushed Fried Biulir Daler Bori & Coriander)

steps.section: Fry bori and temper cumin and bay leaf
steps.text: Fry the bori in mustard oil until deep golden, remove, and crush half of them coarsely; in the same oil, crackle bay leaf, dry red chilli, and whole cumin seeds.

steps.section: Slow-cook julienned bottle gourd in its own juice
steps.text: Add finely chopped bottle gourd, grated ginger, turmeric, cumin powder, green chillies, and salt; cover and cook over medium-low heat without adding water until soft and melted.

steps.section: Fold in whole and crushed bori with coriander
steps.text: Stir in a pinch of sugar, both whole and crushed fried bori, and chopped fresh coriander leaves; simmer 2 minutes until cohesive.

notes: A cooling, quintessential Bengali summer lunch dish where crushed bori thickens the delicate bottle gourd juices.

name: Lau Chingri (Bottle Gourd with Prawns)

steps.text: Season cleaned prawns with salt and turmeric, sear lightly in mustard oil for 2 minutes, and set aside.
Temper oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and cumin seeds. Sauté ginger paste and cumin-coriander powder, then add finely cubed bottle gourd and salt. Cover and let it cook in its own juices.
Add fried prawns, slit green chillies, and a pinch of sugar. Simmer until tender, then finish with chopped coriander leaves and a drop of ghee.

notes: One of the most iconic, comforting heirloom dishes of every Bengali household.

name: Lau Diye Macher Dimer Borar Jhol (Bottle Gourd & Fish Egg Fritter Curry)

steps.text: Whisk fish eggs with chopped onion, besan, salt, and turmeric; fry into golden boras and set aside.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste and turmeric, and cook cubed bottle gourd covered until tender.
Add a splash of warm water, roasted cumin powder, fried fish egg boras, slit green chillies, and fresh coriander; simmer for 5 minutes.

notes: Light, comforting bottle gourd curry enriched with savory fish roe dumplings.

Heat mustard oil, splutter nigella seeds, add the ground paste and salt, and cook over medium heat until thick and aromatic.

notes: Use fresh, tender bottle gourd skins for a smooth, non-fibrous texture.

steps.section: Fry bori and sauté potato, brinjal and lau stems
steps.text: Fry the bori in mustard oil until golden and remove; temper oil with kalo jeere and dry red chilli, and fry potato wedges, brinjal, and peeled bottle gourd stems.

steps.section: Simmer with lau leaves, posto-shorshe and fried bori
steps.text: Add chopped bottle gourd leaves, salt, turmeric, and posto-shorshe paste with ¼ cup water; cook covered until soft, then fold in fried bori and a drizzle of raw mustard oil.

notes: Soft bottle gourd greens and crisp-chewy bori in poppy-mustard paste are a staple of Bengali home cooking.

name: Lauer Bora / Lau Khoshar Bora (Crispy Bottle Gourd & Bottle Gourd Peel Fritters)

ingredients.name: Bottle Gourd (Lau) or Julienned Tender Bottle Gourd Peel (Lau Khosha)

steps.section: Squeeze excess moisture and bind with flours
steps.text: Salt the grated bottle gourd (or finely shredded bottle gourd peel) for 5 minutes, squeeze out excess water, and mix with besan, rice flour, poppy seeds, kalo jeere, green chillies, and turmeric without adding extra water.
Shape into small flat discs and shallow-fry in hot mustard oil over medium heat until both sides are deep golden and crunchy.

notes: Zero-waste Bengali home cooking that turns tender bottle gourd or its peel into a crunchy meal starter.

name: Lauki / Doodhi Milk Pudding (Sweet Cardamom Bottle Gourd Pudding)

steps.text: Heat desi ghee in a heavy pan, fry cashews and raisins until golden and set aside. In the same ghee, add grated bottle gourd and saute on medium flame for 6-8 minutes until moisture evaporates and raw scent disappears.

Pour 4 cups full-cream milk into the pan. Stir well and bring to a boil. Simmer on medium-low flame for 15 minutes, stirring often, until the lauki becomes tender and translucent and the milk reduces to a thick creamy consistency.
Add sugar, cardamom powder, saffron, and fried dry fruits. Simmer for another 4-5 minutes until rich and thick. Serve warm in winter or chilled during summer months.

notes: A nutritious, melt-in-the-mouth traditional dessert that turns humble bottle gourd into a royal milk pudding.

name: Lauki Paratha / Doodhi Paratha (Spiced Grated Bottle Gourd Stuffed Whole Wheat Paratha)

steps.text: Salt grated bottle gourd, squeeze out excess juice completely (use juice to knead dough!), and toss with ginger, chillies, ajwain, amchur, cumin, and roasted besan.
Pack lauki mixture inside dough portions, dust with flour, and roll out gently.
Cook on griddle with ghee until speckled with golden blisters. Serve warm with homemade raita.

notes: A light, gut-friendly Ayurvedic stuffed flatbread celebrated for its cooling properties.

name: Ledikeni / Ladykini (Bengali Fried Chhena & Semolina Sweet in Rose-Cardamom Syrup)

steps.section: Knead chhena-suji dough and stuff with raisin
steps.text: Knead chhena, suji, maida, melted ghee, and a pinch of baking soda into a smooth dough; shape into oval balls with a raisin and cardamom seed tucked in the center.
Simmer sugar and water with crushed green cardamom pods for 8 minutes until sticky.

steps.section: Deep-fry until dark reddish-brown and soak
steps.text: Fry the ovals over low heat until deep reddish-brown, then transfer into hot syrup and soak for 1–2 hours until soft and juicy.

notes: Created in 1858 by Bhim Chandra Nag in Kolkata in honor of Lady Canning.

name: Lemon Black Tea

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Lemon Coriander Prawn Soup

steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in a saucepan and sauté minced garlic, ginger, chopped green chilli, and coriander stems for 1 minute.
Pour in stock, bring to a boil, and add diced vegetables and prawns. Simmer for 4-5 minutes until prawns turn pink and tender.
Stir in optional cornflour slurry, season with black pepper and salt, switch off heat, and add fresh lemon juice and coriander leaves.

notes: Light, immunity-boosting soup rich in Vitamin C and lean protein.

name: Lemon Coriander Soup (Immunity-Boosting Clear Vegetable Broth with Fresh Lemon & Cilantro)

steps.text: Heat oil in a wok, saute minced ginger, garlic, green chillies, and finely chopped coriander stems for 2 minutes to extract essential citrusy oils.
Add minced carrots, cabbage, and sweet corn. Pour in vegetable stock, season with salt and black pepper, and boil for 5 minutes.
Stir in cornflour slurry to give light body. Turn off heat, immediately stir in fresh lemon juice and chopped coriander leaves to preserve freshness and vitamin C.

notes: Always add lemon juice after turning off heat; boiling citrus juice can turn the soup bitter.

name: Lemon Green Tea

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Lemon Honey Tea

name: Lemon Rice

steps.text: Wash rice until the water runs mostly clear; soak briefly if appropriate.
Heat ghee or oil, add spices and vegetables if using, and stir until fragrant.
Add rice and measured water, cover and cook until tender. Rest briefly before serving.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Lemon Soda (Sweet or Salted)

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Lilva Kachori (Crispy Fresh Tuvar / Green Pigeon Pea Stuffed Kachori)

steps.text: Heat oil with hing and sesame seeds. Add crushed green tuvar, ginger-chilli paste, coconut, garam masala, salt, and sugar. Sauté on low flame until cooked through and moisture dries, then finish with lemon juice.
Knead maida with warm ghee and water. Roll small rounds, place a spoonful of lilva mixture in center, pleat the edges to form a sealed round kachori or potli.
Fry on low-medium heat until the crust becomes golden, blister-free, and crispy. Serve with green coriander chutney and sweet tamarind sonth.

notes: Famous Gujarati and West Indian winter harvest delicacy made when fresh green tuvar is in season.

name: Lomba Begun Fry / Begun Sundori (Bengali Boat-Cut Long Brinjal Fry)

steps.text: Halve slender brinjals lengthwise keeping the green crown/stem intact, and rub with turmeric, chilli powder, and salt.

steps.section: Fry cut-side down then skin-side down
steps.text: Shallow-fry in hot mustard oil until the flesh is golden-caramelized and the purple skin is blistered and tender.

notes: Festive Bengali bhoj-style long brinjal fry served with basanti polao or khichuri.

name: Luchi

steps.text: Rub oil into flour, add water gradually and knead into a smooth firm dough. Rest covered.
Divide into small balls and roll each into a small round disc.
Deep-fry one at a time in hot oil, gently pressing so each luchi puffs.

name: Lyangcha / Shaktigarh Style Langcha (Elongated Khoya & Chhena Fried Sweet in Syrup)

steps.section: Knead chhena-khoya dough and shape elongated cylinders
steps.text: Knead chhena, khoya, maida, ghee, baking soda, and crushed cardamom seeds for 10 minutes until silky, then roll into 3.5-inch cylindrical logs.
Boil sugar and 2 cups water with cardamom pods for 7 minutes into a thin, hot syrup.

steps.section: Deep-fry until dark mahogany and soak
steps.text: Fry the cylinders over low heat until dark mahogany-brown, then plunge into hot syrup and soak for 1–2 hours until plump.

notes: Famous highway delicacy of Shaktigarh in Purba Bardhaman, West Bengal.

name: Lychee Coconut Jelly Pudding (Fragrant Lychee Pulp & Coconut Milk Layered Agar Pudding)

steps.text: In a saucepan, whisk 1.25 tsp agar agar with 0.5 cup water, sugar, and coconut milk. Simmer for 3 minutes until agar dissolves completely. Pour into transparent dessert cups or a square mould until half-filled. Chill for 15 minutes until just firm on the surface.
In another pan, dissolve remaining 1.25 tsp agar agar in 0.5 cup water and lychee juice. Simmer for 3 minutes. Remove from heat and gently stir in chopped lychees.
Gently ladle the warm lychee mixture over the set coconut layer so the layers do not mix. Refrigerate for 2 hours until fully set. Unmould or serve chilled in cups.

notes: Beautiful translucent dual-layer dessert pairing tropical fragrant lychee with creamy, velvety coconut milk.

name: Macchiato

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Macher Dimer Bhapa (Bengali Steamed Mustard & Coconut Fish Eggs)

ingredients.name: Fish Eggs / Fish Roe (Hilsa, Rohu or Katla)

steps.text: Grind soaked mustard seeds, poppy seeds, grated coconut, 2 green chillies, and a pinch of salt with warm water into a smooth paste.

In a steel tiffin box, fold cleaned fish roe (whole lobes or lightly pan-seared pieces) with the ground paste, whisked yogurt, turmeric, salt, and 2 tbsp raw mustard oil. Top with slit green chillies.
Close the lid tightly and steam in a covered pot with boiling water reaching halfway up the box for 18-20 minutes.

notes: Traditional Bengali tiffin-box steamed fish roe dish; serve with steaming hot white rice.

name: Macher Dimer Bharta (Bengali Smoky Mashed Fish Egg with Mustard Oil)

steps.text: Fry dry red chillies and garlic cloves in 1.5 tbsp mustard oil until crisp and golden; set aside. Pan-fry turmeric-salted fish roe covered on low heat until cooked and lightly charred.
Crush the dry red chillies and roasted garlic with salt, then mash thoroughly with the cooked fish roe.

steps.section: Fold in raw onion and mustard oil
steps.text: Mix in finely chopped raw onion, green chillies, fresh coriander leaves, and 1 tbsp pungent raw mustard oil.

notes: Smoky, fiery Bengali bharta meant to be mixed into steaming hot white rice.

name: Macher Dimer Borar Dalna (Bengali Fish Egg Fritter & Potato Dalna)

steps.section: Fry fish roe fritters and potatoes
steps.text: Whisk fish eggs with chopped onion, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry round fritters in mustard oil. Fry potato cubes until golden.
Temper oil with bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves. Sauté onion, ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, and spice powders until oil separates.
Add fried potatoes and warm water; once potatoes soften, add the fish roe fritters, simmer 5 minutes, and finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Slightly richer than everyday jhol, with warm whole spices and a touch of ghee.

name: Macher Dimer Borar Kalia (Festive Spicy Fish Egg Fritter Kalia)

steps.text: Beat fish eggs with chopped onion, green chillies, besan, rice flour, turmeric, and salt; fry until golden and set aside.
Temper mustard oil with whole garam masala, brown the grated onions, and cook ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, whisked yogurt, and Kashmiri chilli powder until glossy.
Add warm water, bring to a boil, gently add the fish egg boras, and simmer for 5 minutes until plump and juicy.

notes: Plump fish egg boras absorb the rich yogurt-onion kalia gravy like sponges.

name: Macher Dimer Borar Tok (Bengali Sweet & Sour Tamarind Fish Egg Curry)

steps.text: Mix fish eggs with chopped onion, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry small fritters in mustard oil and set aside.
Temper 1 tbsp mustard oil with dry red chillies and panch phoron. Pour in strained tamarind pulp, water, mustard paste, turmeric, salt, and jaggery; boil for 5 minutes.
Drop the fried fish egg boras into the tangy-sweet broth and simmer for 4 minutes until soft and juicy.

notes: Traditional Bengali summer meal-ender (tok/ambol) that cools the palate.

name: Macher Dimer Chop (Bengali Spiced Fish Egg Croquettes)

steps.text: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic, and fish roe with spices until cooked through, then mash together with boiled potatoes, crushed peanuts, bhaja masala, and coriander.
Roll into round or oval chops and coat either in breadcrumbs or a thick spiced besan batter.
Deep-fry in hot oil until golden brown and serve hot with puffed rice (muri) or kasundi.

notes: A popular Bengali telebhaja variation for monsoon evenings.

name: Macher Dimer Cutlet (Kolkata Cabin-Style Fish Egg Cutlet)

steps.text: Sauté minced onion, ginger, garlic, and green chillies in 1 tbsp oil, add mashed fish eggs and turmeric, and cook until dry and crumbly. Mix with mashed potato, bhaja masala, garam masala, lemon juice, and coriander.
Shape cooled mixture into flat diamond or oval cutlets, dip in cornflour or egg wash, and coat twice with breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil until crisp and golden brown. Sprinkle black salt and serve with kasundi and onion salad.

notes: Crunchy Kolkata evening snack with a rich, savory fish egg center.

name: Macher Dimer Do Pyaza (Fish Egg Curry with Double Onions)

steps.section: Sear fish roe and onion petals
steps.text: Pan-sear seasoned fish roe slabs and cut into cubes. Toss onion petals and slit green chillies in hot oil for 2 minutes and set aside.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and dry red chilli, brown chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste, then cook chopped tomatoes and spice powders.
Add the fish roe cubes, sautéed onion petals, and a splash of water; simmer for 5 minutes and finish with garam masala and coriander.

notes: Sweet, crisp-tender onion petals contrast nicely with savory fish roe.

name: Macher Dimer Kalia (Bengali Rich Fish Egg Curry)

steps.text: Steam seasoned fish roe in a greased bowl for 8 minutes, cut into neat squares, and fry lightly in mustard oil.
Temper oil with bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Brown grated onions, then cook ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, yogurt, and spices until oil floats.
Add warm water and the fish roe squares, simmer for 6 minutes, and finish with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Steaming the fish roe into a cake before cutting gives neat, firm cubes for kalia.

name: Macher Dimer Korma (Creamy Cashew & Yogurt Fish Egg Korma)

ingredients.name: Fish Eggs / Fish Roe (Steamed or Fried Boras)

steps.text: Either pan-fry small spiced fish egg boras or lightly sear steamed fish roe cubes in ghee.
Temper ghee with cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaf. Sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste, then stir in whisked yogurt and cashew-poppy seed paste.
Add warm water, salt, sugar, and the fish roe pieces; simmer gently for 6 minutes and top with crushed fried onions (birista).

notes: Delicate, mildly spiced korma that pairs beautifully with pulao or paratha.

name: Macher Dimer Narkel Bora (Fish Egg & Grated Coconut Fritters)

steps.text: Mash the cleaned fish eggs in a bowl with freshly grated coconut, chopped onion, green chillies, turmeric, salt, and a tiny pinch of sugar.
Fold in besan and rice flour to form a thick, cohesive batter.
Flatten spoonfuls of the mixture in hot mustard oil and shallow-fry on medium-low heat until golden brown on both sides.

notes: Grated coconut keeps the interior of the fish egg fritters moist and subtly sweet.

name: Macher Dimer Omelette Curry (Bengali Fish Egg Omelette Dalna)

ingredients.name: Egg (Beaten with Fish Roe for Omelette) or 2 Tbsp Besan

steps.section: Make fish roe omelette and cut into diamonds
steps.text: Beat cleaned fish roe with 1 egg (or besan), half the chopped onion, green chillies, salt, and turmeric. Cook as a thick pancake in mustard oil on low heat, then cut into diamond pieces.
Fry potato cubes in oil, temper with bay leaf and whole spices, and sauté remaining onion, ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and ground spices.
Add warm water and cook until potatoes are soft, then gently add the fish roe omelette diamonds, simmer 5 minutes, and finish with garam masala.

notes: Cutting a thick pan-cooked fish roe omelette into diamonds creates soft, uniform pieces that hold up beautifully in gravy.

name: Macher Dimer Paturi (Banana Leaf Wrapped Mustard Fish Eggs)

steps.text: Combine cleaned fish eggs with smooth mustard-poppy seed paste, grated coconut, finely chopped onion, turmeric, salt, and raw mustard oil.
Spoon portions onto oiled, flame-softened banana leaves, top each with a slit green chilli, fold into neat square parcels, and tie with cotton thread.
Cook the banana leaf parcels on a lightly oiled covered tawa over low heat for 7-8 minutes per side until the leaves char and the roe sets firm.

notes: Charred banana leaves infuse the mustard-coated fish roe with an unmistakable smoky aroma.

name: Macher Jhol

steps.text: Season fish with salt and turmeric, then lightly fry on both sides and set aside.
Fry potato wedges; add tomato, cumin and turmeric and sauté until fragrant.
Add water and salt, cook potatoes until nearly tender, then add fish and simmer gently.

name: Macher Kochuri (Bengali Spiced Fish Keema Stuffed Puri)

ingredients.name: Boneless Fish Fillets (Bhetki or Rohu/Katla, Boiled and Flaked)

steps.text: Sauté onions and ginger-garlic in mustard oil until caramelized. Add flaked fish, mashed potato, turmeric, cumin, garam masala, kismis, chillies, and salt. Cook until dry and fragrant; mix in chopped coriander.
Knead maida with ghee, salt, and water. Divide into balls, hollow into cups, pack with fish stuffing, seal edges completely, and roll into rounds with gentle strokes.
Deep-fry in hot oil until puffed, crisp, and pale gold. Serve with kasundi mustard sauce and thinly sliced onions.

notes: An heirloom zamindari recipe from colonial Bengal celebrating freshwater fish.

name: Madatha Kaja / Tapeswaram Kaja (Andhra Crispy Multi-Layered Flaky Ribbon Pastry in Sugar Syrup)

ingredients.name: Rice Flour (Mixed with Ghee for Lamination)

steps.text: Knead maida with ghee and water into a soft dough. Roll into a very thin rectangular sheet, brush generously with ghee-rice flour paste, roll tightly into a swiss roll log, and slice diagonally into 1-inch diamond ribbons.
Gently press each diamond in the center with your thumb. Fry in low-medium oil for 12-15 minutes; the multiple concentric ribbon layers will separate and blossom into a flaky golden pastry.
Drop directly into warm one-string sugar syrup with cardamom and lemon juice for 10 minutes until the layers soak up the syrup.

notes: The famous Andhra delicacy from Tapeswaram: shatteringly crisp pastry layers that gush with sweet syrup with every bite.

name: Maddur Vada (Karnataka Crispy Layered Rice Flour, Semolina, Maida, Onion & Curry Leaf Flat Discs)

ingredients.name: Smoking-hot Oil or Ghee (3 Tbsp for Dough) + Oil

steps.section: Rub flours with smoking-hot oil and onions
steps.text: Mix rice flour, rava, maida, sesame seeds, crushed peanuts, hing, and salt; pour 3 tbsp smoking-hot oil over the flour and rub until crumbly. Add sliced onions, green chillies, curry leaves, and coriander, squeezing to release onion juices.

steps.section: Bind stiff dough and pat into thin discs
steps.text: Sprinkle warm water in small splashes to form a firm, non-sticky dough. Divide into balls and pat on greased parchment or banana leaf into 3.5-inch flat discs.

steps.section: Deep-fry on medium-low flame until flaky and crisp
steps.text: Fry in medium-hot oil, turning occasionally for 5–6 minutes until deep golden brown and crunchy throughout. Serve with coconut chutney.

notes: Famous railway-station snack from Maddur between Bengaluru and Mysuru—requires only pre-ground flours and no blender.

name: Maharashtrian Masala Bhat (Spiced Basmati / Kolam Rice with Tindora, Brinjal, Green Peas, Cashews & Goda Masala)

ingredients.name: Basmati or Ambemohar/kolam Rice (Washed & Soaked 15 Mins)
Tendli (Ivy Gourd / Kundru) or Baby Brinjal Cubes

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pot, crackle mustard seeds, cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, hing, and curry leaves. Fry cashews golden, then saute ginger-garlic-green chilli paste, sliced tendli/brinjal, potato, and green peas for 4–5 minutes.
Add turmeric, red chilli powder, Goda masala, salt, and drained rice; saute gently for 2 minutes so the grains are coated in aromatic spiced ghee.

steps.section: Simmer and garnish with coconut and ghee
steps.text: Pour 3 cups hot water, add a tiny pinch of jaggery, cover and cook on low flame for 12 minutes until tender. Fluff and garnish generously with fresh grated coconut, chopped coriander, and a drizzle of desi ghee.

notes: Traditional Maharashtrian festive one-pot spiced rice served with kadhi or koshimbir.

name: Maharashtrian Pithla (Comforting Creamy Tempered Gram Flour, Garlic & Green Chilli Curry for Bhakri)

steps.text: Whisk besan with 2.5 cups water and a pinch of salt until completely smooth.

steps.section: Prepare garlic, green chilli, and onion phodni
steps.text: Heat oil in a heavy pan, crackle mustard seeds, cumin, hing, and curry leaves. Saute pounded garlic-green chillies and chopped onion with turmeric until golden.

steps.section: Cook creamy pithla on low heat
steps.text: Lower flame, pour in the besan slurry while whisking continuously so no lumps form, then cover and simmer for 6–8 minutes until thick, glossy, and creamy. Top with fresh coriander and a drizzle of raw groundnut oil.

notes: Softer and creamier than dry Zunka; pairs effortlessly with hot jowar/bajra bhakri or steamed rice and ghee.

name: Maharashtrian Zunka (Dry Spiced Gram Flour, Onion, Garlic & Mustard-Curry Leaf Crumble)

ingredients.name: Kanda Lasun Masala / Red Chilli Powder

steps.text: Heat groundnut oil in a kadai, crackle mustard seeds, cumin, hing, and curry leaves. Add crushed garlic-green chilli paste and finely chopped onions; saute until translucent and fragrant.
Add turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, and dry besan directly into the onion mixture. Roast on low heat for 4 minutes until the gram flour turns aromatic.
Sprinkle 1/2 to 3/4 cup warm water in small splashes while stirring, cover with a lid for 4–5 minutes on low steam until cooked into a soft, moist crumble, and finish with generous fresh coriander.

notes: Maharashtra's iconic rural comfort food ('Zunka Bhakar'), traditionally served with hot jowar bhakri and raw onion.

name: Makai Kochuri (Spiced Sweet Corn & Coriander Stuffed Kachori)

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil, add hing and cumin seeds. Stir in ginger-chilli paste and crushed sweet corn. Cook for 5 minutes, then add roasted besan, chaat masala, amchur, salt, sugar, and coriander until thick and dry.
Knead flour with ghee, salt, and water into a smooth pliable dough. Place portions of corn filling inside dough balls, seal neatly, and roll out.
Fry in medium-hot oil until uniformly puffed and golden. Serve with spicy mint dip.

notes: Sweet and savory modern festive kochuri popular across North and West India.

name: Makhana & Peanut Jaggery Laddoo (Ghee-Roasted Fox Nut & Crushed Peanut Laddoo)

ingredients.name: Fox Nuts (Makhana, Roasted & Crushed By Rolling Pin)

steps.text: Roast makhana in 1 tbsp ghee on low heat for 6–7 minutes until brittle, cool, and crush coarsely inside a cloth with a rolling pin. Toast sesame seeds and mix with crushed makhana and peanuts.
Melt jaggery with remaining ghee and 2 tbsp water until soft-ball stage, toss in the makhana-peanut mix and cardamom, and roll into laddoos while warm.

notes: Light, crunchy calcium-rich laddoo great for fasting days and tea-time.

name: Malabar Parotta (Kerala Flaky Layered Coin Parotta)

steps.text: Knead maida, sugar, salt, milk, and water for 8-10 minutes until super elastic; coat generously with oil and rest 45 minutes.
Spread each oiled ball paper-thin on a greased counter, slice into thin ribbons or gather into a long pleated rope, and coil into a pinwheel.
Pat or gently roll into a disc, cook on a hot tawa with ghee until golden, and clap between both hands to fluff the ribbon layers.

notes: Iconic South Indian flaky parotta that pairs with Kerala chemmeen roast, chicken curry, or kurma.

name: Malai Chop

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Malai Ghevar (Rajasthani-Style Honeycomb Sweet Disc Topped with Saffron Rabri)

steps.text: Rub ghee with ice cubes until white and creamy, then whisk in maida, besan, chilled milk, and chilled water to form a thin, watery batter.

steps.section: Pour in thin streams into hot ghee mould
steps.text: Pour small ladlefuls of cold batter from a height into bubbling hot ghee inside a cylindrical ring mould so it sets into a lacy honeycomb disc; lift out when golden.

steps.section: Glaze with syrup and crown with saffron rabri
steps.text: Spoon warm 1-thread cardamom sugar syrup over the crisp ghevar disc, spread thick saffron rabri on top, and garnish with nuts.

notes: Festive lacy honeycomb pastry topped with creamy rabri and nuts.

name: Malai Kofta (Melt-in-Mouth Paneer & Potato Dumplings in Creamy Cashew-Saffron Gravy)

steps.section: Roll nut-stuffed paneer-potato koftas and deep-fry
steps.text: Mix grated paneer, dry-mashed boiled potato, cornflour, cardamom, and salt into a smooth dough, stuff with chopped cashews and raisins, roll into smooth balls, and deep-fry until golden brown.

steps.section: Prepare velvety makhani-cashew gravy and pour over koftas
steps.text: Cook the strained onion-tomato-cashew puree in butter with Kashmiri chilli, garam masala, kasuri methi, and cream until silky; spoon the hot gravy over the fried koftas right before serving so they don't break.

notes: Always pour the hot gravy over the fragile Malai Koftas at serving time rather than boiling them in the pot.

name: Malai Paneer Laddoo (Soft Crumbled Chhena, Milk & Cardamom Laddoo)

ingredients.name: Fresh Paneer or Chhena (Finely Grated/kneaded By Hand)

steps.section: Knead paneer smooth and simmer with condensed milk
steps.text: Mash fresh paneer/chhena with the heel of your palm for 3–4 minutes until creamy. Cook in a greased non-stick pan with condensed milk on low flame for 6–8 minutes, stirring constantly, until thick and leaving the sides.
Fold in cardamom powder, cool until warm, roll into smooth white laddoos, and garnish each with chopped pistachios and saffron.

notes: Melt-in-the-mouth Bengali sandesh-style malai laddoo ready in 25 minutes.

name: Malai Paneer Tikka (Creamy Cheese, Cardamom & White Pepper Marinated Roasted Paneer)

steps.section: Coat paneer in creamy cashew-cheese-cardamom marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd, fresh cream, grated cheese, cashew paste, cornflour, ginger-garlic paste, white pepper, cardamom powder, crushed kasuri methi, lemon juice, and salt; coat paneer and bell peppers and marinate 15 minutes.

steps.section: Pan-grill with butter until blistered and golden
steps.text: Sear on a hot buttered grill pan or cast-iron tawa turning gently until golden blisters form on all sides.

notes: Mild, melt-in-the-mouth creamy starter scented with green cardamom and white pepper.

name: Malvani Prawn Curry (Konkan Kolkambi Rassa)

steps.text: Roast grated coconut, half the onion, ginger, and garlic until golden; grind into a smooth paste (vatan).
Heat oil, sauté the remaining chopped onion, add turmeric and Malvani masala, then stir in the ground coconut vatan and warm water.
Add cleaned prawns, kokum petals, and salt; simmer gently for 6 minutes and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Coastal Maharashtrian specialty known for its smoky roasted coconut vatan and tangy kokum.

name: Mangalore Bajji / Goli Baje (Coastal Karnataka Spongy Sour-Curd, Maida, Besan & Ginger-Curry Leaf Fritters)

ingredients.name: Besan (Gram Flour, for Nutty Golden Color & Softness)

steps.section: Beat elastic curd-flour batter by hand
steps.text: Whisk sour curd, sugar, salt, and hing in a bowl. Add maida, besan, rice flour, grated ginger, green chillies, curry leaves, and cumin. Beat vigorously with your hand for 4–5 minutes into a thick, sticky, stretchy batter (no extra water needed if curd is moist).

steps.section: Rest and fold in baking soda
steps.text: Rest the covered batter for 45 minutes to 1 hour. Right before frying, sprinkle baking soda and beat gently for 1 minute.

With wet fingers, pinch marble-to-golf-ball-sized portions into medium-hot oil; they will puff into round spheres and flip on their own. Fry on medium-low heat until rich golden brown and serve with red coconut chutney.

notes: Udupi-Mangalore tiffin classic; adding 2 tbsp besan and 1 tsp sugar produces a deep golden crust and pillowy crumb.

name: Mangalore Buns (Fluffy Sweet-Savory Ripe Banana, Curd, Cumin & Flour Deep-Fried Puri Buns)

ingredients.name: Maida or Half Maida + Half Whole Wheat Flour

steps.section: Mash ripe bananas with sugar, curd, and cumin
steps.text: Mash ripe bananas thoroughly with a fork or potato masher until creamy, then mix in sugar, sour curd, cumin seeds, baking soda, and salt.
Add flour gradually and knead without adding water into a soft, pliable dough; coat with 1 tbsp ghee and rest covered for at least 30 minutes (or up to 4 hours).

Roll dough balls into slightly thick 4-inch discs (thicker than regular puris) and slide into medium-hot oil. Spoon hot oil on top so they balloon into golden-brown, pillowy buns. Serve warm with spicy coconut chutney and kurma.

notes: Iconic Udupi-Mangalore breakfast pairing sweet banana-scented fried buns with fiery coconut chutney.

name: Mangalorean Prawn Gassi (Yetti Gassi Coconut Red Chilli Curry)

steps.section: Roast spices and grind gassi paste
steps.text: Dry-roast Byadgi chillies, coriander, cumin, fenugreek, and peppercorns in a drop of coconut oil, then grind with grated coconut, garlic, turmeric, and tamarind into a smooth paste.
Bring the ground paste and water to a gentle boil, add cleaned prawns and salt, and simmer for 6-7 minutes.

steps.section: Temper with onions and curry leaves
steps.text: Fry finely sliced onions and curry leaves in coconut oil until crisp and golden brown, then pour over the hot curry.

notes: Pairs beautifully with neer dosa, kori rotti, or boiled red rice.

name: Mango Kulfi

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Mango Lassi

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Mango Milkshake

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Mango Pudding (Eggless Mango Custard Pudding with Agar Agar / China Grass)

ingredients.name: Sweet Ripe Mango Pulp (Alphonso or Kesar)

steps.text: Stir agar agar powder into 0.5 cup warm water in a small pan. Heat on low stirring continuously for 3-4 minutes until agar agar completely dissolves into a clear liquid.

In a saucepan, warm milk, fresh cream, and sugar until sugar dissolves (do not boil). Puree fresh mango pulp until completely smooth. Stir dissolved hot agar agar into the warm milk mixture, then whisk in the smooth mango pulp until thoroughly combined.

Strain mixture through a fine sieve into individual pudding moulds or ramekins for a silky finish. Refrigerate for at least 2-3 hours until set firm. Unmould onto plates, top with fresh mango cubes and mint sprigs.

notes: The king of summer puddings; using sweet Alphonso or Kesar pulp yields a vibrant natural golden color and heavenly aroma without any artificial colors.

name: Mango Shrikhand

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Mangodi Papad ki Sabzi (Marwari Sun-Dried Moong Dal Badi & Papad in Spiced Ghee-Yogurt Curry)

steps.section: Roast mangodi in ghee and simmer until tender
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pot, roast moong dal mangodi until golden and nutty, then add 2 cups water and a pinch of turmeric and simmer covered for 10–12 minutes (or 1 whistle) until mangodis are soft.
In another pan, heat remaining ghee, temper cumin, cloves, bay leaf, hing, and ginger-chilli paste, and stir in curd whisked with coriander and Kashmiri chilli powder until boiling.
Combine the cooked mangodis (with their stock) and yogurt gravy, bring to a boil, stir in broken roasted papads and kasuri methi, simmer 2 minutes, and serve hot.

notes: Classic Rajasthani dry-pantry duet combining nutty sun-dried lentil mangodis and peppery papad.

name: Mangsher Ghugni (Kolkata Street-Style Mutton Keema Yellow Pea Ghugni)

steps.text: Fry potato and coconut bits in mustard oil; in the same pan, sauté onions, ginger-garlic, tomatoes, and spices, then slow-roast (kosha) the minced mutton until rich and oil separates.

steps.section: Simmer with yellow peas and finish with bhaja masala
steps.text: Add boiled yellow peas, fried potatoes, and coconut; simmer for 10 minutes and finish with ghee, Bengali garam masala, bhaja masala, chopped onions, and coriander.

notes: Iconic Kolkata Dacres Lane & cabin-style Mangsher Ghugni—delicious on its own or with luchi/paratha.

name: Mangshor Keema Kochuri (Kolkata Heritage Mutton Keema Stuffed Kochuri)

ingredients.name: Bengali Shahi Garam Masala (Cardamom, Cinnamon, Clove, Mace)

steps.text: Sauté minced onions, ginger, and garlic in mustard oil until deep golden brown. Add minced mutton, spices, and salt; bhunno on medium heat until the meat releases moisture and cooks thoroughly to a completely dry texture.
Knead maida with ghee, salt, and warm water. Rest for 20 minutes. Fill dough balls with cooled mutton keema, seal firmly, and roll with light pressure.

steps.section: Deep-fry to a crisp golden hue
steps.text: Fry in medium-hot oil until puffed, crisp, and deep golden. Serve with aloor dom and pickled green chillies.

notes: The holy grail of North Kolkata cabin snacks, popular at tea shops and evening gatherings.

name: Masala Badam Bhaja / Tasty Peanuts (Crispy Spiced Besan-Coated Fried Peanuts)

steps.section: Coat damp peanuts with spiced besan-rice flour
steps.text: Toss rinsed damp peanuts with ginger-garlic paste, hing, turmeric, chilli powder, besan, and rice flour, sprinkling drops of water so a craggy masala coat clings to each peanut.

steps.section: Deep-fry on medium-low heat until crunchy
steps.text: Drop coated peanuts into medium-hot oil, separating gently with a slotted spoon, and fry on low-medium flame for 8–10 minutes until crisp all the way through.

steps.section: Dust hot peanuts with chaat masala and black salt
steps.text: Drain on absorbent paper and immediately toss with chaat masala, black salt, and amchur powder.

notes: Crunchy masala-crusted peanut namkeen served with evening tea.

Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

name: Masala Gatta Fry / Sukhe Gatte ki Sabzi (Dry Spiced Gram Flour Dumplings with Fennel & Coriander)

steps.section: Boil and slice spiced besan logs
steps.text: Knead besan with oil, curd, ajwain, crushed fennel, red chilli powder, turmeric, and salt into a firm yet pliable dough. Shape into logs, boil for 10 minutes until cooked through, cool slightly, and cut into bite-sized coins.

steps.section: Toss in crackling dry spice tempering
steps.text: Heat oil in a wide pan, crackle cumin, mustard, sesame seeds, hing, crushed coriander-fennel, and slit green chillies. Add the gatta coins and roast on medium heat for 4 minutes until crisp-edged.
Sprinkle amchur powder, Kashmiri chilli powder, a splash of 2 tbsp curd or poaching water to glaze the spices onto the gattas, and toss with fresh coriander.

notes: Ideal travel-friendly dry Rajasthani sabzi that pairs with hot phulkas, thepla, or dal-chawal.

ingredients.name: Mint Powder or Kashmiri Chilli Powder

steps.text: Warm pure ghee in a heavy pan over low flame and roast whole cashews, stirring constantly for 6–8 minutes until evenly golden and fragrant.

steps.section: Toss hot cashews with pepper and chaat masala
steps.text: Transfer the hot ghee-coated cashews to a bowl and immediately toss with cracked black pepper, black salt, and chaat masala so the spices adhere.
Spread on a plate to cool to room temperature before storing in an airtight glass jar.

notes: Rich, crunchy ghee-roasted pepper cashews served on festive platters and with evening tea.

steps.text: Whisk besan, rice flour, turmeric, hing, salt, 1 tbsp hot oil, and water into a smooth pouring batter.

steps.section: Fry crispy boondi pearls through perforated ladle
steps.text: Pour batter through a perforated boondi jhara over hot oil and fry until golden and crunchy.

steps.section: Toss with fried peanuts, curry leaves, and spices
steps.text: Fry peanuts, cashews, and curry leaves until crisp, then toss warm with the boondi, red chilli powder, black salt, and chaat masala.

notes: Crunchy savory boondi mixture great for tea-time snacking or topping raita and chaat.

Sprinkle roasted Bengali bhaja masala and chopped coriander leaves over the hot fried pumpkin before serving.

notes: Fragrant with kalo jeere and roasted bhaja masala.

steps.text: Rub eggplant slices with turmeric, chilli, cumin, coriander, amchur, and salt; rest 5 minutes so moisture releases, then dredge both sides in besan and semolina.
Shallow-fry on a hot cast-iron tawa with mustard oil until the semolina-besan crust is golden and crisp.

notes: The semolina and besan coating prevents the eggplant from absorbing excess oil while adding a crunchy crust.

name: Matar Bharta (Green Peas / Koraishuti Mash)

steps.text: Steam or boil shelled green peas for 5–6 minutes until tender, then drain.
Heat mustard oil, crackle cumin or nigella seeds, and sauté ginger, garlic, and green chillies with the peas for 3 minutes.
Mash or pulse into a coarse bharta, season with salt, lemon juice, and fresh coriander, and serve warm.

notes: Fresh winter green peas make a vibrant, naturally sweet and spicy bharta.

name: Matar Paneer (Homestyle North Indian Green Peas & Cottage Cheese Tomato-Onion Curry)

steps.section: Lightly sear paneer and cook onion-tomato-cashew base
steps.text: Pan-sear paneer cubes until lightly golden and soak in warm water; temper oil with cumin seeds, sauté onion paste and ginger-garlic paste until golden, then cook tomato-cashew puree with turmeric, chilli, and coriander powder until oil separates.

steps.section: Simmer green peas and paneer in gravy
steps.text: Add green peas and 1.25 cups warm water, simmer covered for 5 minutes until peas are tender, then fold in paneer cubes, kasuri methi, garam masala, and fresh coriander.

notes: An everyday Indian household favorite that goes equally well with jeera rice, chapati, or poori.

name: Matar Paratha (Spiced Green Peas Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Coarsely mash steamed peas and sauté in 1 tsp oil with cumin seeds, hing, crushed ginger-green chilli, amchur, garam masala, and salt until dry.
Stuff cooled green pea filling inside soft wheat dough balls and roll out evenly.
Roast on a hot tawa with ghee until golden brown on both sides.

notes: Wholesome winter green pea paratha made with whole wheat flour.

name: Mathura Dubki Wale Aloo (Spicy Tangy Crushed Potato Curry for Bedmi Puri)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil or ghee, temper with cumin, fennel, cloves, black pepper, and hing, then lightly roast 1 tbsp besan and ginger-green chilli paste for 1 minute.

steps.section: Simmer crushed potatoes in thin spicy broth
steps.text: Add hand-mashed potatoes, spice powders, and 2.5 cups water; simmer on low flame for 12-15 minutes.

steps.section: Finish with amchur and garam masala
steps.text: Stir in amchur powder, black salt, garam masala, and fresh coriander.

notes: Famous Mathura and Agra breakfast potato curry without onion, garlic, or tomatoes.

name: Mathura Peda

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Mawa Kachori / Khoya Kochuri (Jodhpur Royal Sweet Khoya & Saffron-Cardamom Stuffed Crisp Kachori in Sugar Syrup)

steps.section: Prepare nut-studded mawa stuffing & sugar syrup
steps.text: Roast crumbled mawa with cardamom and chopped dry fruits until aromatic; let cool. Separately, boil sugar and water with crushed saffron to make a warm one-string syrup.
Knead maida with generous melted ghee and iced water into a firm dough. Enclose mawa stuffing inside thick dough circles and flatten with palm edges.

steps.section: Slow fry and steep in syrup
steps.text: Slow-fry on low flame in ghee until completely crisp and blister-free (about 15 minutes). Poke a hole in the crust, spoon in warm saffron syrup, and garnish with pistachios.

notes: The legendary royal sweet kachori invented in Jodhpur, Rajasthan.

name: Mera Pitha (Sylheti-Bengali Steamed Jaggery & Coconut Rice-Flour Dumplings)

steps.text: Boil water with grated jaggery, coconut, and salt until jaggery melts; stir in rice flour on low heat to form a cohesive dough. Cover 5 minutes, then knead smooth while warm.
Roll dough into smooth round or slightly conical balls by hand and steam in a greased steamer over boiling water for 15–18 minutes until firm and glossy.

notes: Traditional Sylheti winter pitha enjoyed warm with a drizzle of ghee.

name: Methi Besan Chilla (Fresh Fenugreek Leaves, Garlic & Gram Flour Winter Savory Crepes)

steps.text: Whisk besan with curd, crushed garlic-ginger-chilli, ajwain, sesame seeds, spices, salt, and water. Fold in washed, finely chopped fresh methi leaves and rest 10 minutes.

steps.section: Cook thin golden pudla on griddle
steps.text: Pour a ladleful onto a hot greased tawa, spread evenly, and cook on medium heat with a drizzle of oil until both sides are freckled golden brown.
Serve piping hot with green coriander-peanut chutney and masala chai.

notes: Also known as Methi na Pudla in Gujarat; a spoonful of curd balances the earthy bitterness of fresh fenugreek.

name: Methi Besan Muthiya (Gujarati Steamed & Sesame-Tempered Fenugreek & Gram Flour Dumplings)

steps.text: Combine chopped methi leaves with besan, coarse wheat/suji, curd, sugar, ginger-chilli paste, spices, baking soda, 1 tbsp oil, and salt into cylindrical fist-shaped logs (muthiyas). Steam in a greased steamer for 15–18 minutes until cooked through, then cool and slice into rounds.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan, crackle mustard seeds, sesame seeds, curry leaves, and hing, add the sliced muthiyas, and pan-roast for 4–5 minutes until crisp and golden around the edges.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice and garnish with coriander; serve hot with green chutney or chai.

notes: Wholesome steamed Gujarati snack that uses very little oil while packing fresh greens and gram flour.

name: Methi Dana Laddoo (Traditional Winter Fenugreek, Wheat & Jaggery Laddoo)

ingredients.name: Fenugreek Seeds (Methi, Soaked in Milk & Dried or Crushed)

steps.section: Soften methi and roast atta in ghee
steps.text: Dry-roast methi seeds lightly and crush coarsely with a rolling pin (or soak in warm milk 1 hour to reduce bitterness). Slow-roast whole wheat flour in ghee for 12–14 minutes until golden.
Add crushed methi, puffed gond, chopped nuts, and sonth; remove from heat, stir in grated jaggery until melted, and roll into small winter laddoos.

notes: Traditional warming winter tonic laddoo; sonth and jaggery balance the methi bitterness.

name: Methi Gatta ki Sabzi (Fresh Fenugreek & Besan Dumplings in Spiced Marwari Gravy)

steps.text: Saute chopped methi leaves in 1 tsp oil for 1 minute to mellow bitterness, then knead with besan, sesame seeds, ajwain, spice powders, 1 tbsp oil, and curd into logs. Boil for 10 minutes and cut into discs.
Temper cumin, fennel, hing, and ginger-garlic paste in hot ghee. Stir in spiced whisked curd, bring to a boil with poaching stock, and fold in the methi gattas.
Simmer on low flame for 6 minutes until the gravy coats the methi dumplings. Serve hot with bajra roti or chapati.

notes: A classic winter Rajasthani household curry combining earthy fenugreek greens with roasted gram flour notes.

name: Methi Malai Paneer (Cottage Cheese in Fragrant Fenugreek Leaf & Cream Gravy)

steps.section: Sauté chopped methi leaves in ghee to mellow bitterness
steps.text: Sauté finely chopped fresh methi leaves in 1 tsp ghee for 3 minutes until wilted and aromatic; set aside.

steps.section: Simmer creamy onion-cashew gravy with methi and paneer
steps.text: Temper ghee with cumin and green cardamom, cook ginger-green chilli paste and boiled onion-cashew paste, stir in yogurt, cream, white pepper, sautéed methi leaves, and soft paneer cubes, and simmer 4 minutes.

notes: Sautéing fresh methi leaves in ghee removes any harsh bitterness and leaves a warm herbal aroma.

name: Methi Masala Rice / Methi Pulao (Fresh Fenugreek Leaves, Green Peas, Peanuts & Spiced Basmati Rice)

steps.text: Heat ghee, fry peanuts golden, temper cumin and whole spices, then saute onion, ginger-garlic-chilli paste, and tomato.

steps.section: Wilt fresh methi leaves with spices
steps.text: Add chopped methi leaves, green peas, turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder, and garam masala; saute 3 minutes until methi wilts and loses rawness.
Fold in drained rice, 2.75 cups hot water, and salt; cover and simmer 12 minutes until tender and fragrant.

notes: Earthy winter masala rice pairing fresh fenugreek greens with sweet green peas and crunchy peanuts.

name: Methi Matar Paratha (Fresh Fenugreek & Crushed Peas Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil, add ajwain, ginger-chilli paste, chopped methi, and crushed green peas. Sauté until tender and completely dry; season with amchur, garam masala, and salt.
Place the cooled green stuffing inside dough cups, seal tightly, and roll into flat circles.
Roast on tawa with ghee on both sides until crispy and fragrant. Serve with curd and garlic pickle.

notes: A harmonious blend of sweet winter peas and pleasantly bitter fresh fenugreek.

name: Methi Papad ki Sabzi (Rajasthani Fenugreek Seeds & Papad Curry in Spiced Onion-Tomato-Curd Gravy)

ingredients.name: Or Fried Urad/moong Papads (Broken into Bite-sized Pieces)
Fenugreek Seeds (Methi Dana, Boiled 7–8 Mins in Water & Drained)
Amchur (Dry Mango Powder) or Raisins (to Balance Methi)

steps.section: Boil methi dana to remove bitterness
steps.text: Boil fenugreek seeds in 2 cups water for 7–8 minutes until plumped and tender, then drain and rinse once in fresh water so all harsh bitterness is removed.
Heat oil/ghee, temper cumin and hing, saute onion, garlic, and ginger until golden, then cook tomato, dry spices, and whisked curd until oil separates.

steps.section: Simmer with boiled methi and papad
steps.text: Add 1.25 cups hot water, boiled methi dana, and amchur/raisins; simmer 4 minutes, fold in broken roasted papads for 1 minute, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Signature Bikaner and Jodhpur desert specialty pairing diabetic-friendly boiled fenugreek seeds with spiced papad.

name: Methi Paratha (Homestyle)

steps.text: Mix flour and salt; add water gradually and knead to a soft dough. Rest covered.
Divide into portions and roll or shape according to the bread style.
Cook on a hot tawa or fry as appropriate, turning until cooked and golden.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Methi Prawns (Fenugreek Leaves Prawn Masala)

steps.text: Heat oil, fry chopped garlic, ginger, and onions until golden, then add tomatoes and spice powders and cook until soft.
Add chopped fenugreek leaves and sauté for 3-4 minutes until their bitterness mellows.
Stir in cleaned prawns and a splash of warm water, cover and cook for 5-6 minutes until tender, and finish with garam masala.

notes: Earthy fresh methi leaves complement the natural sweetness of prawns; delicious with chapati or phulka.

name: Methi Thepla (Gujarati Spiced Fenugreek & Yogurt Flatbread)

steps.text: Mix wheat flour, besan, chopped methi leaves, sesame seeds, spices, ginger-chilli paste, 1.5 tbsp oil, and yogurt to knead a soft, pliable dough.
Roll into thin circles and roast quickly on a hot tawa with a smear of oil on both sides for 30-40 seconds so they stay ultra-soft.

notes: Kneading with yogurt gives Methi Thepla a multi-day shelf life—ideal for travel and tiffins.

name: Mexican Tortilla Soup (Spiced Black Bean, Roasted Corn & Tomato Broth with Crispy Tortilla Strips)

steps.text: Heat oil in a pot, cook onions, peppers, and garlic with cumin, smoked paprika, and chilli powder until fragrant. Add fire-roasted tomatoes and broth, simmering for 15 minutes.
Stir in black beans, roasted sweet corn, and fresh lime juice. Simmer for 5 minutes to meld flavors.
Ladle piping hot soup into bowls. Top generously with crispy golden tortilla strips, avocado cubes, fresh cilantro, and crumbled cheese.

notes: Crisp tortilla strips provide the signature crunch that transforms this spiced smoky soup into a complete meal.

name: Mihidana

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Mihidana & Sitabhog (Bardhaman GI-Tagged Fine Saffron Pearls & Chhena Vermicelli Sweet)

steps.section: Press and fry fine chhena-rice vermicelli (Sitabhog)
steps.text: Knead chhena and Gobindobhog rice flour into a soft dough, press through a fine sev mould directly into hot cow ghee for 30 seconds until white-golden, and soak briefly in warm cardamom syrup.
Pour thin saffron-tinted rice-and-besan batter through a micro-perforated brass ladle into hot ghee and soak the tiny golden pearls in warm syrup.

steps.section: Garnish with nikhuti, cashews, and raisins
steps.text: Drain excess syrup and serve the fragrant Sitabhog and Mihidana topped with mini fried nikhuti, cashews, and raisins.

notes: Royal twin GI-tagged sweets of Bardhaman, West Bengal, traditionally served together.

name: Millet Khichdi / Foxtail & Little Millet Vegetable Khichdi (High-Fiber Siridhanya Millet & Moong Dal Khichdi)

ingredients.name: Mixed Seasonal Vegetables (Carrots, Beans, Peas, Bottle Gourd)
Cold-pressed Groundnut Oil or Desi Ghee

steps.text: Rinse and soak millet for 30 minutes to ensure digestibility and fluffy cooking. Heat ghee in a cooker, temper cumin, mustard, curry leaves, and hing, and saute onions, ginger-garlic, and mixed vegetables.

steps.section: Simmer soaked millet and moong dal
steps.text: Add drained millet, washed moong dal, turmeric, crushed black pepper, salt, and 4 cups water. Pressure-cook on medium-low heat for 2 whistles.
Let pressure release naturally, open lid, drizzle 1 tsp ghee and fresh coriander leaves, and serve warm with curd.

notes: Diabetic-friendly, low-glycemic, gluten-free khichdi packed with dietary fiber and plant protein.

name: Mini Dry Namkeen Samosa / Farsan Cocktail Samosa

steps.text: Pulse fried moong dal and sev into coarse crumbs and mix with toasted fennel, crushed coriander, cashews, raisins, amchur, sugar, chilli powder, and 1 tsp tamarind paste.
Roll stiff maida-ghee dough into small ovals, cut in half, form miniature cones, stuff with the dry masala, and crimp the edges tightly.

steps.section: Deep-fry on low heat until crisp
steps.text: Fry on low-medium heat for 14–16 minutes until crisp and golden so they stay crunchy for weeks.

notes: Bite-sized dry farsan samosas with a zero-moisture lentil, cashew, and raisin stuffing.

name: Mint Chutney Vegetable Sandwich

ingredients.name: Filling
ingredients.quantity: mint chutney, tomato, onion and cucumber

steps.text: Wash and slice vegetables or prepare the listed filling.
Spread butter or condiment on bread, add filling and season lightly. Serve fresh or grill until crisp.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

name: Mint Tea

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Mirchi Vada / Jodhpuri Mirchi Bada (Potato-Stuffed Large Green Chillies in Crisp Ajwain-Besan Batter)

steps.section: Prepare tangy Jodhpuri aloo masala and stuff chillies
steps.text: Saute cumin, crushed fennel, coriander seeds, hing, and ginger in 1 tbsp oil, then mash in boiled potatoes, red chilli, turmeric, amchur, garam masala, mint, coriander, and salt. Stuff inside AND coat a thin layer around the slit green chillies.
Whisk besan with ajwain, turmeric, salt, a pinch of baking soda, 1 tsp hot oil, and water into a thick, ribbon-consistency batter that clings to the stuffed chillies without dripping.
Dip each stuffed chilli in the besan batter and fry in medium-hot oil until golden and crisp. Cut diagonally and serve with tamarind and mint chutneys.

notes: Jodhpur's iconic street food where tangy amchur-spiced potato filling and crisp besan batter wrap mild green peppers.

name: Mishti Boondi / Bengali Bonde (Sweet Saffron & Cardamom Fried Gram Flour Pearls)

steps.text: Whisk sieved besan, rice flour, a tsp of hot ghee, and water for 5 minutes into a smooth, lump-free flowing batter.

steps.section: Fry pearls through a perforated ladle (jhara)
steps.text: Hold a perforated boondi ladle above hot ghee/oil, pour batter so round droplets fall into the oil, and fry until crisp without browning.
Toss hot fried boondi directly into warm 1-thread saffron-cardamom sugar syrup with toasted melon seeds and let soak for 30 minutes until plump and glossy.

notes: Classic Bengali sweet boondi enjoyed with luchis, mudhi (puffed rice), or as Puja bhog.

name: Mishti Doi

name: Missi Roti / Missi Paratha (Punjabi Spiced Besan & Wheat Flatbread)

steps.text: Combine besan, wheat flour, chopped onion, green chillies, coriander, ajwain, kasuri methi, turmeric, salt, and 1 tbsp ghee; knead with warm water into a medium-soft dough.
Roll into rounds and cook on a hot tawa, brushing both sides with ghee until golden brown.

notes: Nutty, high-protein Punjabi flatbread.

name: Misti Kumro Bharta (Pumpkin Mash)

steps.text: Peel and cube the pumpkin, then steam or pan-roast covered with a pinch of salt until soft and caramelized at the edges.
In mustard oil, crisp the dry red chillies, splutter kalo jeere, and fry sliced onions until golden.
Mash the warm pumpkin with crushed fried chillies, golden onions, fresh coriander, salt, and a few drops of raw mustard oil.

notes: The natural sweetness of misti kumro balances the smoky heat of fried red chillies and mustard oil.

name: Mixed Berry Smoothie

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Mixed Chowmin / Mixed Hakka Chowmein (Tangra-Style Egg, Chicken & Prawn Noodles)

steps.section: Sear prawns, chicken, and scrambled eggs
steps.text: Toss chicken strips and prawns with ginger-garlic, pepper, and cornflour; sear quickly in hot oil until golden, scramble the eggs alongside, and set aside.
Sauté minced garlic, ginger, and green chillies in hot oil, then stir-fry carrots, beans, cabbage, and bell peppers on high flame for 3 minutes.

steps.section: Toss noodles with meats, prawns, and Tangra sauces
steps.text: Add boiled noodles, chicken, prawns, egg, soy sauces, chilli sauce, vinegar, and black pepper; toss on high heat and finish with spring onion greens and a drizzle of sesame oil.

notes: Signature Tangra Chinatown special mixed chowmin loaded with chicken, prawns, and egg.

name: Mixed Fried Rice (Kolkata Tangra-Style Egg, Chicken & Prawn Special Fried Rice)

steps.section: Sear chicken, prawns, and scrambled eggs
steps.text: Marinate diced chicken and prawns with pepper, soy sauce, and 1 tbsp cornflour; sear in hot oil until golden, scramble the beaten eggs alongside, and set aside.

steps.section: Stir-fry garlic and finely diced vegetables
steps.text: In the same wok, sauté minced garlic and spring onion whites on high heat, then toss in carrots, beans, and bell peppers for 3 minutes.

steps.section: Toss chilled rice with chicken, prawns, and egg
steps.text: Add chilled rice, seared chicken, prawns, scrambled egg, soy sauce, vinegar, and black pepper; toss over high flame for 3 minutes and finish with sesame oil and spring onion greens.

notes: Showstopping Tangra-style Mixed Fried Rice loaded with prawns, chicken, and egg.

name: Mixed Vegetable & Mushroom Kathi Roll (Kolkata Street-Style Veg Masala Roll)

steps.section: Stir-fry spiced vegetable and mushroom filling
steps.text: Sauté mushrooms, julienned vegetables, boiled potato, and paneer cubes on high heat with ginger-garlic, cumin, garam masala, and tomato-chilli sauce so the vegetables stay crisp-tender.
Spoon the hot vegetable filling onto crisp laccha parathas, top with raw onion rings, cucumber, bitnoon, chaat masala, and lemon juice, and roll up.

notes: Wholesome, crunchy Kolkata street-style mixed veg and mushroom roll.

name: Mocha Bori Ghonto (Banana Blossom & Crushed Fried Motor Daler Bori Traditional Curry)

ingredients.name: Motor Daler Bori or Biulir Daler Bori

steps.text: Fry the bori in mustard oil until crisp and golden, then crush half into coarse pieces; in the same oil, temper bay leaf and cumin and fry small potato cubes until golden.

steps.section: Cook boiled mocha with coconut, spices and bori
steps.text: Add ginger paste, turmeric, cumin powder, grated coconut, and boiled chopped mocha; cook until cohesive, then fold in whole and crushed fried bori, sugar, ghee, and gorom moshla.

notes: Crushed Motor Daler Bori adds a nutty crunch that complements the iron-rich banana blossom.

name: Mocha Coffee

name: Mochar Bora (Crispy Banana Blossom & Spiced Lentil Fritters)

ingredients.name: Cholar Dal / Motor Dal Paste (or Besan)

steps.section: Mix minced boiled mocha with lentil paste and coconut
steps.text: Squeeze excess water from boiled minced banana blossom and knead with coarse yellow split-pea paste (or besan), rice flour, grated coconut, ginger, green chillies, roasted cumin, and gorom moshla.

steps.section: Shape and fry until dark golden and crisp
steps.text: Shape into small oval or flat patties and shallow-fry in hot mustard oil until richly browned and crisp on the outside.

notes: Unlike breadcrumb-coated Mochar Chop, Mochar Bora is bound with dal paste and rice flour for a rustic crunch.

name: Mochar Chingri (Banana Blossom with Prawns)

steps.section: Boil banana blossom and fry prawns
steps.text: Boil chopped banana blossom with turmeric and salt, drain and mash lightly. Fry seasoned prawns and cubed potatoes in mustard oil.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste, cumin, coriander, and turmeric powder, and add fried potatoes and grated coconut.
Stir in the boiled banana blossom, fried prawns, salt, and a touch of sugar. Cook until thick and cohesive, finishing with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: A classic heirloom Bengali festive side dish transforming Mochar Ghonto with succulent prawns.

name: Mochar Chop

steps.text: Chop or mash the main ingredients and combine with onion, chilli, spices and binder.
Shape into portions or coat in batter or breadcrumbs as appropriate.
Shallow-fry, deep-fry or bake until golden and cooked through. Drain and serve hot.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Mochar Ghonto

steps.text: Remove florets and hard stems, chop finely and boil with a pinch of turmeric. Drain well.
Sauté spices and potato, add chopped blossom, ginger and salt; cook covered until tender.
Stir in grated coconut and a little ghee, then cook briefly.

name: Modak (Steamed)

name: Mohanthal (Traditional Gujarati Melt-in-Mouth Roasted Besan, Khoya & Saffron Fudge)

steps.section: Create dhaabo granules and roast besan
steps.text: Rub 3 tbsp hot ghee and 3 tbsp warm milk into besan with fingers, rest 15 mins, and pass through a sieve to create uniform granules. Roast the granulated besan in 1 cup ghee on low heat for 18 minutes until nutty and golden.

Stir crumbled mawa into the hot roasted besan until melted. Separately boil sugar, water, and saffron to 1.5 string consistency, pour into the besan mixture, and stir continuously until thick and fudge-like.
Pour into a greased tray, sprinkle with cardamom, nutmeg, and slivered nuts, press gently, cool until set, and slice into diamond pieces.

notes: Lord Krishna's favorite bhog: an exquisite, crumbly Gujarati and Rajasthani sweet fudge.

name: Mooli Paratha (Punjabi Grated Radish Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Sprinkle grated radish with salt, rest for 10 minutes, and squeeze out all excess juice in a muslin cloth (use the nutritious juice to knead the atta dough!).
Mix the dry grated radish with ginger, green chillies, coriander, ajwain, and spices; stuff generously into the dough balls and roll out.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until golden and crisp. Serve with white butter and curd.

notes: Kneading the flour with the squeezed radish water prevents waste and infuses flavor into the crust.

name: Moong Dal Bengali Style

steps.text: Rinse the lentils or legumes. Pressure-cook or simmer with water and turmeric until soft.
Heat oil or ghee; add cumin, garlic, onion and tomato and cook until fragrant.
Mix the tempering into the cooked dal, adjust water and salt, and simmer briefly.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

Heat oil, add mustard or cumin seeds, onion, chilli and vegetables.
Add the main ingredient and the required water or batter; cook until tender and serve hot.

name: Moong Dal Kochuri (Bengali Homestyle Soft Fennel & Yellow Lentil Stuffed Kochuri)

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil, temper with crushed fennel seeds and hing. Add ground moong dal paste, ginger-chilli paste, cumin-coriander powder, salt, and a pinch of sugar; sauté until it forms a non-sticky soft dough.
Knead maida with ghee, salt, and water. Divide into balls, flatten, place a ball of dal filling inside, seal the mouth, and roll into round puris.
Drop in hot oil and gently press with a slotted ladle until it puffs into a soft, fragrant sphere. Serve hot with cholar dal.

notes: A softer, aromatic homestyle Bengali counterpart to Rajasthani khasta kachori.

name: Moong Dal Laddoo (Slow-Roasted Yellow Moong Flour, Ghee & Cardamom Laddoo)

ingredients.name: Yellow Moong Dal Flour (Besan-fine Moong Atta)

steps.text: Heat ghee in a heavy kadhai and roast yellow moong flour on low flame for 15 minutes, stirring continuously, until golden and aromatic.
Remove from heat, let cool until warm, mix in powdered sugar/jaggery, chopped nuts, and cardamom, and roll firmly into round laddoos.

notes: Light, digestible protein-rich laddoo using ready moong dal flour without soaking or grinding.
