name: Motor Paneer Bengali Niramish Style (Green Peas, Potato & Golden Paneer Curry without Onion-Garlic)

ingredients.name: Fresh or Frozen Green Peas (Koraishuti / Motor)

steps.text: Lightly fry paneer cubes in oil-ghee until golden and soak in warm salted water; fry diced potatoes until golden.

steps.section: Simmer tomato-ginger-cashew gravy with green peas and paneer
steps.text: Temper oil with cumin, bay leaf, and hing, cook the tomato-ginger-cashew paste with turmeric and cumin-coriander powder, add green peas, potatoes, and warm water, then fold in paneer, crushed kasuri methi, ghee, and gorom moshla.

notes: Ideal for winter nights with koraishutir kochuri or hot phulkas.

name: Motorshuti O Cheese Kochuri (Bengali Fusion Green Peas & Molten Cheese Stuffed Kochuri)

steps.text: Sauté mashed peas with ginger, green chillies, and roasted cumin until dry. Allow to cool completely, then mix with grated mozzarella, cheddar, black pepper, and oregano.
Knead maida with ghee and salt into a soft dough. Enclose the cheese-pea filling in dough balls, seal carefully to prevent leakage, and roll into medium discs.
Deep-fry in hot oil until puffed and crisp. Serve immediately while the cheese inside is delightfully gooey and melted.

notes: A popular modern Kolkata cafe fusion marrying traditional koraishuti pur with stringy cheese.

name: Mouchak (Bengali Honeycomb-Layered Khoya, Chhena & Boondi Sweet)

steps.text: Sauté chhena and khoya with powdered sugar and cardamom on low heat for 6–8 minutes until soft and creamy.

steps.section: Toss boondi with nuts in warm syrup
steps.text: Fold crisp boondi pearls and fried cashews/raisins into warm sugar syrup until glossy but still distinct.
Press alternating layers of syrup-glazed boondi and creamy khoya-chhena in a greased tray, garnish with pistachios, chill to set, and slice into squares.

notes: Named after its honeycomb ('mouchak') cross-section of golden boondi and white khoya-chhena.

name: Muger Puli / Moong Dal Puli Pithe (Golden Fried Yellow Moong-Rice Dumplings in Gur Syrup)

steps.section: Make moong dal dough and coconut pur
steps.text: Boil moong dal until completely soft and mash smooth with a fork. Stir into boiling salted water with rice flour and maida to form a soft dough. Cook coconut and nolen gur into sticky pur; boil syrup with 1 cup water and cardamom.

steps.section: Stuff, fry golden, and dip in syrup
steps.text: Shape small discs, stuff with coconut pur, seal into pulis, fry on medium heat until crisp golden, and soak in warm syrup for 15 minutes.

notes: Moong dal makes the outer shell melt-in-the-mouth soft after soaking in syrup.

name: Mughlai Paratha (Kolkata Cabin-Style Egg & Spiced Keema Stuffed Paratha)

ingredients.name: Spiced Cooked Chicken/mutton Keema or Crushed Breadcrumbs

steps.text: Knead maida with oil, salt, and water into a smooth dough and rest 20 minutes. Beat eggs with chopped onion, green chillies, ginger, coriander, garam masala, salt, and cooked spiced keema (or breadcrumbs).

steps.section: Stretch thin and fold into envelope
steps.text: Roll a dough ball into a very thin large sheet on an oiled surface, spoon the egg-keema mixture in the center, and fold all four sides over to form a neat rectangular parcel.

Carefully slide into a flat frying pan with medium-hot oil and cook for 4-5 minutes per side until the egg sets puffily inside and the crust is golden and crisp. Cut into squares and serve with aloor torkari, ketchup, and salad.

notes: Iconic Kolkata cabin-restaurant delicacy.

name: Mula Chaukani / Radish Chukauni (Pungent Nepali White Radish & Yogurt Salad)

steps.section: Squeeze radish and fold in curd
steps.text: Lightly salt grated radish, rest 5 minutes, squeeze out excess liquid, and fold into whisked thick curd with diced potato, onion, chillies, cumin, and salt.
Heat mustard oil, crackle fenugreek seeds until dark, add turmeric and red chilli powder, and pour sizzling over the radish-curd mixture.
Mix well, finish with lemon juice and coriander, and serve chilled with steamed rice.

notes: Pungent, digestive, and crunchy radish variation of Chukauni popular during Himalayan winters.

name: Mula ko Achar (Instant Nepali Spiced Radish & Mustard Seed Salad)

steps.text: In a bowl, toss crunchy radish batons with freshly ground mustard powder, red chilli powder, slit green chillies, salt, and lemon juice.
Heat mustard oil in a ladle until smoking, brown the fenugreek seeds, take off heat, add turmeric powder, and pour sizzling over the radish.
Toss vigorously until the yellow mustard seeds coat the radish sticks. Ready to eat immediately or sun-warm for 1 hour for deeper fermentation.

notes: Crisp, pungent instant radish pickle eaten across every Nepali household alongside dal-bhat-tarkari.

name: Mulligatawny Soup (Anglo-Indian Curried Lentil, Apple & Rice Soup with Coconut Milk)

ingredients.name: Yellow Moong Dal or Red Masoor Dal
Pure Desi Ghee or Coconut Oil

steps.text: Heat ghee in a pot, cook onions, ginger, garlic, carrots, and celery for 5 minutes. Stir in Madras curry powder and diced green apple for 2 minutes.
Add rinsed dal and stock. Bring to a boil and simmer on low heat for 18-20 minutes until lentils are completely soft. Puree half the soup for silky body.

steps.section: Enrich with coconut milk and rice
steps.text: Stir in thick coconut milk, cooked basmati rice, and fresh lemon juice. Simmer for 3 minutes, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve warm.

notes: Originating from Tamil 'Milagu-tannir' (pepper water); Anglo-Indian tradition enriched the spiced broth with tart apples, lentils, and coconut milk.

name: Mulo Bharta (Radish Mash)

steps.text: Peel and grate the radish, toss with a little salt, rest 5 minutes, and squeeze out the excess water.
Lightly steam or sauté the grated radish in 1 tsp mustard oil until tender and raw sharpness subsides.
Toss the warm radish with finely chopped onion, crushed roasted red chilli, green chillies, fresh coriander, salt, and raw mustard oil.

notes: A popular winter Bengali side dish served with steamed rice.

name: Mulo Bori Begun Jhol (Winter White Radish, Brinjal & Fried Lentil Dumpling Light Curry)

steps.section: Blanch radish and fry bori and brinjal
steps.text: Parboil radish wedges for 3 minutes and drain; fry the bori and brinjal wedges separately in mustard oil until golden and keep aside.

steps.section: Simmer light ginger-cumin broth with bori
steps.text: Temper oil with panch phoron, fry potato and blanched radish with ginger, turmeric, and cumin powder, add 1.5 cups warm water, and simmer with fried bori, brinjal, green chillies, and coriander until tender.

notes: Comforting winter afternoon jhol that highlights the earthy sweetness of new-season radish and nutty bori.

name: Mulo Fry / Mulo Bhaja (Bengali Grated White Radish Stir-Fry)

steps.text: Toss julienned/grated radish with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes and squeeze out excess water.

steps.section: Stir-fry with kalo jeere and green chillies
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with dry red chilli, kalo jeere, and green chillies, add the radish and turmeric, and stir-fry until golden, dry, and fragrant; finish with coriander leaves.

notes: Earthy, aromatic winter Bengali Mulo Bhaja.

name: Mulor Bora / Radish Fritters (Crispy Grated Winter White Radish & Rice Flour Fritters)

ingredients.name: Besan (Gram Flour) or Soaked Masoor Dal Paste

steps.section: Salt-drain grated radish and mix with herbs
steps.text: Toss grated radish with ½ tsp salt, rest for 8 minutes, squeeze out excess liquid thoroughly, and mix with rice flour, besan, kalo jeere, poppy seeds, ginger, green chillies, and coriander.

steps.section: Flatten and shallow-fry in mustard oil
steps.text: Shape into small flat patties and fry in hot mustard oil over medium heat until deeply browned and crisp.

notes: Squeezing the radish dry turns its sharp bite sweet and earthy once fried in mustard oil.

name: Mumbai Street-Style Tawa Pulao (Pav Bhaji Masala, Butter, Boiled Potato, Peas & Capsicum Spiced Rice)

steps.text: Melt butter with oil on a wide tawa or skillet, crackle cumin seeds, saute onion and ginger-garlic-chilli paste, then add tomatoes and cook until pulpy and bright red.

steps.section: Toss vegetables with Pav Bhaji masala
steps.text: Add diced capsicum, boiled potato cubes, green peas, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli powder, Pav Bhaji masala, and salt; mash lightly in spots and toss 3 minutes.

steps.section: Toss cooked rice on high heat
steps.text: Fold in cooked rice, sprinkle lemon juice and chopped coriander, and toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes until smoky and evenly spiced. Serve hot with boondi raita.

notes: Iconic Mumbai Chowpatty street food turning leftover or pre-cooked basmati rice into a buttery, tangy masala feast.

name: Murgir Keema Kochuri (Kolkata Cabin-Style Spiced Minced Chicken Stuffed Puri)

steps.text: Sauté chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste in mustard oil until browned. Add minced chicken, turmeric, cumin, chilli, and salt; stir vigorously on high heat until the juices evaporate and the mince is dry and tender. Fold in garam masala, mint, and coriander.
Knead maida with ghee, salt, and warm water. Divide into balls, place chicken stuffing in each, seal securely, and roll out gently with oiled rolling pin.
Slide into hot oil and fry until fully puffed, crunchy, and golden brown. Serve hot with salad and kasundi.

notes: Classic evening snack served across heritage tea stalls and cabins in Shyambazar and College Street.

name: Muri Bhaja (Ghee & Curry Leaf Roasted Crispy Puffed Rice)

steps.text: Heat ghee or oil in a wide kadhai on low-medium flame, crackle mustard seeds, and fry peanuts and curry leaves until crunchy.
Stir in turmeric, chilli powder, and black salt, then add puffed rice and toss continuously on low heat for 4 minutes until crisp and golden.

notes: Stores well in an airtight tin for days; great quick tea-time tiffin.

name: Murir Moa

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Mushroom & Baby Corn Fried Rice (Garlic, Button Mushroom & Baby Corn Wok-Tossed Rice)

steps.section: Sear mushrooms and baby corn on high heat
steps.text: Heat oil and butter in a hot wok, add sliced mushrooms and diced baby corn, and sear on high flame for 4 minutes until golden-brown.
Add minced garlic, ginger, carrots, beans, and capsicum and stir-fry on high flame for 3 minutes.

steps.section: Toss with chilled rice and black pepper
steps.text: Add chilled rice, soy sauce, vinegar, salt, and freshly ground black pepper; toss on high heat for 3 minutes and top with spring onion greens.

notes: Savory, aromatic vegetarian fried rice highlighting seared button mushrooms and crisp baby corn.

name: Mushroom & Baby Corn Veg Chowmin / Chowmein (Wok-Tossed Mushroom, Baby Corn & Pepper Noodles)

steps.section: Sear mushrooms and baby corn on high heat
steps.text: Heat 1.5 tbsp oil in a hot wok, add sliced button mushrooms and diagonal baby corn pieces, and sear on high heat for 4 minutes until lightly browned without releasing excess water.
Add minced garlic, ginger, green chillies, carrots, cabbage, and capsicum and toss on high flame for 3 minutes.

steps.section: Fold in noodles and Indo-Chinese sauces
steps.text: Add al dente noodles, soy sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar, salt, and black pepper; toss well and garnish with spring onion greens.

notes: Umami-rich vegetarian chowmin featuring tender button mushrooms and crunchy baby corn.

name: Mushroom & Spring Onion Momo (Juicy Hand-Chopped Button Mushroom Steamed Dumplings)

steps.text: Saute finely chopped mushrooms and garlic in butter/oil on high heat for 4 minutes until excess mushroom water evaporates; stir in soy sauce, black pepper, salt, and spring onion, then cool.
Fill thin maida wrappers with the savoury mushroom mix, pleat tightly, and steam for 10–12 minutes.

notes: Quick high-heat sauteing concentrates umami flavour and stops mushrooms from making wrappers soggy.

name: Mushroom Cheese Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Mushroom Omelette

steps.text: Beat eggs with salt, pepper and optional milk or water; prepare the listed variation ingredients.
Heat butter or oil in a pan. Add vegetables first if needed, pour in eggs and cook gently; fold when set.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

name: Mushroom Paratha (Spiced Sautéed Mushroom, Onion & Pepper Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp butter, sauté onions and garlic until aromatic. Add minced mushrooms, green chillies, black pepper, garam masala, and salt; cook on high heat until the water evaporates and the mixture is dry.
Enclose cooled mushroom filling inside whole wheat dough balls and roll gently.
Cook on a hot tawa with butter until crisp and golden brown. Serve with spicy mint chutney or curd.

notes: Earthy, umami-rich stuffed paratha combining sautéed garlic mushrooms and black pepper.

name: Muslim Wedding Style Kuska Rice / Tamil Bhai Veetu Khuska (Saffron, Caramelized Onion, Cashew & Coconut Milk Dum Khuska)

ingredients.name: Seeraga Samba or Long-grain Basmati Rice

steps.section: Fry crisp cashews and birista onions
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy handi, fry cashews until golden and set aside, then caramelize half the sliced onions until crisp brown (birista).
In the same pot, temper whole spices and kalpasi, saute remaining onions, ginger-garlic-green chilli paste, mint, coriander, Kashmiri chilli powder, and curd until fragrant and glossy.

steps.section: Simmer with coconut milk and steam on dum
steps.text: Add coconut milk, water, lemon juice, and salt; bring to a boil, add drained rice, cook 80% until water reduces to surface level, drizzle saffron milk, scatter fried onions and cashews, seal tightly, and dum-cook on low heat for 10 minutes.

notes: Celebratory Chennai/Ambur wedding-style Kuska infused with coconut milk, stone flower (kalpasi), and saffron.

name: Mutta Bonda / South Indian Egg Bonda (Spiced Hard-Boiled Eggs Coated in Crispy Carom-Rice-Besan Batter)

steps.text: Sprinkle a pinch of black pepper, red chilli powder, and salt over the cut faces of the boiled egg halves.
Whisk besan, rice flour, ginger-garlic paste, ajwain, fennel, turmeric, red chilli, garam masala, hing, baking soda, salt, 1 tsp hot oil, and water into a smooth, thick coating batter.
Coat each egg half completely in the batter and deep-fry in medium-hot oil until puffed and golden. Serve topped with finely chopped raw onion, coriander, and a dash of chaat masala.

notes: Evening street-cart favorite across Chennai, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru.

name: Mutton Kathi Roll (Kolkata Street-Style Spiced Mutton Kabab Roll)

ingredients.name: Boneless Tender Mutton Cubes or Minced Mutton Seekh Kabab

steps.text: Marinate mutton with raw papaya paste, ginger-garlic, yogurt, mustard oil, Kashmiri chilli, and royal garam masala; pan-roast until melt-in-the-mouth tender and lightly charred.
Fry flaky laccha parathas (with or without an egg layer), pile the juicy mutton kababs in the center with onion rings, green chillies, lemon juice, and chaat masala, and roll tightly.

notes: Classic Old Kolkata style mutton kathi roll with aromatic mace and nutmeg notes.

name: Mutton Keema Paratha (Rich Mughlai Spiced Minced Mutton Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Sauté onions and ginger-garlic paste in 1 tbsp ghee until deeply browned. Add mutton keema, spices, and salt; bhunno on medium heat until tender and thoroughly dry. Stir in mint, coriander, and kasuri methi; cool.
Pack keema filling into dough balls, seal neatly, and roll out with light pressure.
Roast on a medium-hot tawa with ghee until deeply golden, crisp on the edges, and fragrant. Serve with cucumber raita and pickled onions.

notes: A regal Mughlai stuffed flatbread made with robustly spiced slow-cooked mutton mince.

name: Mutton Khichuri / Mangshor Khichuri (Rich Bengali Slow-Cooked Mutton & Gobindobhog Rice Khichuri)

steps.text: Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder, and mustard oil. Sear in a heavy pot with whole spices and sliced onions, then pressure-cook for 4 whistles until 85% tender.

steps.section: Combine with roasted dal and Gobindobhog rice
steps.text: In a large handi, combine the cooked mutton along with its rich gravy, washed Gobindobhog rice, roasted dals, fried potato halves, and 5.5 cups hot water.
Cook covered on low flame for 15-18 minutes until rice and dal are velvety and infused with mutton juices. Stir in pure desi ghee, Bengali gorom moshla, and green chillies.

notes: A legendary Nabami or rainy Sunday feast where rich Mutton Kosha and Gobindobhog Khichuri unite in a single pot.

name: Mutton Paya Shorba / Lamb Trotter Broth (Slow-Simmered Spiced Bone Marrow Broth)

ingredients.name: Whole Whole Spices (Black Cardamom, Cinnamon, Cloves, Bay Leaf)

steps.text: Add cleaned paya into a pressure cooker with 6 cups water, half the sliced onions, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, whole spices, and salt. Cook on medium-low for 45-50 minutes (8-10 whistles) until gelatinous and fall-apart tender.
Heat ghee in a pot, fry remaining onions until golden brown. Add remaining ginger-garlic paste, coriander powder, and black pepper, cooking for 3 minutes.
Strain or pour the tender paya and bone-marrow rich broth into the tadka. Simmer together for 10 minutes until deeply flavorful. Serve hot with ginger juliennes and lemon wedges.

notes: Slow-simmering extracts rich collagen and bone marrow, yielding a deeply restorative, therapeutic winter shorba.

name: Mysore Bonda / Mysore Bajji (Crispy Outside & Fluffy Aerated Maida, Rice Flour, Sour Curd & Coconut Fritters)

steps.section: Hand-beat maida, rice flour, and sour curd batter
steps.text: In a wide bowl, combine maida, rice flour, sour curd, salt, baking soda, and 2–3 tbsp water. Beat vigorously by hand in one direction for 5 minutes until thick, elastic, and airy. Fold in cumin, grated ginger, chopped green chillies, curry leaves, coriander, coconut bits, and 1 tbsp hot oil.

steps.section: Rest batter to ferment and aerate
steps.text: Cover the bowl and rest at warm room temperature for 30–60 minutes so the sour curd and baking soda create tiny air pockets.

steps.section: Drop round bondas and deep-fry golden
steps.text: Wet your fingers with water, scoop small portions of batter, and drop smoothly into medium-hot oil. Fry on medium flame while stirring gently in circles for 4–5 minutes until evenly golden, crisp outside, and spongy inside. Serve hot with coconut or ginger chutney.

notes: Vigorous 5-minute manual hand-beating and resting with sour curd give Mysore Bonda its signature airy honeycomb interior without any blender.

name: Mysore Pak (Royal Karnataka Ghee-Aerated Gram Flour & Sugar Syrup Melt-in-Mouth Fudge)

ingredients.name: Fine Besan (Gram Flour, Lightly Dry-roasted & Sifted)

steps.section: Prepare 1-string sugar syrup and add sifted besan
steps.text: Boil sugar and water until a 1-string consistency is reached. Lower heat and gradually whisk in sifted besan (or a smooth slurry of besan and 1/2 cup warm ghee) so zero lumps form.

steps.section: Ladle in piping hot ghee in stages
steps.text: Keep the remaining 1 cup ghee smoking hot on a side burner. Pour a ladleful of hot ghee at a time into the simmering besan-sugar mixture, stirring continuously as it froths, sizzles, and absorbs each addition.

steps.section: Pour into deep tray for porous honeycomb center
steps.text: When the mixture turns frothy, porous, and stops absorbing ghee, stir in cardamom powder and immediately pour into a tall greased tin without pressing down tightly. Score into rectangular bars after 10 minutes and unmold when cool.

notes: Created in the royal kitchens of Mysore Palace; pouring smoking-hot ghee in batches creates the signature honeycomb lattice.

name: Naan (Homestyle)

steps.text: Mix flour and salt; add water gradually and knead to a soft dough. Rest covered.
Divide into portions and roll or shape according to the bread style.
Cook on a hot tawa or fry as appropriate, turning until cooked and golden.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Naan Puri (Bengali Baby Naan / Fluffy Fried Leavened Puri)

ingredients.name: Instant Dry Yeast (or 1/2 Tsp Baking Powder + 1/4 Tsp Baking Soda)

steps.text: Activate yeast in lukewarm milk with sugar (or whisk yogurt with baking powder, baking soda, sugar, and salt). Knead with maida and 2 tbsp oil into a pillowy dough; cover and rest in a warm spot for 1 hour until puffed.
Divide into lemon-sized balls and roll into slightly thick rounds (thicker than regular luchi) with a sprinkle of kalonji if desired.
Slide into medium-hot oil and gently ladle hot oil over the top until each naan puri puffs into a soft, pillowy golden balloon; flip once and drain.

notes: Beloved Bengali catering & festive favorite—soft like a baby naan inside and puffed like a puri outside; pairs with chana masala or aloor dum.

name: Namak Para (Crisp Ajwain & Cumin Savory Flour Ribbon Crackers)

steps.section: Knead stiff maida-suji dough with carom and cumin
steps.text: Rub ghee, salt, ajwain, cumin, and black pepper into maida and suji, then bind with minimal water into a stiff dough; rest 15 minutes.

steps.section: Roll and slice into diagonal ribbon strips
steps.text: Roll dough into medium-thin sheets and cut with a pastry wheel or knife into 2.5-inch diagonal strips.
Deep-fry on medium-low flame, stirring regularly for even coloring, until golden and crisp.

notes: Crisp, carom-scented savory ribbon crackers ideal for tea time.

name: Narkel Bhaja Diye Muri Makha (Pan-Fried Coconut Slices & Mustard-Oil Puffed Rice)

steps.text: Heat 2 tsp oil in a small pan and fry thin coconut slices and peanuts on medium-low heat until golden and crisp; drain.
Mix puffed rice with chopped onion, green chillies, remaining mustard oil, black salt, bhaja masala, and the warm fried coconut and peanuts.

notes: Nutty toasted coconut slices elevate simple muri makha into a festive snack.

name: Narkel Chapa / Chandrakala Narkel Sandesh (Moulded Coconut & Khoya Sweet)

steps.section: Grind coconut into a fine paste
steps.text: Pulse grated white coconut in a grinder with 2 tbsp milk into a smooth, fine paste.

steps.section: Cook with khoya and sugar over low flame
steps.text: Cook the coconut paste, grated khoya, condensed milk, and sugar in a heavy pan over low flame for 15 minutes until it forms a soft, non-sticky dough.
Add cardamom powder, let cool until warm to touch, and press into ghee-brushed floral moulds to form delicate Narkel Chapa.

notes: Refined Bengali moulded coconut-khoya sweet prepared for Kojagori Lakshmi Puja.

name: Narkel Chingri (Prawns in Spiced Grated Coconut)

steps.text: Coarsely grind half the grated coconut with mustard seeds and 2 green chillies, keeping the rest of the grated coconut for texture.
Lightly sear turmeric-salted prawns in mustard oil. Temper the oil with nigella seeds and slit green chillies.
Add both the ground coconut paste and reserved grated coconut with warm water, salt, sugar, and prawns; simmer for 6-8 minutes until rich and fragrant.

notes: Uses whole freshly grated coconut for a textured, sweet-savory Bengali prawn curry.

name: Narkel Diye Chingri Mathar Bora (Prawn Head & Grated Coconut Fritters)

steps.section: Combine ground prawn heads and coconut
steps.text: Mix coarsely ground cleaned prawn heads with freshly grated coconut, chopped onion, ginger, green chillies, turmeric, salt, and a pinch of sugar.
Add rice flour and besan to bind into a firm mixture, shape into flat cakes, and shallow-fry in mustard oil until crisp and golden on both sides.

notes: Sweet grated coconut complements the rich umami of golda chingri head roe.

name: Narkel Naru

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Narkel Patisapta (Classic Bengali Crepes Stuffed with Coconut & Nolen Gur)

steps.section: Cook coconut pur and rest batter
steps.text: Simmer grated coconut with nolen gur and cardamom for 8–10 minutes until sticky. Whisk maida, rice flour, suji, 2 tbsp nolen gur, and milk into a smooth thin batter; rest 20 minutes.

steps.section: Make crepes and roll with coconut
steps.text: Brush a tawa lightly with ghee, spread a thin circle of batter, cook 1 minute, spoon coconut pur along one side, and roll neatly.

notes: Iconic Poush Sankranti Bengali pitha; serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Narkel Porota (Bengali Sweet Grated Coconut & Jaggery Stuffed Paratha)

ingredients.name: Date Palm Jaggery (Nolen Gur) or Grated Sugarcane Jaggery

steps.text: Cook grated coconut and jaggery in a pan on medium-low flame with 1 tsp ghee and cardamom powder until sticky and caramelized (like narkel naru puran); let cool.
Enclose coconut puran inside dough balls, seal edges securely, and roll into round flatbreads.
Cook on tawa with desi ghee on both sides until golden and caramelized. Serve warm as a sweet winter evening treat.

notes: A nostalgic Bengali pithe-style sweet paratha stuffed with caramel-sweet coconut and nolen gur.

name: Navratan Mixture (Nine-Gem Lentil, Potato Lachha, Nut & Raisin Namkeen)

steps.section: Fry crisp potato lachha and lentils
steps.text: Rinse and dry grated potato juliennes and deep-fry until crisp; separately fry soaked chana, moong, and masoor dals until crunchy.

steps.section: Fry dry fruits and curry leaves
steps.text: Lightly fry peanuts, cashews, almonds, melon seeds, and raisins until golden.

steps.section: Combine nine components with sweet-tangy-mint masala
steps.text: Toss potato lachha, fried dals, besan sev, boondi, and dry fruits with black salt, amchur, powdered sugar, dried mint, and warm spices.

notes: Classic nine-ingredient ('Navratan') festive namkeen blending crunchy lentils, potato sticks, and dry fruits.

name: Nepali Chaukani / Chukauni (Palpali Spiced Potato Yogurt Salad)

steps.text: In a mixing bowl, combine diced boiled potatoes with whisked yogurt, sliced red onion, green chillies, roasted cumin powder, salt, and lemon juice or amchur.

Heat mustard oil in a small pan until smoking hot. Add fenugreek seeds and cook until dark brown and aromatic. Turn off heat, quickly stir in turmeric and red chilli powder, and immediately pour the sizzling oil over the potato-yogurt mixture.
Gently fold the golden oil into the creamy yogurt salad, garnish with fresh chopped coriander leaves, and serve warm or chilled.

notes: The authentic Palpa district specialty: a creamy, tangy, and aromatic spiced potato yogurt salad ready in minutes.

name: Nikuti / Nikhuti (Bengali Tiny Fried Chhena & Khoya Sweets in Cardamom Syrup)

steps.section: Knead chhena-khoya dough and shape tiny cylinders
steps.text: Knead fresh chhena, grated khoya, maida, suji, cardamom powder, and a pinch of baking soda until smooth, then roll into bite-sized 1-inch cylindrical shapes.
Boil sugar with 1.5 cups water and crushed cardamom pods for 6–7 minutes to form a sticky single-thread light syrup; keep warm.

steps.section: Slow-fry until golden brown and soak
steps.text: Deep-fry the nikhuti cylinders on low-medium heat in ghee/oil until deep golden-brown, then transfer directly into warm sugar syrup and soak for 1 hour.

notes: Classic Bengali miniature pantua-style sweet served standalone or as a garnish over payesh and sitabhog.

name: Nimbu Pani

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Niramish Aloor Dum (Bengali No-Onion No-Garlic Festive Potato Dum)

steps.text: Fry halved potatoes in mustard oil with a pinch of turmeric and salt until golden brown; set aside.

Temper oil with bay leaf, whole garam masala, cumin seeds, and hing. Sauté ginger paste, tomato puree, Kashmiri chilli, cumin-coriander powder, whisked yogurt, and cashew-melon seed paste until oil floats.
Add fried potatoes, warm water, salt, and a touch of sugar; cover and cook until fork-tender, finishing with ghee and Bengali garam masala.

notes: Traditional Bengali puja bhog and Ashtami luchi accompaniment without onion or garlic.

name: No-Fry Tawa Bread Pakora (Shallow-Crisped Besan-Coated Stuffed Bread Triangles)

steps.text: Sandwich spiced mashed potato between bread slices and cut diagonally. Whisk besan with ajwain, turmeric, chilli, salt, and water into a light batter.
Coat each triangle lightly with batter and toast on a lightly oiled hot tawa on medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp, cooked through, and golden.

notes: Low-oil everyday alternative to deep-fried bread pakora.

name: Nokshi Pitha / Nakshi Pitha (Ornamental Hand-Carved Crisp Rice-Flour Pitha in Gur Syrup)

steps.section: Knead dough and carve floral patterns
steps.text: Stir rice flour into boiling salted water, cover 5 minutes, and knead smooth. Roll 1/4-inch thick, cut into rounds or leaves, brush lightly with oil, and carve geometric or floral motifs using a toothpick/clean bamboo skewer.

steps.section: Double-fry crisp and coat in syrup
steps.text: Fry on medium-low heat until crisp pale gold (or fry twice for extra crunch), then dip briefly in warm thick jaggery-cardamom syrup and drain.

notes: Traditional Bangladeshi-Bengali artistic pitha prized for its intricate hand-carved motifs.

name: Nolen Gur Payesh

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Nolen Gurer Rosogolla (Winter Date Palm Jaggery Spongy Rasgulla)

ingredients.name: Liquid Nolen Gur (Date Palm Jaggery / Jhola Gur)

steps.section: Knead chhena until silky and roll balls
steps.text: Knead the moist chhena with maida for 10 minutes until smooth and non-grainy, then roll into 12–14 smooth balls without cracks.

steps.section: Simmer nolen gur and sugar syrup
steps.text: Boil water, sugar, and Nolen Gur in a wide deep pot, skimming any foam so the aromatic amber syrup boils briskly.

steps.section: Cook covered until spongy and plump
steps.text: Gently slide in the chhena balls, cover tightly, and boil on medium-high flame for 18–20 minutes until spongy and soaked through with smoky date-palm jaggery.

notes: Signature Bengali winter sweet made with aromatic new-season Nolen Gur.

name: Note Shak Bori Chorchori (Green Amaranth Stems, Potato, Pumpkin & Fried Lentil Dumpling Chorchori)

steps.section: Fry bori and sauté vegetables and amaranth stems
steps.text: Fry the bori in mustard oil until golden and set aside; temper oil with panch phoron and dry red chilli, and sauté potato, pumpkin, brinjal, and tender note shak stems with turmeric and salt.

steps.section: Cook with amaranth leaves, mustard-poppy paste and bori
steps.text: Add the chopped note shak leaves, mustard-poppy paste, green chillies, and a splash of water; cook covered until tender and fold in the fried bori and a pinch of sugar.

notes: A rustic Bengali summer chorchori that celebrates tender amaranth stems and sun-dried bori.

name: Notun Aloor Dum (Bengali Winter Baby Potato Dum)

steps.text: Parboil peeled baby new potatoes in salted turmeric water for 6 minutes, drain, prick with a fork, and fry in mustard oil until golden.
Temper oil with bay leaf, whole garam masala, and hing. Cook ginger-green chilli paste, tomato puree, and spice powders until oil separates.

steps.section: Simmer on dum with green peas
steps.text: Add fried baby potatoes, fresh green peas, and warm water; cover and cook on low heat for 8 minutes. Finish with ghee, bhaja masala, and chopped coriander.

notes: Essential companion to Koraishutir Kochuri at every Bengali winter picnic and feast.

name: Oats & Besan Chilla (High-Protein Rolled Oats, Gram Flour & Herb Breakfast Crepes)

steps.text: Whisk powdered oats, besan, curd, spices, salt, and 1.25 cups water into a smooth batter. Let rest for 10 minutes so the oats soften.

steps.section: Stir in vegetables and cook crepes
steps.text: Fold in onion, grated carrot, tomato, ginger, green chilli, and coriander. Spread on a hot greased tawa and cook on medium flame for 2.5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Serve hot with mint-curd chutney or plain yogurt.

notes: High-fiber, low-glycemic breakfast combining soluble beta-glucan fiber from oats with plant protein from besan.

name: Oats & Peanut Jaggery Laddoo (Toasted Rolled Oats, Crushed Peanuts & Gur Laddoo)

steps.text: Dry-roast oats and desiccated coconut on low-medium heat for 6 minutes until crisp and nutty; crush slightly by hand once cool enough.
Melt jaggery with ghee and 2 tbsp water until bubbling, toss in toasted oats, coconut, crushed peanuts, and cardamom, and shape into warm laddoos.

notes: Quick fibre-rich snack laddoo for breakfast or afternoon tiffin.

name: Oats & Sooji Vegetable Toast (Wholesome Semolina, Rolled Oats & Carrot Tawa Sandwich)

ingredients.name: Multigrain or Whole Wheat Bread Slices

steps.section: Soak oats and sooji in curd
steps.text: Mix sooji, quick oats, whisked curd, vegetables, pepper, cumin, and salt; rest 10 minutes until oats and sooji soften.
Spread on bread slices and toast topping-side down on a lightly oiled tawa for 3–4 minutes, then flip and crisp the other side.

notes: High-fibre morning toast combining oats and semolina.

name: Oats Paratha (Spiced Rolled Oats & Vegetable Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Sauté ginger, chillies, onions, carrots, and capsicum in 1 tsp oil, add toasted oats, cumin, chaat masala, salt, and 2 tbsp water to moisten slightly; cool.
Pack the oats-vegetable mixture into dough balls, seal, and roll into circles.
Cook on hot tawa with ghee or oil until crisp and nicely browned. Serve with spiced curd.

notes: A high-fiber, heart-healthy modern breakfast flatbread.

name: Oats Vegetable Khichdi (Savory Rolled Oats, Yellow Moong Dal & Garden Vegetable Khichdi)

steps.text: Heat ghee in a pan or cooker, crackle cumin, mustard, curry leaves, and hing. Saute onions, ginger, tomatoes, carrots, beans, and soaked moong dal with 2.5 cups water until dal is soft.
Add dry-toasted rolled oats, turmeric, pepper, and salt plus 1 cup hot water. Simmer on low heat for 4-5 minutes until creamy and porridge-like.
Finish with fresh coriander leaves and lemon juice; serve hot as a light dinner or wholesome breakfast.

notes: Quick, heart-healthy beta-glucan rich khichdi ready in 20 minutes without rice.

name: Odia Machha Bihana Bara (Odia Spiced Garlic Fish Egg Fritters)

steps.text: Combine cleaned fish eggs with crushed garlic-cumin paste, chopped onion, green chillies, curry leaves, turmeric, besan, rice powder, and salt.
Shape into flat patties and pan-fry in hot mustard oil over low-medium heat until golden and cooked through.

notes: A classic Odia accompaniment to Pakhala Bhata (fermented water rice) or dalma.

name: Odia Machha Bihana Besara (Fish Eggs in Odia Mustard-Garlic Gravy)

steps.section: Pan-fry fish egg cakes and potatoes
steps.text: Mix fish eggs with 1.5 tbsp besan, salt, and turmeric; pan-fry into small cakes alongside potato wedges in mustard oil.
Temper oil with panch phoron and dry red chilli, sauté chopped tomato, turmeric, and the ground mustard-garlic-cumin paste with warm water and potatoes.

steps.section: Add fish egg cakes and ambula
steps.text: Once potatoes are soft, add the fish egg cakes and soaked ambula, simmer 5 minutes, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Garlic-scented mustard paste (besara) and tangy ambula make this a signature Odia fish roe curry.

name: Ol Bharta (Elephant Foot Yam / Suran Chokha)

ingredients.name: Mustard Paste (Shorshe Bata) or Roasted Mustard Powder

steps.text: Oil your palms before peeling and cubing the elephant foot yam, then boil or pressure-cook with a slice of lemon and salt until very soft.
Drain thoroughly and mash the warm yam while hot until completely smooth.
Mix in mustard paste, chopped green chillies, lemon juice, salt, and pungent mustard oil.

notes: Lemon juice neutralizes any natural calcium oxalate itchiness in the yam and brightens the flavour.

name: Ol Chingri Dalna (Elephant Foot Yam & Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Parboil cubed elephant foot yam in salted water for 5 minutes, drain, and fry until golden alongside potato cubes. Lightly fry prawns and set aside.
Temper mustard oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, cook onion and ginger-garlic paste with tomato and spice powders until oil separates.
Add yam, potatoes, and warm water; simmer until tender, then add fried prawns, garam masala, and ghee.

notes: Meaty elephant foot yam cubes soak up the spiced prawn gravy wonderfully.

name: Ol Fry / Ol Bhaja (Bengali Crispy Elephant Foot Yam / Suran Pan-Fry)

steps.text: Boil sliced elephant foot yam in salted water with 1 tsp lemon juice for 5 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Coat the yam slices with turmeric, red chilli, roasted cumin, rice flour, poppy seeds, and salt, and shallow-fry in hot mustard oil until golden and crisp.

notes: Boiling with lemon juice removes any acridity and makes Ol Fry tender and delicious.

name: Old-Fashioned Baked Bread and Butter Pudding (Golden Raisin & Nutmeg Baked Custard Pudding)

ingredients.name: Soft White Bread or Brioche Slices

steps.text: Generously butter each bread slice on one side, cut diagonally into triangles. Arrange buttered side up in an overlapping pattern in a greased baking dish, scattering golden raisins between layers.

Whisk together milk, heavy cream, eggs, caster sugar, vanilla extract, cinnamon, and freshly grated nutmeg until smooth and sugar dissolves. Pour custard evenly over the bread triangles and let soak for 15 minutes.

Sprinkle Demerara sugar on top for crunch. Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 35-40 minutes until custard is gently set in the center and bread tops are crisp and golden brown. Serve warm with cream.

notes: Classic heritage dessert turning humble bread into a comforting, fragrant baked custard with crispy golden peaks and custardy soft center.

name: Oler Bora / Elephant Foot Yam Fritters (Crispy Spiced Suran & Coconut Fritters)

steps.section: Combine mashed boiled yam with mustard, coconut and lemon
steps.text: Mash boiled ol with lemon juice, mustard paste, grated coconut, green chillies, ginger, kalo jeere, turmeric, salt, besan, and rice flour into a firm mixture.

steps.section: Shape and fry until crisp and golden
steps.text: Form into flat round cakes, dust lightly with rice flour or poppy seeds, and shallow-fry in hot mustard oil until both sides are crisp.

notes: A traditional Bengali autumn specialty served with steaming rice and ghee.

steps.text: Boil, peel and slit eggs if making curry; whisk if making bhurji or omelette.
Sauté onion and tomato with spices until soft and fragrant.
Add eggs and a little water for curry, or scramble gently for bhurji; cook through.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (Coarsely Grated, Rinsed and Squeezed Dry)

steps.text: Saute sliced onion in 1 tbsp butter/oil on medium-low heat for 6 minutes until sweet and golden.

steps.section: Crisp potatoes with onion and pepper
steps.text: Add remaining oil/butter, spread dried grated potatoes over the onions, season with salt and crushed black pepper, and cook 6 minutes per side until crisp.

notes: Sweet sauteed onions contrast wonderfully with bold cracked black pepper.

name: Onion Capsicum Sandwich

steps.text: Thinly slice the onion and capsicum. Add tomato if desired, and season with salt, black pepper and a little chaat masala.
Heat a little butter or oil in a pan. Sauté onion and capsicum for 3–4 minutes until slightly softened but still crisp. Add cheese if desired.
Spread butter or green chutney on the bread. Add the vegetable filling and close with the remaining bread slices.
Toast in a pan or sandwich maker until golden and crisp. Cut and serve hot.

notes: Adjust the vegetables and seasoning to taste. For a raw version, skip sautéing and use thinly sliced vegetables.

steps.text: Wash and slice vegetables or prepare the listed filling.

steps.text: Beat eggs with salt, pepper and optional milk or water; prepare the listed variation ingredients.
Heat butter or oil in a pan. Add vegetables first if needed, pour in eggs and cook gently; fold when set.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

name: Onion, Tomato & Green Chilli Sooji Toast (Desi Street-Style Rava Bread Sandwich)

steps.text: Combine sooji, curd/milk, 2 tbsp water, onion, tomato, green chillies, coriander, chilli powder, and salt; rest 8 minutes.
Spread onto bread slices, toast topping-side down in butter on medium-low heat until golden, flip to crisp the bottom, and sprinkle with chaat masala.

notes: Quick 20-minute street-style rava toast with pantry staples.

name: Open-Faced Cheese Tomato Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Orange Citrus Custard Pudding (Fresh Orange Zest & Juice Infused Silky Custard Pudding)

steps.text: In a saucepan, simmer 1 cup of orange juice with 2 tbsp sugar for 5 minutes until slightly reduced and flavors intensify. Let cool.

Whisk cornflour into 0.5 cup cold milk. Heat remaining milk, orange zest, remaining sugar, and remaining orange juice. Whisk in the cornflour slurry and cook on medium-low flame, whisking continuously for 4-5 minutes until thick, glossy, and bubble bursts appear. Whisk in butter.
Spoon custard into serving coupes. Chill in the refrigerator for 2 hours. Top with fresh juicy orange segments and a spoonful of the orange reduction before serving.

notes: Bright and invigorating dessert balancing sweet creamy milk custard with the zesty, floral acidity of freshly picked oranges.

name: Oreo Milkshake

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Paal Payasam

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Pabda Bhaja

Heat oil and lightly fry or sear fish; set aside.
Cook potato, tomato and spices, add water, then return fish and simmer gently until cooked through.

name: Pabda Macher Tel Bori Jhol (Pabda Catfish with Fried Bori, Eggplant & Fresh Coriander)

steps.section: Fry bori, eggplant and pabda fish
steps.text: Fry the bori in hot mustard oil until golden and remove; fry eggplant wedges and set aside, then carefully fry pabda fish (covered to prevent spluttering) until lightly golden.

steps.section: Simmer tel-jhol with kalo jeere, bori and coriander
steps.text: Temper oil with kalo jeere and green chillies, sauté tomato quarters with turmeric, cumin, and Kashmiri chilli powder, add 1.25 cups warm water, and simmer pabda fish, fried bori, and brinjal for 4 minutes; top with chopped coriander.

notes: Winter coriander leaves, kalo jeere, and fried bori make Pabda Tel Bori Jhol a Sunday lunch classic.
