name: Pakon Pitha (Bengali Crisp Patterned Moong Dal & Rice-Flour Pitha in Syrup)

ingredients.name: Yellow Moong Dal (Dry-roasted, Boiled Soft & Mashed)

steps.section: Knead moong-rice dough and imprint designs
steps.text: Mix smooth mashed moong dal with rice flour, maida, ghee, salt, and warm water into a pliable dough. Roll thick discs and press fork or skewer patterns on top.

steps.section: Fry crisp and soak briefly in syrup
steps.text: Fry on medium-low heat until deep golden and crisp, then dip into warm spiced jaggery/sugar syrup for 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Dry-roasting the moong dal before boiling gives a rich nutty aroma.

name: Pakora

steps.text: Chop or mash the main ingredients and combine with onion, chilli, spices and binder.
Shape into portions or coat in batter or breadcrumbs as appropriate.
Shallow-fry, deep-fry or bake until golden and cooked through. Drain and serve hot.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Palak Besan Chilla (Iron-Rich Fresh Spinach Puree & Carom-Spiced Gram Flour Pancakes)

ingredients.name: Fresh Spinach (Palak, Blanched & Pureed or Finely Shredded)

steps.text: Blend blanched spinach leaves with ginger and green chillies into a vibrant green puree, or finely shred fresh baby spinach.
Mix besan, spinach puree, finely chopped onion, ajwain, sesame seeds, turmeric, black pepper, salt, and water into a smooth pouring batter.
Spread ladlefuls onto a hot greased tawa, sprinkle a few sesame seeds on top, and roast with a little ghee on both sides until crisp-edged and cooked through.

notes: Vibrant green savory crepes that pair wonderfully with garlic-tempered curd or tomato chutney.

name: Palak Corn Paratha (Spiced Spinach & Sweet Corn Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Sauté garlic and chillies in butter, add chopped spinach and crushed corn; cook on high heat until dry, then season with chaat masala, amchur, and salt.
Enclose filling in whole wheat dough portions and roll out into neat discs.
Cook on a hot tawa with butter or ghee until crisp with golden blisters. Serve with yogurt or pickle.

notes: A delicious pairing of sweet golden corn and tender green spinach.

name: Palak Gatta Curry (Spinach & Gram Flour Dumplings in Garlic-Tempered Yogurt Curry)

steps.text: Combine besan, finely chopped spinach, 1 tbsp oil, ajwain, ginger-chilli paste, turmeric, and salt. Knead into cylindrical logs (the moisture from spinach requires very little water) and boil in simmering water for 10 minutes. Slice into emerald-flecked medallions.

Heat ghee, temper cumin, hing, and golden minced garlic. Whisk curd with coriander, turmeric, and red chilli powder, pour into the pan on low heat while stirring, and bring to a gentle boil with reserved poaching water.
Add the sliced spinach gattas into the simmering curry and cook for 5–6 minutes until the dumplings absorb the tangy garlic-yogurt flavors.

notes: Fresh spinach leaves folded into the besan dough keep the gattas naturally moist, vibrant, and iron-rich.

name: Palak Masala Rice / Spinach Corn Pulao (Pureed Spinach, Sweet Corn, Garlic & Whole Spice Fragrant Rice)

ingredients.name: Fresh Spinach Leaves (Palak, Blanched & Pureed with 1 Green Chilli)

steps.text: Heat ghee, temper cumin and whole spices, then saute minced garlic, ginger, and diced onion until translucent. Toss in sweet corn kernels for 2 minutes.
Stir in fresh spinach puree, coriander powder, garam masala, and kasuri methi; simmer 3 minutes.

steps.section: Simmer rice until vibrant green and fluffy
steps.text: Fold in drained basmati rice, 2.25 cups hot water, salt, and a squeeze of lemon juice; cover and simmer 12 minutes.

notes: Nutritious green masala rice where sweet corn pops against garlic-spiced spinach.

name: Palak Paneer (Cottage Cheese Cubes in Velvety Spiced Spinach Puree)

steps.section: Blanch spinach in boiling water and shock in ice water
steps.text: Blanch spinach leaves with green chillies in boiling water for 2 minutes, transfer immediately to ice-cold water to lock in bright green color, and blend into a smooth puree.

steps.section: Sauté garlic-onion tadka and simmer with spinach and paneer
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil, crackle cumin seeds and chopped garlic, sauté chopped onion, ginger, and tomato with cumin-coriander powder, stir in the spinach puree and soft paneer cubes, simmer 4 minutes, and finish with kasuri methi, garam masala, and cream.

notes: Shocking blanched spinach in ice water keeps Palak Paneer vibrant emerald green.

name: Palak Paneer Paratha (Spiced Spinach & Cottage Cheese Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Combine squeezed chopped spinach with crumbled paneer, garlic, ginger, green chillies, garam masala, cumin, kasuri methi, and salt.
Place filling inside rolled dough rounds, pinch to seal, and roll out with light pressure.
Cook on griddle with ghee until speckled with golden spots. Serve with curd and pickle.

notes: Brings the classic restaurant curry flavors of Palak Paneer inside a crisp stuffed whole wheat paratha.

name: Palak Paratha (Spiced Spinach Whole Wheat Paratha)

steps.text: Blend blanched spinach with ginger, garlic, and green chillies; knead with wheat flour, besan, ajwain, salt, and 1 tsp oil into a soft green dough.
Roll each ball, brush with a drop of ghee, fold into a triangle or square, and roll out evenly.
Cook on a medium-hot tawa with ghee until cooked through and lightly browned.

notes: Iron-rich, colorful flatbread that stays soft for hours in lunchboxes.

name: Palak Prawns (Prawns in Spiced Spinach Gravy)

steps.text: Blanch spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, plunge into cold water, and blend smooth with green chillies.
Lightly sear seasoned prawns and set aside. In the same pan, crackle cumin seeds, brown chopped garlic and onion, and cook tomato with spices.
Stir in the vibrant spinach puree and seared prawns, simmer gently for 5 minutes, and finish with garam masala and a swirl of cream or butter.

notes: Iron-rich spinach and high-protein prawns make a nutritious curry for roti or rice.

name: Palak Puri (Crispy Spiced Spinach Poori)

steps.text: Knead wheat flour, fine sooji, ajwain, cumin, hing, salt, 1 tbsp hot oil, and spinach puree into a firm, tight poori dough; rest 15 minutes.
Roll small balls into even discs and fry in hot oil until they puff into vibrant green, crispy puris.

notes: Adding 2 tbsp fine semolina keeps Palak Puris puffed and crisp for longer.

name: Palak Shorba / Cream of Spinach Soup (Spiced Velvety Spinach & Cardamom Green Soup)

steps.text: Blanch washed spinach leaves in boiling water for 1.5 minutes, then plunge immediately into iced water to preserve its vivid emerald green hue.
Heat ghee, temper with cumin seeds and green cardamom. Saute onions, garlic, and diced potato in broth for 10 minutes until potato is tender.
Blend cooked potato broth with the blanched spinach until silky smooth. Warm gently, swirl in fresh cream, roasted cumin, and black salt.

notes: Ice-shocking preserves chlorophyll, giving the shorba an irresistible bright emerald color.

name: Palang Shaker Kochuri (Bengali Spiced Spinach & Hing Stuffed Puri)

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil, add hing, ginger-chilli paste, and thick spinach puree. Cook on medium heat with roasted cumin-fennel powder, salt, and sugar. Stir in roasted besan until it forms a cohesive dough-like filling; cool.
Knead maida with ghee, salt, and water. Shape into cups, fill with emerald spinach paste, seal tightly, and roll gently.
Fry in medium-hot oil until puffed and crisp. Serve with dum aloo or chana masala.

notes: Vibrant emerald winter kochuri scented with asafoetida and dry-roasted spices.

name: Palong Shak Bori Ghonto (Winter Spinach, Eggplant, Radish & Fried Lentil Dumpling Medley)

ingredients.name: Biulir Daler Bori or Motor Daler Bori

steps.section: Fry bori and sauté winter vegetables with panch phoron
steps.text: Fry the bori in mustard oil until crisp and golden, then set aside; temper the oil with bay leaf, dry red chilli, and panch phoron, and sauté potato, radish, flat beans, pumpkin, and brinjal with ginger and turmeric.

steps.section: Wilt spinach and finish with crushed fried bori
steps.text: Add chopped palong shak, salt, and roasted cumin powder, cover until the vegetables are tender in the spinach's moisture, and fold in whole and half-crushed fried bori with a touch of sugar.

notes: Fried bori is the signature finishing touch of a winter Bengali Palong Shaker Ghonto.

name: Palong Shaker Bora / Palak Pakora (Crispy Spinach Leaf Fritters)

ingredients.name: Whole Tender Leaves or Roughly Chopped

steps.text: Wash tender spinach leaves thoroughly, drain off all excess moisture, and either keep whole leaves (for Palak Patta Chaat/Fritters) or chop coarsely.

steps.section: Coat in spiced besan-rice batter and fry
steps.text: Dip whole leaves in a thin rice-besan batter (or bind chopped spinach with dry flours, kalo jeere, green chillies, and salt) and fry in hot mustard oil until emerald-green and shatteringly crisp.

notes: Pairs wonderfully with hot masoor dal and steamed rice on winter afternoons.

name: Panch Phoron Aloor Torkari (Bengali Five-Spice Homestyle Potato Curry)

ingredients.name: Panch Phoron (Fenugreek, Nigella, Cumin, Black Mustard, Fennel)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil until smoking lightly, then temper with bay leaf, dry red chillies, and panch phoron until the seeds pop.
Add cubed potatoes, quartered tomato, slit green chillies, turmeric, and salt; stir-fry for 4 minutes.
Add warm water and a pinch of sugar, cover and cook until potatoes are soft, mash 2-3 pieces to thicken the gravy, and garnish with coriander.

notes: Simple, fragrant 5-spice Bengali potato curry that requires zero spice grinding.

name: Panchmel Dal Khichdi / Satpadi Khichdi (Rajasthani Five-Lentil & Spiced Ghee Khichdi)

ingredients.name: Five-lentil Blend (Moong, Masoor, Chana, Toor, and Urad Dal)

steps.section: Soak and boil rice with five lentils
steps.text: Wash and soak the five-lentil blend and rice for 20 minutes. Pressure-cook with 4.5 cups water, turmeric, bay leaf, cloves, and salt for 3-4 whistles until rich and creamy.
Heat desi ghee in a pan, crackle cumin seeds, hing, and dry red chillies. Saute ginger-chilli paste, tomatoes, coriander powder, amchur, and garam masala until oil separates.
Fold the cooked five-lentil khichdi into the tempering, simmer for 3 minutes, and garnish with fresh coriander and extra ghee.

notes: Combines the distinct textures and amino-acid profiles of five traditional Indian dals in one nourishing pot.

name: Panchmishali Sabjir Bora / Mixed Vegetable Pakora (Crispy Five-Vegetable Bengali Telebhaja)

steps.section: Toss julienned mixed vegetables with salt and aromatics
steps.text: Combine thin matchsticks of potato, potol, brinjal, carrot, and cabbage with salt, ginger, green chillies, coriander, kalo jeere, poppy seeds, and bhaja moshla; rest for 5 minutes.

steps.section: Bind with besan and rice flour and deep-fry
steps.text: Fold in besan and rice flour so the vegetables are lightly bound by their own moisture, then drop jagged clusters into medium-hot mustard oil and fry until golden and crisp.

notes: A classic Bengali rainy-evening telebhaja served with jhalmuri, kasundi, and adrak wali cha.

name: Panchmishali Sabzi Fry / Bhaja Thali (Bengali Five-Vegetable Crispy Fry Platter)

steps.section: Season all five vegetables with turmeric and salt
steps.text: Rub potol, kakrol, kumro, begun, and aloo separately with turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt.

steps.section: Pan-fry in batches in mustard oil
steps.text: In a cast-iron kadai with smoking mustard oil, fry aloo, potol, kakrol, kumro, and finally begun until each vegetable is golden brown and crisp, and arrange around steamed rice and dal.

notes: Traditional Bengali Panch-Bhaja (five-vegetable fry) platter served at festive lunches and Pujo bhog.

name: Paneer & Mushroom Schezwan Chowmin / Chowmein (Spicy Cottage Cheese, Mushroom & Bell Pepper Noodles)

steps.text: Lightly dust paneer cubes with cornflour and pan-fry with sliced button mushrooms in hot oil for 4 minutes until golden; set aside.

steps.section: Stir-fry garlic, vegetables, and Schezwan sauce
steps.text: Sauté minced garlic on high flame, stir-fry cabbage, carrots, and bell peppers for 3 minutes, and stir in Schezwan sauce and soy sauce.

steps.section: Toss with boiled noodles, paneer, and mushrooms
steps.text: Add al dente chowmin, seared paneer, and mushrooms; toss over high flame for 3 minutes and top with spring onion greens.

notes: Hearty vegetarian Schezwan chowmin loaded with golden paneer and seared mushrooms.

name: Paneer & Sweet Corn Schezwan Fried Rice (Spicy Paneer, Corn & Capsicum Wok-Tossed Rice)

steps.text: Pan-fry diced paneer in 1.5 tbsp hot oil until golden on the edges and set aside.

steps.section: Stir-fry garlic, sweet corn, veggies, and Schezwan sauce
steps.text: Sauté minced garlic and spring onion whites, toss in carrots, beans, capsicum, and sweet corn for 3 minutes, then add Schezwan sauce and soy sauce.

steps.section: Fold in chilled rice and golden paneer
steps.text: Add chilled Basmati rice and fried paneer cubes, toss on high flame for 3 minutes, and garnish with spring onion greens.

notes: Spicy-sweet contrast of fiery Schezwan sauce, golden paneer, and juicy sweet corn kernels.

name: Paneer 65 (South Indian Style Crispy Spiced Yogurt & Curry Leaf Fried Paneer Starter)

steps.section: Marinate paneer in spiced yogurt-rice flour batter and deep-fry
steps.text: Coat paneer cubes in thick yogurt, rice flour, cornflour, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri red chilli, cumin, garam masala, lemon juice, and salt; deep-fry in hot oil until crunchy and crimson.

steps.section: Toss in tempered curry-leaf and garlic yogurt glaze
steps.text: In 1 tbsp oil, crackle mustard seeds, minced garlic, slit green chillies, and curry leaves, stir in 1 tbsp spiced yogurt and chilli powder, and toss the crispy fried paneer on high heat until coated.

notes: Crispy curry leaves and rice-flour batter give Paneer 65 an addictive crunch.

name: Paneer Bhurji (Spiced Scrambled Cottage Cheese with Onion, Tomato, Ginger & Coriander)

steps.section: Sauté onion, ginger, green chillies and tomato in butter
steps.text: Heat oil and butter, crackle cumin seeds, sauté chopped onion, ginger, green chillies, and capsicum until soft, then cook chopped tomatoes with turmeric, chilli powder, and garam masala/pav bhaji masala.

steps.section: Fold in crumbled paneer with a splash of milk
steps.text: Add hand-crumbled paneer and 2 tbsp milk (to keep the scramble moist and creamy), toss on medium flame for 2-3 minutes without overcooking, and finish with kasuri methi and fresh coriander.

notes: Adding 2 tablespoons of milk keeps Paneer Bhurji soft and creamy rather than dry and crumbly.

name: Paneer Bhurji Paratha (Spicy Scrambled Cottage Cheese & Green Chilli Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Sauté onion, ginger, and green chillies in 1 tbsp butter, add tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, pav bhaji masala, and salt. Cook until mushy, stir in crumbled paneer and kasuri methi, and cook until dry; let cool.
Pack paneer bhurji inside wheat dough portions, seal tightly, and roll out gently.
Roast on a hot griddle with butter until golden and crisp. Serve with spiced raita and green chutney.

notes: Street-style spiced tawa paneer bhurji stuffed into a buttery, flaky paratha.

name: Paneer Bhurji Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Paneer Bhurji Sooji Sandwich (Crispy Semolina Sandwich Stuffed with Spiced Crumbled Paneer)

steps.section: Make sooji batter and spiced paneer bhurji
steps.text: Whisk sooji, curd, salt, and 1/2 cup water; rest 10 minutes. Saute onion, capsicum, and green chilli in 1 tsp oil for 2 minutes, toss in crumbled paneer, spices, and salt, and cook 2 minutes.
Stir baking soda into batter. Spread half on a greased pan/sandwich maker, layer paneer bhurji in the center, cover with remaining batter, and cook covered 4 minutes per side until crisp golden.

notes: Protein-packed breadless sandwich with crisp semolina crust and soft paneer filling.

name: Paneer Bhurji Stuffed Besan Chilla (Street-Style Spiced Cottage Cheese Stuffed Gram Flour Pancake)

steps.text: Toss crumbled paneer with finely diced onion, capsicum, grated carrot, green chillies, fresh coriander, chaat masala, roasted cumin powder, black pepper, and a pinch of salt.

Whisk besan with water, ajwain, turmeric, ginger paste, and salt into a smooth pouring batter. Pour onto a hot greased tawa and spread into a thin, even round. Cook with butter/ghee until the underside is crisp and golden, flipping briefly for 30 seconds.

Spread a generous line of seasoned paneer stuffing down the center of the chilla, fold both sides into a roll, slice in half diagonally, and serve immediately with green chutney and sweet tamarind chutney.

notes: A North Indian street-food and wedding live-counter favorite packed with protein from both gram flour and cottage cheese.

name: Paneer Butter Masala (Creamy Tomato, Cashew & Butter Gravy with Soft Paneer Cubes)

steps.section: Simmer and puree tomatoes, cashews and aromatics
steps.text: Simmer roughly chopped tomatoes, soaked cashews, ginger, garlic, green cardamom, and Kashmiri red chilli powder with 1 cup water for 10 minutes; cool and blend into a silky-smooth puree, then strain.

steps.section: Cook strained makhani gravy in butter and add paneer
steps.text: Melt 2 tbsp butter in a pan, add the strained tomato-cashew puree, coriander powder, salt, and 1 tsp sugar/honey; simmer 5 minutes, fold in soft paneer cubes, crushed kasuri methi, garam masala, and fresh cream.

notes: Straining the tomato-cashew puree gives restaurant-style velvety smoothness.

name: Paneer Chowmin / Paneer Chowmein (Crispy Fried Paneer & Bell Pepper Hakka Noodles)

steps.text: Dust paneer strips lightly with cornflour, salt, and black pepper and shallow-fry in hot oil until golden-crisp on the edges; drain and set aside.
Sauté chopped garlic and ginger on high flame, then stir-fry carrots, cabbage, and tri-color bell peppers for 3 minutes.

steps.section: Toss noodles with crispy paneer and sauces
steps.text: Add boiled noodles, crispy paneer fingers, soy sauce, chilli sauce, ketchup, vinegar, and black pepper; toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes.

notes: Rich vegetarian Indo-Chinese chowmin studded with golden-crisp paneer strips.

name: Paneer Corn Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Paneer Do Pyaza (Cottage Cheese Cooked with Caramelized & Crunchy Onion Petals)

steps.section: Pan-sear paneer cubes and onion petals
steps.text: Sear paneer cubes and crisp onion petals in 1 tbsp ghee with a pinch of turmeric and crushed coriander seeds for 2 minutes; remove and set aside.

steps.section: Cook spiced onion-tomato-yogurt masala and combine
steps.text: Temper oil with cumin, fennel, and dry red chillies, sauté finely chopped onions until golden, cook ginger-garlic, tomatoes, and whisked yogurt with spices, and fold in the seared paneer and onion petals.

notes: 'Do Pyaza' uses onions at two stages—slow-caramelized in the base and crisp-seared petals at the end.

name: Paneer Fried Rice (Golden-Fried Paneer Cubes, Sweet Corn & Bell Pepper Fried Rice)

steps.text: Toss paneer cubes with a pinch of salt, pepper, and 1 tsp cornflour, then pan-fry in hot oil until golden on all sides; set aside.

steps.section: Stir-fry garlic, sweet corn, and bell peppers
steps.text: Sauté minced garlic, ginger, and green chillies on high flame, then stir-fry carrots, beans, sweet corn, and bell peppers for 3 minutes.

steps.section: Fold in chilled rice and golden paneer
steps.text: Add chilled rice, fried paneer cubes, soy sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar, and black pepper; toss gently on high heat for 3 minutes and garnish with spring onion greens.

notes: Protein-rich vegetarian Indo-Chinese fried rice with golden paneer cubes and crunchy bell peppers.

name: Paneer Jalfrezi (Stir-Fried Paneer Batons, Bell Peppers, Baby Corn & Tangy Tomato Glaze)

ingredients.name: Tomato Puree (0.5 Cup) + Tomato Ketchup (1 Tbsp) + Vinegar/lemon Juice

steps.section: Stir-fry paneer batons and crunchy vegetables on high heat
steps.text: Lightly sear paneer batons in oil and remove; in the same hot wok/kadai, crackle cumin seeds and stir-fry ginger juliennes, onions, bell peppers, and baby corn on high flame for 3 minutes so they stay crisp-tender.

steps.section: Toss in tangy spiced tomato glaze
steps.text: Add tomato puree, Kashmiri chilli, roasted cumin, garam masala, ketchup, vinegar, and salt; cook 2 minutes, toss in the paneer batons and tomato juliennes, and serve hot.

notes: Originating in colonial Bengal ('Jhal' + 'Frezi'), this colorful semi-dry stir-fry is ideal with parathas or rotis.

name: Paneer Kolhapuri (Fiery Roasted Coconut, Sesame & Red Chilli Maharashtrian Paneer Curry)

steps.section: Roast and grind Kolhapuri coconut-sesame masala
steps.text: Dry-roast whole spices, red chillies, sesame seeds, poppy seeds, and grated coconut until golden brown, then grind into a smooth paste with a splash of water.

steps.section: Cook spicy gravy and simmer with paneer
steps.text: Sauté finely chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste in oil, add tomato puree and the ground Kolhapuri masala, cook until oil floats on top, add warm water and seared paneer cubes, and simmer 4 minutes.

notes: Bold, smoky, and deeply spiced with toasted coconut and sesame.

name: Paneer Kosha (Spicy Slow-Braised Bengali Onion-Ginger-Garlic Paneer Curry)

steps.section: Caramelize onions and braise kosha masala
steps.text: Lightly sear paneer cubes and soak in warm water; in smoking mustard oil tempered with sugar and whole garam masala, fry sliced onions until deep brown, then slow-braise (kosha) with ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, yogurt, and spices.

steps.section: Fold in cashew paste and paneer cubes
steps.text: Stir in cashew paste and ½ cup warm water, add the soft paneer cubes, simmer for 4 minutes until coated in thick dark-glossy masala, and finish with ghee and gorom moshla.

notes: Cooked in the style of Bengali Kosha Mangsho for a bold, rich accompaniment to luchi, paratha, or pulao.

name: Paneer Lababdar (Rich Tomato-Cashew Gravy with Grated & Cubed Paneer)

steps.section: Prepare chunky onion-capsicum and smooth tomato-cashew base
steps.text: Sauté finely chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste, and diced capsicum in butter with whole spices, then add the smooth boiled tomato-cashew-melon seed puree and cook with Kashmiri chilli and coriander powder.

steps.section: Fold in grated paneer and paneer cubes
steps.text: Stir in 50g grated paneer to thicken the gravy into a luscious texture, add the lightly seared paneer cubes, kasuri methi, garam masala, and cream, and simmer 3 minutes.

notes: Adding grated paneer directly into the tomato-cashew gravy is what gives Paneer Lababdar its signature thick, textured body.

name: Paneer Manchurian (Crispy Paneer Fritters in Savory Ginger-Garlic-Coriander Manchurian Sauce)

steps.text: Dip paneer cubes in a smooth batter of cornflour, maida, ginger-garlic paste, pepper, and salt, and deep-fry until crisp and golden.

Sauté finely minced garlic, ginger, green chillies, chopped onion, and coriander stems in hot oil, add soy sauce, chilli sauce, ketchup, vinegar, and ¾ cup water thickened with 1 tbsp cornflour slurry, then toss in fried paneer and spring onions.

notes: Finely chopped coriander stems and garlic give Manchurian sauce its unmistakable savory depth.

name: Paneer Masala Papad Cone / Stuffed Papad Cones (Crispy Roasted Papad Cones Filled with Tangy Paneer, Corn & Chaat)

ingredients.name: Large Round Urad Papads (Halved into Semi-circles)

steps.section: Roast papad halves and shape into cones
steps.text: Roast each half-moon papad on a dry hot tawa pressing with a cloth until crisp, then immediately roll into a cone while still warm and pliable, holding for 10 seconds until it sets into a rigid cone.
In a bowl, toss diced paneer, sweet corn, onion, tomato, cucumber, roasted peanuts, chutneys, chaat masala, cumin powder, black salt, lemon juice, and coriander.

steps.section: Fill cones and crown with sev and pomegranate
steps.text: Spoon the paneer chaat mixture into the crispy papad cones just before serving and top with nylon sev and pomegranate pearls.

notes: Shaping the roasted papad within 5 seconds of lifting it off the hot tawa locks in the cone shape effortlessly.

name: Paneer Pakora (Crispy Ajwain-Spiced Gram Flour Batter-Fried Cottage Cheese Fritters)

ingredients.name: Green Mint-coriander Chutney or Chaat Masala

steps.section: Season paneer pieces and whisk spiced besan batter
steps.text: Sprinkle paneer slabs with chaat masala (or sandwich green chutney between two thin slices); whisk besan, rice flour, ajwain, kasuri methi, ginger-chilli paste, turmeric, chilli powder, salt, and water into a thick coating batter.

steps.section: Dip and deep-fry until golden and crisp
steps.text: Dip each spiced paneer piece in the batter and fry in medium-hot oil until golden brown and crisp outside while warm and soft inside.

notes: Serve hot with coriander-mint chutney, tomato ketchup, and evening masala chai.

name: Paneer Paratha (Spiced Cottage Cheese Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Mix grated paneer with finely chopped onion, green chillies, grated ginger, coriander leaves, ajwain, amchur, garam masala, and salt just before rolling so the filling stays dry.
Enclose a generous ball of paneer stuffing inside each soft wheat dough portion, dust with dry flour, and roll gently without tearing.
Roast on a hot tawa with ghee or butter until crisp golden spots appear on both sides. Serve hot with curd and pickle.

notes: Protein-rich Punjabi breakfast paratha.

name: Paneer Paratha Roll / Tawa Paneer Masala Kathi Wrap (Spiced Tawa Paneer & Pickled Onion Paratha Wrap)

ingredients.name: Flaky Wheat or Maida Laccha Parathas

steps.section: Toss spiced tawa paneer strips with capsicum
steps.text: Sauté ginger-garlic paste, onion, and capsicum strips on a hot tawa, add paneer strips, Kashmiri chilli, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and salt, and toss on high flame for 4 minutes until charred at the edges.
Spread mint chutney over warm crisp parathas, pile on the smoky tawa paneer filling, top with lemon-pickled onion rings, chaat masala, and a drizzle of ketchup, and roll tightly in paper.

notes: A quick, protein-packed meal or tiffin wrap.

name: Paneer Pasanda (Stuffed Paneer Sandwiches in Rich Almond-Cashew Cream Gravy)

ingredients.name: Cornflour Slurry (2 Tbsp Cornflour + 3 Tbsp Water) for Sealing

steps.section: Stuff paneer triangles, dip in cornflour slurry and shallow-fry
steps.text: Mix crumbled paneer with chopped nuts, raisins, mint, green chilli, and salt; sandwich between two thin paneer triangles, dip the edges in cornflour slurry, and shallow-fry until golden.

steps.section: Simmer rich nut-tomato gravy and arrange stuffed triangles
steps.text: Cook the smooth onion-tomato-cashew-melon seed paste in butter with spices and fresh cream until velvety; pour the hot gravy around the halved stuffed paneer triangles.

notes: A showstopping festive paneer dish with jewel-toned nut-and-mint filling inside every slice.

name: Paneer Paturi (Mustard-Poppy Coated Paneer Steamed in Banana Leaf Parcels)

ingredients.name: Black Mustard Paste (2 Tbsp) + Poppy Seed Paste

steps.section: Coat paneer slabs in thick mustard-poppy-coconut paste and wrap
steps.text: Mix mustard paste, poppy paste, grated coconut, green chilli paste, turmeric, salt, and 2 tbsp mustard oil; spread a thick layer on each wilted banana leaf, place a paneer slab and a slit green chilli, coat the top, and tie into neat parcels with cotton thread.

steps.section: Pan-roast banana leaf parcels on a tawa
steps.text: Brush a hot tawa with mustard oil, arrange the banana leaf parcels, cover, and cook on low heat for 6-7 minutes per side until the leaves are charred and aromatic.

notes: Charred banana leaves infuse the mustard-coated paneer with an unmistakable smoky aroma.

name: Paneer Posto (Bengali Cottage Cheese Cubes in Creamy Poppy Seed & Green Chilli Paste)

steps.section: Lightly pan-fry paneer cubes in mustard oil
steps.text: Heat mustard oil in a pan and lightly sear the paneer cubes with a pinch of salt for 2 minutes until pale golden; remove and keep aside.

steps.section: Simmer posto-kaju paste with kalo jeere and paneer
steps.text: Temper the remaining oil with kalo jeere and a dry red chilli, add the ground poppy-cashew-green chilli paste with ½ cup warm water, bring to a gentle simmer, fold in the paneer cubes for 3 minutes, and drizzle 1 tsp raw mustard oil on top.

notes: Rich, nutty, and quick to prepare for a comforting Bengali lunch with steamed rice.

name: Paneer Pulao / Peas Paneer Pulao (Fragrant Basmati Rice Cooked with Golden Paneer, Peas & Whole Spices)

steps.section: Fry paneer cubes, cashews and raisins in ghee
steps.text: Heat ghee in a heavy pot, fry cashews and raisins until plump and remove, then fry paneer cubes until golden and soak in warm salted water.

steps.section: Sauté soaked rice with whole spices and simmer on dum
steps.text: Temper the ghee with shahi jeera and whole garam masala, sauté ginger, green chillies, green peas, and drained rice for 2 minutes, add 2.75 cups hot water, salt, and 1 tsp sugar; when 80% cooked, fold in drained paneer, fried cashews, raisins, and saffron milk, and steam on low heat for 5 minutes.

notes: Fluffy, aromatic one-pot meal that pairs effortlessly with raita, dal makhani, or Aloo Dum.

name: Paneer Pyaz Paratha (Spiced Cottage Cheese & Onion Stuffed Paratha)

steps.section: Mix paneer and crunchy onion filling
steps.text: Toss grated paneer with chopped raw onion, chillies, ginger, coriander, ajwain, amchur, cumin, garam masala, and salt.
Enclose stuffing inside dough discs, seal the top, and roll into flat circles.
Cook on hot tawa with generous ghee or butter until crispy and golden brown. Serve hot with pickle and curd.

notes: A Punjabi breakfast favorite featuring creamy paneer complemented by the sweet crunch of fresh onions.

name: Paneer Rezala (Kolkata Nawabi White Yogurt, Cashew & Kewra Gravy with Paneer)

ingredients.name: Onion Paste (for Non-niramish) or Melon-seed Paste

steps.section: Temper whole spices and dry red chillies in ghee
steps.text: Heat ghee and white oil, lightly sear the paneer cubes and set aside; temper the fat with bay leaf, whole dry red chillies, green cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, mace, and peppercorns.

Cook boiled onion paste and ginger-garlic paste, stir in whisked yogurt and cashew-poppy paste with white pepper powder, sugar, and warm water; simmer with paneer for 4 minutes and finish with kewra water and ghee.

notes: Kolkata-style Rezala is famous for its ivory-white silky gravy scented with mace and kewra.

name: Paneer Roll (Kolkata Street-Style Spiced Paneer Tikka Kathi Roll)

steps.text: Marinate paneer cubes in hung curd, ginger-garlic paste, mustard oil, Kashmiri chilli, cumin, garam masala, kasuri methi, and salt. Sear on a hot tawa with capsicum and onion strips until smoky and charred at the edges.

steps.section: Crisp laccha paratha and assemble roll
steps.text: Shallow-fry flaky laccha parathas until crisp, pile the smoky paneer masala down the center, top with raw onion rings, cucumber, green chillies, chaat masala, bitnoon, lemon juice, and sauces, and roll tightly.

notes: Kolkata's favorite vegetarian kathi roll with smoky tawa-seared paneer tikka filling.

name: Paneer Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and slice vegetables or prepare the listed filling.
Spread butter or condiment on bread, add filling and season lightly. Serve fresh or grill until crisp.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

name: Paneer Steamed Momo (Spiced Crumbled Cottage Cheese, Cabbage & Ginger Dumplings)

steps.text: Squeeze moisture from grated cabbage and combine with hand-crumbled paneer, onion, ginger, garlic, green chilli, coriander, soy sauce, black pepper, 1 tsp oil, and salt.
Roll thin maida rounds, spoon paneer stuffing in the center, pleat tightly, and steam over boiling water for 12 minutes.

notes: Rich vegetarian protein-packed momo popular across Indian street stalls.

name: Paneer Stuffed Bread Pakora (Halwai-Style Spiced Cottage Cheese Slice Bread Fritters)

steps.text: Rub paneer slabs on both sides with chaat masala, Kashmiri chilli, cumin powder, and black salt. Sandwich each slab between two bread slices and cut diagonally into triangles.

steps.section: Coat in halwai batter and fry
steps.text: Dip each paneer bread triangle in smooth ajwain-spiced besan batter and fry in medium-hot oil until golden, puffed, and crisp.

notes: Rich Punjabi halwai-style snack; serve hot with tamarind-jaggery relish or ketchup.

name: Paneer Stuffed Hashbrowns (Crispy Grated Potato Patties with Spiced Paneer Center)

steps.section: Season paneer filling and potato shell
steps.text: Mix crumbled paneer with green chilli, coriander, chaat masala, and a pinch of salt. Mix dried grated potatoes with cornflour, salt, and pepper.
Sandwich 1 tbsp spiced paneer between two thin layers of grated potato, press edges to seal into a patty, and shallow-fry 6–7 minutes per side until crisp golden.

notes: Crispy laccha potato exterior with a soft spiced paneer core.

name: Paneer Tikka

steps.text: Wash, chop or mash ingredients and mix with seasoning.
Marinate paneer and vegetables in spiced yogurt, thread onto skewers and grill or pan-sear.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

name: Paneer Tikka Masala (Charred Marinated Paneer & Capsicum in Smoky Spiced Gravy)

steps.section: Marinate and char-grill paneer tikka on tawa or grill
steps.text: Marinate paneer, capsicum, and onion petals in hung curd, roasted besan, mustard oil, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, and tandoori spices for 15 minutes; sear on a smoking cast-iron tawa until charred at the edges.

steps.section: Simmer smoky onion-tomato masala and fold in tikka
steps.text: Sauté chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste in butter, add tomato-cashew puree and spices, simmer until thick, and fold in the charred paneer tikka, kasuri methi, and cream.

notes: Charring the yogurt-marinated paneer on high heat before adding it to the gravy imparts restaurant-style tandoori smokiness.

name: Paneer Tikka Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Pantua

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Papad Pakora / Batter-Fried Masala Papad Bhajiya (Spiced Besan-Rice Batter Coated Crispy Papad Fritters)

steps.text: Whisk besan, rice flour, ajwain, sesame seeds, hing, turmeric, red chilli, chopped coriander, a light pinch of salt, and water into a medium-thin coating batter.
Dip each raw papad triangle into the spiced batter and slide immediately into medium-hot oil; fry 1.5–2 minutes per side until puffed, golden, and super crispy.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle chaat masala, and serve hot with evening tea and green chutney.

notes: Quick monsoon tea-time telebhaja/pakora when you want something ultra-crunchy in 15 minutes.

name: Papad Paratha (Spiced Crushed Roasted Papad & Coriander Stuffed Crunchy Paratha)

ingredients.name: Urad Dal Papad (Plain or Black Pepper)

steps.text: Crush roasted papads into coarse bits. Mix with chopped onion, chillies, coriander, chaat masala, cumin, chilli powder, and 1 tsp ghee.
Enclose papad mixture inside dough balls and roll out carefully with light pressure.
Cook on tawa with ghee until crisp on both sides. Serve immediately with curd or pickle.

notes: A quick, crunchy Rajasthani-inspired paratha that turns simple roasted papad into an exciting meal.

name: Papad Pyaz ki Sabzi (Jodhpuri Dry Stir-Fry of Sliced Onions, Roasted Papad & Crushed Fennel-Coriander)

ingredients.name: Spiced Urad/moong Papads (Roasted Crisp & Broken into Bite-sized Shards)
Thickly Sliced Red Onions (or Spring Onions)

steps.section: Stir-fry sliced onions with crushed spices
steps.text: Heat oil in a wide pan, crackle cumin, crushed fennel, crushed coriander seeds, and hing, then saute sliced onions, ginger, and green chillies on medium-high flame for 4 minutes so the onions stay juicy-crisp.

steps.section: Season with dry spices and splash of water
steps.text: Add turmeric, Kashmiri red chilli, amchur, salt, and 2 tbsp water; cook 2 minutes so a glossy masala coats the onions.
Toss in the broken roasted papad pieces and chopped coriander, stir on low heat for 1 minute, and serve immediately with hot rotis.

notes: Quick 10-minute dry tiffin sabzi where sweet caramelized onions hug smoky roasted papad shards.

name: Papad Roll / Crispy Potato-Pea Stuffed Papad Cigar Rolls (Spiced Aloo Masala Wrapped in Papad & Fried Crisp)

steps.text: Mix boiled mashed potatoes with green peas, finely chopped onion, grated carrot, ginger, green chillies, coriander, roasted cumin, amchur, chaat masala, garam masala, and salt; shape into 6 cylindrical fingers.

Dip one papad at a time in water for 3 seconds, place on a damp cloth for 30 seconds until flexible, set a potato log near the bottom edge, fold in both sides, roll tightly like a spring roll, and seal the flap with maida/besan paste.
Fry the stuffed papad rolls in medium-hot oil for 2–3 minutes, turning gently until blistered and golden brown. Slice diagonally and serve hot with mint and tamarind chutneys.

notes: Produces a shatteringly crisp blistered shell around a soft, spiced potato center.

name: Papor Bharta / Paporer Chokha (Bengali Crushed Roasted Papad Mash with Mustard Oil, Onion & Roasted Dry Chilli)

ingredients.name: Urad or Moong Dal Papads (Dry-roasted Over Open Flame or Fried)
Whole Dried Red Chillies (Roasted Crisp in Mustard Oil)

steps.section: Roast papads and dry red chillies
steps.text: Roast papads directly over a stovetop flame with tongs (or fry in oil) until blistered and crisp. Fry whole dried red chillies in 1 tsp mustard oil until dark and crunchy.

steps.section: Crush chillies with onion and mustard oil
steps.text: In a bowl, crumble the roasted dry red chillies with a pinch of salt and black salt using your fingers, then rub in finely chopped onion, green chilli, coriander leaves, and raw pungent mustard oil.

steps.section: Fold in crushed papad and serve immediately
steps.text: Coarsely crush the roasted papads into bite-sized shards, toss into the spiced onion-mustard oil mixture, and serve immediately alongside hot steamed rice or khichuri.

notes: Ready in 5 minutes; always mix the crushed papad right before eating so it stays super crunchy.

name: Paporer Chorchori / Papor Aloo Bori Ghonto (Bengali Crushed Fried Papad, Potato & Bori Dry Masala Medley)

steps.section: Fry papad, bori, and diced vegetables
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, fry papads and bori until crisp and set aside. Temper panch phoron, dry red chilli, and bay leaf, then saute diced potatoes and brinjal until golden.
Add grated ginger, chopped tomato, green chillies, turmeric, cumin, chilli powder, and salt with 1/2 cup water; cover and cook until potatoes are soft and almost dry.

steps.section: Toss in crushed papad and bori
steps.text: Fold in coarsely crushed fried papad, crushed bori, a pinch of sugar, and chopped coriander; toss for 1 minute and serve hot with dal and steamed rice.

notes: Adding the crushed papad at the very end preserves a delightful contrast of crunchy and saucy textures.

name: Paporer Dalna / Aloo Paporer Jhol (Traditional Bengali Niramish Fried Papad & Potato Cumin-Ginger Curry)

steps.section: Fry papad quarters and golden potato wedges
steps.text: Heat mustard oil in a kadai, fry the quartered papads until crisp and set aside. In the same oil, fry potato wedges with a pinch of turmeric and salt until golden.

Temper bay leaf, dry red chilli, cumin seeds, and hing. Add grated ginger, tomato wedges, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric, and Kashmiri chilli with a splash of water; cook until oil separates, then add fried potatoes and 2 cups warm water and simmer 8 minutes until potatoes are tender.

steps.section: Fold in fried papads and finish with ghee
steps.text: Gently tuck the fried papad pieces into the simmering jhol, cook 1–2 minutes so they soften slightly while keeping their shape, and finish with 1 tsp desi ghee and gorom moshla.

notes: Beloved Bengali household rainy-day and niramish lunch curry when fresh green vegetables are scarce.

name: Paporer Dolma / Papader Dolma (Bengali Stuffed Papad Rolls with Spiced Potato, Chhena & Nut Filling in Rich Ginger-Cumin Gravy)

ingredients.name: Besan or Maida Paste (for Sealing) + Mustard Oil

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan, temper cumin and grated ginger, then saute mashed potatoes and crumbled chhena/paneer with turmeric, chilli powder, bhaja moshla, chopped cashews, raisins, a pinch of sugar, and salt. Cool completely.

steps.section: Soften papads, stuff into cigar rolls, and shallow-fry
steps.text: Briefly dip each papad in lukewarm water for 3–4 seconds and lay on a clean cloth for 1 minute until pliable. Place a log of potato-chhena stuffing near one edge, fold sides in, roll tightly into a neat cylinder (dolma), seal the edge with thick besan/maida paste, and shallow-fry in mustard oil until crisp and golden.

steps.section: Simmer niramish ginger-cumin-curd gravy and plate
steps.text: In the remaining oil, temper bay leaf, whole garam masala, cumin, and hing. Cook ginger paste, chopped tomato, cumin-coriander powder, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli, and whisked curd until oil separates, then add 1.25 cups warm water and simmer 5 minutes into a velvety gravy. Finish with ghee and Bengali gorom moshla, and pour hot gravy over the crispy paporer dolmas just before serving.

notes: Lost-recipe Thakurbarir and traditional Bengali niramish delicacy; pouring the hot gravy over the stuffed papad rolls right at serving time keeps them crisp-tender.

name: Paporer Tok / Papor Ambol (Bengali Sweet-and-Sour Tamarind, Jaggery & Panch-Phoron Papad Chutney)

ingredients.name: Papads (Fried or Roasted & Broken into Large Pieces)

steps.section: Temper panch phoron and simmer tamarind-jaggery broth
steps.text: Heat mustard oil in a pan, crackle dry red chilli and panch phoron (or mustard seeds), then pour in tamarind pulp, 1.25 cups water, turmeric, salt, and jaggery. Simmer 5–6 minutes until glossy and slightly syrupy.
Add the fried papad pieces to the bubbling sweet-and-sour tamarind broth, simmer 1 minute, and turn off heat.
Dust with roasted panch-phoron powder and black salt; serve as the palate-cleansing final course of a Bengali meal.

notes: Traditional rural Bengal summer lunch closer combining tangy tamarind, sweet jaggery, and soft-crisp papad.

name: Paratha (Homestyle)

steps.text: Mix flour and salt; add water gradually and knead to a soft dough. Rest covered.
Divide into portions and roll or shape according to the bread style.
Cook on a hot tawa or fry as appropriate, turning until cooked and golden.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

steps.text: Clean fish and season lightly with salt and turmeric.
Heat oil and lightly fry or sear fish; set aside.
Cook potato, tomato and spices, add water, then return fish and simmer gently until cooked through.

name: Pasta e Fagioli (Rustic Italian Ditalini Pasta & Borlotti Bean Stew)

steps.section: Saute soffritto and puree half beans
steps.text: Heat olive oil in a pot, cook onions, celery, carrots, and garlic until tender. Puree 1 cup of beans with 0.5 cup broth until smooth (to naturally thicken the stew), reserving remaining beans whole.
Add crushed tomatoes, bean puree, remaining whole beans, broth, rosemary, and bay leaf. Simmer on medium heat for 15 minutes until fragrant and comforting.
Add ditalini pasta directly into the pot, simmering for 8 minutes until tender. Discard rosemary sprig, ladle into wide bowls, and top with olive oil, black pepper, and grated cheese.

notes: Classic Italian country dish; pureeing half the beans creates a velvety body without needing heavy cream or flour.

name: Pasta Primavera (Vibrant Garden Vegetables & Herb Garlic Penne)

steps.text: Cook pasta in boiling salted water for 8 minutes; in the last 2 minutes, drop in broccoli florets. Drain and reserve 0.5 cup pasta water.
Heat olive oil in a wide skillet, saute bell peppers, zucchini, and garlic on medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Add halved cherry tomatoes for 1 minute.
Toss cooked pasta and broccoli into the skillet. Drizzle fresh lemon juice, zest, torn basil leaves, and Parmesan, tossing with pasta water until glossy and vibrant.

notes: Celebration of spring vegetables; keeping the vegetables crisp with bright lemon juice keeps the pasta light and refreshing.

name: Patishapta

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Patol Bharta (Pointed Gourd / Parwal Mash)

steps.text: Wash and scrape patol (pointed gourd). Either char whole over an open flame or boil halved patol until soft, removing any tough mature seeds.
Coarsely mash or grind the cooked patol with garlic and green chillies.

Heat mustard oil, temper with nigella seeds and dry red chilli, sauté chopped onion until translucent, and stir in the patol mash until moisture evaporates. Finish with coriander and a drop of raw mustard oil.

notes: Also known as Potol Bharta in West Bengal and Parwal Chokha in Bihar and eastern UP.

name: Patoli / Maharashtrian Patodi Rassa (Vidarbha-Style Spiced Besan Rolls in Saoji Coconut-Onion Gravy)

steps.section: Cook besan sheet and roll with coconut-coriander stuffing
steps.text: Cook spiced besan and water paste over low heat until thick and spreadable. Spread thinly onto a greased surface, sprinkle toasted grated coconut, sesame, poppy seeds, and fresh coriander, roll tightly like a Swiss roll, and slice into pinwheel patodis.

Grind roasted onions, dry coconut, ginger, garlic, and coriander into a smooth paste. Saute in hot oil with mustard, curry leaves, kala masala, and red chilli powder until oil floats on top, then add water and simmer.
Arrange the stuffed besan patodi slices in shallow bowls and ladle the piping hot Vidarbha rassa over them just before serving.

notes: Nagpur and Vidarbha classic; keeping a few crispy patodi slices aside as a starter while dunking the rest in rassa gives the best texture contrast.

name: Patshaker Bora (Crispy Jute Leaf Fritters)

ingredients.name: Besan (Gram Flour) or Soaked Masoor Dal Paste

steps.section: Bundle or chop tender jute leaves
steps.text: Either stack 3-4 whole jute leaves into neat folded packets or chop the leaves coarsely and mix with green chillies, kalo jeere, turmeric, and salt.

steps.section: Coat in crisp rice-flour batter and shallow-fry
steps.text: Dip leaf packets (or bind chopped leaves) in rice flour and besan batter and shallow-fry in hot mustard oil until crisp outside without turning mucilaginous.

notes: Using a higher ratio of rice flour keeps jute leaf fritters extra crunchy.

name: Patta Gobi Roll / Cabbage & Cauliflower Veg Kathi Roll (Bandhakopi-Phulkopi Street Roll)

steps.text: Heat oil in a kadhai, add minced ginger and green chilli, then toss in chopped cauliflower and carrot on high heat for 6 minutes. Add shredded cabbage, onion, salt, black pepper, and optional soy-vinegar; stir-fry 4 minutes so vegetables stay crisp-tender.
Dust with chaat masala, spoon onto crisp tawa parathas, and roll tightly.

notes: Combines both patta gobi (cabbage) and phulkopi (cauliflower) for crisp street-style crunch.

Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

Heat ghee or oil, add spices and vegetables if using, and stir until fragrant.
Add rice and measured water, cover and cook until tender. Rest briefly before serving.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Penne Arrabbiata (Spicy Garlic & Crushed Tomato Sauce Penne)

ingredients.name: Dried Red Chilli Flakes or Fresh Red Bird's Eye Chillies

steps.text: Boil penne in generous salted water for 9-10 minutes until al dente. Reserve 0.5 cup pasta water.

Warm olive oil in a skillet, add sliced garlic and chilli flakes, cooking gently until garlic is fragrant and translucent. Add crushed tomatoes, salt, and simmer over medium heat for 10-12 minutes until reduced and rich red.
Transfer drained penne directly into the simmering spicy sauce. Toss vigorously over medium heat for 1 minute with parsley and a splash of cooking water. Serve with grated Pecorino.

notes: 'Arrabbiata' translates to 'angry' in Italian, describing the assertive heat of chillies infused into rich sweet garlic tomato sauce.

name: Pepe Aloo Bori Dalna (Green Papaya, Potato & Fried Lentil Dumpling Homestyle Curry)

ingredients.name: Biulir Daler Bori or Motor Daler Bori

steps.section: Fry bori and sear papaya and potato cubes
steps.text: Fry the bori in mustard oil until golden-brown and set aside; temper oil with cumin, bay leaf, and dry red chilli, and fry papaya and potato cubes until lightly golden.

steps.section: Simmer spiced dalna and finish with bori, ghee and gorom moshla
steps.text: Add ginger paste, chopped tomato, turmeric, and cumin-coriander powder, pour in 1.5 cups warm water, cook covered until papaya is fork-tender, and finish with fried bori, sugar, ghee, and gorom moshla.

notes: Adding fried bori and ghee turns humble green papaya into a comforting Bengali dalna.

name: Pepe Bharta (Raw Papaya Mash)

steps.text: Peel green papaya, remove seeds and inner membrane, and cut into even cubes.
Boil or pressure-cook the papaya cubes with a pinch of salt until very soft, then drain excess water.
Mash the hot papaya with finely chopped green chillies, optional grated coconut, salt, and raw mustard oil or ghee.

notes: Gentle on the stomach and frequently included in convalescent and wholesome daily diets.

name: Pepe Fry / Kacha Pepe Bhaja (Bengali Grated Raw Papaya Stir-Fry)

steps.section: Temper and stir-fry julienned raw papaya
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle mustard seeds/kalo jeere and slit green chillies, add julienned raw papaya with turmeric and salt, and stir-fry over medium flame until tender and lightly golden.
Fold in fresh grated coconut and a tiny pinch of sugar, tossing for 2 minutes before serving.

notes: Light, wholesome, and easy-to-digest Bengali raw papaya fry.

name: Pepper & Mustard Tadka Sooji Sandwich (South Indian-Style Curry Leaf & Rava Tawa Sandwich)

steps.text: Crackle mustard seeds, urad dal, curry leaves, and green chilli in 1 tsp oil; pour over rested sooji-curd-vegetable batter along with crushed black pepper and baking soda.
Cook covered in an oiled pan or sandwich toaster on low heat 4 minutes per side until crisp and aromatic.

notes: Aromatic South Indian upma-style tempering inside a crisp tawa sandwich.

name: Peppermint Herbal Tea

steps.text: Heat fresh water. Steep tea leaves or prepare coffee using the method appropriate to the style; avoid over-steeping tea.
Add spices, lemon, milk or sweetener only as listed for the chosen drink. For black tea or black coffee, omit milk.
Strain into a cup or pour over ice for an iced version. Adjust strength and sweetness to taste.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Pesarattu

steps.text: Wash, chop and measure the ingredients. Soak or ferment the base if the recipe requires it.
Heat oil, add mustard or cumin seeds, onion, chilli and vegetables.
Add the main ingredient and the required water or batter; cook until tender and serve hot.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Pesto Genovese Pasta (Fresh Basil, Pine Nut, Garlic & Parmesan Fusilli)

steps.text: Pulse pine nuts and garlic in a mortar or food processor. Add fresh basil leaves and a pinch of coarse salt, pulsing in short bursts while slowly drizzling cold olive oil until smooth. Stir in grated cheeses by hand (never heat pesto).
Cook fusilli in heavily salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 0.5 cup pasta water and drain.
In a warm serving bowl, toss the drained hot pasta with fresh pesto and 2-3 tbsp pasta water until a creamy emerald green coating covers every spiral. Serve immediately.

notes: Never cook pesto over direct flame as heat turns delicate fresh basil dark and bitter; emulsify strictly using the heat of freshly boiled pasta.

name: Peyaj Aloo Bhaja (Bengali Onion & Potato Stir-Fry)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle nigella seeds and slit green chillies, and stir-fry potato matchsticks with turmeric for 5 minutes.
Add thinly sliced onions and salt; fry uncovered on medium flame until both potatoes and onions turn golden brown.

notes: Everyday Bengali comfort stir-fry for roti, paratha, or dal-rice.

name: Peyaj Diye Korola Fry (Caramelized Onion & Bitter Gourd Stir-Fry)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with kalo jeere, and fry turmeric-salted bitter gourd slices until lightly crisp.
Add sliced onions and slit green chillies and stir-fry together until the onions turn golden and sweet, balancing the bitterness of the korola.

notes: Sweet caramelized onions balance the bitter gourd beautifully.

name: Peyaj Kochuri (Kolkata Sweet-Shop Flaky Spiced Onion Kachori / Bengali Pyaaz Kochuri)

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp oil with crushed coriander, fennel, cumin, and hing. Sauté sliced onions until golden brown. Add ginger-chilli paste, mashed potato, amchur, garam masala, salt, and sugar; cook until completely dry.
Rub generous ghee into maida until it holds shape when pressed. Knead with cold water, divide into balls, fill with the spiced onion mixture, and flatten gently.
Fry on low-to-medium heat for 12-14 minutes until the shell turns exceptionally flaky, crisp, and golden. Serve with tamarind chutney.

notes: Kolkata sweet-shop take on the North Indian pyaaz kachori, featuring caramelized onions and whole crushed spices.

name: Peyaji Diye Muri Makha (Crispy Onion Fritter & Jhalmuri Tiffin)

steps.text: Mix sliced onions with besan, rice flour, green chillies, kalonji, salt, and minimal water; drop small clusters into hot oil and fry until crisp and brown.
Break hot crispy peyaji into bite-sized pieces and toss with puffed rice, raw mustard oil, chopped onion, chanachur, and black salt.

notes: Beloved Bengali street and home evening tiffin.

name: Peyajkoli Chingri Bhaja (Spring Onion Stalks Stir-Fried with Prawns)

steps.text: Season small prawns with salt and turmeric, fry lightly in hot mustard oil, and set aside.
Temper oil with nigella seeds and green chillies, stir-fry potato matchsticks for 3 minutes, then add onion stalks, turmeric, and salt.
Return the fried prawns to the pan and toss over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.

notes: A quintessential Bengali winter stir-fry served with hot steamed rice and dal.

name: Peyajkoli Diye Macher Dimer Bora (Spring Onion Stalk & Fish Egg Fritters)

steps.text: Mash cleaned fish eggs with finely chopped peyajkoli, onion, green chillies, coriander, turmeric, salt, besan, and rice flour.
Drop spoonfuls into hot mustard oil, flatten slightly, and fry on medium-low heat until golden and crisp.

notes: Sweet, crunchy winter onion stalks add great texture to fish egg boras.

name: Peyajkoli Diye Macher Dimer Jhuri Bhaja (Spring Onion Stalks & Scrambled Fish Egg Stir-Fry)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with nigella seeds, and fry seasoned fish roe while breaking it into golden granules; push to the side.
Add sliced onion, green chillies, and onion flower stalks with salt and turmeric; stir-fry on medium heat for 6-8 minutes until tender-crisp.

notes: Quick winter stir-fry pairing sweet onion stalks with savory scrambled fish roe.

name: Peyajkolir Bora / Spring Onion Stalk Fritters (Crispy Bengali Peyajkoli Pakora)

steps.section: Toss peyajkoli sticks in spiced rice-besan batter
steps.text: Combine cut peyajkoli stalks with besan, rice flour, poppy seeds, kalo jeere, green chillies, turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, and a splash of water so a thick batter clings to the stalks.

steps.section: Fry crisp bundles in hot mustard oil
steps.text: Drop small clusters of batter-coated peyajkoli into hot mustard oil and fry until the stalks are sweet-tender and the crust is golden and crunchy.

notes: Sweet winter peyajkoli (onion scapes) make one of the crunchiest Bengali fritters.

name: Philly-Style Mushroom Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

Cook on a hot tawa or fry as appropriate, turning until cooked and golden.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Phulkopi Aloo Chingri Jhol (Cauliflower, Potato & Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Lightly sear seasoned prawns and set aside. Fry cauliflower florets and potato wedges in mustard oil until golden at the edges.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, sauté ginger paste, chopped tomato, turmeric, and cumin powder until fragrant.
Add fried potatoes, cauliflower, and warm water; simmer until tender, then add prawns, slit green chillies, and fresh coriander leaves.

notes: Hearty Bengali winter lunch curry featuring fresh seasonal cauliflower and prawns.

steps.section: Roast in mustard oil until golden-charred

notes: Delicious with dal-rice, khichuri, or roti.

Temper oil with cumin and bay leaf, cook ginger, tomato, and dry spices, add warm water, potatoes, cauliflower, and green peas until tender, then fold in paneer, ghee, and gorom moshla.

notes: Combines winter cauliflower and soft paneer in a fragrant Bengali dalna.

steps.text: Blanch cauliflower florets in salted boiling water for 2 minutes, drain thoroughly, and toss with ginger-green chilli paste and roasted cumin powder.

steps.section: Dip in posto-besan batter and deep-fry
steps.text: Whisk besan, rice flour, kalo jeere, poppy seeds, turmeric, salt, baking soda, and water into a thick batter; coat florets and fry in medium-hot mustard oil until crisp and golden.

notes: A beloved winter evening snack across Kolkata, served piping hot with kasundi and black salt.

name: Phulkopir Kochuri (Bengali Spiced Cauliflower Stuffed Puri)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil with hing and kalo jeere. Add ginger paste, green chillies, and grated cauliflower. Sauté on medium flame with cumin, coriander, garam masala, salt, and a pinch of sugar until dry and tender.
Knead maida with ghee and water into a smooth dough. Shape into cups, fill generously with cooled cauliflower mixture, pinch shut, and roll carefully.
Fry in moderately hot oil until fully puffed and crisp. Serve hot with Bengali aloor dum.

notes: A coveted winter morning breakfast delicacy across Bengali households when fresh seasonal cauliflower arrives.

name: Pineapple Juice

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Pineapple Kesari

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Piro Aloo (Nepali Spicy Sesame & Timur Boiled Potato Salad)

ingredients.name: Red Chilli Paste or Kashmiri Chilli Powder

steps.text: Warm mustard oil in a pan, add garlic, ginger, red chilli paste, timur, and salt; sauté on low flame for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Tumble in boiled potatoes and ground roasted sesame powder; toss vigorously on medium-high heat until every piece is richly coated.
Remove from heat, squeeze fresh lemon juice, toss with cilantro, and serve warm or at room temperature.

notes: Fiery, numbing, and nutty street-style potato snack served with beaten rice or sel roti.

name: Pista Phirni Pudding (Chilled Kashmiri Ground Basmati Rice & Pistachio Pudding)

steps.text: Soak basmati rice for 30 minutes, drain completely on a clean kitchen towel, then pulse in a dry grinder until it resembles coarse semolina (suji) granules (do not make a fine powder).

Bring full-cream milk to a rolling boil in a heavy pot. Slowly rain in the ground rice while whisking continuously to prevent lumps. Simmer on low heat for 18-20 minutes, stirring frequently, until rice is completely cooked and the pudding thickens.

steps.section: Infuse pistachios and chill in earthen pots
steps.text: Add ground pistachios, sugar, saffron, and cardamom. Cook for another 4 minutes until thick and glossy. Stir in kewra water, ladle into traditional unglazed terracotta bowls (sakoras), and chill for 4 hours until firmly set.

notes: Royal North Indian chilled ground rice pudding; serving in earthen sakoras absorbs excess moisture, creating an intensely creamy, thick texture with delicate pistachio aroma.

name: Pitai Paratha (Kolkata Street-Style Petai Porota)

steps.text: Mix maida, salt, sugar, baking soda, and 1.5 tbsp oil. Knead with lukewarm milk and water into a very soft, stretchy dough; coat with oil and rest covered for 30 minutes.

steps.section: Pleat and coil for flaky layers
steps.text: Roll each dough ball thin, brush generously with oil/ghee, dust with dry flour, fold into accordion pleats, coil into a spiral peda, and roll out gently.
Cook on a hot heavy tawa with oil until golden blisters form on both sides, then immediately clap and crush between both palms on the counter so the flaky layers shatter open.

notes: Signature West Bengal street-style crushed flaky paratha traditionally served by weight with spicy ghugni or aloor torkari.

name: Piyaji

steps.text: Thinly slice onions. Mix with chopped chilli, salt, turmeric and besan; add only a little water if needed.
Drop small portions into medium-hot oil and fry, turning once, until crisp and deep golden.

name: Pizza Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.

name: Pizza-Style Sooji Bread Toast (Crispy Semolina Crust with Oregano, Capsicum & Cheese)

steps.text: Combine sooji, curd, ketchup, capsicum, onion, corn, grated cheese, oregano, chilli flakes, and salt; rest 8 minutes.
Spread on bread slices and toast topping-side down in butter on low heat 3–4 minutes until crisp and cheesy, then toast the bottom 2 minutes.

notes: Kid-favourite crunchy pizza toast made on a flat tawa with zero oven.

name: Plain Omelette

steps.text: Beat eggs with salt, pepper and optional milk or water; prepare the listed variation ingredients.
Heat butter or oil in a pan. Add vegetables first if needed, pour in eggs and cook gently; fold when set.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust seasoning and quantities to taste.

name: Poha

steps.text: Wash, chop and measure the ingredients. Soak or ferment the base if the recipe requires it.
Heat oil, add mustard or cumin seeds, onion, chilli and vegetables.
Add the main ingredient and the required water or batter; cook until tender and serve hot.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Poha & Jaggery Laddoo / Avalakki Laddoo (Roasted Flattened Rice, Coconut & Gur Laddoo)

ingredients.name: Thin or Thick Poha (Flattened Rice, Dry-roasted & Hand-crushed)

steps.text: Dry-roast poha on low heat for 5 minutes until crisp, cool briefly, and crush coarsely by hand or rolling pin. Toast cashews, raisins, and coconut in 1 tbsp ghee.
Melt jaggery with 2 tbsp water until syrupy, fold in crushed poha, coconut, nuts, remaining ghee, and cardamom, and roll into laddoos while warm.

notes: Krishna Janmashtami-style Avalakki laddoo made without any mixer.

name: Poha Paratha (Spiced Softened Flattened Rice, Potato & Herb Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Temper mustard seeds in 1 tsp oil, add onion and ginger-chilli paste. Mix with softened poha, mashed potato, turmeric, lemon juice, sugar, salt, and coriander.
Pack poha filling into wheat dough portions, seal edges, and roll into flat rounds.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee on both sides until golden brown. Serve with mint chutney.

notes: An innovative breakfast creation combining the flavors of Kanda Poha inside a stuffed paratha.

name: Pointed Gourd & Potato Fry (Aloo Potol Fry / Aloo Potol Bhaja)

steps.section: Fry potol wedges first, then potatoes
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, temper with kalo jeere and green chillies, add potol and potato wedges with turmeric and salt, and stir-fry uncovered until golden and crisp on the outside.

steps.section: Season with roasted cumin and chilli
steps.text: Sprinkle red chilli powder and roasted cumin powder and toss on high heat for 2 minutes.

notes: Classic homestyle Aloo Potol Fry that pairs with both dal-rice and roti.

name: Poori (Homestyle)

Divide into portions and roll or shape according to the bread style.
Cook on a hot tawa or fry as appropriate, turning until cooked and golden.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Posto Diye Chingri Mathar Bora (Poppy Seed & Prawn Head Fritters)

ingredients.name: White Poppy Seeds (Posto — Half Ground, Half Whole)

steps.text: Fold crushed prawn heads with poppy seed paste, whole poppy seeds, chopped onion, green chillies, turmeric, salt, and rice flour.
Flatten into small discs and pan-fry in hot mustard oil over medium-low heat until nutty, golden, and crisp.

notes: Crunchy poppy seeds and rich prawn head paste make an irresistible starter with dal-bhaat.

name: Posto Diye Macher Dimer Bora (Poppy Seed Fish Egg Fritters)

ingredients.name: White Poppy Seeds (Posto — Half Ground, Half Whole)

steps.text: Mix mashed fish eggs with poppy seed paste, chopped onion, green chillies, turmeric, salt, and flour.
Shape into small patties and press whole white poppy seeds onto the surface for a nutty crunch.
Fry on medium-low heat in mustard oil for 4-5 minutes per side until crisp and golden.

notes: Nutty roasted poppy seeds pair wonderfully with savory Bengali fish roe.

name: Posto Diye Macher Dimer Bora Curry (Fish Egg Fritters in Poppy Seed Gravy)

steps.text: Mix fish eggs with chopped onion, green chilli, besan, turmeric, and salt; fry boras in mustard oil. Fry optional potato wedges.
Temper oil with nigella seeds, fry sliced onion until soft, and stir in ground poppy seed paste with warm water.
Add the fried boras and slit green chillies, simmer gently for 5 minutes until coated in creamy posto, and drizzle with raw mustard oil.

notes: Rich, nutty poppy seed gravy with tender fish roe dumplings.

name: Posto Potol Fry (Poppy Seed Crusted Crispy Pointed Gourd Fry)

steps.section: Marinate and crust with poppy seeds
steps.text: Toss potol halves with turmeric, chilli powder, salt, rice flour, and white poppy seeds (posto) so the seeds coat every piece.

steps.section: Fry until poppy seeds crackle and turn golden
steps.text: Shallow-fry in hot mustard oil with slit green chillies until the potol is tender and the posto crust is nutty and crunchy.

notes: Nutty toasted poppy seeds give this Bengali potol fry a wonderful crunch.

name: Postor Bora (Authentic Bengali Crispy White Poppy Seed Fritters)

steps.section: Grind soaked poppy seeds into a coarse paste
steps.text: Grind soaked poppy seeds with 2 green chillies and minimal water on a shil-nora or mixer into a thick, slightly coarse paste; reserve 1 tbsp whole dry posto for crusting.

steps.section: Fold in aromatics and shallow-fry in mustard oil
steps.text: Mix the posto paste with chopped onion (or grated coconut for niramish), chopped green chillies, kalo jeere, rice flour, and salt; pat into small flat discs, coat with reserved whole posto, and shallow-fry in mustard oil until golden.

notes: One of the crown jewels of Rarh Bengal (Bankura-Birbhum-Burdwan) cuisine, eaten with hot steamed rice.

name: Postor Kochuri (Bengali Royal Poppy Seed / Khus-Khus Stuffed Puri)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil with kalo jeere, add ginger paste and thick poppy seed paste. Sauté continuously with salt and a hint of sugar on low heat until the water completely evaporates and the paste leaves the pan.
Knead maida with warm ghee and water. Roll into small cups, fill with the nutty posto paste, seal tightly, and roll gently.
Deep-fry in hot oil until inflated and delicately crisp. Serve with light potato curry or sweet tomato chutney.

notes: A royal Bankura and Rarh Bengal delicacy celebrated for the velvety texture and nutty flavor of posto.

name: Potato & Carrot Hashbrowns (Two-Root Crispy Skillet Pancakes)

steps.text: Squeeze grated potato and carrot together in a clean towel until dry, then toss with cornflour, spring onion, salt, and pepper.
Cook flat patties in heated oil/butter for 6–7 minutes per side until golden and tender.

notes: Vibrant orange-gold colour and mild natural sweetness from grated carrots.

ingredients.name: Egg (Lightly Beaten, or 2 Tbsp Cornflour for Eggless)

steps.text: Squeeze grated potato and grated onion together in a cloth until dry, then mix immediately with beaten egg, maida, salt, and pepper.
Drop spoonfuls into hot shimmering oil, flatten lightly with a spatula, and fry 5–6 minutes per side until lacy, crisp, and deep golden.

notes: Serve hot with curd or apple-cinnamon/tomato relish.

name: Potato Roll / Aloo Roll (Kolkata Street-Style Spiced Masala Aloo Kathi Roll)

steps.text: Heat oil on a tawa, sauté chopped onions and green chillies, add boiled potato cubes, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli, bhaja masala, chaat masala, and crushed roasted peanuts, mashing lightly until crusty and aromatic.

Fry flaky laccha parathas until golden, spoon the hot spiced potato filling along the center, top with crunchy onion rings, cucumber, coriander, lemon juice, bitnoon, and tangy sauces, and wrap tightly.

notes: Classic, budget-friendly Kolkata street-side Aloo Roll seasoned with aromatic bhaja masala and crunchy peanuts.

name: Potato Sandwich

ingredients.quantity: boiled potato slices with chaat masala

Add the vegetables and a little water; cover and cook until tender. Adjust seasoning.

name: Potol Bharta (Pointed Gourd Mash)

steps.text: Lightly scrape the skin of the potol, trim the ends, and halve lengthwise.
Steam or boil the potol until tender, drain, and mash. Temper mustard oil with kalo jeere, garlic, onion, and green chilli, then stir in the mashed potol and cook until thick and fragrant.
Adjust salt, drizzle a few drops of raw mustard oil, and serve hot with steamed rice.

notes: Adding a few small fried prawns (chingri) or roasted garlic is a popular Bengali variation.

name: Potol Chingri (Pointed Gourd & Potato Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Lightly sear seasoned prawns and remove. Fry scraped pointed gourd halves and potato wedges in mustard oil until golden brown.
Temper oil with bay leaf and cumin seeds, fry chopped onion until golden, and cook ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and spices until oil separates.
Add fried potatoes, potol, and warm water; cook until tender, then stir in the prawns, simmer 4 minutes, and finish with ghee and garam masala.

notes: One of the most popular Bengali everyday and festive prawn-vegetable combinations.

name: Potol Fry (Bengali Crispy Pan-Fried Pointed Gourd / Parwal Fry)

steps.section: Peel in alternating stripes and score
steps.text: Wash the potol, trim both ends, peel the skin in alternating lengthwise stripes so the gourd holds its shape, and halve lengthwise (or score diagonal slits on whole potol).
Toss the halved potol with turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt, and rest for 5 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a flat kadai or tawa until smoking, place potol cut-side down first over medium heat, then flip and fry both sides until blistered, golden brown, and tender inside.

notes: An everyday Bengali lunch staple served alongside hot steamed rice, dal, and a wedge of Gondhoraj lebu.

name: Potol Khosa Bharta (Pointed Gourd Peel Mash)

steps.text: Wash pointed gourd peels thoroughly and boil in salted water for 5–7 minutes until soft, then drain well.
Grind the boiled peels with garlic cloves and green chillies to a smooth paste using minimal water.
Heat mustard oil, crackle kalo jeere, add the ground peel paste, salt, and a pinch of sugar, and stir-fry until dry and glossy.

notes: A classic Bengali zero-waste delicacy (Potol Khosa Bata / Bharta) served with hot steamed rice.
