steps.text: Scrape the pointed gourds in alternating stripes, halve lengthwise, and make thin vertical fan cuts leaving one end intact (or slice into thin lengthwise slabs); rub with a pinch of salt and turmeric.
Whisk besan, rice flour, kalo jeere, white poppy seeds, turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, and cold water into a smooth, medium-thick coating batter.

steps.section: Dip and fry until golden and crisp
steps.text: Dip each potol piece in the batter and fry in medium-hot mustard oil for 3-4 minutes per side until puffed, golden brown, and shatteringly crisp.

notes: Fan-cutting the potol (Potol Pata Bora style) creates lacy crispy edges that pair wonderfully with dal-bhat or evening cha.

name: Potoler Dorma with Chingri Stuffing (Prawn-Stuffed Pointed Gourd)

steps.text: Scrape potol skins and scoop out the seeds gently. Sauté minced prawns, scooped potol pulp, onion, ginger, grated coconut, and garam masala until dry; stuff inside each hollowed potol.
Shallow-fry the stuffed potols gently in mustard oil until golden on all sides.
Cook onion paste, tomato puree, cashew-posto paste, whisked yogurt, and spices into a velvety gravy, then nestle the stuffed potols inside and simmer gently for 7 minutes.

notes: An aristocratic Bengali culinary classic served on special occasions.

name: Pranhara Sandesh (Soft Chhena Sandesh Coated in Powdered Khoya)

steps.text: Lightly warm 60 g of grated khoya in a dry pan for 2 minutes, let cool, and rub through a fine sieve to create a snowy khoya crumb coating.
Knead chhena, remaining 40 g khoya, and powdered sugar until smooth, then cook on low heat for 7–8 minutes with cardamom and rose water.

steps.section: Roll balls and coat generously in khoya crumbs
steps.text: Roll warm mixture into bite-sized balls or discs and roll immediately in the sieved khoya crumbs until evenly coated.

notes: Melt-in-the-mouth Bengali sandesh whose name means 'stealer of hearts'.

name: Prawn 65 (South Indian Spicy Deep-Fried Prawns)

steps.text: Mix prawns with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, red chilli powder, spices, rice flour, cornflour, and salt; rest for 15 minutes.
Fry marinated prawns in hot oil for 3 minutes until crisp and vibrant red; drain on paper towels.
In 1 tsp hot oil, crackle mustard seeds, chopped garlic, slit green chillies, and curry leaves, then toss the crispy prawns in the tempering.

notes: Crispy, fiery South Indian restaurant-style prawn starter.

name: Prawn Balchao (Goan Tangy Pickled Prawn Masala)

steps.text: Grind dry red chillies, cumin, peppercorns, cloves, cinnamon, garlic, and ginger with vinegar (no water) into a smooth fiery paste.
Quickly sear salted prawns in oil and set aside. In the same oil, fry chopped onions until deep brown and add chopped tomato.
Add the ground balchao paste, fry until oil separates, then toss in the prawns, salt, and a pinch of sugar; simmer for 5 minutes.

notes: Tangy, spicy Goan preparation inspired by Portuguese-Goan pickling traditions.

name: Prawn Bhuna (Thick Spiced Prawn Bhuna)

steps.text: Heat oil, temper with cumin seeds, and sauté finely chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste until rich golden brown.
Add chopped tomatoes and spice powders, roasting on medium-high heat until thick and oil separates from the sides.
Toss in the cleaned prawns and stir-fry for 5 minutes until cooked through and coated in the clinging bhuna masala. Garnish with coriander.

notes: Rich, semi-dry prawn bhuna ideal with parathas, rotis, or jeera rice.

name: Prawn Biryani (Fragrant Dum Prawn Biryani)

steps.section: Parboil basmati rice and fry birista
steps.text: Fry sliced onions in ghee and oil until crisp golden (birista). Boil soaked basmati rice with whole spices and salt until 75% cooked, then drain.
Sauté ginger-garlic paste, tomato, yogurt, biryani masala, half the birista, and herbs; add prawns and cook for just 3 minutes.
Layer the partially cooked basmati rice over the prawn masala, top with remaining birista, mint, saffron milk, and ghee, and seal on low dum heat for 10 minutes.

notes: Cooking the prawns only briefly before the final dum keeps them plump and tender.

name: Prawn Butter Masala (Creamy Tomato Butter Prawns)

steps.text: Season prawns with salt, turmeric, and Kashmiri chilli; sear in 1 tbsp butter for 2 minutes and set aside.
Melt remaining butter, sauté ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, Kashmiri chilli powder, and cashew paste until rich and glossy.
Add warm water, salt, a pinch of sugar, and the seared prawns. Simmer 4 minutes, then stir in fresh cream and crushed kasuri methi.

notes: Velvety, mildly spiced restaurant-style butter masala that pairs great with butter naan or pulao.

name: Prawn Caldine (Goan Mild Yellow Coconut Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Thin Coconut Milk (or 1 Cup Grated Coconut)

steps.text: Grind coriander seeds, cumin, turmeric, peppercorns, and garlic with thin coconut milk into a smooth golden paste.
Sauté sliced onion and chopped tomato in oil until soft, then add the ground yellow paste and simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.section: Add prawns and thick coconut milk
steps.text: Add cleaned prawns, slit green chillies, tamarind, and thick coconut milk; simmer gently for 6 minutes until cooked through.

notes: A gentle, aromatic Goan curry without red chillies, getting its gentle warmth from green chillies and black pepper.

name: Prawn Chowmin / Chingri Chowmein (Kolkata Style Stir-Fried Prawn & Garlic Noodles)

steps.text: Toss prawns with a pinch of salt, black pepper, and cornflour, then sear in hot oil for 2–3 minutes until pink and crisp-tender; set aside.
Sauté garlic, ginger, and green chillies in the same wok, then stir-fry carrots, beans, cabbage, and capsicum on high flame for 3 minutes.
Add boiled noodles, seared prawns, soy sauce, chilli-garlic sauce, vinegar, and black pepper; toss over high flame for 2–3 minutes and top with spring onion greens.

notes: Juicy golden prawns tossed with garlic-scented chowmin and crisp vegetables.

name: Prawn Curry (Homestyle Indian Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Toss cleaned prawns with salt and turmeric; lightly sear in oil for 1-2 minutes and set aside.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and bay leaf, brown the chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste, and cook tomatoes with spice powders until oil separates.
Add warm water to reach desired gravy consistency, return the prawns, simmer for 5 minutes, and garnish with garam masala and fresh coriander.

notes: Classic everyday Indian prawn curry suitable for both lunch and dinner.

name: Prawn Cutlet (Kolkata Cabin-Style Chingri Cutlet)

steps.text: Slit large prawns down the back and gently flatten them into cutlets while keeping the tail intact. Marinate with ginger-garlic-green chilli paste, lemon juice, black pepper, and salt for 15 minutes.
Dust each butterflied prawn in flour, dip into beaten egg, and press firmly into breadcrumbs twice for a crisp crust.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Sprinkle with black salt and serve with kasundi and salad.

notes: Signature heritage Kolkata cabin-style prawn cutlet.

name: Prawn Do Pyaza (Prawns with Double Onions)

steps.text: Quickly toss onion petals and slit green chillies in hot oil for 2 minutes until glossy and crisp-tender; set aside with lightly seared prawns.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and whole dry red chilli, fry finely chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste, then cook chopped tomatoes and spice powders.
Add prawns, sautéed onion petals, and a splash of water; simmer for 5 minutes and finish with garam masala and coriander leaves.

notes: Uses onions in two stages for both a rich gravy base and sweet, crunchy onion petals.

name: Prawn Fried Rice (Indo-Chinese Wok-Tossed Shrimp Fried Rice)

ingredients.name: Prawns (Small or Medium, Peeled and Deveined)

steps.text: Heat oil in a wok, stir-fry seasoned prawns for 2 minutes until pink, push aside or remove, and scramble the beaten eggs.
On high flame, stir-fry minced garlic, spring onion whites, finely diced carrots, beans, and capsicum for 2-3 minutes so they stay crisp.
Add cold cooked rice, prawns, scrambled egg, soy sauce, vinegar, white pepper, and salt; toss on high heat and finish with spring onion greens.

notes: Day-old or thoroughly chilled rice gives the best non-sticky restaurant wok texture.

name: Prawn Fry (Chingri Macher Bhaja / Masala Prawn Fry)

steps.text: Rub cleaned prawns with turmeric, red chilli powder, ginger-garlic paste, cumin, black pepper, lemon juice, and salt; rest for 10 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a skillet until smoking lightly, arrange prawns in a single layer, and fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crisp on the outside.

notes: Simple, flavorful pan-fried prawns that pair perfectly with dal and steamed rice.

name: Prawn Ghee Roast (Mangalorean Kundapur Prawn Ghee Roast)

steps.text: Marinate prawns with yogurt, turmeric, lemon juice, and salt. Dry-roast Byadgi chillies, coriander, cumin, fenugreek, and pepper; grind smooth with garlic and tamarind.
Heat 1.5 tbsp ghee, sear marinated prawns on high heat for 2 minutes, and remove.
In the remaining ghee, slow-roast the ground chilli-garlic paste until dark red and ghee separates, then fold in the prawns, a pinch of jaggery, and crisp curry leaves.

notes: Iconic Kundapur Mangalorean delicacy famous for its rich ghee aroma and fiery-tangy glaze.

name: Prawn Hakka Noodles (Stir-Fried Shrimp Chowmein)

steps.text: Boil Hakka noodles until al dente, rinse in cold water, and toss with 1 tsp oil. Stir-fry seasoned prawns in hot oil for 2 minutes and set aside.
Heat oil in a wok, sauté garlic, ginger, and sliced onion, then toss julienned cabbage, carrot, and bell pepper on high heat for 2 minutes.
Add boiled noodles, seared prawns, soy sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar, black pepper, and spring onion greens; toss well.

notes: Street-style Kolkata prawn chowmein great as an evening meal or dinner.

name: Prawn Head Fritters (Chingri Macher Mathar Bora)

ingredients.name: Prawn Heads (Golda or Bagda Chingri Matha, Trimmed and Cleaned with Head Roe/ghilu Intact)

steps.text: Remove the hard outer carapace shell, eyes, and sharp rostrum spine from the prawn heads while keeping the soft inner head meat and orange roe/fat (ghilu). Coarsely grind or pound in a mortar/mixer.
Combine the crushed prawn heads with finely chopped onion, crushed garlic-ginger, green chillies, coriander leaves, nigella seeds, turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, besan, and rice flour.
Shape into flat round patties and fry in hot mustard oil over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until deep golden and crunchy. Serve hot with steamed rice and masoor dal.

notes: Adding rice flour alongside besan makes Chingri Macher Mathar Bora extra crispy.

name: Prawn Head Garlic Butter Roast (Ghilu-Infused Garlic Prawn Heads)

ingredients.name: Jumbo Prawn Heads (Cleaned with Orange Roe/ghilu Intact)

steps.text: Heat olive oil and half the butter in a skillet and gently sauté minced garlic and chilli flakes until fragrant.

steps.section: Roast prawn heads and release ghilu
steps.text: Add seasoned jumbo prawn heads, sear for 3-4 minutes per side while pressing gently so the creamy orange head fat emulsifies with the garlic butter.
Swirl in remaining butter, lemon juice, black pepper, and fresh herbs; serve hot with toasted bread or steamed rice.

notes: The rich head roe (ghilu) melts into the garlic butter to create a decadent pan sauce.

name: Prawn Head Pakora (Crispy Chingri Mathar Pakora)

ingredients.name: Prawn Heads (Trimmed of Sharp Spines and Outer Shell)

steps.text: Toss trimmed, cleaned prawn heads with lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, red chilli powder, and salt; rest for 10 minutes.
Mix besan, cornflour/rice flour, sliced onion, green chillies, coriander, ajwain, and a splash of water into a thick coating batter and fold in the prawn heads.
Drop small clusters into medium-hot oil and fry for 4-5 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Sprinkle with chaat masala and serve with kasundi.

notes: Crunchy evening snack or starter that turns leftover prawn heads into a gourmet treat.

name: Prawn in Yogurt Curry (Doi Chingri)

steps.text: Rub prawns with a pinch of salt and turmeric, sear lightly in hot oil for 1 minute per side, and set aside.
Temper oil with cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaf. Cook onion paste and ginger-garlic paste on low heat until raw aroma disappears.
Lower the flame, stir in whisked yogurt mixed with a pinch of flour or cashew paste to prevent curdling, add warm water, prawns, and slit green chillies, and simmer gently for 6-8 minutes.

notes: Always beat the yogurt until velvety and add it over low heat so the gravy stays silky.

name: Prawn Jalfrezi (Stir-Fried Prawns with Peppers & Tomatoes)

steps.text: Sear seasoned prawns for 2 minutes and remove. Stir-fry onion strips and bell peppers on high heat for 2 minutes so they stay crunchy.
Sauté garlic paste, ginger juliennes, tomato puree, and spice powders with a splash of vinegar or ketchup until thick.
Return prawns, crisp peppers, onions, and fresh tomato wedges to the pan; toss for 3 minutes and garnish with coriander.

notes: Colorful, semi-dry Anglo-Indian prawn stir-fry.

name: Prawn Koliwada (Mumbai Style Crispy Fried Prawns)

steps.text: Rub prawns with lemon juice, ginger-garlic-chilli paste, turmeric, and salt; rest for 10 minutes.
Mix besan, cornflour, yogurt, carom seeds, Kashmiri red chilli powder, and cumin powder into a thick paste and coat the prawns.

steps.section: Deep-fry and dust with chaat masala
steps.text: Deep-fry in hot oil for 3 minutes until crunchy. Sprinkle generously with chaat masala and serve with mint-coriander chutney.

notes: Carom seeds (ajwain) and chaat masala give Prawn Koliwada its unmistakable Mumbai seafood punch.

name: Prawn Korma (Creamy Cashew & Yogurt Prawn Korma)

ingredients.name: Onions (Fried Golden and Ground with Yogurt)

steps.section: Sear prawns and prepare korma paste
steps.text: Lightly sear prawns in ghee for 1-2 minutes. Blend fried golden onions with yogurt and soaked cashews into a silky paste.
Temper ghee with cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, and bay leaf; sauté ginger-garlic paste and coriander powder until fragrant.
Stir in the onion-yogurt-cashew paste and warm water, simmer for 5 minutes, then add prawns and cook gently for 5 minutes.

notes: Mild, luxurious prawn curry ideal for guests and festive dinners.

name: Prawn Manchow Soup (Spicy Indo-Chinese Shrimp Soup)

steps.text: Heat oil in a pot, sauté minced garlic, ginger, green chillies, and coriander stems on high heat, then toss in chopped prawns and vegetables for 2 minutes.
Pour in 3 cups water or stock, soy sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar, black pepper, and salt; bring to a rolling boil.

steps.section: Thicken and top with crispy noodles
steps.text: Stir in the cornflour slurry until glossy and lightly thickened. Garnish with spring onions and crunchy fried noodles.

notes: Hearty, warming Indo-Chinese soup.

name: Prawn Masala (Spicy Onion-Tomato Prawn Masala)

steps.text: Marinate cleaned prawns with turmeric, half the chilli powder, lemon juice, and salt for 10 minutes.
Heat oil, fry chopped onions until golden brown, add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, and remaining spice powders, and cook until oil separates.
Add marinated prawns and slit green chillies, cook covered for 5-6 minutes until prawns are tender, and finish with garam masala and fresh coriander.

notes: Versatile Indian prawn masala that goes equally well with steamed rice, roti, or parotta.

name: Prawn Mayo Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Prawn Omelette (Masala Chingri Dim Omelette)

steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in a skillet and sauté chopped prawns with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 2-3 minutes until cooked through.
Beat the eggs aggressively with chopped onion, green chillies, coriander leaves, black pepper, salt, and the cooked prawns.
Pour into the hot oiled skillet, cook on medium-low heat until set underneath, flip gently, and cook until golden on both sides.

notes: High-protein breakfast or quick dinner side dish.

name: Prawn Pakora (Crispy Chingri Pakora)

steps.text: Pat dry the cleaned prawns and toss with lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, red chilli powder, and salt. Rest for 10 minutes.
Whisk besan, rice flour, carom seeds, chopped green chillies, fresh coriander, salt, and cold water into a thick, smooth coating batter.
Dip each marinated prawn into the batter and fry in medium-hot oil for 3-4 minutes until golden and crisp. Serve hot with kasundi or mint chutney.

notes: Adding rice flour keeps the pakora crust crisp; do not overcook prawns so they stay juicy inside.

name: Prawn Pepper Fry (South Indian Milagu Eral Varuval)

steps.text: Toast whole black peppercorns, fennel seeds, and cumin seeds briefly, then crush coarsely in a mortar and pestle.
Heat coconut oil, crackle curry leaves, and fry crushed ginger-garlic and sliced shallots until golden.
Add cleaned prawns, turmeric, and salt; cook for 5 minutes until moisture dries up, then coat with the crushed pepper-fennel masala and lemon juice.

notes: Bold, aromatic black pepper prawn dry fry great as a starter or side with sambar/rasam rice.

name: Prawn Potato Curry (Aloo Chingri Jhol)

steps.text: Season prawns with salt and turmeric; lightly fry in mustard oil for 1-2 minutes and remove. In the same oil, fry potato wedges until golden.
Temper oil with cumin seeds and bay leaf. Sauté sliced onions until golden, then add ginger-garlic paste, chopped tomato, and spice powders with a splash of water.
Add fried potatoes and warm water; cover and cook until potatoes are tender. Stir in the prawns, simmer for 4 minutes, and finish with garam masala.

notes: Classic everyday Bengali and eastern Indian prawn potato curry served with steamed rice.

name: Prawn Pulao (Spiced Basmati Prawn Pilaf)

steps.text: Heat ghee and oil, temper with bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and shahi jeera. Fry sliced onions until golden, then sauté ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and spices.
Stir in cleaned prawns, mint, and coriander leaves; sauté for 2 minutes, then gently fold in the drained basmati rice.
Pour in 2.75 cups warm water or stock, season with salt, cover tightly, and cook on low heat for 10-12 minutes until grains are fluffy.

notes: One-pot fragrant prawn rice meal.

name: Prawn Rezala (Bengali Mughlai White Yogurt & Cashew Gravy)

steps.text: Toss prawns with salt and white pepper, sear lightly in ghee for 1 minute without browning, and set aside.
Temper ghee with bay leaf, green cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and whole dry red chillies. Cook boiled onion paste and ginger-garlic paste on low heat.

steps.section: Simmer with yogurt and cashew paste
steps.text: Add whisked yogurt and cashew-poppy seed paste, pour in warm water, add prawns, white pepper, salt, sugar, and a drop of kewra water; simmer gently for 6 minutes.

notes: Silky, ivory-white Kolkata Mughlai gravy that pairs wonderfully with roomali roti, parotta, or pulao.

name: Prawn Roll / Chingri Roll (Kolkata Street-Style Masala Prawn Kathi Roll)

steps.text: Marinate cleaned prawns with turmeric, Kashmiri chilli, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and salt. Sear in hot mustard oil with sliced onions, capsicum, roasted cumin, and Bengali garam masala for 4-5 minutes until juicy and coated in thick masala.

Shallow-fry flaky laccha parathas until crisp, arrange the spicy tawa prawns down the center, top with cucumber juliennes, onion rings, chaat masala, bitnoon, lemon juice, and a drizzle of pungent kasundi or chilli sauce, and wrap tightly.

notes: Signature Kolkata coastal-street kathi roll loaded with succulent mustard-and-garam-masala tossed prawns.

name: Prawn Salad (Fresh Citrus, Cucumber & Herb Prawn Salad)

steps.text: Sear seasoned prawns in 1 tsp olive oil with garlic and black pepper for 2 minutes per side until pink, then cool slightly.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, honey, chilli flakes, salt, and chopped herbs into a bright vinaigrette.
Toss crisp greens, cucumber, tomatoes, onion, and warm or chilled prawns with the dressing just before serving.

notes: Light, refreshing, protein-packed meal.

name: Prawn Skewers (Tawa Grilled Spiced Prawn Skewers)

steps.text: Toss prawns, cubed bell peppers, and onion petals with ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, spice powders, oil, and salt; rest for 15 minutes.
Alternate marinated prawns, bell peppers, and onions on wooden or metal skewers.
Cook on a hot cast-iron tawa or grill pan with a brush of butter for 3-4 minutes per side until lightly charred; sprinkle with chaat masala.

notes: Party starter that cooks quickly on any flat tawa or grill pan.

name: Prawn Tempura (Light Crispy Batter-Fried Shrimp)

ingredients.name: Egg (Lightly Beaten) or 1/2 Tsp Baking Soda
Ice-cold Sparkling Water or Ice Water

steps.text: Make 3 small shallow cuts across the underside of each prawn so it stays straight while frying, pat completely dry, and dust lightly with flour.
Briefly stir ice-cold water, beaten egg, flour, and cornstarch together with chopsticks, leaving a few small lumps so the batter stays airy.
Dip prawns into the cold batter and fry in 180°C oil for 2-3 minutes until pale golden and shatteringly crisp.

notes: Keeping the batter ice-cold and minimally mixed guarantees a light, lacy tempura crust.

name: Prawn Tikka Masala (Chargrilled Prawns in Spiced Tomato Gravy)

steps.text: Coat prawns in thick yogurt, roasted besan, ginger-garlic, tandoori masala, and lemon juice; pan-grill on high heat until lightly charred.
Sauté chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste in butter and oil until golden, then cook tomato puree and spices until thick and glossy.

steps.section: Simmer with cream and kasuri methi
steps.text: Add warm water, chargrilled prawns, fresh cream, and crushed kasuri methi; simmer together for 3 minutes.

notes: Combines smoky tandoori prawns with a rich North Indian tomato-cream gravy.

name: Prawn Vindaloo (Goan Garlic & Vinegar Spicy Prawn Curry)

ingredients.name: Toddy Vinegar or Apple Cider Vinegar

steps.text: Soak dry red chillies and spices in vinegar, then grind with garlic and ginger into a smooth, vibrant red vindaloo paste.
Heat oil, fry chopped onions until golden, add the vindaloo paste, and roast until oil separates. Add parboiled potato cubes and warm water.
Add cleaned prawns, salt, and a pinch of jaggery; simmer for 5-6 minutes until prawns are tender.

notes: Authentic Goan vindaloo relies on garlic, warm whole spices, and vinegar without dairy.

name: Prawn Xacuti (Goan Roasted Spice, Poppy Seed & Coconut Prawn Curry)

steps.text: Dry-roast whole spices, red chillies, poppy seeds, sliced onion, and grated coconut until golden brown; grind with garlic, turmeric, and tamarind into a smooth, fragrant paste.
Heat coconut oil, sauté finely chopped onion until soft, add the ground Xacuti masala paste and water, and simmer for 6 minutes.
Add cleaned prawns and salt, simmer gently for 5-6 minutes until cooked through, and garnish with fresh coriander.

notes: Complex, deeply aromatic Goan curry featuring toasted coconut, poppy seeds, and warm spices.

name: Pudina Lachha Paratha (Mint Layered Flaky Paratha)

steps.section: Roll and layer with mint & ghee
steps.text: Roll kneaded wheat dough into a thin circle, brush with ghee, and sprinkle crushed mint leaves, chaat masala, and cumin powder.
Fold into accordion pleats, coil tightly, press flat, and roll into a medium circle.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until crisp and aromatic.

notes: Refreshing mint-scented multi-layered paratha.

name: Pudina Masala Rice / Mint Coriander Pulao (Fresh Mint-Coriander-Green Chilli Paste, Cashew & Ghee Spiced Rice)

steps.text: Grind or finely mince mint leaves, coriander leaves, green chillies, ginger, and garlic with 2 tbsp water and a squeeze of lemon juice to preserve bright green color.

steps.section: Saute spices, onion, and herb paste
steps.text: Heat ghee, fry cashews, temper whole spices, saute sliced onion and green peas, then stir in the fresh mint-coriander paste for 2–3 minutes.
Fold in drained rice, add 2.75 cups hot water and salt, cover and simmer 12 minutes until fluffy and emerald-tinted.

notes: Refreshing, cooling herbaceous masala rice ideal for lunchboxes and paired with boondi raita.

name: Pui Patar Bora (Crispy Malabar Spinach Leaf Fritters)

ingredients.name: Large Tender Malabar Spinach Leaves (Pui Pata)
Besan (Gram Flour) or Soaked Red Lentil (Masoor Dal) Paste

steps.section: Fold pui leaves and whisk batter
steps.text: Whisk besan (or ground masoor dal), rice flour, poppy seeds, kalo jeere, green chilli-ginger paste, turmeric, and salt into a thick batter; coat and fold each fleshy pui leaf in half.

steps.section: Shallow-fry in mustard oil until blistered and crisp
steps.text: Fry the coated Malabar spinach leaves in medium-hot mustard oil for 3 minutes per side until the outer crust is golden and crisp and the fleshy leaf inside is tender.

notes: The succulent texture of pui pata inside a crisp rice-posto crust is a classic rural Bengal favorite.

name: Pui Shak Diye Macher Dimer Chorchori (Malabar Spinach, Pumpkin & Fish Egg Medley)

steps.text: Pan-fry turmeric-salted fish roe in mustard oil until firm, break into bite-sized pieces, and set aside.
Temper oil with panch phoron, dry red chilli, crushed garlic, and sliced onion. Add potato, pumpkin, pui shak stems and leaves, turmeric, cumin powder, and salt; cover and cook until tender.
Stir in the fried fish roe pieces, slit green chillies, and a pinch of sugar; cook uncovered for 5 minutes until thick and cohesive.

notes: Rustic Bengali monsoon favorite combining leafy greens and sweet pumpkin with fish eggs.

name: Pui Shak Kumro Chingri Chorchori (Malabar Spinach & Pumpkin with Prawns)

steps.text: Lightly fry seasoned prawns in mustard oil and remove. Fry potato, pumpkin, and brinjal cubes for 3 minutes.
Temper oil with panch phoron, dry red chilli, and bay leaf. Add pui shak stems and leaves, vegetables, ginger paste, turmeric, and salt; cover and cook until tender.
Stir in the fried prawns, mustard paste, slit green chillies, and a pinch of sugar; cook uncovered for 5 minutes until cohesive.

notes: Classic Bengali monsoon and summer chorchori.

name: Puli Pithe

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Pumpkin & Potato Fry (Aloo Kumro Fry / Aloo Kumro Bhaja)

steps.section: Temper with panch phoron and fry potatoes & pumpkin
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle panch phoron and dry red chillies, fry potato cubes for 3 minutes, then add pumpkin cubes, turmeric, and salt and pan-fry until golden and tender.
Toss with a pinch of sugar and fresh coriander leaves; serve hot with luchi, paratha, or rice.

notes: Fragrant panch-phoron tempered Aloo Kumro Fry.

name: Punjabi Kabuli Chana Pulao (Spiced Chickpea, Whole Garam Masala, Ginger Juliennes & Caramelized Onion Rice)

steps.text: Heat ghee, temper cumin, bay leaf, black cardamom, cinnamon, and peppercorns, then fry sliced onions until rich golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato, and ground spices; cook until glossy, then toss in boiled kabuli chana for 3 minutes so the chickpeas absorb the masala.
Fold in drained rice, 2.75 cups hot water (or chickpea stock), and salt. Cover and cook on low heat for 12 minutes, garnish with ginger juliennes and coriander, and serve with raita.

notes: Hearty protein-rich Punjabi one-pot pulao using pre-boiled chickpeas.

name: Punjabi Kadhi Pakora (Tangy Slow-Simmered Yogurt-Besan Curry with Soft Onion-Gram Flour Fritters & Ghee Tadka)

steps.text: Whisk 1 cup besan with ajwain, crushed coriander seeds, red chilli, salt, a pinch of baking soda, and water into a thick batter; fold in sliced onions and coriander. Fry spoonfuls in medium-hot mustard oil until golden and porous; set aside.

Whisk sour curd with 1/2 cup besan, turmeric, red chilli powder, and 5 cups water until lump-free. Temper methi dana, cumin, hing, and ginger-garlic paste in 1 tbsp oil, pour in the yogurt-besan mixture, bring to a boil while stirring, then simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes until velvety.

steps.section: Soak pakoras and crown with Kashmiri chilli ghee tadka
steps.text: Add the pakoras and crushed kasuri methi to the simmering kadhi for 5 minutes so they turn pillow-soft. Pour a sizzling desi ghee tadka of cumin, whole dried red chillies, curry leaves, and Kashmiri chilli powder on top.

notes: Slow-cooking the kadhi for at least 20 minutes develops its signature rich, silky dhaba flavor.

name: Punjabi Methi Mathri (Flaky Kasuri Methi & Black Pepper Whole-Wheat Biscuits)

steps.text: Rub ghee, crushed kasuri methi, coarse black pepper, ajwain, hing, and salt into the flours, then bind with minimal warm water into a tight, crumbly dough.

steps.section: Flatten into rustic discs and prick
steps.text: Pinch small balls, press between your palms into rustic 2-inch discs with cracked edges, and prick with a fork.

steps.section: Slow-fry on low heat until deep golden
steps.text: Fry in low-temperature oil for 14–16 minutes per batch until cooked through and flaky-crisp.

notes: Rustic, flaky fenugreek savory biscuits traditionally served with mango pickle and masala chai.

name: Pur Bhora Chalkumro Fry (Mustard-Poppy Stuffed Ash Gourd Pan-Fry)

steps.section: Stuff ash gourd pockets with shorshe-posto-narkel paste
steps.text: Cut a pocket into each chalkumro slice, rub lightly with salt, and stuff with thick mustard, poppy seed, grated coconut, and green chilli paste.

steps.section: Dip in crisp batter and shallow-fry
steps.text: Dip stuffed slices into seasoned rice-besan batter and shallow-fry in mustard oil until golden brown on both sides.

notes: A prized traditional Bengali delicacy—juicy ash gourd filled with pungent mustard-poppy paste.

name: Pur Bhora Kakrol Fry (Mustard-Coconut Stuffed Spiny Gourd Pan-Fry)

steps.section: Parboil kakrol shells and prepare stuffing
steps.text: Boil halved kakrol in salted turmeric water for 4 minutes, scoop out the inner seeds, and grind the tender seeds with mustard paste, poppy seeds, grated coconut, green chillies, and salt.

steps.section: Stuff shells, dip in batter and fry
steps.text: Fill the kakrol cavities with the spiced mustard-coconut paste, seal the top with a thin rice-flour & besan batter, and shallow-fry in mustard oil until golden and crisp.

notes: A traditional Bengali bhoj-style stuffed spiny gourd delicacy.

name: Pur Bhora Kakroler Bora (Mustard-Coconut Stuffed Spiny Gourd Batter Fritters)

steps.section: Hollow parboiled kakrol and fill with shorshe-narkel pur
steps.text: Boil halved kakrol in salted water for 4 minutes, scoop out the seeds, mash the soft pulp with mustard paste, poppy paste, grated coconut, green chillies, and salt, and pack back into the shells.

steps.section: Enrobe in crisp rice-besan batter and fry
steps.text: Dip each stuffed kakrol half in a thick rice-flour and besan batter and fry in hot mustard oil until the shell is golden and crisp.

notes: One of Bengal's most prized monsoon lunch accompaniments with plain rice and masoor dal.

name: Pur Bhora Potoler Bora (Spiced Mustard-Poppy Stuffed Pointed Gourd Fritters)

steps.text: Scoop out the tender seeds of halved potol, grind or mash them with poppy-mustard paste, grated coconut, green chillies, salt, and a drizzle of raw mustard oil, then stuff into the potol boats.

steps.section: Coat in seasoned rice-besan batter and fry
steps.text: Dip the stuffed potol halves (or sandwich two halves together) into a thick besan, rice flour, and kalo jeere batter and fry in medium-hot mustard oil until crisp and golden.

notes: A traditional Bengali Thakurbarir-style delicacy served with hot steamed rice and Gondhoraj lebu.

name: Puran Poli (Maharashtrian Sweet Chana Dal & Jaggery Stuffed Thin Maida Flatbread)

steps.text: Mash boiled chana dal and cook with grated jaggery on medium-low heat until thick and sticky. Flavor with cardamom and nutmeg, then pass through a sieve (puran yantra) for a velvety smooth stuffing.
Knead maida and atta with turmeric, salt, 2 tbsp oil, and water into an ultra-soft, elastic dough. Rest covered with oil for 30 minutes.

steps.section: Stuff, roll thin and roast with ghee
steps.text: Enclose a generous ball of puran inside dough, dust with flour, roll paper-thin on a board, and roast on a hot griddle with dollops of pure ghee until puffed with golden blisters.

notes: The festive soul of Maharashtra and Gujarat, served with warm milk or katachi amti on Gudi Padwa and Holi.

name: Puri Bhaji Aloo (Maharashtrian / South Indian Yellow Potato Masala)

steps.text: Heat oil, splutter mustard seeds, cumin seeds, urad dal, and chana dal until golden, then add hing, curry leaves, ginger, and green chillies.
Add sliced onions and turmeric powder; sauté until soft and translucent without browning.
Add boiled potatoes, salt, a pinch of sugar, and 1/2 cup warm water; mash slightly and cook covered for 5 minutes. Finish with lemon juice and fresh coriander.

notes: Classic golden potato bhaji served with hot puffed pooris or dosa.

name: Puttu

steps.text: Wash, chop and measure the ingredients. Soak or ferment the base if the recipe requires it.
Heat oil, add mustard or cumin seeds, onion, chilli and vegetables.
Add the main ingredient and the required water or batter; cook until tender and serve hot.

notes: Starter recipe: adjust spice, liquid and cooking time to suit the ingredient and your taste.

name: Pyaz Paratha (Spiced Onion Stuffed Paratha)

steps.text: Toss finely chopped onions with roasted besan, green chillies, coriander, ajwain, crushed coriander seeds, amchur, red chilli powder, and add salt right before stuffing.
Place the spiced onion mixture inside rolled wheat dough cups, seal tightly, and roll out gently.
Pan-fry on a hot tawa with ghee until crisp and golden brown on both sides.

notes: Adding 1 tbsp roasted besan prevents the onions from releasing water while rolling.

name: Quinoa Vegetable Khichdi (High-Protein Tri-Color Quinoa, Yellow Moong Dal & Ghee Tadka Khichdi)

ingredients.name: Thoroughly Rinsed in a Fine Sieve

steps.text: Rub and rinse quinoa thoroughly under cold running water in a fine mesh strainer for 1 minute to remove any natural bitterness.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle cumin seeds and hing, and saute ginger, green chillies, and mixed vegetables for 3 minutes.
Add rinsed quinoa, washed moong dal, turmeric, salt, and 3.5 cups water. Pressure-cook for 2 whistles on medium flame. Fluff with a fork and finish with lemon juice and cilantro.

notes: Complete-protein modern twist on classic khichdi with nutty quinoa pearls and creamy yellow lentils.

name: Rabdi Malpua (Crispy-Edged Spiced Maida & Fennel Pancakes Soaked in Saffron Syrup)

steps.text: Whisk maida, grated khoya, crushed fennel seeds, and warm milk into a lump-free pourable batter; rest for 20 minutes to develop texture.
Boil sugar, water, and saffron for 6 minutes into a sticky syrup; keep warm on low heat.

steps.section: Fry in desi ghee and serve with rabdi
steps.text: Ladle batter into shallow hot ghee in a wide flat pan, fry until lacy and crisp on the edges and soft in the middle. Dip in warm syrup for 2 minutes, then top lavishly with thick rabdi and pistachios.

notes: Pushkar and Varanasi pilgrim specialty: rich, aromatic pancakes crowned with creamy reduced milk rabdi.

name: Rabri

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.

name: Radhaballabhi (Bengali Spiced Urad Dal Stuffed Puri)

steps.text: Grind soaked urad dal with green chillies and ginger into a coarse paste. Temper oil with hing and nigella seeds, sauté the dal paste with roasted fennel-cumin masala, salt, and sugar until dry and aromatic; cool completely.
Knead flour with ghee, salt, and water into a smooth dough. Stuff each dough ball with a portion of spiced urad dal paste, seal tightly, and roll into medium-thick rounds.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil until puffed and golden on both sides. Serve hot with cholar dal or aloor dum.

notes: Iconic Bengali festive stuffed puri scented with roasted fennel (mouri), ginger, and hing.

name: Ragi / Nachni Laddoo (Roasted Finger Millet, Ghee, Jaggery & Sesame Laddoo)

steps.text: Heat ghee in a kadhai and roast ragi flour on low heat for 8–10 minutes until nutty and aromatic; toast sesame seeds and chopped peanuts alongside for the last 2 minutes.
Turn off heat, mix in finely grated jaggery and cardamom so the jaggery melts into the warm flour, and roll into iron-rich round laddoos.

notes: Calcium- and iron-rich Maharashtrian Nachni laddoo ready in 25 minutes.

name: Ragi Malt

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.

name: Rajasthani Besan Pyaz ki Sabzi (Spring Onion / Sliced Onion & Roasted Gram Flour Masala Sabzi)

ingredients.name: Thickly Sliced Onions (or Chopped Spring Onions with Greens)

steps.text: Heat mustard oil, crackle cumin, fennel, kalonji, crushed coriander seeds, and hing. Add thickly sliced onions and saute for 4 minutes until just softened yet still retaining bite.

steps.section: Roast besan and spices with onions
steps.text: Sprinkle turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder, salt, and besan over the onions; roast on low flame for 5 minutes until the besan turns golden and fragrant.
Sprinkle whisked sour curd (or warm water with amchur), cover for 3–4 minutes on low heat until the besan forms a soft, savory coating around the sweet onions, and finish with fresh coriander.

notes: A beloved Jodhpur and Shekhawati household dish that turns humble onions and gram flour into a deeply flavorful accompaniment for rotis.

name: Rajasthani Gatta Pulao / Gatte ke Chawal (Fragrant Basmati Rice Pilaf with Fried Besan Dumplings & Whole Spices)

steps.text: Knead besan with curd, 1 tbsp ghee, ajwain, fennel, chilli powder, and salt into logs. Boil for 10 minutes, slice into coins, and shallow-fry in ghee until golden and crisp on the outside.
Boil soaked basmati rice with salt and a drop of ghee until 90% done; drain and fluff gently.

steps.section: Layer and toss with caramelized onions, nuts, and gattas
steps.text: Heat ghee in a heavy kadai, fry cashews, raisins, and whole spices, then caramelize sliced onions with turmeric, Kashmiri chilli, and garam masala. Gently fold in the fried gattas, cooked basmati rice, mint, and coriander, cover on low dum for 4 minutes, and serve with boondi raita or kadhi.

notes: Festive Marwari rice dish where crisp golden besan dumplings stud aromatic saffron-and-ghee spiced rice.

name: Rajasthani Gatte ki Sabzi (Marwari Spiced Gram Flour Dumplings in Tangy Yogurt Gravy)

steps.text: Rub besan with 2 tbsp warm oil/ghee, carom seeds, crushed fennel, turmeric, red chilli powder, a pinch of baking soda, salt, and 2 tbsp curd. Knead into a smooth, pliable dough using minimal warm water. Roll into 4 cylinder logs and boil in simmering water for 10–12 minutes until blisters appear on the surface and they float.
Drain the boiled logs (reserve the poaching liquid for gravy) and slice into 1/2-inch discs. Optionally toss in 1 tsp ghee for 2 minutes until lightly golden at the edges.

steps.section: Simmer in spiced Marwari yogurt gravy
steps.text: Whisk curd with coriander powder, turmeric, and Kashmiri chilli powder. Heat ghee in a kadai, temper cumin, mustard, hing, and ginger-chilli paste, then lower heat and stir in the spiced curd continuously until it boils. Add reserved gatta water and sliced gattas, simmer 7–8 minutes, and finish with crushed kasuri methi and coriander.

notes: Adding 1 tbsp ghee and 2 tbsp curd into the besan dough ensures melt-in-the-mouth soft gattas that never turn hard.

name: Rajasthani Marwari Kadhi (Spiced Clove, Fenugreek & Asafoetida Tempered Yogurt-Besan Kadhi)

ingredients.name: Sour Buttermilk (Chaas) or Whisked Sour Curd

steps.text: Whisk besan into sour buttermilk with turmeric, salt, and 2 cups water until completely smooth with zero lumps.

Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a deep pot, temper methi dana, mustard, cumin, cloves, bay leaf, hing, curry leaves, and ginger-green chillies. Pour in the buttermilk-besan liquid and stir continuously until it comes to a boil, then simmer gently for 18–20 minutes.

steps.section: Finish with red chilli ghee chhonk
steps.text: Heat remaining 1 tbsp ghee, bloom dried red chillies and Kashmiri red chilli powder, and pour over the hot kadhi with chopped coriander.

notes: Light, pakora-free Marwari kadhi that accompanies steamed rice, khichdi, or bajra rotla.

name: Rajasthani Papad ki Sabzi (Marwari Roasted Moong/Urad Papad Simmered in Tangy Spiced Yogurt Gravy)

ingredients.name: Spiced Rajasthani Moong/urad Papads (Roasted or Fried & Broken into Triangles)

steps.text: Whisk curd smoothly with 1 tsp besan, coriander powder, turmeric, and Kashmiri red chilli powder so it never splits when heated.

steps.section: Temper spices and simmer dahi gravy
steps.text: Heat ghee in a kadai, crackle cumin, mustard, fenugreek seeds, and hing, then saute grated ginger and green chillies. Lower flame, stir in the spiced curd continuously until it boils, add 1.25 cups warm water and salt, and simmer 5 minutes.

steps.section: Fold in roasted papad pieces and kasuri methi
steps.text: Add the roasted papad triangles and crushed kasuri methi, simmer 1–2 minutes until the papad absorbs the tangy gravy, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve immediately with phulkas or rice.

notes: Quickest 15-minute Marwari household curry; go light on added salt as papads already contain salt and Papad Khar.

name: Rajasthani Pitod ki Sabzi / Pitor Curry (Diamond-Cut Steamed Gram Flour Cakes in Tangy Spiced Yogurt Gravy)

steps.section: Cook and set silky besan pitor (pitod) diamonds
steps.text: Whisk besan with 1/2 cup curd, 2 cups water, 1/2 tsp ajwain, cumin, hing, turmeric, chilli flakes, and salt into a lump-free slurry. Cook in a heavy pan over medium-low heat, stirring constantly for 8–10 minutes until thick and glossy. Spread 1/2-inch thick onto a greased thali, cool 10 minutes until set, and slice into diamond katlis.

Heat ghee in a kadai, temper cumin, mustard, hing, garlic, and ginger-chilli paste. Whisk 1 cup curd with coriander, turmeric, and Kashmiri chilli powder, add to the pan while stirring continuously, and simmer with 1.25 cups warm water for 6 minutes.
Slide the diamond-cut besan pitor pieces into the bubbling yogurt gravy, simmer gently for 3–4 minutes without over-stirring, and garnish with kasuri methi and fresh coriander.

notes: Unlike boiled gattas, Pitod (Pitor) are cooked into a custard-smooth gram flour fudge before slicing into delicate diamonds that melt in the mouth.

steps.section: Knead mashed sweet potato and khoya dough
steps.text: Mash boiled ranga aloo until completely smooth and knead with grated khoya, maida, cardamom powder, 1 tsp ghee, and baking powder into soft balls.
Boil sugar, water, and cardamom pods for 7–8 minutes until lightly syrupy.

steps.section: Deep-fry on low heat and soak
steps.text: Fry the sweet potato balls over low-medium heat until deep golden-brown, then soak in warm sugar syrup for 45 minutes.

notes: Traditional Bengali winter sweet transforming earthy sweet potatoes into melt-in-the-mouth pantuas.

name: Ranga Aloor Puli / Sweet Potato Pitha (Soft Sweet-Potato & Rice-Flour Dumplings in Syrup)

ingredients.name: Sweet Potatoes (Ranga Aloo, Boiled & Mashed Smooth)

steps.section: Knead sweet potato dough and stuff
steps.text: Knead mashed boiled sweet potato with maida, rice flour, and a pinch of cardamom into a soft dough. Stuff small discs with coconut-jaggery pur and seal into smooth ovals or half-moons.

steps.section: Fry golden and soak in syrup
steps.text: Fry in medium-hot oil until golden brown, then soak in warm cardamom-sugar syrup for 20 minutes until soft and juicy.

notes: Ranga aloor puli stays pillowy-soft even at room temperature.

name: Rasbari (Delicate Nepali Spongy Cottage Cheese Balls in Cardamom Syrup)

ingredients.name: Fresh Homemade Chhena (From Whole Cow Milk)

steps.text: Knead fresh, dry chhena on a clean board with your palm heel for 6-8 minutes until completely smooth, soft, and no graininess remains. Mix in 1 tsp suji and shape into smooth crack-free small spheres.

steps.section: Boil in light syrup under high pressure
steps.text: Bring sugar, water, and cracked cardamom to a rolling boil in a wide deep pot. Drop in the chhena balls, cover tightly, and boil on high heat for 15 minutes without opening.

steps.section: Cool and infuse with rose water
steps.text: The rasbari will expand to twice their size into airy, spongy spheres. Remove from heat, stir in rose water, and let cool completely in the syrup before serving.

notes: Nepal's iconic national sweet, revered across Kathmandu and Pokhara for its airy, cloud-like spongy texture.

steps.text: Combine besan with finely ground cloves, black pepper, ajwain, hing, dry ginger, chilli powder, salt, and 3 tbsp hot oil; knead with warm water into a soft dough.

steps.section: Extrude thick strands into hot oil
steps.text: Press the dough through a medium-thick sev disc into medium-hot oil.
Fry until golden and crisp on both sides, drain, and break into bite-sized pieces.

notes: Bold, aromatic Malwa-style thick sev packed with warming clove, ajwain, and black pepper.

name: Rava Fish Egg Fry (Konkani Semolina-Crusted Fish Roe Fry)

steps.text: Cut firm fish roe into thick slabs and marinate with tamarind or kokum extract, red chilli powder, turmeric, a pinch of hing, and salt for 10 minutes.

steps.section: Crust in rava and rice flour
steps.text: Mix fine semolina and rice flour on a plate and press each marinated roe slice firmly into the mixture.
Shallow-fry on medium-low heat in coconut oil for 4 minutes per side until golden and crunchy.

notes: Traditional Goan and Malvani coastal fish roe fry (Gabholi Rava Fry).

name: Rava Prawn Fry (Crispy Semolina-Crusted Prawns)

ingredients.name: Coconut Oil or Vegetable Oil for Shallow Frying

steps.section: Coat prawns in tangy spice paste
steps.text: Mix ginger-garlic paste, tamarind or lemon juice, red chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, and salt; rub thoroughly over the prawns and rest 15 minutes.

steps.section: Dredge in semolina and rice flour
steps.text: Combine fine rava and rice flour on a plate with a pinch of salt and press each spiced prawn into the mixture so it is evenly crusted.
Shallow-fry on a hot tawa or skillet with oil for 2-3 minutes per side until the semolina crust turns golden and crisp.

notes: Goan and Karwar coastal favorite with a super-crunchy golden semolina crust.

name: Reuben-Style Sandwich

steps.text: Wash and finely slice or mash the filling ingredients. Mix with the listed seasonings and spreads; cook any raw meat or seafood fully before assembling.
Spread butter, chutney or sauce on the bread. Add the filling evenly and close or leave open-faced as desired.
Toast or grill in a lightly greased pan until the bread is crisp and any cheese has melted. Cut and serve fresh.

notes: Starter quantities are approximate; cook poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly and refrigerate perishable fillings promptly.

name: Ribbon Pakoda / Nada Thenkuzhal (Crisp Spiced Rice & Besan Ribbon Namkeen)

steps.text: Mix rice flour, besan, roasted gram flour, sesame seeds, chilli powder, hing, salt, strained garlic water, and hot butter into a soft dough.

steps.section: Extrude flat ribbons directly into hot oil
steps.text: Use the flat ribbon slot attachment in a murukku press to press concentric ribbon coils into medium-hot oil.

steps.section: Fry until crisp and break into pieces
steps.text: Fry on medium flame until crisp and golden-red, drain, and break into bite-sized ribbons.

notes: Crisp, savory rice-and-gram flour ribbon snack flavored with garlic and asafoetida.

name: Roasted Butternut Squash & Sage Soup (Velvety Spiced Pumpkin / Butternut Squash Cream Soup)

steps.section: Roast squash with garlic and sage
steps.text: Toss butternut squash cubes, whole garlic cloves, and fresh sage leaves with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast at 200°C (400°F) for 30 minutes until squash is caramelized and tender.
Transfer roasted squash, soft garlic, and crispy sage into a blender with warm vegetable broth. Puree until completely velvety and golden.
Pour pureed soup into a pot, stir in ground nutmeg, ginger, and cream. Simmer for 3 minutes, ladle into bowls, and scatter toasted pumpkin seeds on top.

notes: Roasting squash with fresh sage caramelizes natural sweetness while imparting an earthy, herbaceous depth.

name: Roasted Masala Makhana & Peanut Namkeen (Spiced Ghee-Roasted Fox Nuts)

steps.text: Roast fox nuts in a heavy kadai with 1 tsp ghee on low flame for 7–8 minutes until they crush cleanly with a loud crunch.

steps.section: Temper peanuts, cashews, and curry leaves in ghee
steps.text: In the same pan, heat remaining ghee, fry peanuts, cashews, melon seeds, and curry leaves until golden, then add turmeric, chilli, cumin, black salt, and chaat masala.

steps.section: Toss crisp makhana in spiced ghee
steps.text: Return the roasted makhana to the pan and toss for 1–2 minutes until evenly coated.

notes: Light, protein-rich crunchy fox-nut and peanut namkeen.

Cook potato, tomato and spices, add water, then return fish and simmer gently until cooked through.

Cook potato, tomato and spices, add water, then return fish and simmer gently until cooked through.

name: Rose Falooda Pudding (Basil Seed / Sabja & Saffron Rose Milk Agar Pudding)

steps.section: Bloom sabja seeds and dissolve agar agar
steps.text: Soak sabja seeds in 0.5 cup water until plump and gelatinous. In a small pan, dissolve agar agar powder in 0.5 cup warm water and simmer for 3 minutes until clear.
Warm milk and condensed milk in a pot, stir in rose syrup until beautifully pink and fragrant. Whisk in the hot dissolved agar agar liquid and simmer gently for 2 minutes.

Let rose milk cool slightly for 3 minutes, then gently fold in the drained bloomed sabja seeds so they disperse evenly throughout the pudding rather than sinking. Pour into silicone moulds or dessert glasses and chill for 2 hours until set. Garnish with pistachios and dried rose petals.

notes: Translates the beloved street-style Mumbai/Kolkata Falooda drink into a stunning, cooling set jelly-pudding dessert.

steps.text: Measure the ingredients. Brew tea or coffee with hot water as appropriate, or wash and cut fresh fruit and herbs.
Combine the ingredients listed for this drink. Simmer tea spices if needed; blend milkshakes and smoothies until smooth.
Strain if desired, adjust sweetness and strength, then serve hot or chilled with ice as appropriate.

notes: Use potable water and fresh ingredients. Refrigerate dairy-based drinks promptly; sweeten to taste.
